data.description: A benign tumor composed predominantly of fibroblasts and dense collagen, usually arising in ventricular myocardium. The collagen-rich appearance of the supplied histology makes this a leading consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Apparently well-defined mass near the left ventricular apex
Abundant fibrous tissue visible in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 57 is less typical because cardiac fibromas occur more commonly in children
The conspicuous vascular channels in the histology warrant consideration of a vascular lesion

data.description: A benign tumor of blood vessels that can develop in any cardiac chamber or within myocardium. Some lesions contain substantial fibrous tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Vascular channels visible within the supplied tissue sections
Apparent contrast enhancement of the mass on the supplied imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly dense collagenous tissue is less typical of a conventional hemangioma

data.description: A benign cardiac tumor composed of myxoma cells in a gelatinous extracellular matrix. Most arise in the left atrium, but ventricular tumors occasionally occur.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac mass in a middle-aged woman
Mass projecting toward the left ventricular cavity
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular apical location is uncommon for a myxoma
The supplied histology appears predominantly collagenous rather than characteristically myxoid

data.description: A rare benign, tumor-like proliferation of mature cardiac muscle cells, often accompanied by fibrosis and abnormal vascular structures.
symptoms_in_common: Fibrous tissue and vascular structures in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied histology does not clearly show the disorganized, hypertrophied cardiac myocytes expected to dominate this lesion

data.description: A blood clot within the left ventricle that can become fibrotic and resemble a tumor. It usually develops with impaired ventricular contraction, myocardial infarction, or an apical aneurysm.
symptoms_in_common: Fibrous tissue and vascular channels can occur in an organized, recanalized thrombus
symptoms_not_in_common: No known cardiac disease or relevant medical history to predispose to ventricular thrombosis
Apparent enhancement and a discrete tissue mass are less typical of an uncomplicated thrombus

data.description: A congenital region of abnormal lung within the normal pleural covering that receives blood from a systemic artery, usually the aorta. The left basal lesion and apparent aortic feeding vessel make pulmonary sequestration a leading possibility, although the subtype cannot be established confidently from these images alone.
symptoms_in_common: Left upper quadrant pain from irritation near the diaphragm
Left basal tissue-like lesion with vascularity and an apparent systemic feeding vessel on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain worsened by lying down is not a characteristic feature
No leukocytosis despite suspected infection, although this does not exclude it

data.diagnosis: Inflamed or infected extralobar pulmonary sequestration
data.description: A congenital mass of nonfunctioning lung with its own pleural covering and systemic arterial supply. It often lies near the left diaphragm and can cause abdominal or pleuritic pain when inflamed, infected, or complicated by torsion.
symptoms_in_common: Basal vascular lesion with an apparent vessel arising near the aorta
symptoms_not_in_common: Productive cough is less typical because the lesion usually lacks communication with the airways
Pain worsened by lying down is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Left lower lobe pneumonia with diaphragmatic pleurisy
data.description: An infection of the lower left lung that can irritate the diaphragm and present predominantly as upper abdominal pain in children.
symptoms_in_common: Tissue-like basal lung abnormality that could resemble consolidation
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparent systemic arterial feeding vessel is not typical of ordinary pneumonia
Pain worsened by lying down is not a defining feature
No leukocytosis, although pneumonia can occur with a normal white blood cell count

data.description: A congenital abnormality of lung development containing malformed airways or cysts that may first become symptomatic during childhood infection. A hybrid lesion can also have the systemic arterial supply of a sequestration.
symptoms_in_common: Localized abnormal tissue at the left lung base
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied images do not clearly show the characteristic multiple cystic air spaces
An apparent systemic feeding vessel favors sequestration or a hybrid lesion rather than an isolated airway malformation
Positional pain is not characteristic

data.description: A localized collection of pus caused by necrotizing lung infection, potentially developing within abnormal congenital lung tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Left upper quadrant pain from a lesion close to the diaphragm
symptoms_not_in_common: Only mild cough and whitish rather than purulent sputum
No leukocytosis
No clearly demonstrated thick-walled cavity or air-fluid level on the supplied images
An apparent systemic feeding vessel is not explained by an isolated lung abscess

data.description: A hepatic infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica, sometimes presenting months or years after exposure in an endemic region. The CT shows hypodense hepatic lesions compatible with abscesses, although imaging alone cannot establish their cause.
symptoms_in_common: Marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Diaphragmatic discomfort and difficulty with deep inspiration, potentially from a left-lobe hepatic abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized arthralgia is not a characteristic feature
Multiple hepatic lesions are less typical than a solitary right-lobe abscess
Absence of abdominal tenderness is less typical, although it does not exclude the diagnosis

data.description: A bacterial infection producing one or more pus-filled cavities in the liver, usually arising from biliary infection, intra-abdominal infection, or bloodstream spread.
symptoms_in_common: Pain on deep inspiration and tachypnoea from diaphragmatic irritation
symptoms_not_in_common: Loose stools are not a characteristic presenting symptom
Generalized arthralgia is not typical
No abdominal tenderness or evident biliary symptoms
Negative blood cultures provide no microbiological support, although they do not exclude an abscess

data.description: An infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, acquired from contaminated soil or water in endemic areas, including northern Australia and Southeast Asia. It can produce multiple visceral abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to Western Australia, if exposure occurred in its tropical northern region
Marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Multiple hypodense hepatic lesions compatible with abscesses
symptoms_not_in_common: Loose stools are not a defining manifestation
Normal chest radiograph provides no evidence of the common pulmonary presentation
Negative blood cultures provide no confirmation of disseminated infection
The apparently mild clinical condition is less typical of severe disseminated melioidosis

data.description: A liver cyst caused by Echinococcus infection that develops secondary bacterial infection. Exposure may occur in sheep-raising regions, including parts of Australia, but cysts generally develop over a prolonged period.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, neutrophilia, and high C-reactive protein if secondary infection is present
Discomfort on deep inspiration from a lesion near the diaphragm
Travel to a region where hydatid disease can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Loose stools are not characteristic
Generalized myalgia and arthralgia are nonspecific
The acute illness would be atypical for an uncomplicated hydatid cyst
The provided CT does not clearly demonstrate characteristic daughter cysts or a calcified cyst wall

data.description: An uncommon extrapulmonary manifestation of tuberculosis that can cause focal hepatic lesions or abscesses. Confirmation generally requires tissue sampling and mycobacterial testing.
symptoms_in_common: Negative routine blood cultures, which do not reliably detect tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt three-day presentation is less typical than a subacute or chronic illness
Severe neutrophilia is less characteristic
Loose stools and generalized arthralgia are not typical of isolated hepatic tuberculosis
No reported weight loss, night sweats, or persistent cough

data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disease causing steadily progressive neurological disability, often dominated by spinal cord dysfunction. This is a leading consideration, but the available findings alone do not establish diagnostic criteria.
symptoms_in_common: Four years of progressively worsening gait
Spasticity, brisk reflexes and sustained ankle clonus
Reduced visual acuity and dyschromatopsia with apparent bilateral optic nerve atrophy and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Small cerebral white matter signal abnormalities on the supplied MRI, although these are nonspecific
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow visual deterioration over a decade without a reported episode of acute optic neuritis
Maternal history of blindness, which raises the possibility of inherited optic neuropathy
Relatively preserved vision despite substantial retinal nerve fiber layer thinning

data.diagnosis: OPA1-related dominant optic atrophy plus syndrome
data.description: An inherited mitochondrial disorder causing optic atrophy, sometimes accompanied by neurological manifestations such as spastic paraplegia, peripheral neuropathy or ataxia.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent bilateral optic disc pallor and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Maternal history of blindness compatible with dominant inheritance
Progressive spastic gait and sensory disturbance
Urinary symptoms potentially associated with a spastic paraplegia phenotype
symptoms_not_in_common: Visual symptoms first recognized around age 50 rather than the more usual childhood onset
CSF oligoclonal bands are not a characteristic finding
Predominantly superior and inferior retinal nerve fiber layer thinning rather than the classic temporal predominance

data.diagnosis: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy with an MS-like syndrome (Harding disease)
data.description: A mitochondrial optic neuropathy that can coexist with an inflammatory demyelinating syndrome resembling multiple sclerosis, particularly in women.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal history of blindness compatible with mitochondrial inheritance
Apparent optic atrophy and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Progressive spastic gait, sensory disturbance and bladder dysfunction
CSF oligoclonal bands compatible with the associated MS-like syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow, mild visual deterioration over many years rather than typical subacute, marked central visual loss
No detectable visual field defect, whereas central or cecocentral scotomas are typical
Visual onset around age 50 is later than usual
Preserved ability to drive despite longstanding visual symptoms

data.diagnosis: Complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia with optic atrophy
data.description: A group of inherited disorders causing progressive corticospinal tract dysfunction, with some subtypes also producing optic atrophy, sensory abnormalities and other neurological features.
symptoms_in_common: Increased lower-limb tone, brisk reflexes and sustained ankle clonus
Preserved lower-limb power despite prominent spasticity
Progressive visual dysfunction with apparent optic atrophy
Maternal blindness suggesting a possible inherited neurological disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF oligoclonal bands are not typical
No reported family history of spastic gait or paraplegia
Maternal Parkinson's disease with dementia is not a defining feature of most subtypes

data.description: An inflammatory disorder primarily affecting the optic nerves and spinal cord. Seronegative disease is possible, but stricter clinical and imaging criteria are required.
symptoms_in_common: Visual dysfunction with apparent optic nerve atrophy
Spastic gait and sensory disturbance compatible with spinal cord dysfunction
Negative aquaporin-4 antibodies do not completely exclude the disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Steady progression over four years without discrete optic neuritis or myelitis attacks
Mild, slowly progressive visual loss rather than typically severe attack-related loss
CSF oligoclonal bands are less typical than in multiple sclerosis
No clear longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesion is demonstrated in the supplied image
Maternal blindness suggests an inherited alternative

data.description: An autosomal recessive disorder of copper transport causing hepatic, neurological, and ocular copper accumulation. The homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) variant establishes this as the leading diagnosis; the ocular and brain findings provide additional support.
symptoms_in_common: Generalized pruritus associated with liver dysfunction
Petechiae and ecchymoses potentially related to hepatic coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia
Corneal findings consistent with Kayser-Fleischer rings
Bilateral basal ganglia MRI signal abnormalities
Liver biopsy appearances suggestive of chronic injury and fibrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial acne is not a characteristic manifestation
Pruritus-dominant presentation is less typical than other hepatic presentations

data.description: Liver injury caused by toxic or idiosyncratic reactions to herbal products, sometimes producing cholestasis and impaired hepatic synthetic function. It could coexist with Wilson disease but does not explain the genetic findings.
symptoms_in_common: Chinese herbal medicine exposure for approximately 9 months
Petechiae and ecchymoses if hepatic synthetic function is impaired
Possible inflammatory and fibrotic liver biopsy changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B variant is not explained
Kayser-Fleischer-like corneal findings are not typical
Bilateral basal ganglia abnormalities are not typical of uncomplicated herbal liver injury
Amenorrhea, menstrual irregularities, and acne are not characteristic

data.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory liver disease that can occur in adolescent girls and cause chronic hepatitis, fibrosis, jaundice, and coagulopathy. It is a substantially less likely alternative given the diagnostic ATP7B finding.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses potentially associated with advanced liver dysfunction
Menstrual irregularities potentially associated with chronic liver disease
Liver biopsy appearances suggesting inflammation and fibrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent generalized pruritus is less typical unless cholestasis overlaps
Kayser-Fleischer-like corneal findings are not characteristic
Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B variant is not explained
Basal ganglia MRI abnormalities are not a typical primary manifestation
Facial acne is not characteristic

data.description: A chronic inflammatory and fibrosing disease of the bile ducts that can occur in children and cause cholestatic liver disease. Confirmation requires biliary evaluation, and it does not account for the Wilson-specific findings.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses if advanced liver disease or vitamin K deficiency is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B variant is not explained
Kayser-Fleischer-like corneal findings are not characteristic
Bilateral basal ganglia MRI abnormalities are not typical
Amenorrhea, menstrual irregularities, and acne are not characteristic presenting features

data.description: A group of inherited bile-transport disorders causing persistent cholestasis, often with severe itching and progressive liver fibrosis. Some forms present in adolescence, although the supplied ATP7B result instead supports Wilson disease.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae and ecchymoses potentially associated with vitamin K deficiency or advanced liver dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B variant indicates a different inherited disorder
Kayser-Fleischer-like corneal findings are not characteristic
Basal ganglia MRI abnormalities are not typical
Facial acne and pigmentation are not characteristic
Amenorrhea and menstrual irregularities are not typical primary manifestations

data.description: A drug-triggered acute neutrophilic dermatosis causing fever and tender red plaques or nodules. The timing after azathioprine initiation and neutrophilic leukocytosis make this a leading possibility; skin biopsy is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt onset of fever and lethargy
Painful erythematous plaques or nodules on the limbs
Symptoms beginning shortly after azathioprine initiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Knee effusions with noninflammatory synovial fluid are not a defining feature
Mild rheumatoid factor elevation is nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.description: An idiosyncratic systemic reaction to azathioprine, often developing within the first few weeks and producing fever, malaise, rash, and joint pain. It can overlap with drug-induced Sweet syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilic leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete tender plaques or nodules suggest a specific cutaneous reaction such as Sweet syndrome rather than a nonspecific drug eruption
Knee effusions are possible but not a characteristic finding

data.description: A medication-associated inflammatory reaction characterized by fever, rash, and polyarthralgia, usually appearing one to two weeks after exposure. Unlike classic serum sickness, renal involvement is generally absent.
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful plaques or nodules are less typical than an itchy urticarial or morbilliform eruption
Marked neutrophilic leukocytosis favors a neutrophilic dermatosis

data.description: An inflammatory disorder of subcutaneous fat causing tender red nodules, usually on the shins, sometimes triggered by medications, infections, or systemic inflammatory disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: The pictured lesions include plaques on upper limbs rather than predominantly deep nodules on the anterior shins
Prominent neutrophilic leukocytosis is less specific for erythema nodosum

data.description: Inflammation of small skin vessels, potentially triggered by azathioprine, causing painful purpuric lesions and sometimes fever or joint pain. Skin biopsy can distinguish it from neutrophilic dermatoses.
symptoms_not_in_common: The photographed lesions are not clearly the palpable, nonblanching purpura typical of small-vessel vasculitis
Upper-limb plaques are less typical than dependent lower-leg purpura
Normal renal function and urinalysis argue against systemic renal involvement, although they do not exclude skin-limited disease

data.description: Bleeding into the space behind the pharynx following neck trauma. This is the leading consideration given the marked prevertebral soft-tissue expansion on the supplied CT image and posterior pharyngeal swelling. Progressive expansion can cause life-threatening airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising extending onto the anterior chest wall
Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling with potential airway compromise

data.diagnosis: Blunt laryngeal injury with possible laryngeal cartilage fracture
data.description: Trauma to the larynx can cause cartilage fractures, mucosal injury, and hematoma or edema, producing voice changes and potentially obstructing the airway. A fracture is not established by the supplied image.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent posterior pharyngeal wall swelling is less typical of an isolated laryngeal injury
Bruising tracking onto the chest suggests more extensive soft-tissue bleeding

data.diagnosis: Cervical ligamentous injury with associated prevertebral hematoma
data.description: A fall can injure cervical ligaments, particularly through hyperextension, causing bleeding anterior to the spine even without an obvious fracture. CT soft-tissue swelling may suggest this possibility, but MRI is generally needed to assess ligament integrity.
symptoms_in_common: Hoarseness and potential airway compromise from adjacent swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of cervical spine tenderness makes a symptomatic spinal injury less apparent but does not exclude it
Extensive superficial bruising onto the chest is not typical of an isolated ligament injury

data.diagnosis: Traumatic cervical vascular injury with expanding neck hematoma
data.description: Injury to a cervical artery or vein can produce an expanding hematoma extending into deep neck spaces. CT angiography would be needed to identify an injured vessel or active bleeding; neither is established by this single image.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall
Posterior pharyngeal swelling with potential airway compromise
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain specifically associated with neck movement is less characteristic of an isolated vascular injury

data.description: A tear in the hypopharyngeal wall following blunt trauma can cause deep neck swelling, pain, dysphagia, and airway compromise. Extraluminal gas or a contrast leak would support this diagnosis, but these are not established by the supplied image.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive bruising tracking onto the chest is more suggestive of hemorrhage than an isolated pharyngeal tear

data.description: An insulin-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that causes endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. This is the most likely diagnosis given fasting hypoglycemia, elevated insulin and C-peptide, and a hypervascular pancreatic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent episodes after several hours without eating, especially at night or early morning
Elevated insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycemia
Confusion, poor concentration, irritability, and memory lapses
Weakness, fatigue, and cold clammy episodes
Craving sweets and symptom relief after drinking cola
Marked weight gain from frequent carbohydrate intake

data.description: A rare disorder of excessive insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells, sometimes associated with diffuse beta-cell abnormalities termed nesidioblastosis. It usually causes postprandial rather than fasting hypoglycemia.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide
Confusion, poor concentration, and memory lapses
Weakness, fatigue, and cold clammy episodes
Weight gain associated with repeated eating to prevent symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly fasting, nighttime, and early-morning episodes
Discrete hypervascular pancreatic lesion, which favors insulinoma

data.description: Insulin-binding autoantibodies can cause inappropriate release of bound insulin and recurrent hypoglycemia without administered insulin. Episodes are often postprandial, although fasting episodes can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated C-peptide compatible with endogenous insulin secretion
Weakness, fatigue, and cold clammy episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete pancreatic lesion, which is not explained by this syndrome
Predominantly fasting episodes rather than the more typical delayed postprandial pattern

data.description: Exposure to insulin-secretagogue medications can cause hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide, mimicking insulinoma. A blood or urine drug screen during an episode helps distinguish this cause.
symptoms_in_common: Low glucose with elevated insulin and C-peptide
Confusion, poor concentration, and memory lapses
Weakness, fatigue, and cold clammy episodes
Episodes worsened by prolonged periods without eating
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported absence of medication use or known exposure
Hypervascular pancreatic lesion, which medication exposure does not explain

data.description: Deficient cortisol production can impair maintenance of blood glucose during fasting and cause weakness, fatigue, and hypoglycemia. It is substantially less likely here because adrenal testing was normal and the biochemical findings indicate inappropriate insulin secretion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated insulin and C-peptide during hypoglycemia
Normal adrenal testing
Marked weight gain rather than typical weight loss
Normal electrolytes and stable vital signs
Hypervascular pancreatic lesion

data.description: Hypermobility of the lower costal cartilages, usually ribs 8–10, can irritate adjacent intercostal nerves. This is the leading possibility; the ultrasound views suggest differing relative positions of the lower ribs, but confirmation requires dynamic imaging correlated with pain.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent sharp pain in the right lower anterior chest wall
Pain triggered by exercise, particularly abdominal crunches
Absence of symptoms during ordinary daily activities

data.description: Overuse or injury of muscles between the ribs can cause localized chest wall pain during movements that load the thorax.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms specifically triggered by abdominal crunches rather than a broader range of chest wall movements are less characteristic

data.description: Overuse injury at the upper attachment of the rectus abdominis to the lower costal cartilages can produce pain near the anterior costal margin.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms beginning with a new exercise regimen
Pain especially triggered by abdominal crunches
Pain in the lower anterior thoracic wall
No symptoms during normal daily activities
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent sharp rib-region pain is less characteristic than localized muscular soreness, although it can occur

data.description: Inflammation or mechanical irritation of the rib cartilage attachments causes anterior chest wall pain, usually at the upper parasternal joints.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain confined to the lower right anterior chest wall rather than the upper parasternal region
Pain predominantly triggered by abdominal crunches
Complete absence of symptoms during ordinary daily activities is less characteristic

data.description: Repetitive loading can cause a small rib fracture without a single traumatic event. The supplied ultrasound images alone do not establish a fracture.
symptoms_not_in_common: Remaining entirely asymptomatic during ordinary daily activities after two months is less characteristic of an ongoing stress fracture
Pain particularly associated with abdominal crunches is less specific for a bony injury

data.description: A clonal myeloid malignancy characterized by persistent eosinophilia, abnormal marrow morphology, and possible eosinophil-mediated organ injury. The illustrated dysplastic cells and apparent chromosome 1/7 abnormality raise suspicion, but marrow evaluation and molecular testing are needed for classification.
symptoms_in_common: Dry cough, wheezing, and dyspnea potentially caused by pulmonary eosinophilic infiltration
Illustrated immature eosinophils and abnormal myeloid morphology
Failure to improve with treatment directed at asthma
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly unilateral right lower lung involvement is less typical than diffuse pulmonary involvement

data.description: A clonal bone marrow disorder causing ineffective blood-cell production and cellular dysplasia. Anemia, illustrated megaloblastoid and abnormal granulocytic morphology, and an apparent chromosome 1/7 abnormality make this an important possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Illustrated megaloblastoid cells and irregularly hypersegmented neutrophils
Apparent cytogenetic abnormality involving chromosomes 1 and 7
Eosinophilia, which can occur in a subset of myelodysplastic neoplasms
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked eosinophilia is uncommon in most myelodysplastic neoplasms
Wheezing and chronic dry cough are not typical direct manifestations
Focal ground-glass opacities and consolidation require an associated pulmonary process

data.description: A syndrome of persistent substantial eosinophilia with attributable organ injury. Pulmonary involvement can mimic asthma; an idiopathic diagnosis requires exclusion of reactive causes and clonal hematologic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to improve with asthma-directed treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Illustrated myeloid dysplasia and an apparent clonal chromosome abnormality argue against an idiopathic form
Anemia is less typical of uncomplicated idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome
Localized unilateral pulmonary disease is less typical than broader organ involvement

data.description: An eosinophilic inflammatory lung disease producing respiratory symptoms over weeks to months, peripheral eosinophilia, and pulmonary opacities. Confirmation generally requires evaluation of lung eosinophilia and exclusion of secondary causes.
symptoms_in_common: Four months of dry cough and dyspnea
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lower-lung predominance is less typical than bilateral peripheral, often upper-lung opacities
Illustrated marrow dysplasia and an apparent chromosome abnormality are not explained by this disease
Anemia is not a defining feature

data.description: A systemic small-vessel vasculitis associated with eosinophilia, asthma, and eosinophilic tissue inflammation. Pulmonary disease may precede recognizable extrapulmonary vasculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia, which may accompany systemic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Illustrated dysplastic marrow cells and an apparent clonal cytogenetic abnormality are not characteristic
A fixed unilateral lower-lung opacity is less typical than transient or multifocal infiltrates
No established history of asthma or reported sinus disease, neuropathy, rash, or renal involvement supports the usual systemic pattern

data.description: A lymphatic malignancy characterized by Hodgkin and Reed–Sternberg cells within an inflammatory background. The extensive lymphadenopathy and large atypical cells in the supplied images make this a leading possibility, pending confirmation of the immunostains.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and distention associated with bulky abdominal lymphadenopathy
Severe anemia with pallor and dizziness
Imaging showing extensive abdominal and thoracic lymphadenopathy and a focal liver lesion
Biopsy showing scattered large atypical cells in an inflammatory background
symptoms_not_in_common: Bloody stools and intermittent diarrhea are not usual presenting features
Profound microcytosis suggests an additional contributor such as gastrointestinal blood loss
Marked short stature suggests a longer-standing process than the reported one-month illness
Shin ecchymoses are not a characteristic feature

data.description: An aggressive T-cell lymphoma that can occur in children and cause systemic inflammation, lymphadenopathy, and extranodal disease. Its large atypical cells can resemble those of Hodgkin lymphoma; immunophenotyping is needed to distinguish them.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia and markedly elevated inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe microcytic anemia is not a defining feature
Bloody stools and occasional diarrhea are uncommon without intestinal involvement
Marked short stature is not a typical presenting feature
Shin ecchymoses are nonspecific

data.description: An aggressive B-cell malignancy that may involve abdominal lymph nodes, bowel, and liver, causing rapidly progressive systemic and gastrointestinal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal bleeding if the bowel is involved
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered large atypical cells in a mixed inflammatory background are less typical than sheets of malignant B cells
Marked short stature is not typical of a newly presenting aggressive lymphoma
Shin ecchymoses are not characteristic
Profound microcytosis requires an additional explanation such as chronic blood loss

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can cause abdominal pain, diarrhea, intestinal bleeding, anemia, and impaired growth in children. The bulky lymphadenopathy and atypical biopsy cells make it less likely than lymphoma here.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent periumbilical and lower abdominal pain
Occasional diarrhea and blood in stools
Weight loss and very low height and weight percentiles
symptoms_not_in_common: Bulky abdominal and thoracic lymphadenopathy is atypical
A focal liver lesion is not a usual manifestation
Large atypical cells in the supplied biopsy are not characteristic
Shin ecchymoses are not a typical inflammatory skin manifestation

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving abdominal lymph nodes or bowel can cause prolonged fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, and anemia. Thoracic and hepatic involvement may occur, but microbiologic or characteristic histologic evidence is required.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia and markedly elevated inflammatory markers
Diarrhea or intestinal bleeding with bowel involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied biopsy appears to show large atypical lymphoid cells rather than characteristic caseating granulomas
Profound microcytic anemia is not specific and may require concurrent blood loss or iron deficiency
Shin ecchymoses are not characteristic
Marked short stature is not readily explained by the reported one-month illness

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: Mosquito-transmitted parasitic infection causing red blood cell destruction and potentially life-threatening organ dysfunction. This is the leading diagnosis: the supplied rapid test appears positive for falciparum malaria, and the blood smear shows numerous delicate ring forms, including double chromatin dots, compatible with P. falciparum. Acute kidney injury makes urgent treatment necessary.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to Tanzania with mosquito bites
Fever with shaking chills, headache, fatigue, and weakness
Dark urine and low haptoglobin consistent with intravascular hemolysis
Decreased urine output and elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial flushing is nonspecific rather than characteristic
Transient blurry vision during fever is not a defining feature and requires further assessment

data.description: A bacterial infection acquired through water or soil contaminated with infected animal urine. Severe disease can cause jaundice, kidney failure, and thrombocytopenia, but it does not explain the malaria-compatible blood smear and rapid test.
symptoms_in_common: Fever with shaking chills and headache
Lower back pain, fatigue, and weakness
Reduced urine output and elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent intravascular hemolysis with low haptoglobin and dark brown urine is less characteristic
Blurry vision confined to fever episodes is not typical
Intraerythrocytic ring forms and a falciparum-positive rapid test are not explained by leptospirosis

data.diagnosis: Dengue fever with severe organ involvement
data.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection that can cause thrombocytopenia, liver injury, and, in severe cases, kidney dysfunction. It is a travel-related alternative but is substantially less consistent with the parasitologic findings.
symptoms_in_common: Thrombocytopenia and elevated AST and ALT
Acute kidney dysfunction can occur in severe disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hemolysis with low haptoglobin and dark brown urine is not typical
Jaundice is uncommon outside severe hepatic involvement
Intraerythrocytic parasites and a falciparum-positive rapid test are not explained by dengue

data.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection found in parts of Africa that can progress to jaundice, liver injury, bleeding, and kidney failure. Exposure location and vaccination history affect its likelihood; it does not explain the malaria test findings.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, chills, headache, fatigue, and weakness
Scleral icterus, hyperbilirubinemia, and elevated liver enzymes
Decreased urine output and elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Low haptoglobin suggesting prominent intravascular hemolysis is not characteristic
Nonbloody diarrhea is less characteristic
Intraerythrocytic ring forms and a falciparum-positive rapid test are not explained by yellow fever

data.description: A usually tick-transmitted infection of red blood cells that can cause hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and kidney injury. Its ring forms can resemble malaria on microscopy, but travel to Tanzania, mosquito exposure, and the apparent falciparum-positive test strongly favor malaria.
symptoms_in_common: Fever with shaking chills, headache, fatigue, and weakness
Hemolysis with low haptoglobin, dark urine, and jaundice
Intraerythrocytic ring forms on blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Mosquito exposure is not the typical transmission route
A falciparum-positive malaria rapid test is not expected
Transient blurry vision and facial flushing are not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Delayed cervical esophageal perforation caused by spinal fixation hardware erosion
data.description: Cervical fixation plates or screws can erode into the pharynx or esophagus years after surgery, causing leakage and deep infection. The apparent exposed hardware and communication with a pus-containing cavity in the images strongly suggest this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Fever and chills from secondary infection
Prior cervical spine fixation with metal plates
symptoms_not_in_common: Preexisting traumatic quadriplegia is not caused by esophageal perforation

data.diagnosis: Retropharyngeal or prevertebral abscess with thoracic extension
data.description: A deep neck-space infection can cause a collection behind the pharynx or adjacent to the cervical spine and spread downward into the thorax.
symptoms_in_common: Large abscess involving cervical and thoracic paraspinal tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: Preexisting traumatic quadriplegia is not a manifestation of this infection
Extension to T11 is unusually extensive for an isolated retropharyngeal abscess

data.diagnosis: Descending mediastinitis secondary to pharyngoesophageal leakage
data.description: A severe mediastinal infection can develop when contamination from a cervical pharyngeal or esophageal defect spreads into the chest. The images labeled with mediastinal pus support this complication.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent pus within a mediastinal cavity
symptoms_not_in_common: Preexisting traumatic quadriplegia is unrelated to the acute mediastinal infection

data.diagnosis: Delayed cervical spinal implant infection with paraspinal abscess
data.description: An infection involving spinal fixation hardware can present years after implantation and cause extensive adjacent soft-tissue abscesses, sometimes following contamination from esophageal erosion.
symptoms_in_common: History of cervical metal plate implantation
Dysphagia and odynophagia from adjacent inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent communication with the esophageal lumen is not typical of an isolated implant infection
Preexisting traumatic quadriplegia does not indicate a new implant infection

data.diagnosis: Cervicothoracic vertebral osteomyelitis with paraspinal abscess
data.description: Infection of vertebral bone, sometimes involving adjacent discs, can arise near implanted hardware or spread from neighboring infected tissues and produce a paraspinal abscess. Confirmation requires evidence of vertebral or disc involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysphagia and odynophagia are not typical unless infection extends into adjacent neck tissues
Apparent exposed hardware within the esophageal lumen suggests an additional perforation rather than isolated bone infection
Longstanding traumatic quadriplegia is not evidence of new infection-related neurological injury

data.description: A full-thickness esophageal tear caused by forceful vomiting, allowing air and gastrointestinal contents to enter the mediastinum and pleural space. This is the leading concern and a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate specialist assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Repeated vomiting preceding severe chest pain
Chest pain radiating to the back
Images appear to show pneumomediastinum extending into the neck
Left pneumothorax and bilateral pleural effusions, larger on the left
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever and a normal complete blood count are less typical of established mediastinal infection, but do not exclude early rupture

data.description: Air leaks from ruptured alveoli into the mediastinum after a sudden rise in intrathoracic pressure, such as during vomiting. Esophageal rupture must be excluded in this presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent mediastinal air extending into cervical soft tissues
Afebrile presentation with normal blood counts
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantial left-sided pleural fluid is unusual for uncomplicated spontaneous pneumomediastinum
Severe chest pain radiating to the back with pleural air and fluid raises greater concern for esophageal rupture

data.description: Air accumulates in the left pleural space, partially collapsing the lung. It may occur independently or as a complication of another thoracic process.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent left pleural air on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Worsening nausea for 72 hours and repeated vomiting are not typical primary manifestations
Bilateral pleural effusions are not explained by an uncomplicated pneumothorax
Extensive mediastinal and cervical air suggests an additional source of air leakage

data.description: A tear in the aortic inner lining allows blood to separate layers of the aortic wall, producing potentially fatal vascular complications.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chest pain radiating to the back
A normal initial cardiac workup does not exclude dissection
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain occurring in the context of repeated vomiting favors an esophageal injury
Mediastinal and cervical air are not typical of aortic dissection
Left pleural air is not a typical finding

data.description: Reduced coronary blood flow causes myocardial ischemia or infarction. It is an important chest-pain differential, although the reported testing and imaging favor a noncardiac cause.
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported normal cardiac workup reduces the likelihood, depending on test timing and serial results
Mediastinal and cervical air are not explained by myocardial ischemia
Left pneumothorax and asymmetric pleural effusions are not typical
Chest pain following repeated vomiting favors esophageal rupture

data.description: Involuntary seizure-like episodes caused by altered nervous-system functioning rather than epileptic discharges. This is a leading possibility; the EEG image appears substantially affected by movement artifact, with some preserved posterior background activity, but confirmation requires synchronized video-EEG capture of a typical event.
symptoms_in_common: Preserved alertness during abnormal movements on examination
History of PTSD, depression, and panic disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported feature definitively excludes functional seizures; urinary incontinence and mild lactate or creatine kinase elevations can occur in both functional and epileptic events

data.diagnosis: Focal epilepsy with focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures
data.description: Epileptic activity beginning in one cerebral region and spreading to produce bilateral stiffening and shaking. A single artifact-heavy EEG image cannot establish or exclude this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Visual and autonomic symptoms preceding events
Sudden stiffening followed by limb and trunk shaking
Mild elevations in lactate and creatine kinase after episodes
History of childhood febrile seizure and several concussions
symptoms_not_in_common: Alertness during ongoing nonrhythmic movements
Repeated convulsions lasting 5–8 minutes without a described postictal recovery period
Persistent mutism with intermittent irregular tremulous movements is not a typical tonic-clonic seizure presentation

data.description: Transient loss of consciousness from reduced cerebral blood flow, sometimes accompanied by stiffening or brief jerking. Vasovagal mechanisms or a cardiac arrhythmia are possible causes.
symptoms_in_common: Blurred vision and nausea before collapse
Urinary incontinence, which can occur during syncope
symptoms_not_in_common: Convulsive activity reported to last 4–8 minutes, much longer than typical syncopal jerking
Mutism and stiff posture while awake and alert
Intermittent ongoing nonrhythmic movements on examination

data.description: Episodes of intense autonomic arousal that can cause palpitations, nausea, tremulousness, and impaired concentration; dissociation may accompany severe attacks.
symptoms_not_in_common: Falls with sustained generalized stiffening and convulsive shaking
Urinary incontinence
Persistent mutism and rigid posture are not typical of an uncomplicated panic attack

data.diagnosis: Catatonia associated with a psychiatric or medical disorder
data.description: A psychomotor syndrome that can include mutism, abnormal posturing, rigidity, and either reduced activity or agitation. It could explain the examination findings but is less satisfactory as an explanation for the entire recurrent-event history.
symptoms_in_common: Mutism despite being awake and alert
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent discrete convulsive episodes with falls and urinary incontinence
Blurred vision, palpitations, and nausea as a stereotyped prodrome
Episodes described as sequential stiffening followed by generalized shaking

data.diagnosis: Incarcerated right obturator hernia causing small-bowel obstruction
data.description: Small bowel herniates through the obturator canal and becomes trapped, causing obstruction and potentially strangulation. The CT images strongly suggest a bowel-containing right obturator hernia. This is an urgent surgical condition.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced age, very low BMI, and multiparity are characteristic risk factors
Sudden right knee pain without local swelling or tenderness, consistent with referred pain from obturator nerve compression
Flexion of the right knee for pain relief, compatible with the Howship–Romberg sign
Nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and radiographic small-bowel obstruction
Small right-sided extraluminal mass on rectal examination
CT appearance of a bowel loop extending into the right obturator region
Absence of a palpable abdominal mass

data.diagnosis: Incarcerated right femoral hernia causing small-bowel obstruction
data.description: Bowel becomes trapped in the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament. Femoral hernias occur particularly in older women and can cause acute bowel obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal tenderness without initial peritoneal irritation
symptoms_not_in_common: Knee pain relieved by flexion is more characteristic of obturator nerve compression
Right-sided extraluminal mass on rectal examination suggests a deeper pelvic hernia
The depicted CT location is more consistent with the obturator canal than the femoral canal

data.description: A rare pelvic hernia in which bowel passes through a sciatic foramen, potentially causing obstruction and pain from adjacent nerve compression.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and small-bowel obstruction
Deep pelvic mass detected on rectal examination
Lower-limb pain without knee swelling or tenderness
Absence of a palpable abdominal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated knee pain relieved by flexion is more typical of an obturator hernia
The CT abnormality appears anterior in the obturator region rather than posterior in a sciatic foramen

data.description: Twisting of small bowel around its mesentery produces mechanical obstruction and can compromise intestinal blood supply.
symptoms_in_common: No previous abdominal surgery, compatible with primary volvulus
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden isolated right knee pain relieved by flexion
Small right-sided extraluminal mass on rectal examination
CT appearance of a focal bowel-containing pelvic hernia rather than an evident mesenteric twist

data.diagnosis: Small-bowel obstruction due to pelvic malignancy
data.description: A pelvic tumor can compress or invade bowel and cause obstruction; involvement of pelvic nerves can also produce referred lower-limb pain.
symptoms_in_common: Very low BMI, although chronic weight loss is not documented
Nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and small-bowel obstruction
Extraluminal pelvic mass on rectal examination
Lower-limb pain could occur with pelvic nerve involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt knee pain relieved by flexion is more suggestive of mechanical obturator nerve compression
The CT images suggest herniated bowel rather than a solid pelvic tumor
The short symptom duration is less typical of progressively developing malignant obstruction

data.description: An immune-mediated small-vessel endotheliopathy affecting the retina, inner ear, and brain. This is the leading consideration given apparent branch retinal artery occlusions, low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, and corpus callosum lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bilateral visual field defects with relatively preserved central visual acuity
Retinal whitening and arterial wall hyperfluorescence on the supplied retinal images
Sudden left-sided hearing loss, with predominantly low-frequency loss on audiometry
Recurrent severe headache and arm numbness
Apparent central corpus callosum lesions on MRI
Mildly elevated CSF protein without oligoclonal bands

data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system that can cause recurrent visual and sensory disturbances and corpus callosum lesions, but does not usually cause retinal arterial occlusions.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult woman with recurrent neurological symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent branch retinal artery occlusions and retinal arterial wall hyperfluorescence
Sudden predominantly low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss with tinnitus
Preserved central visual acuity and no relative afferent pupillary defect are less typical of substantial unilateral optic neuritis
Absence of CSF oligoclonal bands reduces support, although it does not exclude the disease

data.diagnosis: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
data.description: A rare inflammatory vasculitis confined predominantly to the brain and spinal cord, producing headache, focal neurological deficits, and multifocal ischemic lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Normal systemic inflammatory markers can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent retinal arterial occlusions are not typical of a vasculitis confined to the central nervous system
Sudden low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus
The combined retinal, cochlear, and central callosal pattern favors Susac syndrome

data.description: An autoimmune thrombotic disorder that can cause retinal arterial occlusion and cerebral ischemia; diagnosis requires appropriate clinical findings and persistently positive antiphospholipid antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent visual field defects consistent with retinal arterial ischemia
Apparent ischemic lesions on brain MRI
Sudden hearing loss can rarely occur from inner-ear ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody testing argues against this diagnosis
Retinal arterial wall hyperfluorescence and central callosal lesions are more suggestive of Susac syndrome
The retinal and low-frequency hearing-loss combination is not a usual presentation

data.description: A rare inflammatory disorder characterized by ocular inflammation, usually interstitial keratitis, and audiovestibular dysfunction; atypical forms can involve retinal vasculitis and systemic vessels.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal anterior segment examination without interstitial keratitis
Recurrent focal visual field defects associated with apparent retinal arterial occlusions rather than typical inflammatory corneal disease
Central corpus callosum lesions are not characteristic
Normal ESR and CRP provide less support for active systemic inflammation

data.diagnosis: Myoclonic epilepsy with ragged-red fibers (MERRF spectrum mitochondrial disease)
data.description: A mitochondrial DNA disorder with variable expression that can cause myopathy, cerebellar ataxia, hearing loss, seizures, and cardiac abnormalities. Myoclonus and epilepsy may be absent in atypical presentations. The maternal-pattern pedigree and apparent ragged-red fibers in the supplied biopsy strongly support a mitochondrial disorder; genetic testing is needed to establish the subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive paraspinal muscle atrophy and stooped posture
Neck flexion and proximal limb weakness
Mildly elevated creatine kinase and myopathic EMG changes
Apparent ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy
Maternal family history of bent spine, with elevated creatine kinase and a seizure in relatives
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at age 63 is unusually late for the classic presentation
Thyroid autoantibodies, rheumatoid factor, and antinuclear antibodies are not defining features

data.description: A mitochondrial disorder caused by single or multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions, producing progressive muscle weakness and sometimes cerebellar, auditory, cognitive, or cardiac involvement. Muscle pathology and molecular testing help distinguish it from other mitochondrial syndromes.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive axial and proximal muscle weakness
Apparent mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent maternal transmission is less typical of a single large mitochondrial DNA deletion
Positive thyroid and systemic autoantibodies are not characteristic

data.description: An inherited muscle disease predominantly affecting spinal muscles, causing paraspinal wasting and progressive bent-spine posture. Some forms also involve neck and proximal limb muscles, although an isolated axial myopathy would not explain the entire multisystem presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Mild proximal limb weakness and difficulty climbing stairs
symptoms_not_in_common: Cerebellar ataxia and cerebellar atrophy
Sensorineural hearing loss
Mild cognitive impairment
Apparent ragged-red fibers suggest a mitochondrial cause rather than an isolated axial myopathy

data.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders causing progressive cerebellar dysfunction. Certain subtypes can include cognitive changes or peripheral neuromuscular involvement, but marked axial myopathy is unusual.
symptoms_in_common: Cerebellar atrophy on the supplied brain images
Family history suggesting an inherited disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe selective paraspinal muscle atrophy
Myopathic EMG changes and elevated creatine kinase
Apparent ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy
Frequent premature cardiac contractions
Thyroid autoantibody positivity

data.diagnosis: Steroid-responsive encephalopathy associated with autoimmune thyroiditis
data.description: Also called Hashimoto encephalopathy, this uncommon diagnosis can produce cognitive dysfunction, seizures, and occasionally cerebellar ataxia in patients with thyroid autoantibodies. Antibody positivity alone is not diagnostic, and alternative explanations must be excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated antithyroglobulin and antithyroid peroxidase antibodies
symptoms_not_in_common: A decade-long, steadily progressive muscle-predominant course
Severe paraspinal atrophy and familial bent-spine posture
Myopathic EMG changes
Apparent ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy
Sensorineural hearing loss
Cardiac premature contractions

data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma that can involve lymph nodes, extranodal soft tissues, and occasionally blood or bone marrow. Tissue morphology and additional molecular studies are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Painful mass-like lesion involving muscle near the left hip
Strong CD19, CD20, and CD45 expression
Lambda-restricted surface IgG with absent TdT and CD34, supporting a mature B-cell neoplasm
Large atypical lymphoid cells in the supplied microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 2 years is uncommon
Aberrant CD13 and CD117 expression is unusual

data.description: A rapidly growing mature B-cell lymphoma occurring in children, usually associated with a MYC rearrangement and an exceptionally high proliferation rate.
symptoms_in_common: Basophilic, partly vacuolated cytoplasm in the supplied smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Surface IgG rather than the more typical surface IgM
CD10 expression in only a minority of neoplastic cells
Aberrant CD13 and CD117 expression
An isolated hip-region muscle mass is an uncommon presentation

data.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma with blastoid or intermediate-sized cell morphology that does not meet criteria for another defined lymphoma. Classification requires tissue, proliferation, and genetic studies.
symptoms_in_common: Mature clonal B-cell phenotype with strong CD19 and CD20 and lambda-restricted surface IgG
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation in a 2-year-old is very uncommon
CD13 and CD117 coexpression is not characteristic

data.description: A rare mature B-cell lymphoma that can resemble Burkitt lymphoma but lacks its defining MYC rearrangement and instead has a characteristic chromosome 11q gain-and-loss pattern. The unlabeled cytogenetic images alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 2 years is younger than the usual presentation
Partial rather than strong diffuse CD10 expression
Aberrant CD13 and CD117 expression
Circulating atypical lymphocytes are less characteristic than localized nodal disease

data.description: A malignancy of immature B-cell precursors common in young children. It can cause anemia, musculoskeletal pain, lymphadenopathy, and tissue masses, but the reported mature B-cell phenotype makes it substantially less likely here.
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong lambda-restricted surface IgG indicates mature rather than precursor B cells
Absent TdT strongly argues against conventional B-lymphoblastic disease
Absent CD34 provides no support for an immature phenotype
Strong CD20 expression in nearly all neoplastic cells is less typical

diagnoses.name: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Burkitt lymphoma
diagnoses.title: B-cell lymphoma unclassifiable with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess associated with Schistosoma mansoni infection
data.description: A bacterial infection producing a pus-filled liver lesion. Schistosomal hepatic inflammation can predispose to bacterial abscess formation; the complex right-lobe lesion shown is concerning for this complication.
symptoms_in_common: Complex hypoechoic and low-attenuation right hepatic lesion on imaging
Documented Schistosoma mansoni infection as a possible predisposing condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea is not usually explained by a liver abscess alone
Prior trauma is not necessary for this diagnosis

data.description: Schistosoma mansoni infection causes intestinal inflammation and hepatic egg-related granulomas, sometimes progressing to periportal fibrosis and portal hypertension. Stool eggs establish infection, but do not establish the cause of the focal liver lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Fever can occur during active infection
symptoms_not_in_common: A large complex focal hepatic lesion is not typical of uncomplicated hepatointestinal schistosomiasis
Persistent fever for two months raises concern for an additional infection
History of trauma is unrelated to schistosomiasis

data.description: Entamoeba histolytica infection can spread from the intestine to the liver, commonly causing an abscess in the right hepatic lobe.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea could reflect accompanying intestinal infection
Right hepatic lobe lesion compatible with an abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Schistosoma mansoni eggs indicate a separate infection rather than confirming amoebiasis
Prior trauma is not a typical cause
Splenic enlargement is not a characteristic feature of an isolated amoebic abscess

data.description: Traumatic bleeding within the liver can form a complex collection that subsequently becomes infected, causing persistent fever and localized pain.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged fever if the collection is infected
Complex right hepatic lesion on ultrasound and CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea is not explained by a hepatic hematoma
Schistosoma mansoni eggs represent a concurrent infection
Apparent splenic enlargement is not usually explained by a localized traumatic hematoma

data.description: Echinococcus infection produces hepatic hydatid cysts. Secondary bacterial infection can cause fever, pain, and a complex cystic appearance, although characteristic cyst features are not clearly established in these images.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged fever if a cyst becomes infected
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diarrhoea is not a typical manifestation
Schistosoma mansoni eggs do not support echinococcosis
Prior trauma is not the cause of hydatid infection
Apparent splenic enlargement is not typical of an isolated hepatic hydatid cyst

data.description: Acute coronary artery occlusion causing anterior myocardial injury, often involving the left anterior descending artery. The severe symptoms and anterior ST-segment elevation with prominent hyperacute T waves on the supplied ECG are highly concerning and require emergency cardiac evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Severe substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm
Chest pain awakening him from sleep
Anterior ST-segment elevation and prominent hyperacute T waves on ECG
Leukocytosis, which can accompany acute myocardial infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Month-long episodes lasting hours to days with partial relief from antacids
Longstanding thrombocytosis is not explained by myocardial infarction alone
Generalized pruritus after hot showers is not explained by myocardial infarction

data.description: A myeloproliferative neoplasm causing increased red cell production, often accompanied by leukocytosis and thrombocytosis. Aquagenic pruritus and arterial thrombosis are characteristic; confirmation requires further testing, including JAK2 mutation analysis and serum erythropoietin.
symptoms_in_common: Historical thrombocytosis suggesting a chronic hematologic disorder
Acute ischemic chest pain and ECG abnormalities potentially resulting from coronary thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Partial relief of preceding chest discomfort with antacids or omeprazole
Month-long burning chest discomfort is not a characteristic direct manifestation

data.description: A clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by persistent thrombocytosis and increased risk of arterial or venous thrombosis, including myocardial infarction. Elevated hemoglobin and aquagenic pruritus warrant careful exclusion of polycythemia vera.
symptoms_in_common: Previously documented thrombocytosis approximately 12 years earlier
Severe chest pain with left-arm radiation
Troponin elevation and anterior ischemic ECG changes potentially reflecting coronary thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated hemoglobin is less characteristic than in polycythemia vera
Pruritus after hot showers is more characteristic of polycythemia vera
Partial relief of burning chest pain with acid-suppressive treatment

data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm causing myocardial ischemia, typically at rest or during the night. Sustained spasm can cause myocardial infarction, but the supplied ECG must be treated as possible acute coronary occlusion rather than presumed benign spasm.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chest pain awakening him from sleep
symptoms_not_in_common: Episodes lasting hours to days are longer than typical uncomplicated vasospastic attacks
Longstanding marked thrombocytosis
Pruritus after hot showers
Elevated hemoglobin
Partial relief with antacids or omeprazole

data.description: Reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus causing burning retrosternal discomfort, sometimes worse when lying down. It could explain the preceding month of symptoms but does not adequately explain the acute ischemic presentation or ECG findings.
symptoms_in_common: Nonexertional episodes lasting hours to days
Partial relief with antacids or omeprazole
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe chest pain radiating to the left arm
Anterior ST-segment elevation and hyperacute T waves
Elevated troponin
Marked leukocytosis
Persistent marked thrombocytosis
Elevated hemoglobin
Pruritus after hot showers

diagnoses.name: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
diagnoses.title: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

data.description: Congenital abnormal lung tissue supplied by a systemic artery, usually arising from the aorta, rather than the pulmonary circulation. The apparent aortic feeding vessel to the left basal lesion makes this the leading structural diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Left lower thoracic lesion on CT
Doppler and CT appearances suggest an arterial supply arising from the aorta
Severe neonatal respiratory compromise requiring mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery is unusual for an isolated small sequestration
Prenatal right-sided urinary tract dilatation is not a characteristic feature
Bilateral pleural air is not a usual primary manifestation

data.diagnosis: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation, possibly a hybrid lesion with sequestration
data.description: A developmental malformation of the distal airways producing cystic or solid abnormal lung tissue. A hybrid lesion combines these changes with the systemic arterial supply of sequestration.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent cystic changes within the left basal pulmonary lesion
Congenital lung abnormality presenting with neonatal respiratory failure
Possible systemic feeding artery, supporting a hybrid lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: An aortic feeding artery is not typical of an isolated pulmonary airway malformation
Right-sided urinary tract dilatation is not a defining feature
The severity of delivery-room arrest may require an additional perinatal explanation

data.diagnosis: Neonatal pneumothorax, including possible left tension pneumothorax
data.description: Air in the pleural space can compress the lung and, under tension, shift the mediastinum and impair circulation. Resuscitation and positive-pressure ventilation increase the risk.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographs appear to show bilateral pleural air
Marked left-sided hyperlucency with apparent rightward mediastinal displacement on one radiograph
Exposure to prolonged resuscitation and mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: A persistent left basal tissue lesion with an apparent systemic feeding artery is not explained by pneumothorax
Prenatal urinary tract dilatation is unrelated
The arrest preceded the documented imaging, so pneumothorax cannot be assumed to have caused it

data.description: Aspiration of meconium around delivery causes airway obstruction, chemical pneumonitis, respiratory failure, and sometimes air-leak complications.
symptoms_in_common: Term delivery following nonreassuring fetal status
Absent respiratory effort and need for intubation
symptoms_not_in_common: The focal left basal lesion and apparent aortic arterial supply are not explained by meconium aspiration
The images do not show a clear classic pattern of widespread coarse pulmonary opacities
Prenatal right-sided urinary tract dilatation is unrelated

data.description: Brain injury caused by inadequate oxygen delivery and blood flow around birth. The profound neonatal depression and prolonged resuscitation raise strong concern, although neurological assessment is required for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Nonreassuring fetal status after prolonged labor
Limp appearance and absent respiratory effort at birth
Cardiorespiratory arrest requiring 16 minutes of resuscitation
symptoms_not_in_common: The left basal pulmonary lesion with an apparent systemic arterial supply is not explained by hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
Pleural air collections represent a separate pulmonary complication
Prenatal urinary tract dilatation is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome)
data.description: Dysregulated alternative complement activation causes small-vessel endothelial injury, hemolysis, and renal failure. The biopsy images appear to show vascular narrowing and concentric intimal thickening compatible with thrombotic microangiopathy, although these findings do not establish its cause.
symptoms_in_common: Persistently reduced C3 with normal C4
Elevated LDH, mild anemia, and rare schistocytes
Family history of relatively early dialysis-dependent renal failure
Apparent small-vessel injury and concentric intimal thickening on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Only mild anemia and rare schistocytes are less typical of pronounced systemic microangiopathic hemolysis, although renal-limited disease is possible
Cocaine exposure provides an alternative trigger for vascular injury

data.diagnosis: Hypertensive emergency with renal thrombotic microangiopathy
data.description: Severe hypertension can damage renal arterioles, causing hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis, microangiopathic hemolysis, and progressive kidney failure.
symptoms_in_common: Blood pressure of 172/110 mmHg with renal and neurologic dysfunction
Jugular venous distension and basal crackles consistent with volume overload
Apparent onion-skin vascular thickening and luminal narrowing on biopsy
Echogenic kidneys suggesting chronic renal injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent isolated C3 hypocomplementemia is not typical of hypertension alone
Family history of early renal failure raises concern for an underlying inherited disorder

data.description: Cocaine can cause vasoconstriction, hypertension, and endothelial injury, producing renal small-vessel damage and sometimes thrombotic microangiopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Positive urine toxicology for cocaine and metabolites
Apparent renal vascular injury on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent low C3 with normal C4 is not a usual defining feature
A sister requiring dialysis at age 45 is not explained by an acquired cocaine-related injury
Echogenic kidneys suggest chronic disease beyond a purely acute toxic exposure

data.description: Alternative complement pathway dysregulation causes C3-dominant glomerular deposits and progressive renal disease. Diagnosis requires immunofluorescence and usually electron microscopy.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent C3 hypocomplementemia with normal C4
Family history potentially compatible with inherited complement dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated LDH and schistocytes favor microangiopathic injury rather than isolated glomerular disease
The supplied images emphasize vascular narrowing and concentric thickening rather than a characteristic glomerular lesion
Cocaine exposure suggests an additional vascular cause of renal injury

data.description: Chronic hepatitis C can promote cryoglobulin-containing immune complexes that deposit in glomeruli, causing proteinuria, complement consumption, and renal dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Volume overload with jugular venous distension and basal crackles
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal C4 despite persistently low C3 is atypical because cryoglobulinemia commonly causes marked C4 reduction
Schistocytes and elevated LDH are more suggestive of thrombotic microangiopathy
The supplied biopsy images show predominantly vascular changes rather than characteristic immune-complex glomerular injury
Familial early renal failure is not explained by hepatitis C-associated disease

data.diagnosis: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) presenting with area postrema syndrome
data.description: An inflammatory astrocytopathy associated with AQP4 antibodies. Involvement of the dorsal medulla and area postrema causes persistent nausea and vomiting. The apparent medullary MRI abnormality and positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG make this the leading consideration, although isolated CSF positivity warrants confirmation with a validated assay.
symptoms_in_common: Seven weeks of progressive, treatment-resistant nausea and vomiting
Marked weight loss with normal gastrointestinal investigations
Horizontal nystagmus and loss of pharyngeal reflex
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
Acute respiratory failure compatible with severe medullary involvement
Apparent medullary signal abnormality on the supplied MRI images
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative serum AQP4-IgG despite positive cerebrospinal fluid testing is unusual
Decreased unilateral tendon reflexes are less typical than hyperreflexia in central motor pathway disease
Metabolic alkalosis is a consequence of prolonged vomiting rather than a primary feature

data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disorder that can involve the brainstem and produce bulbar, ocular motor, and motor deficits. Serum MOG-IgG testing would help evaluate this alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Brainstem-associated nystagmus and impaired pharyngeal reflex
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
Respiratory failure with severe brainstem involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG favors NMOSD rather than MOGAD
An isolated, prolonged area postrema syndrome is less characteristic
Profound weight loss and metabolic alkalosis are secondary complications rather than typical disease features

data.description: A central nervous system demyelinating disease that can cause brainstem lesions, ocular motor abnormalities, weakness, and pyramidal signs. Additional characteristic MRI lesions and cerebrospinal fluid oligoclonal bands would be needed to support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Loss of pharyngeal reflex from brainstem involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG argues against multiple sclerosis
Seven weeks of dominant, intractable nausea and vomiting is uncommon
Acute respiratory failure from an isolated medullary presentation is unusual
Marked weight loss and metabolic alkalosis are not characteristic primary manifestations

data.description: Inflammation of the brainstem and cerebellum caused by infection, such as Listeria, or immune-mediated disease. It can produce asymmetric neurological deficits, bulbar dysfunction, and respiratory compromise.
symptoms_not_in_common: A seven-week vomiting-dominant course without a reported febrile illness is less typical of infectious rhombencephalitis
Largely normal laboratory studies provide little support for systemic infection
Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG favors a specific autoimmune astrocytopathy

data.diagnosis: Adult brainstem glioma involving the medulla
data.description: An infiltrative brainstem tumor that may progressively disrupt vomiting-control pathways, cranial nerve function, motor tracts, and respiratory centers. Contrast-enhanced MRI and follow-up imaging would be needed to assess this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Horizontal nystagmus and loss of pharyngeal reflex
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG is not characteristic of a glioma
Abrupt neurological deterioration after a prolonged gastrointestinal presentation is less typical of a slowly growing tumor
Metabolic alkalosis reflects vomiting rather than a direct tumor manifestation

data.description: An uncommon bacterial infection of a heart valve. Some Lactobacillus species have intrinsic vancomycin resistance and variable cephalosporin susceptibility, making this a leading possibility given the reported susceptibility profile. Species identification and blood cultures are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Two months of fever and malaise
Aortic diastolic murmur suggesting aortic regurgitation
Echocardiographic findings concerning for aortic valve dysfunction
Marked vancomycin and cephalosporin resistance in the supplied susceptibility results

data.description: A rare zoonotic bacterial infection that can cause destructive endocarditis, frequently involving the aortic valve. Intrinsic vancomycin resistance and relatively low penicillin MICs support consideration, although the extreme cephalosporin resistance is less characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: High vancomycin MIC with a relatively low penicillin MIC
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported extreme cephalosporin resistance is less typical

data.description: A rare opportunistic infection of a heart valve caused by intrinsically vancomycin-resistant bacteria. It can resemble other forms of subacute bacterial endocarditis; microbiological identification is necessary to distinguish it from Lactobacillus and related organisms.
symptoms_in_common: Aortic diastolic murmur suggesting valve involvement

data.description: An infection of the aortic valve caused by Enterococcus species, often producing a subacute febrile illness. Enterococci are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins, and some strains are vancomycin resistant.
symptoms_in_common: Vancomycin resistance, if caused by a resistant strain

data.diagnosis: Viridans group streptococcal aortic valve infective endocarditis
data.description: A common cause of subacute endocarditis, especially on previously abnormal valves. The clinical presentation fits, but the supplied vancomycin and cephalosporin resistance profile argues strongly against typical viridans streptococci.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked vancomycin resistance is highly atypical
Extreme ceftriaxone and other cephalosporin resistance is atypical

data.diagnosis: Paradoxical air embolism through a patent foramen ovale
data.description: Venous air introduced during venesection can cross a patent foramen ovale into the arterial circulation, causing cerebral and coronary ischemia. This is the leading unifying possibility. The arrowed low-density focus on the CT may represent intravascular gas, although confirmation requires review of the full study.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden gurgling sensation in the arm during venesection
Immediate severe chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm
Severe dyspnoea and oxygen saturation of 88%
Inferior T-wave inversion and elevated troponin
Confirmed patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting

data.diagnosis: Venous air embolism affecting the pulmonary circulation
data.description: Air entering the venous circulation can obstruct pulmonary blood flow and produce acute hypoxaemia, dyspnoea, and chest pain. An isolated venous air embolism would not fully explain focal cerebral ischemia without arterial passage through the demonstrated shunt.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intravascular gas on the supplied CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient left hemiplegia and dysphasia are not typical without paradoxical embolization
Jaw and left-arm radiation with myocardial injury is less typical of isolated pulmonary air embolism

data.diagnosis: Acute pulmonary thromboembolism with paradoxical systemic thromboembolism
