data.description: A venous blood clot can embolize to the lungs, while clot crossing a patent foramen ovale can cause cerebral or coronary ischemia. This could explain the combined respiratory, cardiac, and neurological findings, but the procedural gurgling strongly favors air rather than thrombus.
symptoms_in_common: Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the arm immediately during venesection
Possible intravascular gas on CT rather than a thrombotic filling defect

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome, including non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia can cause characteristic chest pain, ECG changes, and elevated troponin. A primary coronary event alone does not adequately explain the simultaneous transient neurological deficit and the apparent venous air-entry event.
symptoms_in_common: Radiation to the jaw and left arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the arm during venesection
Transient left hemiplegia and dysphasia at symptom onset
Marked hypoxaemia without reported pulmonary oedema
Possible intravascular gas on CT

data.diagnosis: Acute aortic dissection with coronary and cerebral malperfusion
data.description: An aortic dissection can compromise coronary and cerebral arterial blood flow, producing abrupt chest pain, myocardial injury, and stroke-like deficits. It is a dangerous alternative, although no dissection is demonstrated in the provided information.
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the arm during venesection
Possible intravascular gas on CT
Hypoxaemia is not typical without an associated cardiopulmonary complication

data.diagnosis: Residual or recurrent pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma (PXA), CNS WHO grade 2
data.description: A circumscribed astrocytic tumor commonly affecting superficial temporal regions in young adults and frequently harboring BRAF V600E. This is the leading consideration given the established pathology; recurrence requires comparison with prior imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Previously confirmed grade 2 PXA with BRAF V600E mutation
Apparent right temporal enhancement and surrounding FLAIR signal abnormality

data.description: A higher-grade PXA that may arise through progression of a grade 2 tumor. Imaging alone cannot establish transformation; repeat tissue evaluation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: History of a molecularly confirmed PXA
Apparent enhancement within the previously affected temporal region
symptoms_not_in_common: The original specimen showed grade 2 rather than grade 3 disease
The prolonged seizure history is more suggestive of an initially indolent tumor

data.description: A usually slow-growing mixed neuronal and glial tumor associated with temporal-lobe epilepsy. BRAF V600E can occur, but the documented PXA pathology makes this a less likely alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Seizures beginning in the early twenties
BRAF V600E mutation, which can also occur in ganglioglioma
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy/resection identified PXA rather than a mixed neuronal and glial tumor

data.description: An aggressive glioblastoma pattern that can harbor BRAF V600E and overlap with PXA morphologically. Consideration would require evidence of high-grade progression and additional pathological characterization.
symptoms_in_common: BRAF V600E mutation, which occurs in some epithelioid glioblastomas
symptoms_not_in_common: Long clinical history beginning in early adulthood
Original pathology demonstrated grade 2 PXA rather than glioblastoma

data.description: Scarring and reactive changes after brain tumor surgery can produce FLAIR hyperintensity and enhancement near a resection cavity. Distinguishing these changes from residual or recurrent tumor requires serial imaging and treatment history.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent right temporal postoperative cavity with adjacent FLAIR hyperintensity
Seizures, which can persist because of cortical scarring
symptoms_not_in_common: Seizures began before surgery
Headaches developed before the initial resection
The original lesion was a histologically confirmed BRAF-mutant PXA, not postoperative scarring

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by proximal muscle weakness and distinctive skin lesions. This is the strongest fit for the reported presentation; severe weakness and generalized edema can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Gottron papules over the finger joints and extensor surfaces of the elbows and knees
Progressive proximal muscle weakness with difficulty walking, rising from a squat, and climbing stairs
Severe neck and limb weakness with preserved sensation and reflexes
Pitting edema, which can accompany severe disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild grip and ankle weakness is less typical than predominantly proximal weakness
Diminished breath sounds at both lung bases are not a defining feature and require evaluation for pulmonary involvement or pleural fluid

data.diagnosis: Overlap myositis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease
data.description: An inflammatory muscle disease occurring alongside another systemic autoimmune connective tissue disorder, sometimes with dermatomyositis-like skin findings, edema, and pulmonary or pleural involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished basal breath sounds, potentially reflecting pleural involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The combination of heliotrope rash and Gottron papules favors dermatomyositis specifically rather than an otherwise unspecified overlap disorder
Profound rapidly progressive weakness is less typical of connective tissue disease without substantial associated myositis

data.description: An autoimmune syndrome associated with antibodies to aminoacyl-transfer RNA synthetases, often causing inflammatory myopathy, interstitial lung disease, arthritis, and characteristic hand changes.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished basal breath sounds, which warrant assessment for associated pulmonary disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Heliotrope rash and Gottron papules are more characteristic of dermatomyositis, although they can occur in overlap presentations
Generalized pitting edema is not a characteristic feature
The described finger papules differ from the fissured, hyperkeratotic skin of mechanic's hands

data.description: An autoimmune muscle disorder causing muscle fiber necrosis and often severe, subacute proximal weakness, sometimes associated with anti-SRP or anti-HMGCR antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Inability to lift the limbs or head against gravity
symptoms_not_in_common: Heliotrope rash
Gottron papules on the fingers, elbows, and knees
Periungual erythema and edema
Generalized pitting edema
Diminished basal breath sounds are not a characteristic presenting feature

data.description: Muscle dysfunction caused by thyroid hormone deficiency, producing muscle pain and predominantly proximal weakness; family history of thyroid disease provides a limited supporting clue.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty walking, rising from a squat, and climbing stairs
Limb swelling, although hypothyroid edema is usually nonpitting
symptoms_not_in_common: Heliotrope rash
Gottron papules over extensor joints
Periungual erythema
Pitting rather than typically nonpitting edema
Normal reflexes rather than the delayed relaxation sometimes seen in hypothyroidism
Rapid progression to profound limb and neck weakness

data.description: Defective bone mineralization associated with long-term phenytoin use, which can accelerate vitamin D breakdown. This is a leading consideration given the medication history and bilateral Looser’s zones.
symptoms_in_common: Phenytoin treatment for more than 20 years
Bilateral femoral-neck Looser’s zones, characteristic of osteomalacia
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear discordant clinical features; vitamin D, calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and parathyroid hormone measurements are needed for confirmation

data.description: An acquired phosphate-wasting disorder caused by excess FGF23 production, usually from a small phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor. The focal abnormality near the left proximal femur on the supplied functional and MRI images raises this possibility but does not establish it.
symptoms_in_common: Focal imaging abnormality near the left proximal femur
symptoms_not_in_common: Long-term phenytoin exposure provides an alternative explanation for osteomalacia
Longstanding epilepsy is not a typical manifestation

data.description: Insufficient vitamin D from low intake, limited sunlight exposure, or malabsorption impairs calcium and phosphate availability for bone mineralization.
symptoms_in_common: Normal renal and liver function is compatible with this diagnosis
symptoms_not_in_common: A focal left proximal femoral imaging abnormality is not explained by nutritional deficiency alone
Longstanding epilepsy is not typical
Prolonged phenytoin exposure suggests a medication-related rather than purely nutritional cause

data.description: Proximal renal tubular dysfunction causes urinary losses of phosphate and other solutes, potentially producing osteomalacia. Overall renal filtration can remain normal.
symptoms_in_common: Looser’s zones from defective bone mineralization
symptoms_not_in_common: A focal left proximal femoral imaging abnormality is not typical
Longstanding epilepsy is not a characteristic feature
Phenytoin exposure more directly supports altered vitamin D metabolism than generalized proximal tubular dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Primary hyperparathyroidism with metabolic bone disease
data.description: Excess parathyroid hormone increases bone turnover and renal phosphate loss, potentially causing bone pain, weakness, and skeletal fragility.
symptoms_in_common: Age and sex compatible with a common presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral Looser’s zones are more characteristic of osteomalacia than uncomplicated primary hyperparathyroidism
Long-term phenytoin exposure is not explained by this diagnosis
A focal left proximal femoral imaging abnormality is not a typical defining feature

data.diagnosis: Group A streptococcal infective endocarditis of the mitral valve
data.description: The leading unifying diagnosis: bacterial infection of the mitral valve with probable vegetation, complicated by mitral regurgitation and systemic septic embolization.
symptoms_in_common: Blood culture positive for group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus
Neutrophilia and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Echocardiographic mass suggestive of a mitral valve vegetation
Color Doppler findings suggestive of substantial mitral regurgitation
Acute focal neurological deficits consistent with cerebral embolization
Respiratory distress and elevated NT-pro-BNP consistent with associated heart failure

data.diagnosis: Acute cerebral embolic infarction secondary to infective endocarditis
data.description: A likely complication in which infected valvular material embolizes to a cerebral artery, causing ischemic brain injury. Additional MRI sequences are needed to characterize the displayed brain lesion definitively.
symptoms_in_common: Focal left-sided cerebral abnormality on the supplied MRI
Probable mitral valve vegetation providing an embolic source
symptoms_not_in_common: An isolated cerebral infarction does not explain streptococcal bacteremia
Loud apical systolic murmur
Respiratory distress with markedly elevated NT-pro-BNP
Possible splenic lesions

data.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure due to severe mitral regurgitation
data.description: Mitral valve incompetence, potentially caused by infective destruction, produces pulmonary congestion and cardiac volume overload. This is a likely cardiac complication rather than a separate explanation for the entire presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Grade 4/6 systolic murmur most prominent at the apex
Color Doppler appearance suggestive of substantial mitral regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Group A streptococcal bacteremia is not explained by heart failure alone
Fever and elevated inflammatory markers
Acute focal neurological deficits
Possible splenic lesions

data.description: Infected emboli from endocarditis can seed the spleen and produce abscesses. The hypoechoic lesions in the supplied abdominal ultrasound raise this possibility, although splenic infarcts are an alternative and further imaging is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilia and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Probable cardiac vegetation as a source of septic emboli
Multiple hypoechoic splenic lesions on the supplied ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute dysarthria and impaired right-hand coordination are not explained by splenic abscesses alone
Loud apical systolic murmur
Respiratory distress and markedly elevated NT-pro-BNP

data.description: Invasive streptococcal infection with systemic illness and possible organ dysfunction, likely arising from the suspected endocarditis. Sepsis may coexist with the embolic and cardiac complications.
symptoms_in_common: Positive blood culture for group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus
Heart rate of 116 beats per minute
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal dysarthria and right-hand coordination impairment suggest a structural cerebral complication rather than uncomplicated septic encephalopathy
A loud apical murmur and probable valvular vegetation indicate a specific cardiac source
Marked mitral regurgitation is not a typical consequence of sepsis alone

data.description: A rare inherited ciliopathy affecting skeletal development, hair, teeth, nails, and kidneys. Progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease can cause renal failure in early childhood. This is the strongest overall fit, although molecular testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Dolichocephaly, frontal bossing, and broad nasal bridge
Narrow chest, pectus excavatum, and rhizomelic limb shortening
Short humeri and fibulae, brachydactyly, and joint laxity
Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin or short nails
Early progressive kidney dysfunction with reduced eGFR and elevated creatinine
Increased renal cortical echogenicity and decreased corticomedullary differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria already present in the early neonatal period are less characteristic than progressive childhood tubulointerstitial disease
Elevated cholesterol and triglycerides are not defining features

data.description: An inherited skeletal ciliopathy characterized by cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses, chronic kidney disease, and retinal degeneration, with variable skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Severe kidney dysfunction in early childhood
Increased renal echogenicity and reduced corticomedullary differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Sparse hair, small teeth, and abnormal nails are more characteristic of cranioectodermal dysplasia
Dolichocephaly and the described facial pattern are not defining features
Neonatal glycosuria and hematuria are not characteristic presenting findings
Hyperopia and strabismus are less characteristic than retinal degeneration

data.description: A genetically heterogeneous ciliopathy causing a narrow thorax and short limbs, sometimes accompanied by progressive kidney disease, retinal disease, or liver involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Bronchopneumonia, potentially aggravated by thoracic restriction
Abnormal renal echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin or short nails are not typical defining features
Dolichocephaly and prominent craniofacial dysmorphism are less characteristic
Joint laxity is not a central feature
Proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria beginning neonatally are not the usual renal presentation

data.description: An inherited SMARCAL1-related disorder combining skeletal dysplasia, progressive proteinuric kidney disease, and variable T-cell immunodeficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent proteinuria and progressive renal impairment
Urinary tract infection and bronchopneumonia, which could occur with immune dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Rhizomelic shortening is less characteristic than the usual short-trunk spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia
Normoglycemic glycosuria suggests tubular dysfunction rather than the typical predominantly glomerular disease
Sparse hair, small teeth, and abnormal nails are not defining features
Dolichocephaly and the combination of hyperopia, strabismus, and nystagmus are not typical

data.description: An X-linked OCRL-related disorder in males causing congenital ocular disease, neurologic abnormalities, and proximal renal tubular dysfunction that may progress to chronic kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Early-onset proteinuria and glycosuria despite normal blood glucose
Progressive kidney dysfunction with elevated creatinine and reduced eGFR
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital rhizomelic limb shortening and short humeri and fibulae are not typical; skeletal problems usually reflect secondary renal bone disease
Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin or short nails are not characteristic
Dolichocephaly, narrow chest, and the described facial pattern are not typical defining features
Hyperopia is less characteristic than congenital cataracts or glaucoma
Hematuria is not a defining manifestation

data.diagnosis: Malignancy-associated dermatomyositis, potentially associated with oesophageal carcinoma
data.description: An inflammatory muscle and skin disease that can occur as a paraneoplastic syndrome. The hand lesions resemble Gottron papules, and focal thoracic PET uptake together with abnormal endoscopy raises concern for an oesophageal malignancy; biopsy is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetrical widespread rash on the face, torso, and limbs
Scaly erythematous lesions over the finger joints resembling Gottron papules
Markedly elevated creatine kinase of 7070 U/L
Abnormal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and focal thoracic PET uptake

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy characterized by muscle weakness, elevated muscle enzymes, and characteristic skin eruptions. Swallowing muscles may also be affected.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetrical rash involving the face, torso, and limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal thoracic PET uptake and abnormal endoscopy are not explained by uncomplicated dermatomyositis and require separate investigation

data.description: An inflammatory myopathy causing predominantly symmetrical proximal weakness, elevated muscle enzymes, and sometimes swallowing impairment, but without the characteristic rash of dermatomyositis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread symmetrical rash
Scaly lesions over the finger joints resembling Gottron papules
Abnormal endoscopy and focal thoracic PET uptake are not typical direct manifestations

data.description: An autoimmune muscle disease causing substantial muscle fiber injury, often with severe weakness and very high creatine kinase levels. It may be associated with specific autoantibodies, statin exposure, or malignancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent widespread inflammatory rash
Hand lesions resembling Gottron papules
Abnormal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy is not a typical direct manifestation

data.description: An autoimmune syndrome involving inflammatory myopathy, often accompanied by interstitial lung disease, arthritis, Raynaud phenomenon, and rough fissured skin on the hands called mechanic's hands.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory skin changes can occur in patients with a dermatomyositis-pattern presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: The pictured joint-centered hand lesions resemble Gottron papules rather than classic mechanic's hands
Abnormal endoscopy and focal thoracic PET uptake are not typical defining manifestations

data.description: Childhood osteonecrosis of the femoral head caused by disruption of its blood supply. This is the leading consideration given the age, examination, and apparent femoral head flattening and fragmentation on the radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent leg pain, which can be referred from the hip
Painful, reduced hip internal rotation and abduction
Apparent femoral head epiphyseal flattening and fragmentation

data.description: A temporary, usually self-limited inflammation of the hip joint, often following a viral illness, that commonly causes limping in children.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent femoral head flattening and fragmentation are not explained by uncomplicated transient synovitis

data.description: Displacement of the proximal femoral growth plate, usually occurring during adolescence, that produces hip or referred knee pain and restricted internal rotation.
symptoms_in_common: Painful, reduced hip internal rotation and abduction
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 8 is younger than usual
Apparent femoral head fragmentation and flattening are more characteristic of Perthes disease than a primary growth-plate slip

data.description: Chronic inflammatory arthritis beginning in childhood that can cause joint pain, stiffness, restricted motion, and limping. Isolated hip involvement is less common.
symptoms_in_common: An afebrile, otherwise well appearance is possible
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated unilateral hip symptoms are a less typical initial presentation
Apparent localized femoral head flattening and fragmentation are not typical early findings

data.description: A bacterial infection of the hip joint requiring urgent assessment and treatment. It usually causes acute severe pain, fever, and difficulty bearing weight, although atypical presentations occur.
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile presentation
Otherwise healthy appearance
Occasional rather than severe, persistent pain
Continued ability to walk
Apparent femoral head fragmentation and flattening without a reported acute systemic illness

data.description: A bacterial infection producing a pus-filled cavity within the liver. The large gas-containing fluid collection along the right hepatic margin strongly suggests an abscess, although its precise intrahepatic versus subcapsular location requires formal imaging review.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening right upper abdominal pain
Right upper quadrant tenderness and guarding
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Large gas-containing collection associated with the right side of the liver

data.description: An infected collection beneath the right diaphragm, often arising from an abdominal infection or perforation. Gas within the collection can mimic free intraperitoneal air on an erect chest radiograph.
symptoms_in_common: Upper abdominal pain, most pronounced in the right upper quadrant
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Right subdiaphragmatic gas on the chest radiograph
Gas-fluid collection adjacent to the liver on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: The CT collection appears closely associated with the hepatic capsule rather than clearly separate from the liver, making a purely subphrenic location less certain

data.description: Secondary bacterial infection of a pre-existing liver cyst, causing fever, focal pain, and occasionally gas formation within the cyst.
symptoms_in_common: Two-week progression of upper abdominal pain
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Large localized fluid collection containing gas near the liver
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized abdominal tenderness and localized guarding suggest inflammation extending beyond an uncomplicated cyst infection
The elongated peripheral configuration of the collection is less typical of a simple hepatic cyst

data.description: A liver cyst caused by Echinococcus infection that has developed secondary bacterial infection. Geographic background can support consideration, but characteristic cyst structures or confirmatory testing are needed.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Large hepatic-region cystic collection with gas, potentially reflecting secondary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied images do not clearly demonstrate typical daughter cysts, detached membranes, or a calcified cyst wall
The predominantly gas-fluid appearance is more typical of a bacterial abscess than an uncomplicated hydatid cyst

data.diagnosis: Contained perforated duodenal ulcer with a perihepatic abscess
data.description: A duodenal ulcer that perforates but is locally contained, allowing an infected gas-fluid collection to develop near the liver rather than producing widespread free air.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, tachycardia, and substantial inflammatory marker elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: The gradually worsening two-week course is less typical of an uncontained acute ulcer perforation
The supplied CT images show a localized hepatic-margin collection without a clearly demonstrated duodenal defect or direct connection

data.description: A chromosomal disorder caused by deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5. The reported 5p15.2 deletion establishes this as the primary diagnosis. Associated brain abnormalities can include pontine hypoplasia, which appears present on the supplied MRI.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypotonia confined to the left leg is less typical than generalized hypotonia

data.description: A chromosome 4p deletion disorder associated with microcephaly, developmental impairment, hypotonia, characteristic facial features, and congenital malformations. It is a phenotypic alternative, not an explanation for the documented chromosome 5 deletion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Documented 5p15.2 deletion rather than a 4p deletion
Unilateral rather than generalized hypotonia

data.description: A chromosomal deletion syndrome causing developmental delay, hypotonia, variable microcephaly, eye abnormalities, and congenital heart disease. Confirmation requires a chromosome 1p36 deletion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Documented chromosome 5p deletion rather than a 1p36 deletion
Isolated left leg hypotonia

data.description: A genetically heterogeneous group of disorders involving underdevelopment of the pons and cerebellum, often with microcephaly and severe developmental impairment. Apparent pontine hypoplasia warrants consideration, although the supplied images do not establish accompanying cerebellar hypoplasia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Ventricular septal defect
Documented 5p15.2 deletion favors Cri-du-chat syndrome instead
Normal tendon reflexes and focal hypotonia are less typical of some severe subtypes

data.description: A disorder usually caused by pathogenic variants or deletions involving ZEB2, characterized by developmental impairment, microcephaly, distinctive facial features, and variable congenital heart and brain abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Documented 5p15.2 deletion does not represent the usual genetic cause
Hypotonia limited to the left leg

data.diagnosis: Primary extragonadal yolk sac tumor of the jejunum
data.description: A rare malignant germ cell tumor arising outside the gonads that typically produces alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). This is the leading diagnosis given the elevated AFP and characteristic combination of histologic patterns; confirmation requires appropriate immunohistochemistry and exclusion of another primary site.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated serum AFP at 1,210 ng/mL
Microcystic, reticular, papillary, solid, and tubule-glandular tumor patterns
Marked nuclear atypia and abundant mitoses
Normal pelvic reproductive organs, supporting an extragonadal origin
symptoms_not_in_common: The jejunum is an exceptionally rare primary site
Enlarged lymph nodes with reactive hyperplasia do not demonstrate nodal tumor involvement

data.diagnosis: Mixed extragonadal malignant germ cell tumor with a yolk sac component
data.description: A malignant tumor containing more than one germ cell tumor component. A yolk sac component can account for AFP elevation, while additional components must be established by tissue sampling and immunohistochemistry.
symptoms_in_common: Jejunal mass with heterogeneous histologic architecture
Marked nuclear atypia and abundant mitoses
Unremarkable ovaries and other pelvic reproductive organs
symptoms_not_in_common: The described architectural diversity can occur in a pure yolk sac tumor and does not establish mixed components
No distinct teratomatous, embryonal carcinoma, or choriocarcinoma component is reported
A primary jejunal location is exceptionally unusual

data.diagnosis: AFP-producing jejunal adenocarcinoma with hepatoid or enteroblastic differentiation
data.description: A rare intestinal epithelial malignancy with fetal intestinal or liver-like differentiation that may produce AFP and resemble a yolk sac tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Tubule-glandular, papillary, and solid tumor patterns
Marked nuclear atypia and frequent mitoses
symptoms_not_in_common: Small-bowel adenocarcinoma is exceptionally rare in a 7-year-old
Prominent microcystic and reticular patterns favor yolk sac tumor
No characteristic hepatocyte-like morphology or associated mucosal dysplasia is reported

data.description: An aggressive malignant germ cell tumor that can show solid, glandular, and papillary architecture. AFP elevation can occur, particularly when a yolk sac component is also present.
symptoms_in_common: Solid, papillary, and glandular histologic patterns
Elevated AFP can occur in tumors with associated yolk sac differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcystic and reticular architecture more strongly favors yolk sac tumor
A primary jejunal site in a prepubertal girl is exceptionally unusual
The substantial AFP elevation is more characteristic of yolk sac differentiation than pure embryonal carcinoma

data.description: A rapidly proliferating B-cell lymphoma that commonly involves abdominal structures in children and can cause intestinal masses, lymphadenopathy, and ascites.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked AFP elevation is not characteristic of lymphoma
Microcystic, reticular, papillary, and tubule-glandular architecture is not typical of Burkitt lymphoma
Sampled lymph nodes showed reactive hyperplasia rather than lymphoma

diagnoses.name: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.title: Yolk sac tumour, unspecified site, female

data.diagnosis: Meckel diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: A congenital ileal outpouching that may contain acid-secreting gastric tissue, causing adjacent ulceration and substantial intestinal bleeding. The focal abdominal uptake on the provided scan suggests ectopic gastric mucosa and favors this diagnosis, although an enteric duplication can produce similar findings.
symptoms_in_common: Large-volume reddish rectal bleeding with a clot
Marked anemia with elevated reticulocytes and low serum iron
Pallor, tachycardia, and hypotension from blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe intermittent pain with leg flexion and episodic rigidity is less typical of uncomplicated bleeding from a Meckel diverticulum and may indicate an associated complication

data.description: Telescoping of one bowel segment into another, causing intermittent obstruction, impaired blood supply, and bloody stools. A Meckel diverticulum or duplication cyst can occasionally serve as a lead point.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent severe abdominal pain with crying and leg flexion
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound anemia with low serum iron is less typical of a short uncomplicated episode
Near-complete bloody stool with a large clot is less typical than blood mixed with mucus

data.diagnosis: Enteric duplication cyst containing ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: A congenital duplication of the intestinal tract that may contain gastric tissue, causing ulceration, bleeding, pain, or obstruction. It can also produce focal uptake on gastric-mucosa scintigraphy.
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly discordant reported symptoms; this diagnosis is uncommon and requires anatomic confirmation

data.description: A non-IgE-mediated reaction to dietary proteins, commonly cow's milk, causing distal intestinal inflammation and blood-streaked stools in infants.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe episodic pain with leg flexion and abdominal rigidity
Large-volume bleeding with a large clot
Profound anemia with hemoglobin of 5.7 g/dl
Hypotension and tachycardia
Marked right-predominant tenderness

data.description: Abnormal intestinal rotation permitting twisting around the mesenteric blood supply, leading to obstruction and potentially bowel ischemia. This is a surgical emergency.
symptoms_in_common: Bloody stools, potentially from intestinal ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent pain over two days is less typical than progressive symptoms in established volvulus
Profound blood-loss anemia and low serum iron are less typical as the dominant presentation

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia (DIPNECH)
data.description: A rare proliferation of pulmonary neuroendocrine cells, usually in older nonsmoking women, associated with constrictive bronchiolitis, air trapping, and pulmonary nodules or carcinoid tumors. This is the leading consideration, but confirmation requires further evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with FEV1 32% predicted
CT images appear to show mosaic attenuation or air trapping and multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules

data.description: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine lung tumors that may appear as rounded or lobulated nodules and cause bronchial obstruction. Multiple carcinoids can occur in association with DIPNECH.
symptoms_in_common: Well-defined, lobulated pulmonary nodules or masses visible on CT
Nonsmoking status is compatible with typical carcinoid tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe diffuse small-airway obstruction is not usually explained by isolated peripheral carcinoid tumors
Widespread apparent air trapping would suggest associated bronchiolitis rather than tumors alone

data.description: Fibrotic narrowing of small airways causing persistent airflow obstruction and expiratory air trapping. It may be idiopathic or associated with autoimmune disease, exposures, infections, or DIPNECH.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with FEV1 32% predicted
Small-airway pattern on the flow-volume loop
Apparent mosaic attenuation or air trapping on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple substantial, well-defined pulmonary nodules are not typical of isolated constrictive bronchiolitis
No relevant medical or drug history is reported to suggest a common secondary cause

data.description: Inflammatory airway disease that can begin in older adults and cause marked airflow limitation and air trapping. Bronchodilator testing would help assess whether the obstruction is reversible.
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules or masses are not explained by asthma
A steadily progressive six-month course is less characteristic than variable or episodic symptoms

data.description: An immune-mediated response to inhaled antigens that can involve the small airways and produce breathlessness, mosaic attenuation, air trapping, and centrilobular nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent mosaic attenuation or air trapping on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: The larger, sharply defined nodules or masses are unlike the usually small, ill-defined centrilobular nodules of hypersensitivity pneumonitis
Profound predominantly obstructive physiology is less typical than restrictive or mixed impairment

diagnoses.name: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.title: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, possibly nodular sclerosis subtype, with pulmonary involvement
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy that commonly affects young adults and can involve supraclavicular nodes and lungs. The supplied histology appears to show broad fibrous bands and scattered large atypical cells, raising this possibility; immunohistochemistry is needed for confirmation. Associated granulomatous reactions can obscure diagnosis in small biopsies.
symptoms_in_common: Firm, rubbery, nontender supraclavicular lymph node
Elevated ESR, CRP, and soluble IL-2 receptor
Cough and hemoptysis with cavitary left upper lung abnormalities
Granulomatous inflammation potentially representing a tumor-associated reaction
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymph node enlargement waxing and waning for approximately 12 years is unusually prolonged for untreated classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Acute respiratory presentation over only a few days
Extensive pulmonary cavitation is an uncommon manifestation

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause upper-lobe cavitation, hemoptysis, and cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Negative routine cultures do not exclude tuberculosis; specific mycobacterial testing is required.
symptoms_in_common: Left upper-lobe cavitary and consolidative abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No night sweats or weight loss
Respiratory symptoms present for only a few days
A freely mobile, rubbery node is less characteristic than matted or necrotic tuberculous nodes
No pathogens identified in the available biopsy or microbiologic studies

data.diagnosis: Sarcoidosis with atypical cavitary pulmonary involvement
data.description: A systemic inflammatory disorder characterized by noninfectious granulomas, often involving lungs and lymph nodes. Cavitation can occur but is rare, and infection and malignancy must be excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Cough, low-grade fever, and mild hypoxemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent unilateral cavitary consolidation rather than typical bilateral hilar adenopathy or diffuse nodules
Hemoptysis is relatively uncommon
Neutrophilic leukocytosis and an acute febrile presentation are less characteristic

data.description: A necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis that can cause cavitary lung lesions and pulmonary hemorrhage, often accompanied by upper-airway or kidney disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding isolated supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is not characteristic
No reported sinus, nasal, ear, or renal manifestations
The biopsy report does not describe necrotizing vasculitis
A single dominant upper-lobe process is less characteristic than multiple pulmonary nodules

data.description: Environmental mycobacteria can cause chronic granulomatous lung infection with upper-lobe cavities. Diagnosis requires organism-specific cultures and correlation with clinical and imaging findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age without reported structural lung disease or immunodeficiency
Respiratory symptoms lasting only a few days rather than a chronic course
Longstanding supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is unusual in localized pulmonary disease
No mycobacterial organisms have been demonstrated

data.description: JC polyomavirus infection causing progressive brain demyelination in immunosuppressed patients. Prior natalizumab exposure and a high anti-JCPyV antibody index raise concern for carryover PML. Negative CSF JCPyV-DNA does not exclude early disease. The supplied image is a viral regulatory-region schematic, not diagnostic brain imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Homonymous hemianopia and visual field defects
Seizures, particularly with involvement near the cerebral cortex
Focal neurological abnormalities, including nystagmus and tremor
Elevated CSF protein with a low cell count and normal glucose
Immunosuppression associated with natalizumab exposure and marked leukopenia
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-limb spasms are nonspecific and may reflect preexisting multiple sclerosis
Marked leukopenia is not caused directly by PML and may be treatment-related

data.description: Inflammatory worsening of underlying PML as immune surveillance recovers after natalizumab withdrawal. It requires evidence supporting PML and an inflammatory response, neither of which is established by the supplied schematic.
symptoms_in_common: New neurological deterioration after natalizumab discontinuation
Nystagmus and other focal neurological abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked leukopenia during fingolimod treatment suggests continued systemic immunosuppression rather than straightforward immune recovery
Low CSF cell count provides limited support for an inflammatory syndrome, although it does not exclude it
Distal tremor and upper-limb spasms are nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis relapse or rebound after natalizumab withdrawal
data.description: Recurrent inflammatory demyelination after stopping natalizumab, potentially occurring during a transition to another disease-modifying treatment. Brain MRI is needed to distinguish this from PML and other causes.
symptoms_in_common: Neurological deterioration after changing disease-modifying therapy
Visual field defects if posterior visual pathways are affected
Elevated CSF protein with normal glucose
symptoms_not_in_common: Seizures are less typical of an ordinary multiple sclerosis relapse
Marked leukopenia is not explained by a relapse itself
Homonymous hemianopia is less common than visual symptoms caused by optic neuritis

data.description: A syndrome of predominantly posterior cerebral vasogenic edema that can occur with medication exposure or endothelial dysfunction. Fingolimod-associated PRES is rare; diagnosis requires compatible brain imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CSF protein with few cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Distal tremor and upper-limb spasms are not characteristic presenting features
Nystagmus is less typical
Marked leukopenia is not a direct feature of PRES

data.description: Brain infection caused by herpes simplex virus or varicella-zoster virus, considered in an immunosuppressed patient with new seizures and focal deficits. CSF viral testing and brain MRI are needed to evaluate this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Focal neurological deficits, including visual field loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Low CSF cell count is less typical than the pleocytosis usually seen, although immunosuppression can blunt it
Distal tremor and upper-limb spasms are not characteristic
Nystagmus is not a typical dominant finding

data.diagnosis: Fabry disease with cardiac and early renal involvement
data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A, leading to glycosphingolipid accumulation. The markedly reduced enzyme activity and hemizygous GLA mutation strongly establish this diagnosis. The images appear consistent with ventricular hypertrophy and intracellular lamellar storage inclusions.
symptoms_in_common: Burning extremity pain beginning in childhood

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder causing ventricular hypertrophy and sometimes myocardial ischemia or arrhythmias. It is a cardiac differential for the apparent hypertrophy and ECG abnormalities, but does not explain the multisystem findings or Fabry-specific laboratory results.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent ventricular hypertrophy on cardiac imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset burning extremity pain
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Proteinuria
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA mutation
Intracellular lamellar storage inclusions

data.diagnosis: Systemic amyloidosis with cardiac and renal involvement
data.description: A disorder involving extracellular deposition of abnormal proteins that can produce ventricular wall thickening, neuropathy, and proteinuria. It is substantially less likely than Fabry disease because the specific enzyme, genetic, ocular, and skin findings are not explained.
symptoms_not_in_common: Neuropathic pain beginning in childhood
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA mutation
Intracellular lamellar inclusions rather than extracellular amyloid deposits

data.description: Lysosomal phospholipid accumulation caused by medications such as chloroquine, hydroxychloroquine, or amiodarone. It can mimic Fabry disease through corneal deposits and lamellar tissue inclusions, but no relevant drug exposure is reported and it does not explain the GLA findings.
symptoms_in_common: Intracellular lamellar inclusions on electron microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Burning extremity pain beginning in childhood
Angiokeratomas on the trunk
Tinnitus
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA mutation

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency. Angiokeratomas and childhood onset make it a remote phenotypic differential, but its usual progressive neurologic and developmental manifestations differ from this case, and it does not explain the Fabry-specific testing.
symptoms_in_common: Evidence of lysosomal storage on tissue imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic childhood acroparesthesias
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Proteinuria with preserved renal function
Atypical chest discomfort as a presenting complaint
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA mutation

data.description: Gallbladder inflammation without gallstones, often caused by bile stasis and impaired blood supply in critically ill or severely injured patients. This is a leading consideration, although the single ultrasound image is not definitive.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance suggestive of a thick-walled gallbladder containing internal echoes
symptoms_not_in_common: The intrahepatic hematoma is a separate traumatic injury, not a typical manifestation of cholecystitis

data.description: Secondary bacterial infection of a traumatic blood collection within the liver, potentially developing into an abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed onset of fever after hospitalization
symptoms_not_in_common: The ultrasound structure appears potentially gallbladder-shaped rather than clearly representing an intrahepatic hematoma

data.description: A localized bacterial infection forming a pus-filled cavity in the liver, sometimes arising from an infected hematoma or biliary infection.
symptoms_in_common: An apparent complex fluid-containing structure on ultrasound
Recent liver trauma as a possible predisposing factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The elongated appearance of the imaged structure may favor gallbladder pathology rather than a hepatic abscess

data.description: An infected collection of leaked bile caused by traumatic injury to intrahepatic bile ducts.
symptoms_in_common: An apparent fluid-containing structure on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: An intrahepatic hematoma alone does not establish a bile leak
The ultrasound appearance may represent the gallbladder rather than a separate bile collection

data.description: Gallbladder inflammation caused by a gallstone obstructing the cystic duct. Ultrasound confirmation of an obstructing stone would help distinguish it from acalculous cholecystitis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible gallbladder wall thickening and intraluminal echoes on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite shadowing gallstone is identifiable in the supplied image
The severe-trauma ICU context more strongly favors acalculous cholecystitis
The traumatic intrahepatic hematoma is not a typical manifestation

data.description: A rare inflammatory reaction to iodine exposure that can produce pustular, bullous, or vegetating skin lesions, often with a dense neutrophilic infiltrate. This is the leading consideration given the contrast exposure and biopsy findings.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt eruption several hours after iodinated contrast administration
Generalized pustules, coalescing vesicles, and pus-filled bullae
Prominent facial and auricular lesions shown in the photographs
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and diffuse neutrophilic dermal infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria preceding contrast exposure is not a characteristic manifestation
Mild eosinophilia is nonspecific rather than a defining feature

data.description: An acute, usually drug-induced eruption of numerous sterile, nonfollicular pustules. Iodinated contrast can trigger it, and eosinophilia may accompany the eruption.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid onset after exposure to iodinated contrast
Generalized pustular eruption involving the trunk and limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Large pus-filled bullae and prominent vegetating facial lesions are less typical than small superficial pustules
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and diffuse dermal neutrophilic infiltration are less characteristic than subcorneal or intraepidermal pustules
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis is unusual
Hematuria is not a typical manifestation

data.description: A variant of acute neutrophilic dermatosis in which inflammatory plaques develop vesicles or bullae. Biopsy typically shows a dense sterile neutrophilic infiltrate in the dermis.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt onset of extensive inflammatory skin lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized pus-filled lesions with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia are less characteristic
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis is not a typical biopsy finding
Mild eosinophilia is not a defining feature
Hematuria is not a usual manifestation

data.description: A severe inflammatory form of psoriasis characterized by widespread sterile pustules that may coalesce into larger collections of pus.
symptoms_in_common: Generalized pustular eruption involving the trunk and extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Close temporal association with iodinated contrast favors a contrast-induced reaction
Prominent vesicles and bullae on the face and ear are less typical
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis and a diffuse dermal infiltrate are less characteristic than spongiform epidermal pustules
Mild eosinophilia is not typical
Hematuria is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A severe, usually drug-induced reaction causing epidermal death, blistering, and detachment, commonly with mucosal involvement. The full-thickness epidermal necrosis warrants consideration, although the pustular morphology argues against it.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to a potential medication trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly pustular and pus-filled lesions rather than dusky macules and sheets of epidermal detachment
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia
Dense neutrophilic dermal infiltration rather than typically sparse inflammation
Onset within hours is less typical without prior sensitization
Hematuria preceding the eruption is not a characteristic presenting feature

data.diagnosis: Capnocytophaga canimorsus sepsis with purpura fulminans
data.description: A potentially fatal infection transmitted through dog saliva, especially after bites. Heavy alcohol use increases susceptibility. Sepsis can cause disseminated intravascular coagulation, widespread purpura, and tissue necrosis. This is the leading possibility; the pictured slender, fusiform bacteria are compatible but require laboratory confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Dog bites three days before illness
Acute nausea, epigastric pain, and vomiting
Delayed capillary refill indicating impaired perfusion
Necrotic bite wounds with purplish borders
Widespread purplish skin discoloration and dusky digits visible in the photographs
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertension is less typical of established septic shock, although it does not exclude early sepsis

data.diagnosis: Pasteurella multocida wound infection with sepsis
data.description: A dog- or cat-associated bacterial infection that commonly causes rapidly developing wound cellulitis and can occasionally progress to bacteremia, severe sepsis, and coagulation abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Recent dog bites to the hands and forearms
Ill appearance, hypothermia, tachycardia, and tachypnea
Nausea and vomiting during systemic illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive purpura and dusky digits are unusual for uncomplicated Pasteurella wound infection
Prominent epigastric pain is not a characteristic presenting feature
The pictured long, slender bacteria are less typical than Pasteurella's short coccobacillary morphology

data.diagnosis: Necrotizing soft-tissue infection arising from dog-bite wounds
data.description: A rapidly progressive bacterial infection of deeper soft tissues that may follow contaminated wounds and cause tissue destruction and systemic toxicity. It requires urgent surgical assessment; absence of visible gas on a radiograph does not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Purplish discoloration surrounding the forearm lesion
Ill appearance and impaired peripheral perfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized purpura away from the wounds suggests an accompanying systemic coagulopathy rather than a purely localized infection
Epigastric pain and vomiting are nonspecific rather than characteristic local manifestations

data.description: An invasive Neisseria meningitidis bloodstream infection that can produce rapidly progressive sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, purpura, and peripheral tissue ischemia, sometimes without meningitis.
symptoms_in_common: Widespread purplish skin lesions and dusky digits visible in the photographs
symptoms_not_in_common: Dog-bite-associated necrotic wounds suggest a different infectious source
The pictured slender bacteria are not typical of meningococcal diplococci
Hypertension is less typical of advanced meningococcal shock

data.description: Acute pancreatic inflammation commonly triggered by heavy alcohol intake. It can cause epigastric pain, vomiting, and a severe systemic inflammatory response, but would not adequately explain the bite-associated necrosis and apparent bacteremia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Necrotic dog-bite wounds with purplish borders
Widespread purpura and dusky digits are not typical, except in rare severe cases with coagulopathy
Bacteria visible in the supplied microscopy image suggest an infectious process not explained by uncomplicated pancreatitis

data.diagnosis: MT-TL1-related mitochondrial disease with a MELAS-like phenotype
data.description: A mitochondrial energy-production disorder causing myopathy and neurological dysfunction. The m.3303C>T variant supports MT-TL1-related disease, although the apparent large-vessel occlusion raises concern for an embolic stroke rather than a purely metabolic MELAS stroke-like episode.
symptoms_in_common: Childhood-onset generalized weakness, hypotonia, muscle atrophy, and gait disturbance
Recurrent neurological episodes with hemiplegia, aphasia, and dysarthria
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent major cerebral arterial occlusion is not typical of a purely metabolic stroke-like episode
Markedly low C3 is not a characteristic finding
Suppressed TSH is not a defining feature

data.description: Cardiac muscle dysfunction caused by defective mitochondrial energy metabolism. MT-TL1-associated cardiomyopathy may cause arrhythmias, syncope, and ventricular dysfunction that predisposes to intracardiac thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic intracavitary masses that could represent thrombi associated with ventricular dysfunction
Recurrent strokes potentially caused by cardiac emboli
symptoms_not_in_common: Aphasia and hemiplegia are secondary complications rather than direct manifestations
Low C3 is not typical
Suppressed TSH is not explained by mitochondrial cardiomyopathy alone

data.description: Brain infarction caused by an embolus originating in the heart. The focal brain lesion, apparent right-sided major arterial flow interruption, and possible intracardiac thrombi make this an important explanation for the current neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Previous stroke at a young age
Large right hemispheric hyperintense lesion on the supplied brain image
Apparent right internal carotid or proximal middle cerebral arterial flow interruption on angiographic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset muscle weakness and atrophy are not caused by cerebral embolism
Mitochondrial muscle-biopsy findings and elevated lactate require an underlying separate disorder
Low C3 is not typical of uncomplicated cardioembolic stroke

data.description: A clot within the left ventricle, often associated with impaired ventricular contraction, that can embolize to cerebral arteries. The echogenic masses indicated on the echocardiograms are suspicious for thrombi, although additional cardiac imaging is needed to distinguish them from other masses.
symptoms_in_common: Echogenic intracavitary masses on the supplied echocardiograms
Current hemiplegia and aphasia compatible with systemic embolization
Underlying mitochondrial disease that can predispose to cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding generalized muscle weakness and hypotonia are not caused by a ventricular thrombus
Mitochondrial genetic and biopsy findings are not explained by thrombosis itself
Low C3 and suppressed TSH are not characteristic findings

data.description: A cerebral arteriopathy involving stenosis or occlusion of the terminal internal carotid arteries and development of collateral vessels. It is a less likely alternative explanation for young-onset recurrent strokes; the supplied angiographic image does not clearly demonstrate the characteristic collateral network.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent strokes in a young adult
Apparent severe unilateral anterior-circulation arterial flow reduction or occlusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Possible intracardiac thrombi favor an embolic mechanism instead
Childhood mitochondrial myopathy is not a typical manifestation
Elevated lactate and the MT-TL1 mutation are not explained by moyamoya alone
Markedly low C3 is not characteristic

diagnoses.name: MELAS syndrome
diagnoses.title: MELAS - [Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes] syndrome

data.description: A malignant tumor of pancreatic duct cells. A pancreatic-head tumor can obstruct both the bile and pancreatic ducts. The apparent pancreatic-head lesion, ductal dilation, and irregular glands in fibrous stroma on the supplied images make this a leading possibility, although formal pathology interpretation is required.
symptoms_in_common: Diarrhea and bloating, potentially from impaired pancreatic digestion
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 29 is very uncommon
Abrupt onset of watery diarrhea after eating sushi is not characteristic

data.description: A gland-forming cancer at the junction where the bile and pancreatic ducts empty into the duodenum. It can cause early obstructive jaundice and dilation of both ducts.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent bile and pancreatic duct dilation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 29 is unusually young
Watery diarrhea beginning after sushi consumption is not characteristic
A lesion centered within the pancreatic head rather than the ampulla would favor another diagnosis

data.description: A cancer of the lower common bile duct that causes progressive biliary obstruction. Its gland-forming histology can resemble pancreatic adenocarcinoma; determining the tumor's anatomical origin is essential.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 29 is unusually young
Persistent watery diarrhea is not a typical presenting symptom
Prominent pancreatic duct dilation and a pancreatic-centered lesion would favor pancreatic or ampullary disease

data.description: An immune-mediated pancreatic inflammatory disease that can produce a mass-like pancreatic enlargement and bile duct narrowing, mimicking cancer. It requires characteristic pathology and supporting clinical testing.
symptoms_in_common: Diarrhea and bloating from possible pancreatic dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset after eating sushi is not characteristic
Failure to improve with methylprednisolone is less supportive, although an unspecified short course does not exclude it
The apparent irregular gland-forming lesions in fibrous stroma raise concern for malignancy rather than uncomplicated autoimmune inflammation

data.description: A stone lodged in the common bile duct that blocks bile drainage, causing jaundice, itching, and liver test abnormalities. It is a common alternative explanation for biliary obstruction but would not explain malignant glandular pathology.
symptoms_not_in_common: Seven weeks of progressive watery diarrhea and bloating are not typical
A pancreatic-head mass is not explained by a bile duct stone
The supplied gland-forming tissue abnormalities are not explained by choledocholithiasis

data.description: A gallstone that has entered the intestinal tract and lodged in the rectum, causing mechanical difficulty with defecation. This is the best-supported explanation because the stone was identified and removed endoscopically.
symptoms_in_common: Limited rectal bleeding from local mucosal irritation

data.description: An abnormal connection between the gallbladder and colon that can allow a gallstone to pass directly into the large bowel. The arrowed gallbladder–bowel interface on the supplied images raises suspicion for this route, although confirmation requires review of the complete imaging study.
symptoms_in_common: Gallstone found in the rectum, compatible with passage through the colon
Difficulty passing stool if the migrated stone becomes impacted
Rectal foreign-body sensation from the migrated stone
symptoms_not_in_common: Limited rectal bleeding is not a typical direct manifestation of the fistula itself

data.description: An abnormal connection between the gallbladder and duodenum, commonly related to chronic gallstone inflammation. It offers an alternative route for a gallstone to enter the bowel and eventually reach the rectum.
symptoms_in_common: Gallstone found within the intestinal tract
Difficulty passing stool if the stone subsequently lodges in the rectum
Rectal foreign-body sensation attributable to distal stone impaction
symptoms_not_in_common: Limited rectal bleeding is not typical of the fistula itself
Isolated rectal symptoms do not establish a duodenal fistula

data.description: Inflammation and scarring from Crohn's disease can narrow the anorectal lumen, impair stool passage, and potentially predispose to impaction of a migrated stone. No stricture is explicitly documented in this case.
symptoms_not_in_common: A gallstone in the rectum is not caused by an anorectal stricture and requires a separate explanation

data.description: Crohn's inflammation involving the rectum can cause bleeding and tenesmus, perceived as incomplete evacuation or a rectal foreign-body sensation. It is a possible coexisting condition but is less explanatory than the documented stone.
symptoms_not_in_common: A gallstone found in the rectum is not explained by proctitis
Mechanical stool-passage difficulty from a discrete stone is not typical of isolated proctitis

data.diagnosis: Acute lateral patellar dislocation with osteochondral fracture and intra-articular loose body
data.description: The leading diagnosis is lateral displacement of the patella with associated injury to the patellar or femoral articular surface, releasing a cartilage-and-bone fragment into the joint. The radiographs suggest an intra-articular fragment, but MRI is needed to establish its origin and extent.
symptoms_in_common: Acute pain and inability to bear weight
Subsequent intermittent locking and palpable loose body
Generalized joint laxity predisposing to patellar instability
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic fatigue syndrome is not explained by this injury

data.diagnosis: Medial patellofemoral ligament tear associated with patellar dislocation
data.description: Damage to the principal soft-tissue restraint against lateral patellar displacement commonly accompanies an acute lateral patellar dislocation. An isolated tear would not explain a true osteochondral loose body.
symptoms_in_common: Tenderness around the medial patellofemoral ligament
Effusion and reduced range of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable intra-articular loose body is not explained by an isolated ligament tear
Mechanical locking suggests an additional intra-articular injury
Chronic fatigue syndrome is unrelated

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the knee with a detached fragment
data.description: A focal disorder of subchondral bone and overlying cartilage, typically affecting adolescents, that can produce an unstable or detached osteochondral fragment and mechanical knee symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute lateral patellar dislocation is not a typical manifestation
Focal medial patellofemoral ligament tenderness favors a dislocation-related injury
Abrupt symptoms during a single injury are less typical than preceding activity-related pain
Generalized joint laxity and chronic fatigue syndrome are not characteristic

data.description: A torn meniscal fragment, particularly a bucket-handle tear, can displace into the joint and cause painful mechanical locking after an injury.
symptoms_in_common: Acute injury followed by knee pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Visible lateral patellar dislocation is not explained by a meniscal tear
Medial patellofemoral ligament tenderness is less typical than joint-line tenderness
A palpable loose body beneath the patella is not typical of a meniscal tear
Chronic fatigue syndrome is unrelated

data.description: An uncommon synovial disorder producing cartilage nodules that may detach as intra-articular loose bodies, causing swelling and locking. It is unusual at this age and generally has a more gradual presentation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden onset during an acute injury is atypical
Lateral patellar dislocation is not a characteristic finding
Medial patellofemoral ligament tenderness favors traumatic patellar instability
Generalized joint laxity and chronic fatigue syndrome are not characteristic

data.description: A rare variant of lichen planopilaris characterized by scarring scalp alopecia, typically nonscarring axillary and pubic hair loss, and spiny follicular papules on the trunk and limbs. This is the strongest fit, although confirmation requires clinicopathologic correlation.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic spiny follicular papules on the trunk and limbs
Scalp alopecia with apparent scarring in the photographs
Images suggest follicular keratin plugging and perifollicular lichenoid inflammation

data.description: An inflammatory disorder in which a lymphocytic immune response damages hair follicles, causing perifollicular scaling and permanent scarring alopecia.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic images suggest perifollicular lymphocytic inflammation and follicular interface injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive spiny papules across the trunk and limbs are less typical of classic scalp-limited disease
Combined axillary and pubic hair loss is more characteristic of Graham-Little-Piccardi-Lassueur syndrome

data.description: A cutaneous T-cell lymphoma involving hair follicles that can produce persistent itchy follicular papules, plaques, and alopecia. Diagnosis requires assessment for atypical folliculotropic lymphocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Poor response to topical steroids and antihistamines
Follicle-associated lymphocytic inflammation in the supplied histologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: The combination of spiny body papules and scalp, pubic, and axillary alopecia is more characteristic of Graham-Little-Piccardi-Lassueur syndrome
The apparent lichenoid follicular injury is less typical than an atypical folliculotropic infiltrate

data.description: A rare, usually inherited follicular keratinization disorder causing widespread spiny follicular papules and progressive scarring alopecia, most often beginning in childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Spiny follicular papules on the trunk and limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in adulthood rather than childhood
Severe persistent pruritus is less characteristic
Prominent pubic and axillary alopecia is less typical
The apparent lichenoid inflammatory pattern favors lichen planopilaris

data.description: A benign follicular keratinization disorder producing grouped rough papules with central keratin spines, usually on the trunk and extremities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Scarring scalp alopecia
Pubic and axillary hair loss
Severe persistent pruritus is less typical
Destructive perifollicular lichenoid inflammation is not characteristic

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy caused by uncontrolled complement activation, often triggered by pregnancy, that produces hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and predominantly renal injury. This is the leading consideration, although confirmatory evaluation is required.
symptoms_in_common: Pregnancy-associated onset with persistent postpartum hypertension and proteinuria
Coombs-negative microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with schistocytes, elevated LDH and bilirubin, and low haptoglobin
Hypertension, edema, heavy proteinuria, and microscopic hematuria
Ulcerative ankle lesions and apparent dermal vascular thrombi in the supplied images, potentially reflecting cutaneous microangiopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Cutaneous ulceration is an uncommon manifestation

data.description: Severe hypertension can injure small vessels, producing renal failure, red-cell fragmentation, and platelet consumption. Hypertension may also be secondary to another thrombotic microangiopathy.
symptoms_in_common: History of poorly controlled severe hypertension
symptoms_not_in_common: The recorded blood pressure of 151/103 mmHg is below the range usually associated with hypertension-induced microangiopathy
Ulcerative skin lesions with apparent dermal vascular thrombosis are not usual features
Severe thrombocytopenia and hemolysis may suggest a primary microangiopathy rather than hypertension alone

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy typically caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, resulting in platelet-rich microvascular thrombosis, hemolytic anemia, and thrombocytopenia.

Pregnancy as a possible precipitating factor

Ulcerative ankle lesions are uncommon

data.diagnosis: Antiphospholipid syndrome with renal thrombotic microangiopathy

Ulcerative ankle lesions with apparent dermal vascular thrombosis

data.diagnosis: KIT-mutant gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) of the ileum
data.description: A mesenchymal gastrointestinal tumor associated with interstitial cells of Cajal, commonly driven by activating KIT mutations. Syncope attributable to severe blood loss

Negative colonoscopy despite bleeding from a small-bowel lesion
KIT exon 11 deletion involving the juxtamembrane region

Spindle-cell component in the provided histology

data.description: A tumor of intestinal neuroendocrine cells, often arising in the distal ileum and appearing as an enhancing mass. It may cause bleeding, but the molecular findings strongly favor GIST.

symptoms_not_in_common: KIT exon 11 deletion is not characteristic
Spindle and epithelioid tumor morphology without evident gland formation is atypical
A discrete enhancing mural mass is less typical than an irregular stenosing lesion

data.description: An uncommon, usually benign nerve-sheath tumor of the intestinal wall that can resemble GIST radiologically and occasionally cause bleeding. The KIT mutation makes this diagnosis unlikely.

symptoms_not_in_common: KIT exon 11 deletion is not characteristic of schwannoma

Severe overt bleeding is an uncommon presentation

data.diagnosis: Gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), possibly epithelioid type

Large heterogeneous upper-abdominal mass with apparent hemorrhagic or degenerative areas

data.description: An inherited disorder of epidermal cell adhesion causing recurrent blistering and eroded plaques in skin folds. This is the leading possibility; the biopsy appears to show extensive acantholysis resembling a dilapidated brick wall.

Markedly thickened plaques with multiple skin tags
Apparent extensive epidermal acantholysis on biopsy
Pseudofolliculitis barbae

data.description: A usually benign but locally aggressive bone tumor affecting skeletally mature young adults. Pelvic tumors can cause expansile bone destruction and a palpable mass; confirmation requires tissue diagnosis.

Expansile lytic lesion involving the left iliac wing on imaging
Absence of fever or preceding trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: The iliac wing is a less common location than the ends of long bones
The apparent peripheral bony rim is less characteristic of an aggressive giant cell tumor

data.description: A benign, expansile bone lesion containing blood-filled spaces, occurring primarily in children and young adults. It may arise independently or develop within another bone tumor.

Expansile left iliac lesion with cortical thinning and internal compartmentalization
symptoms_not_in_common: The prominently enhancing solid-appearing components are less typical of a purely cystic lesion
Characteristic fluid-fluid levels are not clearly demonstrated in the supplied images

data.description: A benign bone-forming tumor most common in adolescents and young adults. Larger lesions can be locally aggressive and may contain secondary aneurysmal bone cyst changes.

Increased tracer uptake at the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: A large palpable iliac-wing mass is an uncommon presentation
The predominantly lytic appearance is less typical than a lesion with more conspicuous bone-forming matrix

data.description: A malignant bone-forming tumor with blood-filled cystic spaces that can resemble an aneurysmal bone cyst. Thick enhancing solid tissue and aggressive bone destruction raise concern; biopsy is needed to distinguish it.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarging tender pelvic mass over one month
Large lytic iliac lesion with enhancing tissue
Increased metabolic activity within portions of the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatively circumscribed expansile appearance and peripheral bony shell are less typical of a high-grade destructive tumor

data.description: A rare benign cartilage-related bone tumor occurring mainly in young people. It typically produces an eccentric, lobulated, expansile lytic lesion and can occasionally involve the pelvis.
symptoms_in_common: Lobulated expansile lytic lesion in the left iliac wing
symptoms_not_in_common: The large size and prominent palpable pelvic mass are less typical

data.description: An autoimmune disorder of impaired inhibitory neurotransmission causing axial and limb rigidity with painful spasms. symptoms_in_common: Progressive paraspinal and lower-limb muscle spasms
Profound mobility impairment and wheelchair dependence
Spasms severe enough to impair breathing

symptoms_not_in_common: Severe clonus is less characteristic of classic stiff-person syndrome and raises consideration of broader central nervous system involvement

data.diagnosis: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)
data.description: A severe stiff-person spectrum disorder, often associated with glycine-receptor antibodies, that produces rigidity, spasms, exaggerated startle, and brainstem or spinal dysfunction. Antibody testing and additional neurologic assessment are needed to distinguish it from classic stiff-person syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Electrophysiologic responses suggestive of impaired inhibitory reflex control

data.description: A disorder of exaggerated startle responses caused by impaired inhibitory signaling in brainstem and spinal circuits. Acquired forms can be autoimmune and overlap with stiff-person spectrum disorders.

Reduced suppression of the second blink-reflex response in the supplied recording
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent progressive paraspinal and lower-limb spasms leading to wheelchair dependence are less typical of isolated hyperekplexia
Severe clonus is not a defining feature of isolated hyperekplexia

data.description: Inflammation of the spinal cord can disrupt descending motor pathways and produce spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, and progressive loss of mobility. Spinal MRI and cerebrospinal fluid testing would be needed to evaluate this possibility.

Breathing impairment specifically during spasms is less typical unless high cervical pathways are involved

data.description: A peripheral nerve hyperexcitability disorder causing persistent muscle activity, stiffness, cramps, and delayed relaxation. Diagnostic needle EMG typically demonstrates neuromyotonic or myokymic discharges, which are not established by the supplied recordings.

data.diagnosis: Severe atherosclerotic supra-aortic arterial disease with ischemic scalp necrosis
data.description: Advanced narrowing or occlusion of arteries supplying the brain and scalp can cause cerebral hypoperfusion and, rarely, scalp tissue death. The angiographic image appears to show marked proximal arterial narrowing, but definitive interpretation requires the full study.

Scalp ulceration with dark necrotic-appearing tissue
Apparent major neck-vessel abnormalities on angiography

data.description: An inflammatory disease of the aorta and its major branches that can produce severe stenoses, cerebral hypoperfusion, and tissue ischemia.

Scalp necrosis potentially caused by compromised arterial supply

data.diagnosis: Giant cell arteritis with scalp necrosis

data.diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis with secondary mixed cryoglobulinemia
data.description: A systemic infection caused by Leishmania parasites transmitted by sandflies. Mediterranean exposure and anti-TNF immunosuppression increase risk.
