symptoms_not_in_common: Documented adrenal insufficiency with markedly elevated ACTH
Severe generalized hyperpigmentation
Hyperreflexia and bilateral extensor plantar responses, rather than the reduced reflexes more typical of this disorder
Congenital cryptorchidism and hypospadias
Hyperkeratosis

data.description: A fluid-filled cavity within the spinal cord that can cause segmental muscle wasting and weakness with long-tract signs below the lesion. The supplied MRI appears to show a central intramedullary fluid-signal cavity, although full imaging review is needed to distinguish syringomyelia from a prominent central canal. This could be a coexisting contributor rather than a unifying diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Distal arm muscle wasting and weakness
Hyperreflexia and bilateral extensor plantar responses
Apparent central spinal cord cavity on the supplied MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Adrenal insufficiency with elevated ACTH and hyperpigmentation
Infancy-onset tear deficiency
Recurrent hypoglycemia and failure to thrive
Progressive dysphagia is not typical of an isolated cervicothoracic cavity
Optic atrophy and developmental delay
Congenital cryptorchidism, hypospadias, and inguinal hernia

data.diagnosis: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), with possible hemorrhagic complications
data.description: An acute encephalopathy caused by disturbed cerebral vascular regulation and endothelial dysfunction. MRI commonly shows posterior-predominant edema; restricted diffusion and small hemorrhages can occur. Normal blood pressure does not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive confusion rapidly worsening to unresponsiveness
Generalized weakness without clear focal neurologic deficits
Bilateral posterior-predominant signal abnormalities on the supplied MRI
Apparent punctate susceptibility abnormalities suggesting small hemorrhages
symptoms_not_in_common: Normotension is less typical than hypertension, although compatible with PRES
No reported headache, seizures, or visual disturbance
Prominent apparent diffusion restriction is less typical of uncomplicated vasogenic edema

data.description: Multiple cerebral infarcts can arise from emboli or cancer-associated hypercoagulability. Bilateral involvement may cause severe encephalopathy, and hemorrhagic transformation can produce susceptibility abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Active metastatic cancer, which increases thrombotic risk
Multiple areas of apparent diffusion restriction
Possible small hemorrhagic components on susceptibility-sensitive imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive generalized symptoms over several days rather than a clearly sudden focal event
No clear focal neurologic deficits
Relatively symmetric posterior abnormalities are less typical of scattered arterial emboli

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous thrombosis with hemorrhagic venous infarction
data.description: Thrombosis of cerebral veins or dural sinuses can cause bilateral edema, restricted diffusion, and hemorrhagic infarcts. Malignancy is an important risk factor; venographic imaging is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral cerebral abnormalities with possible small hemorrhages
Apparent diffusion restriction compatible with venous infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported headache
No reported seizures or papilledema
No clear focal neurologic deficits
The supplied images do not establish a thrombosed vein or sinus

data.description: Breast cancer can spread to the brain, producing lesions with surrounding edema and occasionally hemorrhage. Contrast-enhanced MRI is necessary to evaluate this possibility adequately.
symptoms_in_common: Long-standing stage IV breast cancer with multiple extracranial metastatic sites
Progressive weakness and altered mental status
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal brain MRI only two weeks earlier makes extensive newly symptomatic metastases less likely
No discrete masses are evident on the supplied images
Bilateral posterior-predominant abnormalities are less typical of metastatic masses
No clear focal neurologic deficits

data.diagnosis: Toxic-metabolic encephalopathy, including hepatic or hyperammonemic encephalopathy
data.description: Systemic metabolic disturbances or impaired hepatic function can cause diffuse brain dysfunction, sometimes with bilateral MRI abnormalities. Liver metastases warrant evaluation, but hepatic failure or hyperammonemia cannot be inferred without laboratory testing.
symptoms_in_common: Episodic confusion progressing to profound unresponsiveness
Absence of clear focal neurologic deficits
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior-predominant abnormalities with possible microhemorrhages are not characteristic of hepatic encephalopathy
No reported jaundice, asterixis, or other clinical evidence of hepatic failure
No documented metabolic abnormality or elevated ammonia level

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation confined to the nervous system, potentially producing an enhancing cervical spinal cord lesion. This is the leading consideration given the mildly elevated ACE and the apparent granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells in the supplied histology; confirmation requires exclusion of infectious causes.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive weakness in all four extremities
Hyperreflexia and bilateral Babinski, Hoffmann, and Tromner signs
Asymmetric weakness with crossed sensory deficits resembling a partial Brown-Séquard syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal cerebrospinal fluid is less typical of active neurosarcoidosis but does not exclude it
Absence of systemic organ involvement is less common than systemic sarcoidosis with neurological involvement

data.description: A localized granulomatous spinal cord lesion caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It can mimic an intramedullary tumor or neurosarcoidosis; tissue microbiology and assessment for caseating necrosis help distinguish it.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent focal enhancing cervical cord lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No identified extracranial or systemic involvement
Normal cerebrospinal fluid is less typical if associated tuberculous meningitis is present
Mild ACE elevation is not a characteristic diagnostic finding

data.description: A rare spinal cord infection, such as cryptococcosis or histoplasmosis, that can cause granulomatous inflammation and a mass-like enhancing lesion. Fungal stains, cultures, and organism-specific testing are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Sensory loss below a cervical level
symptoms_not_in_common: No significant medical history suggesting immunosuppression
No detected systemic organ involvement
Normal cerebrospinal fluid is less typical of fungal meningomyelitis
Mildly elevated ACE is nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.description: Inflammatory spinal cord injury causing motor, sensory, and autonomic dysfunction, sometimes without abnormal autoimmune serology or brain MRI findings. The apparent granulomatous histology makes an idiopathic cause less likely.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute progression over approximately one month
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent granulomatous inflammation with giant cells is not typical of idiopathic transverse myelitis
A focal mass-like enhancing lesion is less typical than a non-mass-like inflammatory cord lesion
Normal cerebrospinal fluid provides less support for active inflammatory myelitis

data.description: A spinal cord tumor that commonly occurs in adults and may produce progressive myelopathy with an enhancing intramedullary mass. It is an imaging differential, but the supplied tissue appears inflammatory rather than neoplastic.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive weakness in all four extremities
Normal cerebrospinal fluid and absence of systemic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent granulomatous inflammation with giant cells is not typical tumor histology
Mildly elevated serum ACE is not characteristic
Marked progression over one month is faster than the usual course of many spinal ependymomas

data.description: A fungal lung infection that can occur in otherwise healthy adults and produce nodules, consolidation, or cavities. The tissue images suggest inflammatory changes with possible rounded organisms, but fungal stains and microbiologic testing are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever or marked systemic illness
Right lower-lung consolidation with apparent cavitary lesions on CT
Failure to improve after unspecified initial intravenous treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset immediately after a cold is nonspecific rather than characteristic
Yellow-white sticky sputum is not a distinctive feature
Marked nighttime worsening is not characteristic

data.description: A bacterial infection causing destruction of lung tissue and multiple cavities within consolidation, sometimes following a viral respiratory infection.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided chest pain and right-lung wet rales
Right lower-lung consolidation containing multiple apparent cavities
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills, despite the often severe inflammatory illness
No dyspnea
Only small amounts of sputum
Relatively mild overall illness despite extensive localized imaging abnormalities

data.description: An infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that can produce persistent cough, cavitation, and granulomatous inflammation. Sputum molecular testing and cultures are needed to establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of improvement with unspecified initial treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset after a cold is less characteristic
No fever
No hemoptysis, although its absence does not exclude tuberculosis
Predominantly basal right lower-lung involvement is less typical than upper-lobe involvement in classic adult reactivation disease

data.description: A chronic bacterial infection, usually arising after aspiration of organisms from the mouth, that may cause peripheral consolidation, abscesses, and cavitation. Confirmation requires compatible tissue findings or appropriately collected cultures.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral right lower-lung consolidation with apparent cavitation
Poor response to initial unspecified treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: A 20-day illness is shorter than the usual indolent course
Onset following a cold is not characteristic
No fever
No hemoptysis, which can occur in this disease

data.diagnosis: Localized cystic bronchiectasis with superimposed infection
data.description: Permanent dilation of bronchi can appear as clustered ring-shaped or cystic spaces on CT. A respiratory infection may trigger increased cough, sputum, and surrounding consolidation; full CT review is needed to distinguish dilated airways from true cavities.
symptoms_in_common: Productive cough after a respiratory infection
Coarse breath sounds and right-lung wet rales
Clustered air-containing spaces with surrounding right lower-lung consolidation
No fever or dyspnea in a potentially localized exacerbation
symptoms_not_in_common: Only a short reported history rather than longstanding or recurrent cough
Small sputum volume rather than the copious sputum often seen in advanced cystic bronchiectasis
Previously unremarkable medical history without reported recurrent respiratory infections

data.diagnosis: Subcutaneous dirofilariasis caused by Dirofilaria repens
data.description: A mosquito-transmitted filarial infection associated with dogs that causes localized subcutaneous nodules in humans. It occurs in Croatia. The supplied microscopy appears to show a nematode with a thick, externally ridged cuticle, strongly favoring D. repens; definitive identification requires pathology review or molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Normal blood counts and inflammatory markers, which are common in localized infection
Residence in an endemic Mediterranean region
Outdoor exposure and proximity to a canine reservoir
Microscopic appearance compatible with a ridged filarial nematode

data.description: A mosquito-transmitted canine filarial infection that usually produces pulmonary nodules in humans but can rarely involve subcutaneous tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Outdoor exposure in a region with canine Dirofilaria transmission
symptoms_not_in_common: Migrating subcutaneous arm nodules are less typical than pulmonary involvement
The apparent external cuticular ridges favor D. repens rather than the generally smooth-cuticled D. immitis

data.description: A tissue-invasive nematode infection, usually acquired through raw or undercooked infected freshwater animals, that causes migrating subcutaneous swellings.
symptoms_not_in_common: A persistently painless, well-demarcated nodule is less typical than intermittent itchy or painful swelling
Normal blood counts without reported eosinophilia are less typical
No travel outside Croatia makes this geographically less likely
The apparent ridged filarial morphology is not typical of Gnathostoma larvae

data.description: Infection by a Spirometra tapeworm larva, acquired through contaminated water or infected animal tissues, that can produce slowly migrating subcutaneous nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Few systemic symptoms and potentially normal routine laboratory results
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied microscopy appears to show a cylindrical nematode with a cuticle and internal organs, rather than a solid tapeworm larva
The Croatia-only exposure history provides limited epidemiologic support

data.description: A blackfly-transmitted filarial infection caused by Onchocerca volvulus. Adult worms form firm subcutaneous nodules, while microfilariae can cause itching, dermatitis, and eye disease.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of systemic inflammation can occur with localized nodules
symptoms_not_in_common: Migrating nodules are less typical than fixed onchocercomas
No travel outside Croatia makes exposure to O. volvulus highly unlikely
The apparent longitudinal external cuticular ridges favor D. repens rather than O. volvulus

anonymization.anonymizedText: A 64-year-old male patient from **********, Istria presented with firm, migrating nodules in the brachial region without history of serious disease. He had no travel outside Croatia but spent recreational time in forests and islands near his residence and owned a pet dog. Physical examination revealed a painless, well-demarcated subcutaneous nodule in his right upper arm measuring 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.0 cm. Ultrasonographic findings of the nodule appeared normal. Laboratory tests showed total blood counts, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein within normal values. Serologic results for trichinosis, toxocariasis, schistosomiasis, distomatosis and cysticercosis were negative.
anonymization.anonymizedTextHtml: A 64-year-old male patient from  , Istria presented with firm, migrating nodules in the brachial region without history of serious disease. He had no travel outside Croatia but spent recreational time in forests and islands near his residence and owned a pet dog. Physical examination revealed a painless, well-demarcated subcutaneous nodule in his right upper arm measuring 1.5 × 1.5 × 1.0 cm. Ultrasonographic findings of the nodule appeared normal. Laboratory tests showed total blood counts, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein within normal values. Serologic results for trichinosis, toxocariasis, schistosomiasis, distomatosis and cysticercosis were negative.

data.description: A progressive tau-related neurodegenerative disorder characterized by early backward falls, vertical gaze palsy, axial rigidity, and bulbar dysfunction. This is the strongest fit; the supplied MRI appears to show disproportionate midbrain atrophy with relative pontine preservation.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive vertical gaze limitation and inability to look down
Axial and nuchal rigidity with retrocollis
Bradykinesia-like movement abnormalities without resting tremor
Progressive dysarthria and dysphagia with aspiration
Severe progressive loss of postural control
symptoms_not_in_common: Irregular pupils with sluggish light responses are not characteristic
Complete loss of vestibulo-ocular responses is atypical early, although it can occur in advanced disease
Fixed upward and lateral eye deviation is an unusual advanced presentation

data.description: A progressive synuclein-related disorder causing parkinsonism, cerebellar dysfunction, autonomic failure, and sometimes severe swallowing impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent vertical gaze palsy progressing to complete ophthalmoplegia
Early repeated backward falls
Marked retrocollis rather than the more characteristic disproportionate anterocollis
Fixed upward and lateral eye deviation

data.diagnosis: Corticobasal degeneration presenting with a progressive supranuclear palsy syndrome
data.description: A neurodegenerative tauopathy that usually causes asymmetric rigidity, apraxia, and cortical dysfunction, but occasionally presents with a PSP-like pattern of falls and gaze palsy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly symmetric axial involvement rather than asymmetric limb dysfunction
Severe retrocollis and early backward falls
Complete bilateral ophthalmoplegia with absent vestibulo-ocular responses
Irregular, poorly light-reactive pupils

data.description: An inherited intracellular lipid-trafficking disorder that can produce slowly progressive neurologic disease, including vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, ataxia, movement abnormalities, and dysphagia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Late-life onset is uncommon
Prominent axial rigidity and retrocollis with repeated backward falls are more characteristic of PSP
Fixed upward and lateral eye deviation with complete loss of reflex eye movements is not a typical presenting pattern
Irregular pupils with sluggish light responses

data.description: A rare infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei that can mimic neurodegenerative disease, including supranuclear gaze palsy, gait dysfunction, and progressive neurologic impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dominant symmetric axial rigidity and retrocollis
Early stereotyped backward falls
Fixed upward and lateral eye deviation without reported rhythmic ocular or jaw movements
Irregular pupils with sluggish light responses

data.description: An opportunistic fungal infection of the meninges, usually caused by Cryptococcus neoformans in advanced HIV. This is strongly favored by the elevated CSF pressure and microscopy showing yeast-like organisms with prominent capsular halos.
symptoms_in_common: Two-week history of fever and headache
Elevated CSF opening pressure of 29 cm H2O
Lymphocyte-predominant CSF inflammation and elevated protein
Profound HIV-associated immunosuppression with CD4 count of 7 cells/µL
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF cell count of 340 cells/µL is higher than commonly seen in cryptococcal meningitis with profound HIV-associated immunosuppression

data.description: A subacute infection of the meninges caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with increased susceptibility in advanced HIV.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent encapsulated yeasts on microscopy are not explained by tuberculosis
CSF glucose of 46 mg/dL is less reduced than often seen, although interpretation requires a paired blood glucose

data.description: An opportunistic viral infection of the meninges and brain that occurs particularly in patients with HIV and CD4 counts below 50 cells/µL.
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopy showing apparent encapsulated yeasts
Prominent raised CSF opening pressure is less characteristic
A predominantly meningitic presentation with photophobia and neck stiffness is less characteristic than encephalitic or ventriculitic disease

data.description: Treponema pallidum infection involving the nervous system can produce meningitis and should be considered in sexually active patients with HIV.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection and sexual exposure risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopy showing apparent encapsulated yeasts
Markedly elevated CSF opening pressure is less characteristic
Drowsiness is less typical of uncomplicated syphilitic meningitis

data.description: HSV infection can cause meningitis or encephalitis with fever, meningeal irritation, and altered mental status; early CT imaging may be normal.
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopy showing apparent encapsulated yeasts
Substantial elevation of CSF opening pressure is less typical of uncomplicated HSV meningitis
The subacute presentation with profound immunosuppression favors an opportunistic fungal infection

data.diagnosis: Acute left dorsal pontine ischemic infarction causing internuclear ophthalmoplegia
data.description: A small infarction affecting the left medial longitudinal fasciculus can impair left-eye adduction and cause right-eye abducting nystagmus. The focal dorsal pontine signal abnormality on the supplied diffusion-weighted image supports this diagnosis, although confirmation of restricted diffusion requires the ADC map.
symptoms_in_common: Inability to adduct the left eye
Right-eye nystagmus during attempted left-eye adduction
Otherwise normal neurological examination, compatible with a small isolated brainstem infarction
Advanced age and atrial fibrillation without anticoagulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported diplopia only when looking through the right eye, if this means true monocular diplopia, is not typical of internuclear ophthalmoplegia

data.description: Transient ischemia affecting brainstem ocular motor pathways can cause isolated diplopia and internuclear ophthalmoplegia. This diagnosis is less likely if the imaging abnormality represents an acute infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt onset diplopia lasting three hours
symptoms_not_in_common: A focal diffusion-weighted pontine abnormality, if confirmed as acute infarction, favors stroke rather than transient ischemic attack
True monocular diplopia would be atypical

data.diagnosis: Demyelinating brainstem disease causing internuclear ophthalmoplegia
data.description: Demyelination of the medial longitudinal fasciculus, as can occur in multiple sclerosis, produces impaired adduction with contralateral abducting nystagmus.
symptoms_in_common: Right-eye nystagmus on attempted conjugate gaze
symptoms_not_in_common: First presentation at age 83 is highly atypical for multiple sclerosis
Sudden onset favors vascular injury rather than inflammatory demyelination
True monocular diplopia would not be explained by this lesion

data.diagnosis: Ocular myasthenia gravis with pseudo-internuclear ophthalmoplegia
data.description: Autoimmune impairment of neuromuscular transmission can cause variable extraocular muscle weakness and occasionally mimic internuclear ophthalmoplegia.
symptoms_in_common: An ocular motility pattern that can occasionally be mimicked by myasthenia
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset without reported fluctuation or fatigability is atypical
A focal pontine diffusion-weighted imaging abnormality is not explained by ocular myasthenia
True monocular diplopia would be atypical

data.description: Selective dysfunction of the third cranial nerve can weaken the left medial rectus muscle and cause impaired adduction and diplopia, sometimes from microvascular ischemia in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Inability to adduct the left eye
symptoms_not_in_common: Contralateral abducting nystagmus favors internuclear ophthalmoplegia rather than an isolated third-nerve palsy
No reported ptosis, pupillary abnormality, or impairment of elevation and depression
The apparent dorsal pontine lesion does not localize to the oculomotor nerve or its midbrain nucleus
True monocular diplopia would be atypical

data.diagnosis: Neonatal babesiosis, likely congenital Babesia microti infection
data.description: An infection of red blood cells that causes fever and hemolysis. Maternal exposure in coastal Massachusetts and the blood smear showing intraerythrocytic organisms, including a tetrad resembling a Maltese cross, strongly favor this diagnosis. Transmission before birth is possible.
symptoms_in_common: Pallor, listlessness, and tachycardia consistent with anemia
Dark red urine potentially reflecting hemoglobinuria from hemolysis
Respiratory distress and poor peripheral perfusion in severe infection
Intraerythrocytic ring forms and a tetrad on the supplied blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Proteinuria and granular casts are not defining findings but can occur with secondary kidney injury
A holosystolic murmur is not a defining feature, although anemia can cause a flow murmur

data.description: A maternally acquired Plasmodium infection transmitted to an infant, producing fever, anemia, and splenomegaly. It can resemble babesiosis on a blood smear, but the apparent tetrad and reported exposure location favor Babesia.
symptoms_in_common: Dark urine potentially associated with hemolysis
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent Maltese-cross tetrad on the smear is characteristic of Babesia rather than Plasmodium
Granular urinary casts and proteinuria are not typical presenting features of uncomplicated congenital malaria
A holosystolic murmur is not a characteristic finding

data.description: A serious systemic bacterial infection in a young infant that can cause shock, respiratory distress, and kidney injury. This presentation warrants consideration of sepsis even though the smear strongly suggests a parasitic cause.
symptoms_in_common: Cool, mottled extremities indicating poor perfusion
Proteinuria and granular casts potentially reflecting acute kidney injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Intraerythrocytic parasites and an apparent tetrad are not explained by bacterial sepsis
Splenomegaly is not typical of uncomplicated acute bacterial sepsis
Dark red urine suggesting substantial hemolysis is not a usual presenting feature

data.diagnosis: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency with acute hemolysis
data.description: An inherited red-cell enzyme deficiency that can cause abrupt hemolysis during infection or oxidative stress, particularly in male infants. It could explain anemia and dark urine but not the parasitic smear findings.
symptoms_in_common: Dark red urine potentially representing hemoglobinuria
Respiratory distress associated with severe anemia
Possible kidney injury indicated by proteinuria and granular casts
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever requires an additional trigger or infection rather than being explained by the enzyme deficiency itself
Intraerythrocytic ring forms and an apparent tetrad are not features of this disorder
Splenomegaly is less typical of an isolated acute hemolytic episode

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury. It is uncommon at this age, and confirmation would require laboratory evidence of this triad; the supplied smear instead favors an intraerythrocytic infection.
symptoms_in_common: Dark red urine with blood and protein
Respiratory distress in severe systemic illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Intraerythrocytic organisms and an apparent tetrad are not explained by hemolytic uremic syndrome
Splenomegaly is not a typical defining feature
High fever is not a defining feature
A holosystolic murmur is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Recurrent metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma with rectal invasion
data.description: Recurrence of the previously treated high-grade prostate cancer, potentially involving the prostatectomy bed and invading the rectum. The apparent pelvic mass, pulmonary nodules, and liver lesion raise concern for metastatic disease; biopsy is needed to establish the origin.
symptoms_in_common: Severe tenesmus from possible rectal compression or invasion
symptoms_not_in_common: Dominant rectal symptoms are less typical than urinary or skeletal symptoms, although they can occur with locally invasive recurrence

data.description: A primary rectal malignancy that can cause pain and tenesmus and spread to the liver and lungs. The apparent pelvic mass and distant lesions are compatible with this possibility, but imaging alone cannot distinguish it from recurrent prostate cancer.

data.diagnosis: High-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma of the prostate
data.description: An aggressive prostate malignancy that may arise de novo or in association with prior prostate adenocarcinoma. It can produce bulky pelvic disease and visceral metastases, sometimes with relatively little PSA elevation; tissue examination is required.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal pain from possible pelvic invasion
Severe tenesmus from possible rectal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Rectal pain and tenesmus as the dominant presenting symptoms are less typical unless the tumor involves the rectum

data.description: A malignancy of the anal canal that can cause persistent anorectal pain and tenesmus. Advanced disease can spread to the liver and lungs, although the provided images do not establish an anal primary.

data.diagnosis: Aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma with pelvic and extranodal involvement
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy, such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, that can involve pelvic tissues, the gastrointestinal tract, liver, and lungs. This is a less likely alternative to metastatic carcinoma and requires biopsy for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal pain if pelvic or rectal tissue is involved
Tenesmus if a pelvic mass compresses or infiltrates the rectum
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe localized rectal pain and tenesmus are unusual presenting symptoms without direct rectal or pelvic involvement

anonymization.anonymizedText: 70-year-old man with history of Gleason 9 (4+5) adenocarcinoma treated with radical prostatectomy 10 years ago. Presented to primary care with rectal pain persisting for several weeks. Patient had lost 20 lbs over 3-4 weeks and complained of progressive fatigue, poor appetite, severe tenesmus, and rectal pain. Patient had been living independently on ********** but relocated to ********* to be closer to adult children.
