Presented to primary care with rectal pain persisting for several weeks. Patient had lost 20 lbs over 3-4 weeks and complained of progressive fatigue, poor appetite, severe tenesmus, and rectal pain. Patient had been living independently on   but relocated to   to be closer to adult children.

data.diagnosis: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis due to Graves disease
data.description: Hyperthyroidism-associated intracellular potassium shifts cause acute hypokalemic weakness. The thyroid ultrasound appears diffusely enlarged and hypervascular, supporting Graves disease; thyroid-function tests and TSH-receptor antibodies are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe weakness affecting the legs more than the arms
Months of weight loss, loose stools, insomnia, and fine hand tremor
Brisk patellar reflexes, compatible with underlying thyrotoxicosis
Mild muscle-enzyme elevation and liver-test abnormalities
Bilateral conjunctival injection, potentially compatible with thyroid-associated eye disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Venous acidemia is not typical of an isolated intracellular potassium shift
Progressive myalgias over three days are less typical than abrupt painless weakness
Brisk reflexes are less typical during the paralytic episode itself

data.diagnosis: Autoimmune thyroiditis with hashitoxicosis and hypokalemic paralysis
data.description: Autoimmune thyroid inflammation can transiently release excess thyroid hormone and occasionally precipitate hypokalemic paralysis. The supplied histology shows prominent lymphocytic infiltrates and lymphoid follicles, supporting autoimmune thyroid disease, although histology alone cannot establish the cause of thyrotoxicosis.
symptoms_in_common: Weight loss, insomnia, loose stools, and hand tremor consistent with thyrotoxicosis
Lymphocytic infiltration and lymphoid follicles in the supplied thyroid histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked thyroid hypervascularity favors Graves disease over destructive thyroiditis
Conjunctival injection is not a characteristic manifestation of hashitoxicosis
Venous acidemia is not explained by uncomplicated hashitoxicosis

data.description: Some herbal products cause potassium depletion through laxative or diuretic effects, or through licorice-induced mineralocorticoid activity. The supplement could have precipitated the acute episode, although its ingredients and renal potassium handling must be assessed.
symptoms_in_common: Herbal supplement initiation shortly before the acute illness
Myalgias and mildly elevated CK and aldolase
Liver-test abnormalities potentially compatible with supplement toxicity
Loose stools, which could contribute to potassium loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Weight loss, tremor, and insomnia began months before supplement exposure
The thyroid imaging and histology suggest an independent thyroid disorder
Venous acidemia is atypical for licorice-associated hypokalemia, which usually causes metabolic alkalosis

data.diagnosis: Hypokalemic paralysis due to renal tubular acidosis
data.description: Renal tubular acidification defects can produce metabolic acidosis, renal potassium wasting, and severe weakness. Venous acidemia makes this a consideration, but bicarbonate, anion gap, urine pH, and urine potassium are required to establish it.
symptoms_in_common: Acute proximal limb weakness with inability to stand
symptoms_not_in_common: Fine tremor, insomnia, and weight loss suggest thyrotoxicosis rather than renal tubular acidosis
Conjunctival injection is not typical
Diffuse thyroid hypervascularity and autoimmune thyroid histology are not explained by renal tubular acidosis

data.description: An inherited skeletal-muscle ion-channel disorder causes episodic weakness associated with intracellular potassium shifts, often beginning in adolescence or young adulthood. It is an alternative explanation for the acute paralysis but does not account for the thyroid findings.
symptoms_in_common: Acute symmetric weakness, more pronounced in the legs
Mild muscle-enzyme elevation during an attack
symptoms_not_in_common: Months of weight loss, loose stools, insomnia, and tremor
Brisk rather than reduced reflexes during weakness
Venous acidemia
Conjunctival injection and abnormal thyroid imaging and histology
Several days of progressive myalgias rather than a predominantly episodic weakness syndrome

data.description: A benign bony outgrowth along the midline of the hard palate that can become large and lobulated. This is the most likely diagnosis based on the photograph and longstanding, minimally symptomatic history; palpation would help confirm its bony consistency.
symptoms_in_common: Lobulated mass appearing centered on the hard palate
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported presence since birth is less typical, as these growths usually become apparent later

data.description: A benign, slow-growing tumor composed of mature bone that can occasionally arise from the palate.
symptoms_in_common: Mechanical difficulty cleaning around the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported presence since birth is unusual
Broad, multilobulated midline appearance is more characteristic of torus palatinus

data.description: A benign localized overgrowth of normal palatal bone outside the classic midline torus pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Food trapping and difficulty maintaining oral hygiene
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent midline location favors torus palatinus rather than a non-torus exostosis
Reported presence since birth is uncommon

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma of a minor salivary gland
data.description: A benign salivary gland tumor that may present as a painless, slowly enlarging palatal mass, typically away from the midline.
symptoms_in_common: Few symptoms despite a prominent lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported presence since birth strongly argues against an acquired salivary gland tumor
Midline, multilobulated appearance is atypical
A lifelong minimally symptomatic course is unusual

data.description: A benign reactive overgrowth of fibrous tissue caused by chronic irritation, generally presenting as a smooth, mucosa-colored oral nodule.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty cleaning around a protruding lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Reported presence since birth is inconsistent with a typical acquired reactive lesion
Large, multilobulated midline palatal mass is atypical
The apparent size is greater than that of most irritation fibromas

data.diagnosis: Lumbar disc herniation with nerve-root compression, likely at L4–L5
data.description: Displaced intervertebral disc material can compress lumbar nerve roots, causing sciatica and weakness. The supplied sagittal MRI appears to show a prominent posterior disc extrusion at approximately L4–L5, making this the leading possibility; full MRI review is needed to confirm its location and extent.
symptoms_in_common: Lower back pain radiating into the left leg
Left-leg weakness with power reduced to 3/5
Acute symptoms superimposed on chronic back pain

data.description: Degenerative changes, sometimes compounded by a herniated disc, narrow the spinal canal or nerve-root passages. The apparent lower-lumbar canal narrowing on the image could contribute to nerve compression.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating into the left leg
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt two-day onset of marked weakness is less typical of uncomplicated, gradually progressive degenerative stenosis

data.diagnosis: Lumbar facet synovial cyst with nerve-root compression
data.description: A fluid-containing cyst arising from a degenerative facet joint can occupy the spinal canal and compress a nerve root. It is an alternative explanation for a focal compressive lesion, although the supplied image appears more suggestive of disc material.
symptoms_not_in_common: A two-day deterioration is less typical unless the cyst enlarges rapidly or develops hemorrhage

data.description: Bleeding into the spinal epidural space can rapidly compress nerve roots, producing acute pain and neurological deficits. The visible lesion appears disc-related rather than clearly hemorrhagic, so this is a lower-probability alternative. New weakness of 3/5 warrants urgent in-person spinal assessment regardless of the cause.
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding chronic back pain is not explained by an acute epidural hematoma

data.description: A usually benign nerve-sheath tumor can cause back pain, radicular pain, and weakness through nerve-root compression. It is a less likely structural alternative because the supplied image appears to show a disc-associated lesion; additional MRI sequences would be needed to characterize a suspected tumor.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute onset over two days is atypical for a usually slow-growing tumor

diagnoses.name: Intervertebral disc prolapse
diagnoses.title: Intervertebral disc degeneration without prolapsed disc with determinant

data.diagnosis: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome with cerebral and cardiac involvement
data.description: A disorder characterized by marked unexplained eosinophilia and eosinophil-mediated organ injury. This is the leading consideration, although exclusion of secondary and clonal causes is required. Cerebral injury may result from thrombosis, endothelial damage, or cardiac emboli.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia of 5,500/μL without an identified secondary cause
Disorientation, attention deficit, and immediate memory disturbance
Dysarthria, bilateral arm weakness, hyperreflexia, and right hemiparetic gait
MRI showing multiple bilateral lesions suggestive of acute ischemic infarcts
Elevated cardiac enzymes and left ventricular inferior wall hypokinesia
Pulmonary nodules visible on chest CT, potentially reflecting pulmonary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal susceptibility signal suggesting a small hemorrhagic lesion is less typical than ischemic cerebral involvement

data.diagnosis: Eosinophilic myocarditis or endomyocardial disease with cardioembolic cerebral infarctions
data.description: Eosinophilic inflammation can injure the myocardium and endocardium, sometimes producing intracardiac thrombi that embolize to multiple cerebral territories. This may be a cardiac manifestation of hypereosinophilic syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral cerebral lesions suggestive of infarctions
Confusion, dysarthria, and focal motor deficits
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary nodules are not directly explained by isolated eosinophilic myocarditis
A focal hemorrhagic-appearing brain lesion is less typical, although hemorrhagic transformation of an embolic infarct is possible

data.description: A systemic eosinophilic small- to medium-vessel vasculitis that commonly involves the respiratory tract, peripheral nerves, and heart; cerebral ischemia can occur but is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac enzyme elevation and ventricular wall-motion abnormality
Neurologic deficits and multifocal ischemic-appearing brain lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of asthma or sinusitis, which strongly weakens this diagnosis
Central cognitive impairment and upper motor neuron findings are less typical than peripheral neuropathy
No identifiable vasculitis on the reported initial evaluation

data.diagnosis: Clonal hypereosinophilia due to a myeloid neoplasm
data.description: A hematologic neoplasm, such as chronic eosinophilic leukemia or a tyrosine kinase fusion-associated myeloid disorder, can cause pronounced eosinophilia with cardiac injury and thrombotic neurologic complications. Molecular and bone marrow testing are needed to distinguish it from idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Cognitive dysfunction, dysarthria, and motor deficits
symptoms_not_in_common: The initial evaluation found no identifiable neoplasm
Pulmonary nodules and a focal hemorrhagic-appearing cerebral lesion are nonspecific rather than characteristic features

data.diagnosis: Helminth-associated secondary hypereosinophilia with neurologic and cardiac involvement
data.description: Tissue-invasive helminth infections can cause marked eosinophilia and pulmonary lesions; selected infections can also affect the brain or heart. This is less likely given the reported negative parasitic evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Cognitive changes and focal neurologic deficits
symptoms_not_in_common: No parasitic infection identified on the reported evaluation
Multiple bilateral ischemic-appearing lesions are less typical than inflammatory, cystic, or granulomatous brain lesions
The combination of myocardial injury and multifocal cerebral ischemia more strongly suggests hypereosinophilic organ damage

data.description: A systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease, commonly involving the lungs and thoracic lymph nodes. This is the leading possibility given the imaging, elevated ACE level, and apparent non-necrotizing granulomas.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT
Intense FDG uptake in thoracic lymph nodes
Biopsy images appear to show well-formed non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas
Mild anemia and leukopenia, which can occur in systemic sarcoidosis

data.description: Non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation associated with cancer or its treatment that can resemble systemic sarcoidosis and mimic metastases on PET imaging.
symptoms_in_common: History of breast cancer and prior cancer treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ACE level and pulmonary opacities may favor systemic sarcoidosis rather than a localized sarcoid-like reaction
Mild anemia and leukopenia are not characteristic of an isolated sarcoid-like reaction

data.diagnosis: Recurrent breast cancer with thoracic metastases
data.description: Breast cancer recurrence involving thoracic lymph nodes or lungs; FDG uptake alone cannot distinguish metastatic cancer from granulomatous inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: History of stage IIIA, node-positive breast cancer
Abnormal FDG uptake in thoracic lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively symmetric bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is more suggestive of sarcoidosis
Apparent non-necrotizing granulomas rather than malignant cells in the supplied biopsy images
Elevated ACE level is not characteristic of breast cancer recurrence

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy that can cause intensely FDG-avid lymphadenopathy and cytopenias; granulomatous reactions occasionally accompany lymphoma.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy images appear dominated by non-necrotizing granulomas rather than a malignant lymphoid population
Elevated ACE level is more supportive of granulomatous inflammation
Symmetric hilar involvement with pulmonary nodular opacities favors sarcoidosis

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can produce granulomatous thoracic lymphadenopathy and FDG-avid pulmonary lesions. Negative immune-based tests reduce suspicion but do not completely exclude active infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative purified protein derivative skin test
Reported negative tuberculosis antigen-specific interferon-gamma testing
Apparent non-necrotizing rather than caseating granulomas
Relatively symmetric bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
Elevated ACE level is more characteristic of sarcoidosis

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with osteosclerotic bone involvement
data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal immunoglobulin and causing organ damage. This is the leading diagnosis; the apparent diffuse skeletal sclerosis suggests an uncommon osteosclerotic presentation rather than typical lytic myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated free kappa light chains and kappa/lambda ratio of 280
Apparent marrow cellular infiltration on the biopsy images
Apparent diffuse osteosclerosis on the pelvic radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse osteosclerosis is unusual in conventional multiple myeloma, which more commonly produces lytic lesions

data.description: A plasma-cell-associated syndrome characterized by polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal protein, and skin changes, often with osteosclerotic bone lesions. The available findings do not establish its required diagnostic criteria.
symptoms_not_in_common: Kappa restriction rather than the more typical lambda restriction
Hypercalcemia
Markedly elevated circulating free light chains
Anemia rather than the thrombocytosis or polycythemia sometimes seen
No reported polyneuropathy
No organomegaly on examination
No reported endocrinopathy or characteristic skin changes

data.diagnosis: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgG paraprotein
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation that usually produces IgM but can rarely produce IgG. Bone marrow examination and immunophenotyping distinguish it from myeloma.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia
Apparent diffuse skeletal sclerosis
Very high free kappa light-chain concentration and ratio
No lymphadenopathy or organomegaly
IgG rather than the usual IgM paraprotein

data.diagnosis: Systemic AL amyloidosis associated with a plasma-cell clone
data.description: A disorder in which monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains form amyloid deposits in organs, commonly affecting the kidneys, heart, and peripheral nerves. Tissue staining is required for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated free kappa light chains
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia
Apparent osteosclerotic bone changes
Normal 24-hour urine protein, which argues against typical renal amyloid involvement
No reported cardiac manifestations, neuropathy, or other characteristic organ involvement

data.diagnosis: Osteoblastic skeletal metastases from an occult carcinoma
data.description: Metastatic solid tumors, including breast carcinoma, can cause diffuse skeletal sclerosis and marrow infiltration. This is a less likely alternative because it does not adequately explain the pronounced monoclonal plasma-cell laboratory findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Large IgG kappa paraprotein
Free kappa light-chain concentration of 1,400 mg/L and ratio of 280
Urinary kappa Bence-Jones protein
Normal alkaline phosphatase despite apparent extensive skeletal sclerosis

data.diagnosis: Intracranial germinoma with suprasellar and pineal involvement
data.description: A germ-cell tumor occurring predominantly in adolescents and young adults. Suprasellar involvement can cause diabetes insipidus and pituitary hormone deficiencies. The apparent enhancing suprasellar and pineal-region lesions make this a leading possibility, but imaging alone is not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Long-standing polydipsia and polyuria, suggesting possible central diabetes insipidus
Minimal facial hair, small testicles, and reduced morning erections, suggesting hypogonadism
Bilateral breast enlargement associated with disturbed gonadal hormone balance
Apparent enhancing lesions involving the suprasellar and pineal regions
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood seizures that resolved years before the current presentation are not a typical presenting pattern
Chronic pilonidal cyst and posterior anal fissure are not characteristic
Recent improvement in polyuria and polydipsia does not exclude the disease but is not a typical untreated course

data.diagnosis: Langerhans cell histiocytosis involving the hypothalamic-pituitary axis
data.description: A disorder of abnormal inflammatory myeloid cells that can infiltrate the pituitary stalk and hypothalamus, producing central diabetes insipidus and anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies.
symptoms_in_common: Small testicles, minimal facial hair, and reduced morning erections
Gynecomastia potentially secondary to pituitary-related hypogonadism
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pineal-region and multifocal intracranial enhancement is less typical than pituitary-stalk involvement
Remote childhood seizures are not a characteristic isolated manifestation
A pilonidal cyst and anal fissure are not typical manifestations

data.description: A granulomatous inflammatory disease that can affect the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, meninges, and other brain structures, causing endocrine and neurological dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Polydipsia and polyuria from possible central diabetes insipidus
Signs of hypogonadism, including small testicles and sparse facial hair
Seizures can occur with central nervous system involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: A discrete pineal-plus-suprasellar distribution is less characteristic than for intracranial germinoma
Childhood seizures followed by a long seizure-free interval are not a typical unified presentation
Chronic pilonidal cyst and posterior anal fissure are not characteristic

data.description: A generally nonmalignant epithelial tumor near the pituitary and hypothalamus that can compress the optic pathways and impair pituitary hormone production.
symptoms_in_common: Minimal facial hair, small testicles, and reduced morning erections
Polydipsia and polyuria from hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction
Constipation and low blood pressure could accompany additional pituitary hormone deficiencies
symptoms_not_in_common: Separate pineal-region and multifocal enhancing lesions are not typical
Remote childhood seizures are not a usual presenting feature
Chronic pilonidal cyst and anal fissure are unrelated findings

data.description: A prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma that can suppress gonadal function and, when large, compress the optic chiasm. Prolactin testing and dedicated pituitary assessment would be needed to evaluate this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced facial hair growth and small testicles
Absence of nipple discharge does not exclude a prolactinoma in a male patient
symptoms_not_in_common: Long-standing polyuria and polydipsia are unusual because diabetes insipidus is uncommon with pituitary adenomas
Apparent separate pineal-region and multifocal intracranial lesions are not explained by a typical macroprolactinoma
Remote childhood seizures are not characteristic
Pilonidal cyst and posterior anal fissure are not characteristic

data.description: Infection of the aortic valve by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, causing vegetations, valve damage, and systemic septic emboli. The echocardiographic images appear to show an aortic valve vegetation, making this the leading diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Five days of swinging fever and rigors
Early diastolic decrescendo murmur consistent with aortic regurgitation
Digital infarct of the left third toe
Left arm weakness and reduced consciousness potentially caused by cerebral septic embolism
History of injecting drug use and recent deep infection

data.diagnosis: Aortic perivalvular abscess complicating infective endocarditis
data.description: Extension of valve infection into the surrounding aortic root tissue. This can damage the cardiac conduction system. The ECG strips appear to show prolonged atrioventricular conduction, and the echocardiographic abnormality adjacent to the valve raises concern for an abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent PR interval prolongation on the ECG strips
symptoms_not_in_common: Left arm weakness and reduced consciousness are not direct manifestations of a localized aortic root abscess
Splinter hemorrhages and digital infarction suggest associated endocarditis and embolization rather than the abscess alone

data.diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke from cerebral septic embolism
data.description: Occlusion of a cerebral artery by infected material shed from a cardiac vegetation. This is a likely neurological complication of the suspected left-sided endocarditis, although brain imaging is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Left arm weakness in an upper motor neuron pattern
MRSA bacteremia with evidence of infective endocarditis
symptoms_not_in_common: Swinging fever and rigors are not typical of an uncomplicated ischemic stroke
Aortic regurgitation murmur and splinter hemorrhages reflect the underlying cardiac infection
Normocytic anemia is not explained by an acute stroke alone

data.description: A localized intracerebral infection that can develop through bloodstream spread of MRSA or septic embolization from endocarditis. It can cause headache, altered consciousness, and focal neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: MRSA bacteremia and recent deep-seated infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Early diastolic cardiac murmur is not explained by a brain abscess
Splinter hemorrhages and toe infarction suggest an additional systemic embolic source
Apparent atrioventricular conduction delay is not typical of a brain abscess

data.diagnosis: Persistent or recurrent MRSA discitis with psoas abscess
data.description: Ongoing spinal and adjacent psoas infection could sustain MRSA bacteremia and seed the heart or other organs. It is an important potential infectious source given the recent admission, but does not adequately explain the whole presentation alone.
symptoms_in_common: Recent hospital admission for discitis and psoas abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Early diastolic murmur suggests cardiac valve disease rather than isolated spinal infection
Splinter hemorrhages and digital infarction suggest infective endocarditis
Focal upper motor neuron weakness of the left arm is not typical of an isolated psoas abscess
Headache and reduced consciousness suggest an additional intracranial complication
Aortic valve and possible perivalvular echocardiographic abnormalities are not explained by isolated discitis

data.diagnosis: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
data.description: Autosomal recessive acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency causes lysosomal glycogen accumulation, particularly in cardiac and skeletal muscle. The markedly deficient GAA activity and two GAA variants in trans strongly establish this diagnosis. CRIM status requires protein testing and cannot be inferred solely from absence of p.D645E.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly reduced GAA activity on newborn screening and confirmatory lymphocyte testing
Compound heterozygous GAA variants c.2024_2026del and c.2040+1G>T in trans
Elevated CK and ALT, consistent with muscle involvement
Markedly elevated pro-BNP, suggesting cardiac stress
Apparently enlarged cardiac silhouette on the chest radiograph, compatible with cardiac involvement
Slightly decreased facial folds, potentially reflecting subtle facial muscle involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal muscle power and reflexes rather than established hypotonia or weakness
Absence of poor feeding, reduced activity, or weak crying
Absence of macroglossia; however, these absent features do not exclude disease detected very early

data.description: An autosomal recessive glycogen debranching enzyme deficiency that can affect liver, skeletal muscle, and heart. It is a differential for metabolic cardiomyopathy but does not explain the confirmed GAA deficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CK, compatible with muscle involvement
Elevated pro-BNP and apparent cardiac enlargement, potentially consistent with cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Profoundly deficient GAA activity is not characteristic
Two GAA variants in trans point to Pompe disease rather than a debranching enzyme defect
Cardiac involvement evident at 7 days is unusually early for this disorder

data.description: An X-linked LAMP2-related lysosomal disorder associated with cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy. Neonatal presentation in a female is very unusual, and the biochemical and genetic findings favor Pompe disease instead.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CK and ALT, which can accompany muscle involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation in a 7-day-old female is atypical
Profound GAA enzyme deficiency is not a feature of Danon disease
Compound heterozygous GAA variants do not support a LAMP2-related disorder

data.description: A mitochondrial energy-production disorder can cause neonatal cardiomyopathy with skeletal muscle and liver abnormalities. This is a broad alternative for the cardiac and enzyme findings, but it does not account for the specific GAA results.
symptoms_in_common: Very early evidence of cardiac stress
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly deficient GAA activity and two GAA variants in trans are not explained by primary mitochondrial disease
Normal activity, feeding, muscle power, and reflexes are less typical of a severe neonatal multisystem mitochondrial presentation

data.diagnosis: Transient neonatal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy associated with maternal diabetes
data.description: Fetal hyperinsulinemia associated with maternal diabetes can produce macrosomia and transient neonatal myocardial hypertrophy. Maternal diabetes is not documented here, and this alternative cannot explain the confirmed metabolic findings.
symptoms_in_common: High birth weight of 4,380 g at full term
Elevated pro-BNP, compatible with cardiac stress
Apparent cardiac enlargement on chest radiography
Preserved feeding, activity, muscle power, and reflexes can occur in mildly symptomatic neonatal cardiomyopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Profoundly deficient GAA activity is not characteristic
Compound heterozygous GAA variants are not explained by maternal diabetes
Elevated CK and subtle facial changes are not typical defining features

data.diagnosis: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia with extramedullary involvement
data.description: A malignancy of immature B lymphocytes that can infiltrate bone marrow, bone, lymph nodes, and other tissues. The blast-like cells and CD19/CD10-positive population shown favor this diagnosis; CD33 can be aberrantly expressed.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged intermittent migratory bone and joint pain
Rib, knee, hip, and back pain with limping
Periorbital and periumbilical discoloration, potentially reflecting bleeding
Apparent multifocal soft-tissue masses on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral periorbital swelling and discoloration are an unusual initial presentation
Left flank pain radiating down the leg is not a characteristic presenting symptom

data.description: A childhood tumor of sympathetic nervous tissue, commonly arising in the adrenal gland or abdominal sympathetic chain. Bone and orbital metastases can cause pain, limping, and periorbital bruising, although the displayed B-cell immunophenotype argues against it.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory bone pain involving ribs and lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Periumbilical discoloration is not a typical presenting feature
A year of intermittent joint-centered pain is less characteristic than progressive pain from metastatic disease

data.description: A malignancy of immature B cells presenting predominantly as tissue masses rather than extensive marrow disease. It shares the CD19/CD10-positive phenotype of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia; marrow assessment is needed to distinguish them.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent multifocal soft-tissue masses on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral periorbital discoloration is uncommon
Periumbilical discoloration is uncommon
A prolonged migratory bone and joint pain syndrome is less typical than a localized or enlarging mass

data.diagnosis: Acute myeloid leukemia with myeloid sarcoma
data.description: A malignancy of myeloid precursor cells that may produce extramedullary masses, including orbital lesions. CD33 expression raises consideration, but the strong B-cell marker pattern shown favors a B-lineage malignancy unless additional testing establishes myeloid differentiation.
symptoms_not_in_common: A year-long intermittent migratory pain course is less typical of acute myeloid leukemia
Periumbilical discoloration is not a characteristic presentation
Flank pain radiating down the leg is not characteristic

data.description: An aggressive bone or soft-tissue sarcoma that can cause pain, fever, and distant skeletal lesions. It is less common at age six, and the displayed lymphoid immunophenotype argues strongly against it.
symptoms_in_common: Rib, knee, hip, and back pain
Limping and pain with hip movement
Possible bone and soft-tissue involvement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent migratory pain over a year rather than persistent focal pain
Bilateral periorbital swelling and discoloration
Periumbilical discoloration
Abdominal distention without a clearly established primary abdominal tumor

data.description: Bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue. The erythema and apparent subcutaneous edema on ultrasound support this possibility, although the images alone are not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Fever may be absent in localized infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical of uncomplicated cellulitis
Possible echogenic foci with shadowing on ultrasound would require evaluation for gas, which is not typical of uncomplicated cellulitis

data.description: A rapidly progressive infection involving subcutaneous tissue and fascia that requires emergency surgical assessment when suspected. Possible gas-related ultrasound artifacts raise concern but cannot establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute painful gluteal swelling over 12 hours
Possible echogenic foci with shadowing on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal blood pressure and heart rate are less typical of advanced infection
Absence of fever or systemic illness is less typical of advanced infection, although early disease can lack these findings

data.description: A localized collection of pus in the gluteal soft tissues, often accompanied by surrounding skin inflammation. A definite fluid collection is not clearly demonstrated in the supplied ultrasound images.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever can occur with a localized abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse swelling without a clearly demonstrated focal fluid collection is less characteristic of a mature abscess
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical of an uncomplicated localized abscess

data.description: A bacterial infection of the superficial dermis and lymphatics that typically produces a tender, bright-red plaque with a raised, sharply defined border.
symptoms_not_in_common: The photographed redness is not clearly sharply demarcated or raised
Apparent deeper soft-tissue abnormalities are less typical of a superficial infection
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical

data.description: Bacterial infection of the gluteal muscle, sometimes progressing to an intramuscular abscess. Deeper imaging would be needed because the supplied images do not establish muscle involvement.
symptoms_in_common: No preceding trauma, which does not exclude muscle infection
symptoms_not_in_common: A 12-hour history is shorter than the usual evolution of primary pyomyositis
Absence of fever is less typical of established pyomyositis
Predominantly superficial abnormalities without demonstrated muscle involvement provide limited support
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical of localized pyomyositis

data.diagnosis: Chronic graft-versus-host disease with cutaneous and musculoskeletal involvement
data.description: A delayed immune complication of allogeneic stem cell transplantation that can cause inflammatory or sclerotic skin changes, fascial restriction, myositis, and liver abnormalities. This is a leading consideration given the transplant history and positive prayer sign.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse erythematous rash involving the face, trunk, and extremities
Rash appearing after sun exposure, which can trigger cutaneous disease
Restricted wrist extension with a positive prayer sign, suggesting skin or fascial tightening
Positive antinuclear antibodies, which can occur with post-transplant immune dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent fever is nonspecific and should also prompt evaluation for infection

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory muscle disease associated with characteristic photosensitive skin eruptions. The facial and upper-chest erythema and reddish-purple dorsal hand lesions in the photographs raise this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Reddish-purple lesions on the dorsal hands
Mild AST and ALT elevation, which can accompany muscle inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: A positive prayer sign from restricted wrist extension is not a typical early feature of uncomplicated dermatomyositis
Elevated alkaline phosphatase is not explained well by isolated muscle inflammation

data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause photosensitive skin eruptions, fever, and musculoskeletal inflammation. A positive ANA supports consideration but does not establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral cheek erythema resembling a malar eruption
Rash involving the trunk and extremities
Positive ANA at a titer of 1:320 with a speckled pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Restricted wrist extension with a positive prayer sign suggests sclerosis or fasciitis rather than typical lupus musculoskeletal disease
Reddish-purple dorsal hand lesions are more suggestive of dermatomyositis than classic lupus skin disease

data.description: An autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by skin fibrosis and possible internal-organ involvement. Skin tightening can limit hand and wrist movement.
symptoms_in_common: Restricted wrist extension with a positive prayer sign
Muscle pain and weakness, particularly if inflammatory myopathy overlaps
symptoms_not_in_common: An acute widespread erythematous rash after sun exposure is not a typical presentation
Intermittent fever is not characteristic of uncomplicated systemic sclerosis
The facial and upper-chest erythema and dorsal hand eruption are more suggestive of an inflammatory photosensitive disorder

data.description: An inflammatory fibrosing disorder of the fascia that can cause limb pain, skin induration, and joint contractures. A similar fascial process can occur in chronic graft-versus-host disease.
symptoms_in_common: Restricted wrist extension with a positive prayer sign, compatible with fascial tightening
Intermittent fever can accompany the inflammatory phase
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent facial and dorsal hand involvement is atypical because these areas are usually spared
A photosensitive rash involving the face and upper chest is not characteristic
A high-titer positive ANA is not a characteristic diagnostic finding
Mild liver enzyme abnormalities are not a usual feature

data.description: An eruption of crateriform, keratin-producing squamous tumors that can resemble squamous cell carcinoma. This is the leading diagnosis because the image timeline reports 15 histologically diagnosed keratoacanthomas.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple papules and nodules on sun-exposed forearms and hands
Central keratin plugs and crusted crateriform lesions
New lesions following excisions, consistent with an isomorphic response
Histology showing crateriform squamous proliferation with prominent keratinization
Reported histologic diagnosis of keratoacanthoma in 15 excised lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: A prolonged, continuously progressive eruption is less typical of solitary keratoacanthomas, which often involute
Sleep-disrupting pruritus is less typical of solitary lesions, although it can occur in eruptive disease

data.description: A malignant keratinocyte tumor that may have a crateriform appearance closely resembling keratoacanthoma. Adequate histologic assessment is needed to distinguish these overlapping lesions.
symptoms_in_common: History of kidney transplantation, a risk context for cutaneous squamous malignancy
Squamous proliferation and keratinization in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe widespread pruritus is not a usual dominant presentation
Numerous similar lesions developing through an isomorphic response are less typical
The image timeline reports keratoacanthomas rather than confirmed invasive squamous cell carcinomas

data.description: A pruritic skin disorder associated with advanced kidney disease and dialysis, characterized by elimination of dermal material through the epidermis, producing centrally plugged papules.
symptoms_in_common: Intensely pruritic papules on the extremities
Lesions arising at sites of trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: Preferential localization to sun-exposed skin is not characteristic
The supplied histology shows keratinizing squamous tumors rather than demonstrated transepidermal elimination of dermal material
Reported histologic confirmation of multiple keratoacanthomas

data.description: A chronic itch-scratch disorder producing firm, excoriated papules and nodules, sometimes associated with chronic kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chronic pruritus with sleep disturbance
Papules and nodules on accessible extensor extremities
Chronic kidney disease as a potential contributor to itching
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinct crateriform lesions containing central keratin plugs
Restriction predominantly to sun-exposed areas
Histologically documented keratoacanthomas rather than reactive epidermal thickening

data.description: A benign human papillomavirus-associated epidermal proliferation producing keratotic papules. Warts may coexist with other lesions; the image timeline reports three histologically confirmed common warts.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple keratotic papules on the hands and forearms
Reported histologic diagnosis of verruca vulgaris in three excised lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe sleep-disrupting pruritus
Large crateriform nodules with central keratin plugs
Predominant distribution on sun-exposed skin
Most excised lesions were reported as keratoacanthomas, so warts do not explain the entire eruption

data.description: Inflammation of the spinal cord associated with direct viral infection or an infection-triggered immune response. This is the leading possibility given Zika PCR positivity in serum, urine, and CSF, together with a spinal cord syndrome and apparent intramedullary T2 signal abnormalities on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Headache and conjunctival hyperaemia preceding neurological deterioration
Acute back pain and limb pain
Loss of temperature sensation below defined thoracic levels
Zika virus detected in serum, urine, and CSF
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly asymmetric weakness is less typical than bilateral weakness, although partial transverse myelitis can be asymmetric
Normal routine CSF findings are less typical of inflammatory myelitis but do not exclude it

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder, often associated with aquaporin-4 antibodies, that can cause severe and longitudinally extensive spinal cord inflammation. Antibody testing and further imaging would be needed to evaluate this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive weakness with upper motor neuron signs
Apparent spinal cord signal abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctival hyperaemia and headache preceding the neurological syndrome are not characteristic
High concentrations of Zika virus in CSF favor a viral-associated process rather than primary autoimmune disease
Marked unilateral predominance is less typical of extensive myelitis

data.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disorder that can cause acute myelitis in children and adolescents, sometimes following infection. Serum MOG-IgG testing is needed to support the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Neurological deterioration following an infectious prodrome
Spinal cord signal abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: High Zika viral concentrations in CSF are not a characteristic finding
Conjunctival hyperaemia is not a typical manifestation of demyelinating disease
Strongly asymmetric hemiparesis is less typical than bilateral deficits in extensive myelitis

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis presenting with acute partial myelitis
data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can initially present with an asymmetric spinal cord syndrome. Diagnosis requires additional evidence, including dissemination in space and time or qualifying supportive findings.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intramedullary demyelinating abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctival hyperaemia is not characteristic
High concentrations of Zika virus in serum, urine, and CSF favor an infectious explanation
An apparently extensive spinal cord process is less typical than the short-segment lesions commonly seen in multiple sclerosis

data.description: An acute immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy associated with Zika infection that causes progressive weakness, sensory symptoms, and sometimes autonomic dysfunction. It is substantially less likely here because the findings primarily localize to the spinal cord.
symptoms_in_common: Urinary retention, which can occur with autonomic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral Hoffman signs indicate central rather than peripheral nervous system involvement
Defined thoracic temperature sensory levels are not typical
Markedly asymmetric hemiparesis is atypical
Intramedullary spinal cord signal abnormalities are not explained by a peripheral neuropathy
Normal electromyography reduces support, although early testing can be normal

data.diagnosis: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), with an atypical TdT-negative phenotype
data.description: An aggressive malignancy of immature T cells involving blood and bone marrow. This is the leading consideration given the blast burden and T-lineage markers. The supplied cytogenetic images indicate TCRA/D-associated rearrangements, including an Xq22.3 region near IRS4, supporting a T-cell neoplasm but not independently establishing its subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Acute presentation in a young adult male
Blasts expressing CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 without B-cell or myeloid markers
Images showing extensive infiltration by blast-like cells
Headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting, which could reflect a neurologic complication requiring urgent assessment
symptoms_not_in_common: TdT negativity is unusual for T-ALL
CD34 negativity provides less support for an immature phenotype, although it does not exclude T-ALL
Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly is less characteristic but does not exclude the disease

data.description: An aggressive mature T-cell leukemia usually occurring in older adults, often with marked lymphocytosis and organ enlargement. Mature T-cell marker expression and absence of TdT make it a differential consideration; confirmation requires characteristic morphology and supporting genetic findings.
symptoms_in_common: CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 expression
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 27 is substantially younger than the usual presentation
Absence of hepatosplenomegaly
Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy
Reported 95% blasts and blast-like morphology rather than typical prolymphocytes
The depicted IRS4-region rearrangement is not a defining T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia abnormality

data.description: An aggressive mature T-cell malignancy associated with HTLV-1 infection. It can produce leukocytosis, marrow involvement, and very high LDH; HTLV-1 testing is necessary to support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis with extensive circulating malignant T cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong CD7 expression is less typical because CD7 is commonly lost
Young age is less typical
Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Blast-like cells rather than characteristic multilobulated 'flower' cells

data.diagnosis: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, with leukemic involvement
data.description: A heterogeneous mature T-cell lymphoma that can rarely involve blood extensively. Tissue evaluation and exclusion of other defined T-cell neoplasms are required.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive marrow infiltration in the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy
Age 27 is younger than the usual presentation
A blood population reported as 95% blasts is unusual
Retention of all reported pan-T-cell markers is less typical than an aberrant pattern with antigen loss

data.diagnosis: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma with leukemic involvement
data.description: A rare aggressive mature T-cell lymphoma affecting predominantly young men, usually involving the spleen, liver, and bone marrow with little lymphadenopathy. Extensive circulating disease is uncommon.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of hepatosplenomegaly strongly argues against the usual presentation
CD5 positivity is atypical
Leukocytosis with 95% circulating blasts is unusual
Diffuse blast-like marrow infiltration rather than the characteristic sinusoidal pattern

data.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation, often triggered by infection or malignancy. This is the leading syndromic diagnosis, although formal diagnostic criteria and the underlying trigger require confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Pancytopenia affecting all three blood cell lines
Rapid deterioration with hypotension and acute respiratory failure
Marrow images appear to show hemophagocytosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent granulomatous inflammation in the tissue images is not explained by HLH alone and suggests an underlying trigger

data.description: Tuberculosis involving multiple organs can trigger HLH and cause severe pulmonary disease. The apparent granulomatous tissue changes support consideration of tuberculosis, but microbiologic or molecular confirmation is necessary.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive bilateral pulmonary opacities on chest CT
Apparent granulomatous inflammation in the tissue images
Pancytopenia, potentially from marrow involvement or secondary HLH
Extreme hyperferritinemia and apparent hemophagocytosis compatible with secondary HLH
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme hyperferritinemia is unusual for tuberculosis without associated HLH
Profound pancytopenia and reduced fibrinogen are not typical of isolated pulmonary tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Disseminated fungal infection with secondary HLH
data.description: Systemic fungal infections, particularly histoplasmosis or talaromycosis, can involve the lungs and bone marrow and provoke HLH. Organism identification and exposure assessment are needed to distinguish these infections.
symptoms_in_common: Extreme hyperferritinemia and apparent hemophagocytosis if complicated by HLH
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme hyperferritinemia and reduced fibrinogen are not typical without secondary HLH
Severe disseminated opportunistic fungal disease is less typical in someone without known immunodeficiency

data.description: An occult lymphoma, particularly a T-cell or NK-cell lymphoma, can trigger severe HLH before the malignancy is recognized. Tissue examination and hematologic testing are required for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid progression to shock and respiratory failure
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent granulomatous tissue inflammation favors an infectious trigger rather than directly demonstrating lymphoma
Extensive bilateral pulmonary consolidation is not a typical primary presentation of most lymphomas

data.diagnosis: Severe bacterial pneumonia with sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and acute respiratory distress syndrome
data.description: Severe pulmonary bacterial infection can cause shock, diffuse lung injury, and consumptive coagulopathy. It could coexist with HLH but is less satisfactory as the sole explanation for this presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Tachypnea, hypoxemia, and bilateral pulmonary rales
Thrombocytopenia and reduced fibrinogen compatible with consumptive coagulopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Ferritin of 375,554 ng/mL is exceptionally unusual for uncomplicated bacterial sepsis
Profound pancytopenia and apparent hemophagocytosis suggest an additional hyperinflammatory syndrome
Apparent granulomatous tissue inflammation is not typical of ordinary bacterial pneumonia
A month of persistent fever is less typical of acute bacterial pneumonia

data.diagnosis: Varicella-zoster virus meningoencephalitis with cerebral vasculopathy
data.description: Varicella-zoster virus can cause brain inflammation and infection of cerebral arteries, producing arterial narrowing and multifocal ischemic strokes, sometimes without a characteristic shingles rash.
symptoms_in_common: High fever and profound impairment of consciousness
Left hemiplegia, right arm paresis, and left Babinski sign
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein with preserved glucose
Imaging suggesting multifocal ischemic lesions and cerebral arterial narrowing
Transient rash, although its appearance is not specified
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked neutrophil predominance in CSF is less typical than lymphocytic predominance
A transient rash is less characteristic than a painful vesicular eruption

data.description: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection that can rarely cause encephalitis, vascular injury, and ischemic neurological complications.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to tropical Pacific destinations where dengue exposure is possible
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein with preserved glucose
Possible multifocal ischemic lesions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound asymmetric paralysis and cerebral arterial narrowing are uncommon complications
Strongly neutrophil-predominant CSF is less typical of established viral encephalitis

data.description: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne infection that occasionally causes severe encephalitis, particularly in older adults; cerebral vascular complications are rare.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory CSF with elevated protein and preserved glucose
symptoms_not_in_common: Multifocal ischemic lesions and arterial narrowing are not usual imaging findings
Marked neutrophil predominance in CSF is less typical than lymphocytic inflammation
Hemiplegia with a Babinski sign is less typical than diffuse encephalopathy

data.description: Herpes simplex virus causes acute, potentially devastating brain inflammation, usually involving the temporal and inferior frontal lobes.
symptoms_in_common: CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein with preserved glucose
Neutrophilic CSF can occur early in the illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient generalized rash is not characteristic
The apparent multifocal ischemic pattern and arterial narrowing are less typical than temporal-lobe inflammation

data.diagnosis: Acute bacterial meningoencephalitis with secondary cerebral vasculopathy
data.description: Bacterial infection of the meninges and brain can cause coma and inflammation or thrombosis of cerebral vessels, resulting in ischemic strokes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible multifocal infarcts and arterial narrowing
symptoms_not_in_common: The preserved CSF-to-blood glucose ratio is less typical of untreated bacterial meningitis
The relatively modest CSF leukocyte count is less typical of severe untreated bacterial meningitis
Transient rash is not typical of most bacterial causes, although it can occur in meningococcal disease

data.description: An IgA-mediated small-vessel vasculitis, often following a respiratory infection, that causes purpura, arthritis, and sometimes gastrointestinal or renal involvement. This is the leading diagnosis given the apparent vascular IgA deposition in the supplied biopsy images.
symptoms_in_common: Upper respiratory illness preceding the rash and joint symptoms
Bilateral purpuric rash on the feet
Skin histology appearing consistent with leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Apparent vascular IgA, C3, and fibrin deposition on immunofluorescence
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly unilateral calf pain and swelling are less typical than the usual bilateral dependent manifestations
Nasal crusting or bleeding suggested by the photograph is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A potential anti-TNF treatment complication causing immune-mediated inflammation of dermal small vessels; it can sometimes have an IgA-mediated pattern. Medication causation cannot be established from this case alone.
symptoms_not_in_common: Respiratory illness immediately preceding the symptoms favors an infectious trigger rather than proving a medication reaction
Nasal crusting or bleeding is not typical of skin-limited drug-associated vasculitis
Severe focal calf pain is less typical of uncomplicated cutaneous disease

data.description: An ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis that commonly affects the upper airways, lungs, and kidneys and may produce skin purpura and arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Nasal crusting or bleeding suggested by the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent vascular IgA deposition favors immune-complex vasculitis rather than the usual pauci-immune pattern
Abrupt unilateral calf swelling is not a characteristic presentation
An intact nasal septum does not support destructive nasal disease, although it does not exclude early disease

data.description: Small-vessel skin inflammation triggered by an infection, usually causing dependent purpura and sometimes arthralgia or localized edema. IgA-dominant staining would favor the more specific diagnosis of IgA vasculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sore throat, cough, rhinorrhea, and chills
Delayed onset of bilateral foot purpura after the respiratory illness
Histologic appearances suggesting neutrophilic small-vessel injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent vascular IgA deposition suggests IgA vasculitis rather than nonspecific postinfectious skin vasculitis
Severe asymmetric calf pain and swelling are less typical
Nasal crusting or bleeding is not explained by skin-limited vasculitis

data.description: A clot in a deep leg vein causing unilateral pain and swelling. Crohn’s disease increases venous thromboembolism risk; this remains an important possible concurrent diagnosis requiring prompt exclusion despite the vasculitic skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly worsening unilateral swelling extending to the foot
Normal peripheral pulses, which do not exclude venous thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral purpuric foot rash
Left ankle synovitis
Skin biopsy appearances suggesting small-vessel vasculitis
Apparent vascular IgA deposition
Preceding upper respiratory symptoms and nasal crusting

data.diagnosis: Left tonsillar squamous cell carcinoma with cervical lymph node metastasis, potentially HPV-associated
data.description: An oropharyngeal malignancy arising in the palatine tonsil that commonly spreads to upper cervical lymph nodes. This is the leading consideration; HPV-associated disease can occur in nonsmokers, but HPV status requires tissue testing.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided neck mass with a firm, fixed upper cervical lymph node
Apparent left tonsillar-region mass on CT
Focal uptake in the left oropharyngeal lesion and cervical node on PET/CT
Rounded hypoechoic cervical node on ultrasound

data.diagnosis: Base-of-tongue squamous cell carcinoma with cervical lymph node metastasis
data.description: A malignancy of the lingual tonsil or tongue base that can cause referred ear pain and present with metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Firm, fixed upper cervical lymph node
Oropharyngeal mass and metabolically active cervical node
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent imaging epicenter is the left palatine tonsillar region rather than clearly the tongue base

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the tonsil and regional lymph nodes, potentially producing unilateral tonsillar enlargement and marked PET uptake.
symptoms_in_common: Metabolically active oropharyngeal tissue and cervical node
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent unilateral referred ear pain is less characteristic
A fixed cervical node is less typical than rubbery, mobile lymphadenopathy

data.diagnosis: Minor salivary gland carcinoma of the oropharynx
data.description: A rare malignancy arising from small salivary glands in the oropharynx, such as mucoepidermoid carcinoma, which may cause a local mass and cervical metastases.
symptoms_in_common: Firm cervical lymphadenopathy compatible with regional spread
symptoms_not_in_common: A tonsillar-region primary with prominent upper cervical nodal involvement is more characteristic of squamous cell carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Chronic tonsillitis with reactive cervical lymphadenopathy
data.description: Persistent tonsillar inflammation can cause throat pain, referred ear pain, regional lymph node enlargement, and increased PET uptake, although the findings here are more concerning for malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Tonsillar-region abnormality and PET uptake that could occur with inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Six months of persistent unilateral symptoms
Firm, fixed cervical lymph node
Apparent discrete unilateral oropharyngeal mass
Rounded, markedly hypoechoic node rather than a typical reactive nodal appearance

data.diagnosis: Primary urinary bladder extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma that can develop in the bladder in association with chronic inflammation. The apparent lymphoid infiltrate and lymphoepithelial involvement favor this diagnosis, but confirmation requires immunophenotyping and interpretation of the molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: No lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or bone marrow involvement
Bladder biopsy images showing a dense lymphoid infiltrate with apparent epithelial involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild anemia is nonspecific and not a defining feature of localized bladder MALT lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia of the bladder (follicular cystitis)
data.description: A benign lymphoid response to chronic bladder irritation or infection that can resemble lymphoma. Organized reactive follicles and a polyclonal lymphoid population would support this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent diffuse lymphoid infiltrate and lymphoepithelial involvement are more concerning for lymphoma
Mild anemia is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Primary urinary bladder diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that rarely arises primarily in the bladder and may cause symptoms resembling cystitis. Diagnosis requires demonstration of a predominantly large, atypical B-cell population.
symptoms_in_common: Negative staging studies can occur in localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The prolonged history without systemic symptoms is less typical of an aggressive lymphoma
The supplied histology does not clearly show a predominance of large atypical lymphoid cells

data.description: A malignant tumor of the bladder lining that can produce persistent urinary irritation and cystoscopic abnormalities. Confirmation requires malignant urothelial cells on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal bladder mucosal appearance on cystoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: The biopsy images appear dominated by lymphoid cells rather than malignant urothelial cells
Repeated Escherichia coli-positive cultures support an infectious component rather than directly supporting carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving the urinary bladder
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma with lymphoplasmacytic differentiation, usually involving bone marrow and often associated with a monoclonal IgM protein. Isolated bladder involvement would be unusual.
symptoms_in_common: Lymphoid infiltrate with some plasmacytoid-appearing cells
An indolent presentation without systemic symptoms is possible
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative bone marrow biopsy
No monoclonal component on serum protein electrophoresis
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Apparent lymphoepithelial involvement favors MALT lymphoma
Recurrent Escherichia coli cystitis is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A gas-forming infection of the bladder wall and lumen, commonly associated with diabetes and organisms such as Klebsiella pneumoniae. This is the leading consideration given the apparent curvilinear gas outlining the bladder on the radiograph; CT can confirm the location of the gas.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
Apparent gas outlining the bladder on pelvic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The fall is not a characteristic manifestation, although infection-related weakness may contribute

data.description: A bacterial bladder infection occurring in a patient with risk factors for complications, such as diabetes and advanced age. Ordinary cystitis does not produce gas within the bladder wall.
symptoms_in_common: Urine culture positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae
Negative blood cultures are compatible with a localized urinary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent gas outlining the bladder is not typical of non-emphysematous cystitis
A fall is not a specific symptom of cystitis

data.description: An abnormal connection between the colon and bladder, often caused by diverticular disease or malignancy, allowing bowel gas and bacteria to enter the urinary tract.
symptoms_in_common: Urinary infection with an enteric organism, Klebsiella pneumoniae
Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
Apparent gas in the bladder region
symptoms_not_in_common: Gas outlining the bladder wall favors emphysematous cystitis rather than a fistula
The fall is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A potentially life-threatening gas-forming infection of the kidney and surrounding tissues, particularly in patients with diabetes. Renal imaging would be needed to assess this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible gas appears centered on the bladder rather than the kidneys
The fall is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A fracture near the hip joint, commonly caused by a low-energy fall in an older adult. The right femoral neck appears abnormal on this image, warranting dedicated hip views or CT for confirmation; this could coexist with the urinary infection.
symptoms_in_common: Possible disruption of the right femoral neck on the pelvic radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Klebsiella pneumoniae in the urine is not explained by a hip fracture
Apparent bladder-wall gas is not explained by a hip fracture
Elevated inflammatory markers may follow trauma but also support the documented infection

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the femoral condyle with an unstable or detached fragment
data.description: A focal disorder of subchondral bone that can cause overlying cartilage and bone to separate, producing an intra-articular loose body. The apparent femoral condylar defect and displaced osteochondral fragment on these radiographs make this the leading possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episode of disabling knee pain

data.diagnosis: Chronic post-traumatic osteochondral fracture with an intra-articular loose body
data.description: An old injury involving articular cartilage and underlying bone can leave a detached fragment that later causes swelling and mechanical obstruction. This could also account for the apparent osteochondral defect and fragment.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent trauma, which argues against an acute osteochondral fracture

data.description: A torn meniscal fragment, particularly a bucket-handle tear, can become displaced and block knee motion. It explains the mechanical symptoms but would not itself explain the apparent bony defect or osteochondral fragment on the radiographs.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent twisting injury, although a chronic tear can become symptomatic without new trauma

data.description: A benign synovial disorder that produces cartilaginous nodules, which may detach and become calcified or ossified loose bodies. It can cause atraumatic swelling and locking, although multiple bodies are more characteristic than the apparent focal osteochondral abnormality here.

data.diagnosis: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor of the knee
data.description: A benign proliferative synovial lesion, including the diffuse form formerly called pigmented villonodular synovitis, that can cause recurrent pain, effusion, and occasionally catching or locking. The apparent osteochondral fragment is not a characteristic imaging feature.
symptoms_not_in_common: True mechanical locking is less typical, particularly for diffuse disease

data.description: A rare lymphoid malignancy involving the pancreas that can cause a pancreatic mass and biliary obstruction. The lymphoid-appearing biopsy raises this possibility, but classification requires identification of the immunohistochemical stains and assessment for disease elsewhere.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice, dark brown urine, and pale stools consistent with biliary obstruction
Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic liver enzymes
Dense lymphoid-appearing infiltrate in the supplied biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely elevated CA19-9 is not characteristic of lymphoma, although biliary obstruction can elevate it
Normal LDH and beta-2-microglobulin are less supportive of aggressive or extensive lymphoma, but do not exclude localized or indolent disease

data.description: A malignant tumor of pancreatic ductal cells, commonly causing obstructive jaundice when located in the pancreatic head.
symptoms_in_common: Dark brown urine and pale stools
Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic liver enzymes
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied biopsy appears predominantly lymphoid rather than showing obvious malignant gland formation
Age 48 is younger than the usual age at presentation

data.description: Cancer of the distal extrahepatic bile duct that can obstruct bile flow near the pancreatic head and resemble a pancreatic tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Dark brown urine and pale stools
Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic liver enzymes
A mass near the pancreatic head could involve the distal bile duct
symptoms_not_in_common: A bulky pancreatic-region mass is less typical than a bile-duct-centered lesion
The lymphoid-appearing biopsy is not typical of an adenocarcinoma
Age 48 is younger than the usual presentation

data.description: An inflammatory pancreatic disorder, often associated with IgG4-related disease, that can produce focal pancreatic enlargement and obstructive jaundice resembling cancer.
symptoms_in_common: Dark brown urine and pale stools
Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic liver enzymes
A lymphoid-rich inflammatory biopsy could be compatible
symptoms_not_in_common: CA19-9 of 11783 IU/mL is unusually high, although severe biliary obstruction can cause substantial elevations
The provided biopsy does not clearly establish characteristic fibrosis or a plasma-cell-rich infiltrate

data.description: A pancreatic neoplasm arising from neuroendocrine cells. A nonfunctioning tumor in the pancreatic head can cause biliary obstruction; confirmation requires neuroendocrine immunohistochemical markers.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice, dark brown urine, and pale stools from possible bile-duct compression
Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic liver enzymes
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely elevated CA19-9 is not characteristic of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
The supplied biopsy appears more lymphoid than classically neuroendocrine
The CT image does not clearly demonstrate the avid enhancement typical of many well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: T-cell/histiocyte rich large B-cell lymphoma

data.description: Mass-like calcium phosphate deposition in soft tissues associated with advanced kidney disease and disturbed phosphate metabolism. This is the most likely diagnosis given the lobulated calcified mass and marked hyperphosphatemia.
symptoms_in_common: Lobulated, densely calcified soft-tissue mass on CT
Marked hyperphosphatemia and poor adherence to phosphate binders
Focal radiotracer uptake at the mass on scintigraphy
symptoms_not_in_common: Lumbar subcutaneous location is less typical than periarticular sites such as the shoulders, elbows, and hips

data.description: Calcium deposition in previously damaged or inflamed skin and subcutaneous tissue, generally occurring independently of systemic calcium and phosphate abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperphosphatemia suggests a systemic metabolic cause rather than dystrophic calcification
No preceding local trauma, inflammation, or tissue injury is reported
Large, lobulated 9 cm mass is less typical of localized calcinosis cutis

data.description: Calcification and thrombosis of small cutaneous vessels, usually in patients with advanced kidney disease, causing ischemic skin injury. The painless mass without skin breakdown makes this substantially less likely.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion is asymptomatic rather than severely painful
No overlying ulceration, necrosis, or retiform purpura is reported
Discrete, bulky lobulated calcified mass is atypical
Slow enlargement over six months without reported skin injury

data.description: Benign formation of mature bone in soft tissue, commonly following trauma and usually involving muscle. Imaging typically shows organized peripheral ossification rather than amorphous calcium deposits.
symptoms_in_common: Focal radiotracer uptake can occur in an ossifying lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Subcutaneous rather than intramuscular location
No preceding trauma is reported
Lobulated calcification without evident organized peripheral bone formation
Hyperphosphatemia and prolonged dialysis favor metabolic calcification

data.description: A rare malignant soft-tissue tumor that produces osteoid or bone without originating in the skeleton. It can present as an enlarging mineralized mass in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lobulated, densely calcified appearance without an obvious substantial noncalcified tumor component is less typical
No destructive invasion is evident in the supplied images
Marked hyperphosphatemia and long-standing dialysis provide a stronger explanation for benign metabolic calcium deposition

data.description: An intra-articular fracture of the upper tibia, often caused by high-energy trauma. The radiographs appear to show a complex proximal tibial fracture involving the plateau and extending into the metaphysis; CT would clarify the fracture pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic evidence of proximal tibial fracture
Intact skin and preserved neurovascular function are compatible with a closed fracture

data.description: A fracture of the tibial spine at the anterior cruciate ligament attachment, potentially producing knee instability. It may occur with other proximal tibial fractures.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent involvement of the central tibial plateau on radiographs
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive proximal tibial fracture lines are not explained by an isolated tibial eminence avulsion

data.description: A tear of the ligament that limits forward movement of the tibia, commonly associated with skiing injuries and rapid traumatic joint swelling. It could accompany the visible fracture but cannot be confirmed on these radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid marked swelling consistent with possible hemarthrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible proximal tibial fracture is not explained by an isolated ligament rupture

data.description: An injury to the ligament that limits backward movement of the tibia, typically resulting from force applied to the upper tibia or severe knee hyperflexion. It is a possible associated injury after high-energy trauma.
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible proximal tibial fracture is not explained by an isolated posterior cruciate ligament injury
Immediate marked generalized swelling is less characteristic of an isolated posterior cruciate ligament injury

data.description: A tear of a knee meniscus caused by compression or twisting. Meniscal injuries can accompany tibial plateau fractures, although radiographs do not directly demonstrate them.
symptoms_in_common: High-energy injury capable of damaging intra-articular structures
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate marked generalized swelling is less typical of an isolated meniscal tear
The visible proximal tibial fracture is not explained by an isolated meniscal tear

diagnoses.name: Tibial plateau fracture
diagnoses.title: Fracture of lower end of tibia[Tibial Plateau]

data.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising in the gastrointestinal wall, often associated with KIT or PDGFRA mutations. The submucosal mass and spindle-cell histology make this a leading possibility; the immunostains and sequencing images require marker and gene labels for definitive interpretation.
symptoms_in_common: Well-delimited mass compressing and infiltrating the rectal wall
Spindle-cell appearance in the supplied histology

data.description: A malignant smooth-muscle tumor that can arise within the rectal wall and produce a bulky spindle-cell mass. Diagnosis requires assessment of atypia, mitotic activity, necrosis, and smooth-muscle immunostains.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell appearance in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth, elastic, sharply delimited mass is less characteristic of an aggressive sarcoma, although possible

data.description: A usually benign nerve-sheath tumor that can present as a well-circumscribed gastrointestinal submucosal mass composed of spindle cells.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell appearance in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: True infiltration of the rectal wall is less typical of a benign schwannoma

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor that can cause a smooth submucosal rectal bulge and obstructive symptoms when sufficiently large.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle-cell appearance in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Rectal wall infiltration is atypical for a benign leiomyoma
A 6-cm mass is larger than most rectal leiomyomas

data.description: A malignant gland-forming tumor of the rectal mucosa that commonly causes altered bowel habits and tenesmus. It is less favored here because the lesion is submucosal and the supplied histology appears spindle-cell rather than gland-forming.
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth, elastic submucosal bulge rather than an irregular mucosal lesion
Sharply delimited mass
Spindle-cell appearance rather than gland-forming morphology in the supplied histology
