diagnoses.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

data.description: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by growth restriction, characteristic facial features, partial lipodystrophy, delayed dentition, and possible insulin resistance. The reported de novo PIK3R1 variant strongly supports this as the leading diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
Triangular face, prominent forehead, and small chin
Hypoplastic nasal alae and thin downturned lips
Lipoatrophy and thin skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss beginning in infancy is not a core feature, although hearing impairment has been reported

data.description: An imprinting-related growth disorder causing prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, low body weight, a prominent forehead, and triangular facial appearance. It is a phenotypic alternative but does not explain the PIK3R1 finding.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Lipoatrophy with thin wrinkled skin and visible vessels
Microdontia and hypoplastic nasal alae
Head circumference below the third percentile at birth rather than typical relative head sparing

data.description: A rare neonatal progeroid disorder, usually associated with biallelic POLR3A variants, featuring prenatal growth restriction, reduced subcutaneous fat, thin skin, and characteristic craniofacial abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent low weight and short stature
Thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss
Delayed teething rather than the natal teeth often described in this disorder
Normal psychomotor development is less typical of severe presentations

data.diagnosis: Mandibular hypoplasia, deafness, progeroid features, and lipodystrophy syndrome
data.description: A POLD1-related disorder combining mandibular hypoplasia, sensorineural deafness, lipodystrophy, growth abnormalities, and a prematurely aged appearance. It overlaps clinically but is not explained by the reported PIK3R1 variant.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked intrauterine growth restriction
Severe hearing loss already evident at three months rather than the more usual later onset
Delayed teething and microdontia are not defining features

data.description: An LMNA-related premature-aging disorder characterized by early-childhood growth failure, loss of subcutaneous fat, skin changes, mandibular hypoplasia, and progressive cardiovascular disease.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked intrauterine growth restriction, as birth measurements are generally near normal
Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in infancy
Thin wrinkled skin rather than the typical early sclerodermatous skin changes

data.description: An adult-onset combined immunodeficiency associated with thymoma, characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, markedly reduced or absent B cells, and variable T-cell dysfunction. It can persist or become apparent after thymoma resection and is the strongest unifying diagnosis here.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections partially responsive to antibiotics
Marked B-cell depletion and absent pneumococcal antibody response
Lymphopenia with low CD3 and CD4 counts
Reduced lymphocyte proliferation to tetanus and Candida
Pneumocystis jirovecii detected in induced sputum
Intermittent diarrhea, weight loss, and low albumin and total protein

data.description: A primary antibody deficiency causing impaired vaccine responses, recurrent respiratory infections, and sometimes chronic gastrointestinal disease. Serum immunoglobulin measurements are needed to assess this possibility; the thymoma history and profound B-cell depletion favor Good syndrome instead.

symptoms_not_in_common: Thymoma is more characteristic of Good syndrome
Marked B-cell depletion is less typical than preserved but dysfunctional B cells
Low CD3 and CD4 counts with impaired lymphocyte proliferation suggest substantial combined immunodeficiency
Pneumocystis infection is uncommon in conventional common variable immunodeficiency

data.description: An opportunistic pulmonary infection associated with impaired cellular immunity. Positive induced sputum together with fever, cough, and dyspnea supports this diagnosis, although organism detection alone does not always distinguish infection from colonization.

Low CD4 count and impaired lymphocyte proliferation
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal right perihilar cavitary consolidation rather than the more typical diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities
Normal resting oxygen saturation is less typical of clinically advanced pneumonia
Marked B-cell depletion and absent pneumococcal antibody response are underlying immune abnormalities rather than consequences of this infection
Recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections and intermittent diarrhea are not explained by this pulmonary infection alone

data.description: A bacterial respiratory infection that can cause pneumonia in patients with impaired host defenses. Detection in sputum and focal pulmonary consolidation support possible infection, although sputum positivity can also reflect airway colonization.
symptoms_in_common: Moraxella catarrhalis detected in induced sputum
Right perihilar pulmonary consolidation on CT
Recurrent sinopulmonary infections partially responsive to antibiotics
Acute and chronic inflammation on lesion biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Cavitation is uncommon in Moraxella pneumonia

Concurrent Pneumocystis detection is not explained by Moraxella infection

data.description: A mycobacterial infection that can cause chronic constitutional symptoms and cavitary lung disease. Ethiopian origin and immunodeficiency increase its relevance, but the reported negative infectious evaluation and nonspecific biopsy reduce support without necessarily excluding it.
symptoms_in_common: Cavitary pulmonary lesion with surrounding consolidation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked B-cell depletion and absent pneumococcal antibody response are not typical consequences of tuberculosis

Biopsy showed nonspecific acute and chronic inflammation rather than characteristic granulomatous inflammation
The extensive infectious evaluation and lesion cultures were reported as negative

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype

Normal routine laboratory results and absence of fever can occur in localized disease

data.description: A T-cell lymphoma characterized by large atypical cells, usually with strong CD30 expression; ALK-positive disease frequently affects young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells in the biopsy
Prominent staining of large cells could support this diagnosis if the stain is CD30
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever and normal inflammatory markers are less typical of aggressive systemic disease
Fibrous bands and lacunar-appearing cells favor nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma instead

symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation dominated by a cervical node rather than a documented bulky anterior mediastinal mass

data.description: A histiocytic disorder that often causes painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Diagnosis requires characteristic histiocytes with emperipolesis and an appropriate immunophenotype.

Normal ESR and blood count
Normal immunoglobulin levels
Biopsy appearance is more suggestive of lacunar-type atypical cells than diagnostic emperipolesis

data.description: Benign lymph-node enlargement caused by immune stimulation, sometimes with enlarged activated lymphoid cells. Preserved architecture and a nonmalignant immunophenotype would be needed to support this diagnosis.

data.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle that can rapidly cause heart failure, cardiogenic shock, and ventricular arrhythmias. The preceding infectious illness raises concern for viral myocarditis, although the cause cannot be established from these images alone.

Cough and wheezing potentially caused by pulmonary congestion
Chest imaging suggestive of pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions
Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest

data.description: Pregnancy-associated heart failure caused by left ventricular systolic dysfunction without another identifiable cause. Twin gestation increases risk; presentation at 32 weeks is earlier than the classic final-month presentation.

Chest imaging suggestive of pulmonary edema and pleural effusions
symptoms_not_in_common: Conjunctivitis with green discharge
Sore throat and ear pain
Initially unilateral painful leg swelling
Sudden crushing chest pain is less typical than progressive heart failure symptoms

data.diagnosis: Acute pulmonary embolism arising from deep vein thrombosis

Sudden chest pain and cardiac arrest

Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is less typical than pulseless electrical activity in massive pulmonary embolism

data.description: Separation within a coronary artery wall can compromise coronary blood flow and cause myocardial infarction during pregnancy or postpartum. The provided angiographic still does not establish a dissection.

symptoms_not_in_common: Several weeks of conjunctivitis, sore throat, and ear pain
Progressive painful leg swelling before the acute chest pain
Prolonged cough and edema preceding the apparent acute coronary event are less typical

symptoms_in_common: Significant physical stress from twin pregnancy and an intercurrent illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age is less typical
Weeks of progressive leg edema and cough are less typical of its usually abrupt presentation
Focal leg pain and tenderness
Conjunctivitis with green discharge, sore throat, and ear pain

data.diagnosis: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with hepatic vascular malformations
data.description: An autosomal dominant vascular disorder causing recurrent bleeding, mucocutaneous telangiectasias, and visceral vascular malformations. Confusion potentially resulting from portosystemic shunting

data.diagnosis: Portosystemic encephalopathy due to intrahepatic vascular shunting

symptoms_not_in_common: Familial epistaxis and mucocutaneous telangiectasias indicate an underlying vascular disorder rather than encephalopathy itself
Chest and left arm pain are not characteristic
Chills are not intrinsic to this condition

data.diagnosis: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension and hepatic encephalopathy
data.description: Chronic hepatic scarring can cause portal hypertension, collateral vascular formation, cytopenias from hypersplenism, and encephalopathy. It is an alternative explanation, but cirrhosis is not established by the supplied findings.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent abdominal vessels that could represent collateral circulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong epistaxis affecting multiple generations is more suggestive of an inherited vascular disorder

Acute chills and diarrhea are not direct manifestations
Chest and left arm pain are not characteristic

data.description: Acute delirium caused by volume depletion and associated electrolyte disturbances or renal dysfunction. Diarrhea and poor intake support this possibility, but laboratory testing is needed to establish the metabolic abnormality.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong familial epistaxis
Multiple mucocutaneous telangiectasias
Abnormal hepatic vascular imaging
Chronic pancytopenia
Hepatomegaly

data.diagnosis: Infection-associated delirium, including possible sepsis from a gastrointestinal source
data.description: An acute infection can produce delirium and profound lethargy in older adults, sometimes without prominent fever. Chills and diarrhea suggest an infectious trigger, but sepsis requires additional clinical and laboratory evidence.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong recurrent epistaxis with a multigenerational family history
Multiple facial, labial, and truncal telangiectasias
Hepatic vascular abnormalities
Longstanding heart failure and pulmonary hypertension are not explained by an acute infection

data.description: Accumulation of mast cells in the skin causes brown or orange-brown lesions, often beginning in infancy. Rubbing may produce localized swelling and redness (Darier sign). This is the leading consideration, but examination and possibly biopsy are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple orange-brown macules on the back and thighs
Variable lesion shapes and uneven pigmentation

Normal growth, laboratory results, and absence of organ enlargement are compatible with skin-limited disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite contradictory feature is reported; rubbing-induced swelling, itching, or flushing is not documented

data.description: A rare, benign pigmentary disorder characterized by spontaneously appearing brown macules without preceding inflammation or medication exposure. Infantile onset is unusual.

Normal general health and laboratory results

Apparent swelling and redness in the close-up photograph would not be typical

data.diagnosis: Neurofibromatosis type 1 presenting with café-au-lait macules
data.description: A genetic disorder that can initially present with multiple café-au-lait macules in infancy. Six or more lesions larger than 5 mm in a prepubertal child constitute one diagnostic criterion, but additional criteria are necessary to establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Normal development at this age does not exclude the condition

Orange hue and uneven pigmentation are less typical

symptoms_not_in_common: Explicit absence of preceding erythema or trauma

data.description: Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery, often after substantial weight loss. symptoms_in_common: Severe underweight status with BMI of 14
Constipation associated with reduced intake or obstruction
Amenorrhea consistent with severe nutritional depletion
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain, although painless presentations occur
Mildly elevated ESR is not a characteristic finding

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without a mechanical obstruction, potentially associated with malnutrition. It can cause postprandial vomiting and weight loss, but does not explain the apparent vascular compression of the duodenum.
symptoms_in_common: Constipation when broader gastrointestinal dysmotility is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Amenorrhea is not a direct manifestation, although it may follow malnutrition

data.description: Impaired intestinal nerve or muscle function producing obstruction-like symptoms without a fixed mechanical blockage. Less likely here because the imaging suggests a focal duodenal compression rather than generalized dysmotility.

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease with gastroduodenal involvement or stricture

symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain

data.description: An immune-mediated reaction to gluten that damages the small intestinal lining and can cause malnutrition, weight loss, and menstrual disturbances. It is a possible contributor to chronic weight loss but does not adequately explain the apparent focal duodenal obstruction.

Elevated ESR is nonspecific and not a characteristic diagnostic finding

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass

Pale floating stools and increased flatus

Severe cachexia and dehydration are not typical of an uncomplicated ulcer

The demonstrated gastrocolic fistula is not explained by bacterial overgrowth alone

Meal-related focal epigastric and left upper quadrant tenderness is not a defining feature

data.description: Transmural inflammatory bowel disease can cause diarrhea, malnutrition, and abnormal connections between gastrointestinal organs, rarely including a gastrocolic fistula. The images establish a fistula but do not establish Crohn disease as its cause.

data.description: Air leaks from ruptured alveoli into the mediastinum, often following coughing or increased airway pressure during an asthma exacerbation. The radiograph appears to show lucency outlining mediastinal structures, making this the leading possibility.

Cough producing small amounts of whitish sputum
Preserved ability to speak in full sentences and normal oxygen saturation in a nonsevere episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain is not typical of uncomplicated asthma

Apparent mediastinal air on the radiograph requires an additional diagnosis

Neck pain is less typical unless associated air extends into the neck
Elevated inflammatory markers are not characteristic of an uncomplicated pneumothorax

Cough producing whitish sputum is less characteristic
Apparent mediastinal air is not explained by pulmonary embolism

Normal temperature does not exclude bronchitis

Apparent mediastinal air is not explained by bronchitis alone

data.description: A nutritional disorder caused by deficiency of niacin or its precursor tryptophan. It produces photosensitive dermatitis and may cause gastrointestinal and neurologic abnormalities. The photographed neck rash resembles a Casal necklace, making this a leading consideration.

Painful distal paresthesias and sensory impairment

Hypertension, which could occur with renal involvement but is nonspecific

The photosensitive-appearing hand, forearm, and neck dermatitis is not characteristic
Severe hypertension is not a typical manifestation

The photographed neck and exposed-extremity dermatitis is not characteristic

Apparent superficial erosions on the forearms

data.description: A BTK-related defect in B-cell maturation causing profound antibody deficiency and recurrent infections in male infants. Markedly reduced BTK expression in patient monocytes

Fever and respiratory distress with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates

Absent or poorly developed lymphoid tissue

Fever, respiratory distress, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates

Absent tonsillar tissue and nonpalpable lymph nodes
Severe neutropenia is not a typical defining feature
BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y) mutation
Markedly reduced BTK expression

data.diagnosis: Proximal penile fracture of the right corpus cavernosum

Severely restricted motor development and absent speech

symptoms_not_in_common: An indurated plaque extending onto the forehead is not typical

Positive antinuclear antibodies and increased C3d are not characteristic findings
The photograph does not show prominent perifollicular scaling

data.description: A granulomatous inflammatory disease that can produce persistent, firm facial or scalp plaques and occasionally scarring alopecia.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic indurated facial and scalp plaque
symptoms_not_in_common: The long linear distribution is unusual
Positive antinuclear antibodies and increased C3d are not characteristic
The supplied biopsy appears to show inflammatory aggregates rather than clearly formed noncaseating granulomas

data.diagnosis: ANA-negative systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus enteritis
data.description: The leading diagnosis is systemic lupus erythematosus with inflammatory or vasculitic bowel involvement. CT appears to show bowel-wall thickening with layered enhancement, compatible with lupus enteritis. Negative ANA testing is unusual but does not entirely exclude lupus when other findings are strongly supportive.
symptoms_in_common: Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and diffuse tenderness
Apparent bowel-wall thickening with layered enhancement on CT
Strongly positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeatedly negative ANA testing is atypical for systemic lupus erythematosus

data.description: An uncommon lupus complication causing impaired intestinal motility without a mechanical blockage. It can accompany urinary tract smooth-muscle dysfunction and bilateral collecting-system dilation, which appears present on the CT; confirmation requires excluding mechanical obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent gas-filled bowel loops on abdominal radiography
Apparent bilateral renal collecting-system dilation on CT
Oral ulcers, cytopenias, low complement, and lupus-associated antibodies
symptoms_not_in_common: Layered bowel-wall thickening is more suggestive of concomitant enteritis than isolated motility dysfunction
Repeatedly negative ANA testing is atypical for the underlying lupus diagnosis

data.description: A systemic inflammatory disorder characterized by recurrent oral ulcers and sometimes intestinal ulceration, which can cause severe abdominal pain and acute abdominal complications.
symptoms_not_in_common: Strongly positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies
Low C3 and C4 concentrations
Combined anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia
Bilateral renal collecting-system dilation is not characteristic
Pericardial effusion is uncommon

data.description: A small-vessel vasculitis occurring predominantly in children that can cause acute abdominal pain, vomiting, and bowel-wall edema. Gastrointestinal symptoms occasionally precede the characteristic purpuric rash.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe abdominal pain and vomiting
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent oral ulcers
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia
Strongly positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies
Low C3 and C4 concentrations
Pericardial effusion
Bilateral renal collecting-system dilation

data.description: An inflammatory bowel disease that may present in adolescence with abdominal pain, oral aphthous ulcers, anemia, and bowel-wall thickening. Vomiting can occur with severe inflammation or intestinal obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia before any treatment
Strongly positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies
Low C3 and C4 concentrations
Pericardial effusion is an uncommon extraintestinal manifestation
Bilateral renal collecting-system dilation is not a typical presenting feature

data.description: A nontraumatic separation of the coronary arterial wall or intramural hematoma that restricts blood flow and causes acute coronary ischemia. This is the leading consideration given the clinical presentation and apparent long-segment coronary narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Recent pregnancy loss, suggesting a possible pregnancy-associated hormonal context
Coronary angiography appears to show long, smooth narrowing compatible with dissection
Apparent renal arterial irregularities suggest an associated systemic arteriopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient chest tightness one year earlier is not clearly explained by a single acute dissection

data.diagnosis: Fibromuscular dysplasia with associated coronary artery dissection
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder that causes stenoses, aneurysms, and dissections, especially in renal and cervical arteries. It is frequently associated with spontaneous coronary artery dissection.
symptoms_in_common: Renal artery images appear to show multifocal irregularity or beading
Renal cortical indentations may represent scarring from prior vascular injury
Coronary narrowing and ischemic chest pain could reflect associated coronary dissection
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute jaw-radiating chest pain and diaphoresis are not typical of uncomplicated renal fibromuscular dysplasia and require a coronary complication to explain them
Familial hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is not a defining feature of fibromuscular dysplasia

data.description: An inherited connective-tissue disorder, usually related to COL3A1 variants, that predisposes to arterial fragility, dissection, and rupture. The reported family history of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome does not establish the vascular subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Possible spontaneous coronary arterial injury at a relatively young age
Possible abnormalities involving more than one arterial territory
A maternal relative died of a cerebral aneurysm
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatives' reported diagnosis is hypermobile rather than vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Renal arterial beading is more suggestive of fibromuscular dysplasia than vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
Recurrent self-resolving anginal episodes are not specific to this connective-tissue disorder

data.description: Transient coronary arterial spasm causing reversible myocardial ischemia, sometimes with myocardial infarction. Demonstrating resolution of narrowing after intracoronary vasodilators would help distinguish spasm from structural arterial disease.
symptoms_in_common: Episodes of chest pain that resolve spontaneously
Substernal pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Coronary narrowing could resemble spasm on a single angiographic image
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain recurring after walking is less characteristic than predominantly resting attacks
Renal arterial irregularities and cortical scarring are not explained by isolated coronary vasospasm
Apparent extensive coronary narrowing raises concern for structural disease such as dissection

data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption and thrombosis, presenting as unstable angina or myocardial infarction. ECG evolution and cardiac troponin measurements are needed to establish myocardial injury.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Coronary angiography shows an apparent flow-limiting abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 41 with no reported conventional atherosclerotic risk factors makes this less likely, though not excluded
Long, smooth coronary narrowing is less typical of focal atherosclerotic plaque disease
Renal arterial beading suggests a nonatherosclerotic arteriopathy
The connective-tissue family history and recent pregnancy loss favor consideration of nonatherosclerotic coronary disease

data.diagnosis: Congenital duodenal web with partial obstruction
data.description: A congenital membrane narrows the duodenal lumen, sometimes allowing enough passage for symptoms to emerge gradually. The apparent proximal duodenal distention and limited downstream contrast passage raise this possibility, although the supplied images are not definitive.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent feeding difficulties beginning in early infancy
Apparent proximal duodenal distention on the contrast study

data.description: An intrinsic narrowing of the duodenum causes partial intestinal obstruction, impaired feeding tolerance, and poor growth.
symptoms_in_common: Possible proximal duodenal distention with passage of contrast distally

data.description: Pancreatic tissue encircles the duodenum and can produce partial or complete obstruction. Additional imaging may be needed to distinguish it from intrinsic duodenal narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Feeding difficulties in a young infant
Possible duodenal obstruction on the contrast study

data.diagnosis: Intestinal malrotation with obstructing Ladd bands
data.description: Abnormal intestinal rotation can produce bands that compress the duodenum and can predispose to midgut volvulus. Assessment requires clear localization of the duodenojejunal junction, which cannot be confidently established from these selected images alone.

Thickening of the pyloric muscle obstructs gastric emptying, typically in infants several weeks old. Ultrasound is the usual diagnostic test; the apparent duodenal abnormality makes this less favored.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent proximal duodenal distention rather than an isolated gastric outlet abnormality

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy affecting muscle and skin. An edematous presentation can cause marked facial and limb swelling and involve swallowing muscles. This is the strongest overall possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous edema of both upper arms
Proximal hip weakness and difficulty rising from a chair
Markedly elevated CK and elevated AST/ALT
MRI showing extensive facial, oral, pharyngeal, and neck muscle edema
Perivascular inflammation and MHC class I expression on muscle biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Initially unilateral periorbital swelling is less typical than bilateral involvement
Prominent tongue and throat swelling preceding limb weakness is an unusual presentation
Normal arm strength despite upper-arm edema is less typical of established generalized proximal myopathy

data.description: An inflammatory myopathy causing proximal muscle weakness and sometimes swallowing dysfunction without characteristic dermatomyositis skin findings. Diagnosis requires exclusion of other inflammatory myopathy subtypes.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced hip strength, inability to jump, and difficulty rising from a seated position
Dysphagia and nasal regurgitation suggesting pharyngeal muscle involvement
Markedly elevated CK and elevated AST/ALT
Muscle inflammation and MHC class I expression
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital erythema and swelling
Prominent subcutaneous edema of the arms and neck
Tongue enlargement and angioedema-like initial presentation
Perivascular rather than the characteristic endomysial inflammatory biopsy pattern

data.description: Autoimmune muscle inflammation occurring with another connective tissue disease, such as systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, or mixed connective tissue disease. Positive ANA supports consideration but does not establish an overlap syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated CK and muscle-associated transaminase elevations
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt unilateral periorbital swelling with tongue enlargement is not a usual initial presentation
Extensive oral and pharyngeal edema is unusual
No reported Raynaud phenomenon, sclerodactyly, inflammatory arthritis, or other defining overlap features

data.description: An autoimmune myopathy characterized by substantial muscle injury, markedly elevated CK, and proximal weakness. Myositis-specific antibodies can be negative, although biopsy typically demonstrates prominent muscle-fiber necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated AST/ALT consistent with muscle injury
Proximal hip weakness and difficulty rising from a chair
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital erythema and pronounced subcutaneous swelling
Tongue and throat edema as the initial manifestations
Biopsy showing mild changes and perivascular inflammation rather than prominent necrosis
Preserved arm strength despite extensive edema

data.description: Nonallergic swelling caused by excess bradykinin, potentially associated with ACE inhibitors or C1-inhibitor abnormalities. It fits the initial painless facial and upper-airway swelling but does not explain the subsequent inflammatory myopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever or recent illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive proximal hip weakness and difficulty rising from a chair
Shoulder and hip pain
Markedly elevated CK and elevated AST/ALT
Extensive edema within multiple muscles on MRI
Perivascular muscle inflammation and MHC class I expression
Nasal regurgitation suggesting swallowing-muscle dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to para-phenylenediamine in black henna
data.description: A delayed hypersensitivity reaction to para-phenylenediamine, an additive commonly used in black henna. This is the most likely diagnosis given the timing and tattoo-shaped eruption.
symptoms_in_common: Onset one week after black henna application
Bullae and weeping on an erythematous plaque
Lesions closely following the tattoo design
symptoms_not_in_common: Golden crusting may suggest secondary bacterial infection, although dried inflammatory fluid can also produce crusting

data.description: A superficial bacterial infection, usually caused by toxin-producing Staphylococcus aureus, that produces fragile blisters and crusted erosions. It could complicate tattoo-associated dermatitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Precise distribution along the tattoo design is more suggestive of contact dermatitis
Delayed onset following black henna exposure suggests an allergic trigger rather than primary infection

data.description: Direct inflammatory injury from chemicals in the tattoo mixture, without requiring an allergic immune response.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammation confined to the exposed skin
symptoms_not_in_common: A one-week delay is less typical than an earlier reaction to a strong irritant
Prominent itching is more suggestive of allergic dermatitis than the burning or stinging typical of irritant dermatitis
Golden crusting may indicate an additional bacterial infection

data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction caused by a photosensitizing substance combined with ultraviolet exposure, sometimes producing patterned redness and blisters.
symptoms_in_common: A patterned eruption at a site of topical exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent itching is less typical than burning or pain
Onset one week after tattoo application is less typical of an acute phototoxic reaction
Golden crusting is not a characteristic primary finding

data.description: A bacterial infection of deeper skin tissue that can develop through disrupted skin. It is a less likely primary explanation but a possible complication.
symptoms_in_common: Disrupted skin with discharge and crusting
Bullae can occur in severe infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Itching rather than pain or tenderness predominates
The eruption closely follows the tattoo design rather than spreading diffusely
Superficial golden crusting is more characteristic of impetigo or weeping dermatitis

data.description: Long-standing monosodium urate deposition causes bulky tophi, joint destruction, and restricted movement. This is overwhelmingly the most likely diagnosis given the crystal-confirmed gout, marked hyperuricemia, and extensive nodules visible in the photographs.
symptoms_in_common: Previously demonstrated negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Markedly elevated uric acid of 725 μmol/L
Multiple nodules involving the auricle, knees, ankles, and toes
Massive nodular enlargement and deformity of both hands
Severe loss of hand flexion and extension
Elevated reported renal marker, which may indicate impaired urate clearance if the intended measurement is creatinine

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory arthritis that can cause symmetric hand deformities and subcutaneous nodules. It is a much less likely explanation than gout here, although coexistence is possible.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negatively birefringent crystals are characteristic of gout rather than rheumatoid arthritis
Marked hyperuricemia is not a defining feature
Auricular and toe nodules in this distribution favor gouty tophi
Extremely bulky, lobulated hand deposits are more suggestive of extensive tophi than typical rheumatoid nodules

data.description: Deposition of calcium pyrophosphate crystals can produce chronic inflammatory arthritis and occasionally mass-like deposits. It is unlikely to account for this presentation compared with established gout.
symptoms_in_common: Periarticular nodules could resemble rare mass-forming crystal deposits
symptoms_not_in_common: The documented negatively birefringent crystals favor monosodium urate; calcium pyrophosphate crystals are typically weakly positively birefringent
Marked hyperuricemia does not specifically support this disease
Multiple auricular and toe tophi are not typical
Widespread massive hand nodules are unusual

data.description: A rare histiocytic disorder causing papulonodular skin lesions and potentially severe destructive polyarthritis. Tissue biopsy would be needed to establish this alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple nodular lesions involving the hands and ears
symptoms_not_in_common: Crystal-confirmed gout is not explained by this disorder
Marked hyperuricemia is not characteristic
The very large confluent masses shown are more typical of advanced tophaceous gout than the usual smaller papulonodular lesions
Nodules at the toes, ankles, and knees in the described gouty distribution favor urate deposition

data.description: A disorder of bulky periarticular calcium-phosphate deposits that can impair joint movement. It is a low-probability mimic; radiographs and mineral metabolism testing would help distinguish it from tophi.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negatively birefringent joint crystals are evidence of gout rather than calcium-phosphate deposition
Marked hyperuricemia is not characteristic
Auricular nodules are not a typical distribution
Extensive finger and toe involvement is less typical than masses around larger joints

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, most likely nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A lymphoma characterized by Hodgkin/Reed–Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background. The nodular sclerosis subtype commonly affects young adults and involves mediastinal and cervical lymph nodes. This is the strongest fit, although definitive subtyping may require additional tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass visible on the supplied CT image
Scattered large atypical cells among reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells
Collagen fibrosis in the lymph node
Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma arising in the anterior mediastinum, usually in young adults, that can cause compressive respiratory symptoms and spread to nearby lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass and widened mediastinum
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered large cells in a prominent reactive inflammatory background rather than sheets of malignant B cells
CD15 positivity is unusual
CD45 negativity is atypical

data.description: A rare mediastinal B-cell lymphoma with overlapping pathological features of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells expressing CD30 and CD15
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered large cells in a mixed inflammatory background more strongly favor classical Hodgkin lymphoma
The supplied immunophenotype does not demonstrate the strong B-cell marker expression or morphological discordance generally needed to support this diagnosis

data.description: An aggressive T-cell lymphoma composed of large atypical cells with strong CD30 expression. ALK-positive disease often occurs in young people.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity is uncommon
CD45 negativity is less typical, although it can occur
Scattered large cells with eosinophils, plasma cells, and collagen fibrosis more strongly suggest classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma of immature T cells that commonly affects adolescent and young adult men and frequently presents with an anterior mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass and widened mediastinum
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered large atypical cells rather than a diffuse population of lymphoblasts
Reactive eosinophil- and plasma-cell-rich background with fibrosis
Combined CD15 and CD30 positivity is not characteristic
CD45 negativity is less typical, although lymphoblasts may express CD45 weakly

data.description: An opportunistic fungal pneumonia associated with advanced HIV infection. This is the leading consideration, although imaging alone cannot establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
Apparent bilateral perihilar interstitial and hazy pulmonary opacities on the chest radiograph

data.description: A mycobacterial lung infection that can produce atypical or diffuse radiographic findings in patients with HIV.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly perihilar hazy pattern is less typical of classic upper-lobe cavitary tuberculosis, although HIV-associated tuberculosis can have atypical appearances

data.description: An opportunistic viral lung infection generally occurring with profound immunosuppression; confirmation requires additional testing.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a potential risk factor
Bilateral interstitial or hazy pulmonary opacities

data.description: Pneumonia caused by organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae or respiratory viruses, sometimes producing diffuse rather than focal pulmonary opacities.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral patchy or interstitial pulmonary opacities

data.description: An HIV-associated vascular malignancy that can involve the lungs and produce perihilar or peribronchovascular opacities.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatively diffuse hazy opacities are less characteristic than the nodular or flame-shaped peribronchovascular opacities often associated with pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma

data.diagnosis: Lung carcinoma with pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis
data.description: Lung cancer spreading through pulmonary lymphatic vessels can cause progressive breathlessness and interlobular septal thickening. The apparent right hilar soft-tissue abnormality and predominantly right-sided septal thickening make this a leading consideration, although tissue sampling is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Older age and substantial smoking history
Predominantly right-sided interlobular septal and peribronchovascular thickening on CT
Raised D-dimer, which can occur with malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Collapse immediately after glyceryl trinitrate is not a characteristic manifestation
Absence of cough, weight loss and haemoptysis makes the presentation less classic but does not exclude lung cancer

data.diagnosis: Thoracic lymphoma with pulmonary lymphatic involvement
data.description: Lymphoma involving hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes can infiltrate or obstruct pulmonary lymphatics, producing interstitial thickening and breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent hilar or mediastinal soft-tissue enlargement
Raised D-dimer, which can accompany malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate is not typical
No reported weight loss
Markedly unilateral pulmonary involvement is less typical than more widespread thoracic disease

data.description: Fluid accumulation in the pulmonary interstitium can produce septal thickening and breathlessness. Although usually bilateral, edema can be asymmetric because of regional vascular or lymphatic obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional chest discomfort that could reflect underlying cardiac disease
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate could reflect a medication-related fall in blood pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent right hilar soft-tissue abnormality is not explained by uncomplicated cardiac edema
Predominantly unilateral interstitial abnormalities are atypical for ordinary cardiogenic edema
Raised D-dimer is not a defining feature

data.description: Thromboembolic obstruction of pulmonary arteries can cause breathlessness, chest pain and syncope. The supplied lung-window CT image cannot establish or exclude embolism; pulmonary arterial imaging is required.
symptoms_not_in_common: One month of gradually worsening symptoms is less typical of a single acute embolic event
Right-sided septal and peribronchovascular thickening is not a typical primary imaging pattern
Apparent hilar soft-tissue enlargement is not explained by uncomplicated pulmonary embolism
Collapse directly after glyceryl trinitrate also suggests a possible medication-related mechanism

data.description: A granulomatous inflammatory disorder that can cause hilar lymphadenopathy and pulmonary abnormalities along lymphatic pathways, including peribronchovascular and septal thickening.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked right-sided predominance is less typical than bilateral involvement
New presentation at age 65 is less typical
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate is not characteristic
Raised D-dimer is not a characteristic diagnostic finding

data.diagnosis: Large pericardial cyst with compressive atelectasis
data.description: A usually benign, fluid-filled sac adjacent to the pericardium. The apparent large, well-defined fluid-density lesion at the right cardiophrenic region favors this diagnosis; compression of adjacent lung can cause respiratory symptoms. The profound hypoxemia requires urgent evaluation and may have additional causes.
symptoms_in_common: Basal aegophony, potentially reflecting compressed lung
Afebrile presentation with a normal white blood cell count
Apparent right cardiophrenic cystic lesion with adjacent atelectatic change on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze is not a typical primary manifestation
Profound resting and exertional hypoxemia is unusual for an uncomplicated pericardial cyst

data.diagnosis: Bronchogenic cyst with airway or lung compression
data.description: A congenital fluid-filled lesion arising from abnormal development of the airways. Large mediastinal bronchogenic cysts can compress bronchi and adjacent lung, although the apparent cardiophrenic location is less typical.
symptoms_in_common: A well-defined cystic thoracic lesion on imaging
Absence of fever and leukocytosis if the cyst is uninfected
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Soft heart sounds
Bilateral basal aegophony is not typical of a localized bronchogenic cyst
Profound hypoxemia is uncommon without substantial compression or another pulmonary condition

data.description: Herniation of abdominal contents through an anterior diaphragmatic defect, often producing a right cardiophrenic opacity and sometimes lung compression. The apparently homogeneous fluid-density lesion is less supportive than visible herniated fat or bowel would be.
symptoms_in_common: Right cardiophrenic opacity on chest radiography
Obesity, which can increase intra-abdominal pressure
Afebrile presentation with a normal white blood cell count
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze
Soft heart sounds
The apparent cystic imaging appearance is not typical of a fat- or bowel-containing hernia
Profound hypoxemia is unusual without extensive lung compression

data.diagnosis: Loculated pleural effusion with compressive atelectasis
data.description: A localized collection of pleural fluid that can resemble a mass and compress adjacent lung. The smooth cardiophrenic lesion could represent a localized fluid collection, although its appearance favors a discrete cyst.
symptoms_in_common: An apparent fluid-density thoracic lesion with adjacent atelectatic change
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat
Wheeze is not a characteristic finding
Soft heart sounds are not usually explained by a localized pleural effusion
Absence of fever and leukocytosis argues against an infected pleural collection, but not a sterile effusion

data.diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
data.description: Acute worsening of airflow obstruction, potentially triggered by a respiratory infection. Smoking, wheeze, and severe hypoxemia support this possibility, but it would not explain the large cardiophrenic lesion and could coexist with it.
symptoms_in_common: Severe resting hypoxemia with further desaturation on exertion
Sore throat as a possible sign of a viral trigger
An exacerbation can occur without fever or leukocytosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Basal aegophony suggests an additional process such as consolidation or compression
The large apparent cystic cardiophrenic lesion is not explained by COPD
Soft heart sounds are nonspecific and do not establish COPD

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the right maxilla
data.description: An aggressive lymphoma that can involve maxillary bone and oral soft tissues. The large atypical lymphoid cells and apparent CD10-negative, BCL6-positive, MUM1-positive staining pattern favor this diagnosis, potentially a non-germinal-center phenotype; confirmation requires a complete immunohistochemical panel.
symptoms_in_common: Large localized right cheek and intraoral swelling
Obliteration of the buccal and palatal vestibules
Destructive right maxillary lesion with an associated soft-tissue mass on CT
Large atypical lymphoid-appearing cells in the supplied microscopy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GTP level is nonspecific and not a characteristic diagnostic feature

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the maxilla
data.description: A rare metastasis of colorectal cancer to jawbone or gingival tissue that can cause swelling, bone destruction, and failure of extraction sockets to heal.
symptoms_in_common: Right cheek and posterior maxillary swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied microscopy predominantly shows dispersed atypical lymphoid-appearing cells rather than recognizable adenocarcinoma glands
The apparent BCL6 and MUM1 staining pattern favors a lymphoid neoplasm rather than colorectal adenocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary gingiva or maxillary sinus
data.description: An epithelial malignancy that can invade the maxilla and present as cheek swelling, an oral mass, or a nonhealing extraction site.
symptoms_in_common: Large oral swelling extending across the buccal and palatal aspects
Maxillary bone destruction and adjacent soft-tissue involvement on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied microscopy shows predominantly dispersed lymphoid-appearing cells rather than cohesive malignant squamous nests or keratinization
The apparent BCL6 and MUM1 staining pattern is more suggestive of lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Plasmablastic lymphoma of the oral cavity
data.description: An aggressive lymphoma with plasma-cell differentiation that often affects the oral cavity. It may resemble other large-cell lymphomas and requires additional lineage markers and Epstein–Barr virus testing for distinction.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells with some plasmacytoid features
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent BCL6 expression is less typical of plasmablastic lymphoma and favors diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Abnormal GTP level is not a characteristic diagnostic feature

data.diagnosis: Post-extraction osteomyelitis of the right maxilla
data.description: Infection and inflammation of maxillary bone following dental infection or extraction, potentially causing persistent socket defects, swelling, and bone destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Recent extraction of right upper posterior teeth
Extraction sockets remaining unhealed after approximately one month
symptoms_not_in_common: The prominent bulky soft-tissue mass is more concerning for malignancy than uncomplicated post-extraction infection
Numerous large atypical lymphoid-appearing cells and the supplied immunostaining pattern are not explained by osteomyelitis alone

diagnoses.name: Primary oral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas

data.diagnosis: Steroid-modified dermatophytosis (tinea incognito involving the groin and body)
data.description: A superficial fungal infection whose appearance and spread are altered by potent topical corticosteroids. This is the leading possibility; skin scrapings for fungal microscopy and culture can confirm it.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple annular, erythematous, scaly plaques on the groin, thighs, and lower abdomen
Concentric borders and partial central clearing
Initial improvement with a clobetasol-containing cream followed by continued spread

data.description: An inflammatory dermatitis producing intensely itchy, coin-shaped, scaly plaques that can resemble fungal infection.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple rounded red plaques with scaling
Initial improvement with topical corticosteroid exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent concentric rings with partial central clearing
Raised peripheral borders suggesting outward fungal growth
Extensive groin-centered involvement

data.description: An uncommon pattern of psoriasis characterized by ring-shaped inflammatory plaques, sometimes with central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Annular lesions on the thighs and lower abdomen
Temporary improvement with a potent topical corticosteroid
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous concentric, advancing peripheral borders
Marked central clearing in several lesions
Progressive spread during use of a steroid-containing combination cream is more suggestive of steroid-modified fungal infection

data.description: A reactive inflammatory eruption producing slowly expanding annular plaques, often with fine scale just inside the advancing edge.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe itching is less typical
Prominent inflamed, scaly outer borders rather than characteristic trailing inner scale
Extensive confluent groin plaques following potent topical corticosteroid use

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to a topical medication
data.description: A delayed hypersensitivity reaction to an ingredient in a topical preparation, causing itchy inflammation where the product is applied and sometimes beyond.
symptoms_in_common: Exposure to a multi-ingredient topical cream
Temporary suppression of inflammation by clobetasol
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinct annular plaques with central clearing
Multiple concentric advancing borders
The rash preceded use of the cream, making medication allergy less likely as the original cause

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma causing gastric outlet obstruction
data.description: An infiltrative stomach cancer that can thicken and narrow the gastric wall without forming a discrete intraluminal mass. This is the leading possibility; the supplied histology appears concerning for malignant epithelial infiltration, requiring formal pathology confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening postprandial nausea and early satiety
Progression from intolerance of solid foods to inability to tolerate liquids
Large amounts of retained gastric food despite prolonged fasting
Marked gastric distention with apparent distal gastric wall thickening on CT
Nodular gastric mucosa and apparent infiltrative cells in the supplied tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly contradictory clinical symptoms; absence of a discrete intraluminal mass does not exclude infiltrative gastric cancer

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the stomach that can cause thickened folds, nodular mucosa, and occasionally obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric wall thickening and nodular mucosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe progressive gastric outlet obstruction is less typical than in stenosing gastric carcinoma
The supplied histology appears more suggestive of epithelial infiltration than a predominantly lymphoid malignancy

data.description: Chronic ulcer-associated inflammation and scarring can narrow the pylorus, producing benign gastric outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive intolerance of solids and liquids
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse nodular gastric mucosa is not typical of an isolated peptic stricture
Apparent infiltrative atypical cells in the supplied histology are not explained by benign ulcer scarring
No ulcer is described on the prior endoscopy

data.description: A rare thickening of the pyloric muscle in adults that narrows the gastric outlet and impairs gastric emptying.
symptoms_in_common: Increasing inability to tolerate oral intake
Apparent thickening near the gastric outlet
No discrete intraluminal mass on the prior endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive nodular mucosal changes are not characteristic
Apparent malignant cellular infiltration on histology is inconsistent with isolated muscular hypertrophy

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying caused by impaired gastric motility rather than a mechanical blockage; it can be idiopathic or associated with systemic disease or medications.
symptoms_in_common: Retained gastric food after prolonged fasting
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent focal distal gastric wall thickening favors mechanical obstruction
Progression to complete liquid intolerance is concerning for severe outlet obstruction
Nodular gastric mucosa and apparent infiltrative tumor cells are not explained by uncomplicated gastroparesis

data.description: An X-linked bleeding disorder caused by deficient factor IX. The sequencing image appears to show a nucleotide substitution in the infant with a mixed peak in the mother, compatible with an inherited X-linked variant, but the gene and variant are not labeled, so hemophilia B cannot be established from this image alone.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising at vitamin K and hepatitis B injection sites
Otherwise normal examination and stable vital signs
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered pinpoint petechiae are more characteristic of platelet disorders than isolated factor IX deficiency

data.description: An X-linked coagulation disorder caused by deficient factor VIII, which can present in newborn boys with bruising or bleeding after procedures. Factor assays and gene-specific testing are needed to distinguish it from hemophilia B.
symptoms_in_common: Normal general examination despite cutaneous bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: Pinpoint petechiae are not typical of isolated factor VIII deficiency

data.description: Maternal antibodies against fetal platelet antigens cause severe thrombocytopenia, often producing petechiae and bruising at birth in an otherwise healthy term infant.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae appearing within hours of birth
Full-term infant with stable vital signs
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported clinical finding strongly contradicts this diagnosis; a platelet count is essential for assessment

data.description: A rare inherited disorder of platelet production, commonly associated with MPL variants, that can cause severe thrombocytopenia from birth without obvious congenital anomalies.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of unusual facial features or other obvious congenital abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported clinical finding strongly contradicts this diagnosis, but persistent severe thrombocytopenia has not been documented

data.description: Deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors can cause bleeding within the first 24 hours, particularly after maternal exposure to medications that interfere with vitamin K. Such exposure is not reported here.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding manifestations within four hours of birth
symptoms_not_in_common: Pinpoint petechiae are less typical than bleeding caused by coagulation-factor deficiency
Absence of umbilical bleeding is less characteristic, although it does not exclude the diagnosis

data.diagnosis: Subacute or chronic right-sided subdural hematoma
data.description: The leading diagnosis: blood collecting between the dura and arachnoid, potentially caused by bridging-vein injury during forceful headbanging. The CT appears to show a crescent-shaped right-sided extra-axial collection with mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Constant, progressively worsening headache over two weeks
Headbanging several weeks before presentation, providing a possible acceleration-deceleration mechanism
Apparent right-sided crescent-shaped collection with ventricular compression and midline displacement
Normal neurological examination, which does not exclude a subdural hematoma
Normal coagulation screening, compatible with mechanically induced bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported direct head impact, although direct impact is not required

data.description: A collection of cerebrospinal fluid in the subdural space, sometimes following an arachnoid tear from minor mechanical injury. It can resemble a low-density chronic subdural hematoma.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent headache after forceful head movements
Normal neurological examination despite an intracranial collection
symptoms_not_in_common: The collection appears denser than simple cerebrospinal fluid, favoring blood rather than a pure hygroma
Marked progressive headache and apparent mass effect are less typical of a small uncomplicated hygroma

data.diagnosis: Right middle cranial fossa arachnoid cyst complicated by subdural hemorrhage
data.description: An arachnoid cyst is a usually congenital cerebrospinal-fluid-filled sac. A middle cranial fossa cyst may predispose adjacent vessels to bleeding after minor mechanical stress; the marked right temporal finding could represent such a cyst, but requires imaging confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible right temporal arachnoid cyst indicated by the marked imaging finding
symptoms_not_in_common: An uncomplicated arachnoid cyst alone would not typically explain a new hemorrhagic-appearing subdural collection
Rapidly worsening headache is less typical of a stable incidental cyst

data.description: Bleeding between the skull and dura, usually following trauma. This is a substantially less likely alternative because epidural hematomas generally have a lens-shaped appearance rather than a crescent-shaped collection.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mechanical injury associated with headbanging
Extra-axial collection with apparent mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: No direct head trauma or reported skull fracture
Delayed presentation over several weeks
Crescent-shaped rather than lens-shaped collection
Normal neurological examination despite the prolonged course

data.description: Thrombosis of intracranial venous drainage pathways can cause progressive headache, sometimes without early neurological deficits. It is less consistent with the supplied CT than a subdural collection and would require venous imaging for assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Normal routine coagulation screening does not exclude venous thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent crescent-shaped extra-axial collection is not a typical primary imaging finding
Headbanging provides a more direct explanation for a mechanically induced subdural injury
No reported thrombosis risk factors

data.description: An aggressive sarcoma that commonly involves abdominal and peritoneal tissues. It usually carries an EWSR1::WT1 fusion and can express neuroendocrine markers. This is a leading consideration, but EWSR1 rearrangement alone does not confirm it.
symptoms_in_common: Synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5 positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: Umbilical secretion shortly after surgery is not a characteristic tumor symptom
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is an unusual initial presentation

data.description: A malignant round-cell sarcoma arising outside bone, usually associated with an EWSR1::FLI1 or related fusion. Tumors with neural differentiation may express neuroendocrine markers; fusion identification and additional immunostains are needed.
symptoms_in_common: Neuroendocrine marker expression, which can occur in tumors with neural differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Omental involvement is an uncommon primary location
Postoperative umbilical secretion is not characteristic
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is not a usual presentation

data.description: A rare gastrointestinal sarcoma with neural differentiation, often carrying EWSR1::CREB1 or EWSR1::ATF1 fusions. It may spread to abdominal tissues, although a bowel-wall primary and supporting S100/SOX10 staining would strengthen this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparently omental or infraumbilical presentation without a demonstrated bowel primary is atypical
Umbilical secretion after hernia repair is not characteristic
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is not a usual presentation

data.description: An aggressive epithelial malignancy with neuroendocrine differentiation that can arise in gastrointestinal organs and metastasize to the peritoneum or omentum. The reported EWSR1 rearrangement favors an alternative sarcoma diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5 positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: EWSR1 rearrangement is not characteristic
Postoperative umbilical secretion is not a typical direct manifestation
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is an unusual presentation

data.description: A localized infection after hernia repair that can cause pain, wound drainage, and a complex mass. It could coexist with the malignancy but cannot explain the malignant histology or EWSR1 rearrangement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Malignant cells in the original omental specimen
Tumor cells expressing neuroendocrine markers
EWSR1 gene rearrangement
Absence of fever is less typical of systemic infection, although a localized abscess can be afebrile

data.diagnosis: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), potentially triggered by dabrafenib/trametinib
data.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive immune activation. The timing suggests a treatment-related trigger, although malignancy or infection could contribute. The marrow image appears compatible with hemophagocytosis, which supports but does not independently establish HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hemophagocytosis in the marrow image
symptoms_not_in_common: The original black skin nodule and metastatic lesions reflect the underlying melanoma rather than HLH itself

data.diagnosis: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
data.description: A severe drug hypersensitivity reaction involving fever, widespread rash, blood abnormalities, and internal-organ injury. Prior immune checkpoint treatment may complicate subsequent drug reactions.
symptoms_in_common: Fever after introduction of new medications
Apparent erythematous rash in the clinical image
Inflammatory skin changes in the biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: Pancytopenia rather than the more characteristic eosinophilia or atypical lymphocytosis
Marked hyperferritinemia is more suggestive of HLH
Possible marrow hemophagocytosis
Onset after 13 days is shorter than the usual latency, although earlier onset can occur

data.description: A severe infection causing systemic inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potentially widespread activation of coagulation. Infection can also trigger secondary HLH.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatosplenomegaly is less typical of acute sepsis
Possible marrow hemophagocytosis and the combined laboratory pattern favor HLH
The close temporal relationship to dabrafenib/trametinib suggests a possible noninfectious drug-related process

data.diagnosis: Dabrafenib/trametinib-associated pyrexia syndrome with systemic toxicity
data.description: A recognized adverse effect of combined BRAF and MEK inhibition that can cause fever and systemic illness, sometimes with organ dysfunction. Severe cytopenias and hyperinflammation warrant evaluation for HLH rather than attribution to uncomplicated pyrexia.
symptoms_in_common: Fever beginning 13 days after starting dabrafenib/trametinib
Apparent rash in the clinical image
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatosplenomegaly
Pancytopenia
Marked hyperferritinemia
Coagulation abnormalities
Possible marrow hemophagocytosis

data.diagnosis: Progressive metastatic melanoma with bone marrow involvement
data.description: Disseminated melanoma can infiltrate the bone marrow, causing cytopenias, and involve the liver, causing biochemical abnormalities. Advanced malignancy can also provoke systemic inflammation or secondary HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Previously resected black postauricular nodule consistent with melanoma
Jugular lymph node, lung, and liver metastases
Pancytopenia if marrow infiltration is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt fever shortly after starting targeted therapy
Splenomegaly and marked hyperferritinemia are not typical consequences of uncomplicated melanoma progression
Possible marrow hemophagocytosis suggests an inflammatory syndrome rather than demonstrating melanoma infiltration
Apparent inflammatory rash is not typical of visceral melanoma progression

data.description: Deficiency of multiple anterior pituitary hormones caused by penetrating injury. The images show a retained metallic projectile projected over the sellar region, strongly suggesting pituitary injury, although CT metal artifact limits precise localization.
symptoms_in_common: Penetrating gunshot injury through the left eye
Retained projectile projected over the sellar region
Slightly low free thyroxine with an inappropriately normal TSH
Low luteinising hormone and undetectable testosterone
Low IGF-1 and markedly low prolactin
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal stature and established pubertal development would be atypical for longstanding untreated panhypopituitarism, but are compatible with acute injury
Left-eye blindness is a consequence of the penetrating injury rather than hormone deficiency itself

data.diagnosis: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to traumatic ACTH deficiency
data.description: Inadequate pituitary ACTH secretion causes insufficient adrenal cortisol production. The profoundly low morning cortisol is particularly concerning during acute trauma; ACTH measurement would help establish the mechanism.
symptoms_in_common: Penetrating injury near the pituitary region
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemodynamic stability and preserved alertness are not typical of an established adrenal crisis, although they do not exclude adrenal insufficiency
Left-eye blindness is not explained by cortisol deficiency

data.description: Insufficient hypothalamic or pituitary stimulation of the thyroid produces low free thyroxine without an appropriately elevated TSH. The borderline thyroid results require confirmation because acute illness can also alter thyroid tests.
symptoms_in_common: Free thyroxine of 13.5 pmol/L, slightly below the reference interval
TSH of 0.63 mIU/L despite low free thyroxine
Concurrent deficiencies in other pituitary-dependent hormones
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound cortisol deficiency and undetectable testosterone are not explained by isolated central hypothyroidism
Left-eye blindness is not a typical manifestation
Normal height is less consistent with longstanding untreated childhood hypothyroidism

data.diagnosis: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism due to traumatic pituitary injury
data.description: Inadequate pituitary gonadotropin secretion leads to insufficient testicular testosterone production and may interrupt pubertal progression. Pubertal-stage-specific reference ranges and follow-up testing are important.
symptoms_in_common: Suspected injury in the sellar region
Evidence of broader anterior pituitary dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Tanner stage S3 indicates prior pubertal progression and is less typical of longstanding complete gonadotropin deficiency
Low cortisol, free thyroxine, IGF-1, and prolactin are not explained by isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Left-eye blindness is not explained by gonadotropin deficiency

data.diagnosis: Acquired growth hormone deficiency due to traumatic pituitary injury
data.description: Damage to pituitary growth hormone secretion can reduce IGF-1 and impair subsequent growth. Low IGF-1 supports suspicion but is not diagnostic alone, especially during acute illness or concurrent endocrine deficiencies.
symptoms_in_common: IGF-1 of 19.4 nmol/L, below the supplied reference interval
Multiple accompanying anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies
symptoms_not_in_common: Height of 1.7 m at the 75th percentile is not typical of longstanding untreated childhood growth hormone deficiency
Profound cortisol deficiency and undetectable testosterone are not explained by isolated growth hormone deficiency
Left-eye blindness is attributable to the traumatic injury rather than growth hormone deficiency

data.diagnosis: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to cerebral aqueduct stenosis or an aqueductal web
data.description: Narrowing or a membrane within the cerebral aqueduct blocks cerebrospinal fluid flow. This is the leading possibility: the supplied MRI appears to show marked lateral and third ventricular enlargement with a relatively small fourth ventricle and possible aqueductal obstruction. Symptomatic hydrocephalus warrants urgent pediatric neurosurgical assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive macrocephaly with head circumference crossing growth percentiles
Frontal bossing and a full fontanelle
Recurrent vomiting, lethargy, and decreased oral intake
Decreased leg tone with brisk patellar reflexes
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not explained by aqueductal obstruction
Brief symmetric shaking with preserved consciousness is nonspecific rather than a characteristic manifestation

data.diagnosis: Tectal plate glioma causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A typically slow-growing midbrain tumor can compress the cerebral aqueduct and cause hydrocephalus. The ventricular enlargement is compatible, but a definite tectal mass is not established by the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Lateral and third ventricular enlargement suggesting aqueduct-level obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Normal eye movements without gaze limitation make a symptomatic midbrain lesion less characteristic, although they do not exclude it
Brief symmetric shaking with preserved consciousness is not a characteristic presentation

data.diagnosis: Intracranial arachnoid cyst causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A cerebrospinal fluid-filled cyst, particularly near the third ventricle or quadrigeminal cistern, can compress ventricular outflow pathways. This is an alternative structural cause, although no definite separate cyst is identifiable in the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Vomiting, lethargy, and reduced oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric morning shaking is not specific to an arachnoid cyst

data.description: Prior meningitis or ventriculitis can impair cerebrospinal fluid absorption or produce scarring that obstructs ventricular flow. Hydrocephalus fits the presentation, but no preceding infection is reported, and the apparent aqueduct-level obstruction favors a focal structural cause.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive head enlargement and full fontanelle
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not a typical consequence of postinfectious hydrocephalus
The recurrent, separated vomiting episodes are less characteristic of an active central nervous system infection

data.description: A congenital posterior fossa malformation involving the cerebellar vermis and cystic enlargement of the fourth ventricle can cause hydrocephalus. It is substantially less likely here because the supplied MRI does not appear to show the characteristic enlarged fourth ventricle or posterior fossa cyst.
symptoms_in_common: Vomiting and lethargy associated with hydrocephalus
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking with preserved consciousness is not characteristic
The apparent relatively small fourth ventricle and lack of a posterior fossa cyst on MRI are atypical

diagnoses.name: Aqueductal stenosis
diagnoses.title: Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius

data.description: Sleep-disordered breathing can cause sustained hypertension through intermittent oxygen deprivation and increased sympathetic activity, particularly in people with obesity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Resting heart rate of 106 bpm is nonspecific and is not a defining feature
Very severe hypertension at age 31 warrants evaluation for additional causes rather than attribution to sleep apnea alone

data.description: Hypertension without a single identifiable secondary cause; obesity and sleep apnea increase its likelihood. These severe readings warrant prompt clinical assessment.
symptoms_in_common: No renal artery stenosis on Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe hypertension at a young age raises concern for a secondary cause
Persistent lethargy is not usually explained by uncomplicated primary hypertension
Resting tachycardia is not a defining feature

data.description: Excess aldosterone production causes sodium retention and hypertension. Potassium can remain normal, so normal electrolytes do not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Sleep apnea, which is associated with an increased likelihood of primary aldosteronism
Headaches compatible with marked blood pressure elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal electrolytes lack the classic hypokalemia, although this is frequently absent
Resting tachycardia is not a characteristic feature
Obesity and lethargy are nonspecific rather than characteristic manifestations

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumor that can cause sustained or episodic hypertension, headaches, and tachycardia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Obesity is not a characteristic manifestation
Prolonged lethargy is nonspecific
No tremor was found, although its absence does not exclude the disease

data.description: Chronic cortisol excess can cause secondary hypertension, weight gain, and fatigue. The absence of characteristic physical findings makes this possibility less strongly supported.
symptoms_not_in_common: No cushingoid features on examination
Resting tachycardia is not a defining feature
Intermittent headaches are nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.diagnosis: Vasospastic angina with spasm-induced myocardial infarction and cardiac arrest
data.description: Transient coronary artery constriction can cause severe myocardial ischemia, infarction, and fatal arrhythmias despite otherwise normal coronary arteries. Sumatriptan can provoke coronary spasm. This is a leading possibility given the previous documented spasm.
symptoms_in_common: Previous chest pain after sumatriptan use
Previous transient inferior and lateral ST elevation
Previously normal coronary arteries apart from minor right coronary ostial spasm and slow flow
Marked anterior ST elevation on the supplied ECG
Markedly elevated troponin during the current episode
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly anterior current ECG changes differ from the previously documented right coronary ostial spasm, although multivessel or different-territory spasm is possible

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction from coronary thrombosis
data.description: Acute coronary obstruction, usually involving the left anterior descending artery in an anterior infarction, causes myocardial necrosis and can trigger cardiac arrest. The supplied ECG and troponin require urgent evaluation for acute coronary occlusion.
symptoms_in_common: Marked anterior ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Previously normal left coronary system, although this does not exclude a new obstruction
Previous transient ST elevation with negative troponin
Previous sumatriptan-associated chest pain and documented coronary spasm favor a vasospastic mechanism

data.description: A spontaneous tear or intramural hematoma in a coronary artery can obstruct blood flow and produce acute myocardial infarction, particularly in middle-aged women without substantial atherosclerosis.
symptoms_in_common: Marked anterior ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous sumatriptan-triggered chest pain with transient ST elevation is more suggestive of vasospasm
Previous angiography documented ostial spasm and slow flow rather than dissection

data.description: Transient ventricular dysfunction that can mimic acute myocardial infarction with chest pain, ST elevation, and elevated troponin despite no obstructive coronary disease. Severe cases may cause shock or cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous medication-associated episodes and documented coronary spasm are more characteristic of vasospastic angina
Recurrent transient inferior and lateral ST elevation with negative troponin is less characteristic of Takotsubo syndrome

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium can cause chest pain, myocardial injury, ST elevation, and life-threatening arrhythmias, mimicking an acute coronary syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous chest pain closely associated with sumatriptan exposure
Previously documented coronary spasm
