Previous transient ST elevation without troponin elevation is less supportive of inflammatory myocardial injury

data.diagnosis: Fecal impaction with stercoral colitis and obstructive megacolon
data.description: Impacted stool can obstruct the colon and cause extreme dilation, pressure-related inflammation, and bowel ischemia. The substantial pelvic stool burden and massive colonic dilation on the supplied images favor this possibility; suspected bowel-wall gas raises concern for complications.
symptoms_in_common: Longstanding severe constipation associated with neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Four days of acute constipation and vomiting
Marked abdominal distension and diffuse tenderness
Marked colonic dilation and substantial pelvic fecal loading on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No guarding or rigidity, which would be more typical if perforation or advanced peritonitis had developed

data.description: Twisting of a redundant sigmoid colon causes a closed-loop large-bowel obstruction and can compromise its blood supply. Severe chronic constipation and neurologic disease are predisposing factors, although a definite twist cannot be established from the supplied images alone.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying neurologic disease and bowel dysmotility
Massively dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantial stool retention in the distal pelvic bowel is less typical of a complete sigmoid volvulus, which often leaves the rectum decompressed

data.description: Also called Ogilvie syndrome, this is acute colonic dilation without a mechanical blockage, usually associated with illness, neurologic dysfunction, or medications. Severe dilation can progress to ischemia or perforation.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple sclerosis and cerebral palsy with neurogenic bowel dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pelvic fecal loading suggests an impacted-stool mechanism rather than uncomplicated pseudo-obstruction
Marked tachycardia and suspected bowel-wall gas are not typical of uncomplicated pseudo-obstruction and suggest a complication

data.description: Failure of intestinal propulsion produces functional obstruction without a physical blockage. Neurologic dysfunction, medications, metabolic disturbances, and inflammation can contribute.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme, predominantly colonic dilation is less typical than the more generalized small- and large-bowel dilation of ileus
Substantial pelvic fecal loading favors fecal impaction
Suspected bowel-wall gas is not typical of uncomplicated ileus

data.diagnosis: Acute colonic ischemia secondary to severe distension or obstruction
data.description: Reduced blood supply to the colon can result from excessive intraluminal pressure or strangulating obstruction. Suspected pneumatosis on the supplied CT images warrants urgent assessment, although it does not by itself prove bowel necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated C-reactive protein and mildly elevated lactate
Possible gas within the bowel wall on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Constipation rather than the bloody diarrhea commonly seen in mucosal ischemic colitis
No reported rectal bleeding
Normal blood pressure and near-normal pH do not suggest established shock or advanced systemic acidosis
No guarding or rigidity to suggest established peritonitis

data.description: An opportunistic fungal pneumonia, usually associated with impaired cellular immunity. The fluorescent image appears compatible with clustered Pneumocystis cyst forms, although the stain and specimen must be confirmed. This diagnosis alone would not explain the meningitic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Patchy bilateral pulmonary opacities on the supplied CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Neck stiffness and photophobia
Prominent headaches suggesting meningitis
Yellow sputum rather than the more typical dry cough
Prominent wheezing
Five-month respiratory course is less typical than a course of weeks

data.diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmonary infection and meningitis
data.description: Cryptococcus infection can involve the lungs and spread to the central nervous system, causing subacute meningitis. It provides a potential unifying explanation for the respiratory and neurological illness, but requires cryptococcal antigen testing and microbiological confirmation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing and chest tightness are less characteristic
Thin yellow sputum is not a characteristic feature
The fluorescent structures are not clearly characteristic of encapsulated cryptococcal yeast

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with pulmonary involvement and tuberculous meningitis
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can cause chronic pulmonary disease and disseminate to the meninges. Healthcare employment may increase exposure risk, depending on the work setting.
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheezing and chest tightness are less characteristic
Abrupt development of systemic symptoms over 10 days is less typical of the usual insidious course
The fluorescent image does not resemble typical acid-fast bacilli

data.diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with central nervous system involvement
data.description: Histoplasma capsulatum is an inhaled fungus that can cause pulmonary infection and, less commonly, disseminated disease with meningitis. Travel to endemic regions makes exposure possible, but does not establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing is less characteristic
Thin yellow sputum is nonspecific rather than characteristic
The fluorescent image is not typical of the small intracellular budding yeasts expected in histoplasmosis

data.description: Legionella bacteria cause pneumonia with prominent systemic symptoms, sometimes after travel-associated exposure to contaminated water aerosols. Neurological symptoms can occur, but true meningitis is unusual.
symptoms_not_in_common: Five months of respiratory symptoms is inconsistent with the usual acute illness
Neck stiffness and photophobia suggesting meningitis are unusual
Prominent chronic wheezing is not characteristic
The fluorescent image is not typical of Legionella bacilli

data.description: A complement-mediated glomerular disease characterized by dominant C3 deposition and highly electron-dense deposits within glomerular basement membranes. The apparent basement-membrane deposits in the electron micrographs make this a leading consideration, although stain identities and a formal pathology interpretation are needed.
symptoms_in_common: Negative autoimmune, infectious, and serum protein electrophoresis studies
Apparent glomerular fluorescence and dense basement-membrane deposits on the supplied biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lumbar pain is less typical than a generalized glomerular presentation
Normal blood pressure and absence of peripheral edema are less typical of advanced nephritic disease

data.description: An alternative-complement-pathway disorder producing predominantly C3-containing glomerular deposits. Unlike dense deposit disease, deposits are generally distributed in mesangial and capillary-wall locations without the characteristic continuous, highly dense intramembranous ribbons.
symptoms_in_common: Glomerular fluorescence and structural abnormalities on the biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lumbar pain is not a characteristic presenting feature
The apparent markedly dense intramembranous material would favor dense deposit disease instead
Absence of edema and hypertension is less typical of a substantial nephritic presentation

data.description: An immune-complex glomerular disease defined by predominant mesangial IgA deposition, often causing visible hematuria. Confirmation requires identification of the immunofluorescence stains.
symptoms_in_common: Lumbar pain, which can accompany episodes of gross hematuria
Normal blood pressure and absence of edema can occur
Negative systemic autoimmune and infectious studies
Apparent mesangial fluorescence in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly dense, extensive basement-membrane deposits are not characteristic
Moderate normocytic anemia is not typical of uncomplicated IgA nephropathy

data.description: A glomerular injury pattern caused by immune-complex deposition, with mesangial proliferation and capillary-wall remodeling. It may be associated with infection, autoimmune disease, or monoclonal proteins, but can remain idiopathic.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent glomerular remodeling and deposits on the biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lumbar pain is not a usual defining feature
Normal blood pressure and absence of edema are less typical of clinically significant disease
Negative infectious, autoimmune, and serum protein electrophoresis studies provide no identified secondary cause
If the fluorescence is C3-only, that would favor C3 glomerulopathy rather than immune-complex disease

data.description: A rare glomerular disease caused by deposition of randomly arranged fibrils, usually associated with IgG staining and DNAJB9 positivity. Electron microscopy and specific immunostaining are necessary for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Glomerular deposits and structural injury on biopsy
Negative systemic studies do not exclude this disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lumbar pain is not characteristic
Absence of edema and hypertension is less typical of substantial disease
The supplied electron micrographs do not clearly demonstrate the characteristic randomly arranged fibrils

data.description: Abnormal connections between uterine arteries and veins can develop after pregnancy loss and cause recurrent, severe bleeding. This is an important possibility, but the supplied images appear black and cannot support diagnostic interpretation. Active bleeding with this degree of anaemia requires urgent assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bleeding shortly after medical treatment
Marked anaemia with reported haemoglobin of 77
History of miscarriage a few months earlier

data.description: Placental or other pregnancy tissue remaining in the uterus after miscarriage can cause persistent or recurrent bleeding, sometimes with increased uterine vascularity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation several months after miscarriage is less typical than bleeding soon after pregnancy loss, although delayed presentation can occur

data.description: A contained injury to a uterine artery can cause intermittent or sudden major uterine haemorrhage. It is usually associated with pregnancy-related vascular injury or uterine instrumentation, which is not documented here.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bleeding after apparent initial improvement

data.description: Persistent or malignant pregnancy-related trophoblastic tissue, including choriocarcinoma, can develop after miscarriage and cause uterine bleeding. Assessment requires serum beta-hCG testing and appropriate imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding months after a pregnancy loss

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumour protruding into the uterine cavity can cause heavy menstrual bleeding, anaemia, and occasionally pregnancy loss.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bleeding despite initial medical treatment
History of miscarriage, which may occur with cavity-distorting fibroids
symptoms_not_in_common: The post-miscarriage timing is less specifically explained by a fibroid than by a pregnancy-related uterine disorder

data.description: Post-infectious bowel dysfunction can cause abdominal discomfort and altered bowel habits after an acute diarrheal illness. This best fits the second presentation, although three weeks of symptoms is insufficient to meet formal IBS duration criteria. Positive C. difficile PCR may reflect colonization rather than active infection.
symptoms_in_common: Preceding episode of severe watery diarrhea
Initial recovery followed by new abdominal discomfort
Abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
Normal examination, blood counts, and albumin
symptoms_not_in_common: Only three weeks of current symptoms, which does not meet formal IBS duration criteria
The initial episode of 10–12 watery stools daily is more suggestive of acute infection or antibiotic-associated diarrhea than IBS

data.diagnosis: Clostridioides difficile infection, with possible recurrence
data.description: An antibiotic-associated intestinal infection that typically causes frequent unformed stools and abdominal pain. The initial illness is compatible with this diagnosis, but recurrent active infection is less convincing because the current stools are formed. PCR detects toxigenic organisms but does not establish active toxin-mediated disease.
symptoms_in_common: Recent azithromycin exposure before the initial illness
Initial abdominal pain and frequent watery diarrhea
Positive C. difficile PCR at the second presentation
Renewed gastrointestinal symptoms after an interval of recovery
symptoms_not_in_common: Current Bristol type 4 stools rather than unformed diarrhea
Abdominal discomfort specifically relieved by bowel movements
Normal WBC and unremarkable examination, which argue against severe infection but do not exclude mild infection

data.description: Antibiotics can disrupt intestinal microbiota and cause diarrhea without active C. difficile infection. This could explain the initial episode; residual microbiome disruption could contribute to later bowel changes.
symptoms_in_common: Onset of watery diarrhea after azithromycin
Abdominal pain during the initial illness
Normal blood counts and albumin at the later presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: A symptom-free interval followed by a separate episode six weeks later
Current increased frequency of formed stools rather than diarrhea
Positive C. difficile PCR, which raises an alternative explanation but can also represent colonization

data.description: A protozoal intestinal infection that can cause prolonged or fluctuating diarrhea and abdominal discomfort. It is a less likely alternative because no exposure history is provided and the current stools are formed.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal symptoms recurring over several weeks
Normal routine laboratory studies can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Current Bristol type 4 stools rather than persistent loose, greasy, or malabsorptive stools
Complete return to baseline between episodes is less characteristic of ongoing infection
Positive C. difficile PCR is not explained by giardiasis
The temporal association with azithromycin favors an antibiotic-related cause

data.description: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis cause chronic or relapsing intestinal inflammation with abdominal pain and altered bowel habits. They are less likely here because the current presentation lacks clear inflammatory features, although normal laboratory studies do not exclude mild disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Current formed stools
Discomfort relieved by bowel movements favors a functional bowel disorder
Normal WBC, hemoglobin, platelets, and albumin provide little evidence of systemic inflammation
Initial symptoms closely following antibiotic exposure favor an antibiotic-associated process
Positive C. difficile PCR is not explained by inflammatory bowel disease alone

diagnoses.name: Clostridioides difficile colonization
diagnoses.title: Intestinal infections due to Clostridioides difficile

data.diagnosis: Progressive disseminated histoplasmosis with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: An opportunistic fungal infection that can disseminate to the lungs, gastrointestinal tract, lymph nodes, and bone marrow in advanced HIV. Residence in Central America and agricultural exposure increase its plausibility; tissue examination and fungal antigen testing are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Profound immunosuppression with a CD4 count of 10/mm³
Fever and marked unintentional weight loss
Severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and gastrointestinal bleeding
Diffuse tiny pulmonary nodules on the supplied chest images
Apparent mesenteric lymphadenopathy on the abdominal image
symptoms_not_in_common: White oral exudate is more suggestive of concurrent candidiasis
Pain radiating to the throat is not a characteristic manifestation
Chronic flat hyperpigmentation of the legs is nonspecific rather than a typical histoplasmosis skin lesion

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with miliary pulmonary and abdominal involvement
data.description: Disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can produce innumerable small pulmonary nodules and abdominal lymph node or intestinal disease, especially in advanced HIV.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, cachexia, and substantial weight loss
Diffuse pulmonary micronodules compatible with a miliary pattern
Abdominal pain and reduced oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: White exudate beneath the tongue is not typical of tuberculosis
Throat-radiating epigastric pain and hematemesis are less typical presentations
Chronic macular leg hyperpigmentation is not a usual manifestation

data.description: A disseminated opportunistic mycobacterial infection seen predominantly when CD4 counts fall below 50/mm³. It can involve abdominal lymph nodes, intestinal tissue, liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain, nausea, and poor oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse miliary pulmonary nodules are less characteristic than in tuberculosis or histoplasmosis
Hematemesis and severe throat-radiating pain are not usual dominant manifestations
White oral exudate suggests a separate mucosal infection
Chronic leg hyperpigmentation is not characteristic

data.description: CMV can cause ulcerative gastrointestinal disease in advanced HIV, producing painful swallowing or upper abdominal pain and sometimes bleeding. Endoscopy with biopsy is needed to establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Profound immunosuppression with a CD4 count below 50/mm³
Severe epigastric pain radiating toward the throat and worsened by eating
Nausea, vomiting, and decreased oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse pulmonary micronodules are not typical of isolated CMV gastrointestinal disease
Peripheral and mesenteric lymphadenopathy are not characteristic
White oral exudate is more consistent with concurrent candidiasis
Chronic leg hyperpigmentation is not typical

data.diagnosis: HIV-associated non-Hodgkin lymphoma with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: An aggressive lymphoid malignancy associated with HIV that may involve abdominal lymph nodes and the gastrointestinal tract, causing systemic symptoms, pain, obstruction, or bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and gastrointestinal bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: Uniform diffuse pulmonary micronodules favor a disseminated infection over typical lymphoma
White oral exudate suggests concurrent candidiasis rather than lymphoma
Chronic macular leg hyperpigmentation is not characteristic
Sore throat is not a typical manifestation without direct local involvement

data.description: A mature T-cell malignancy associated with HTLV-1 that can involve skin, lymph nodes, and blood. This is a leading consideration, but confirmation requires immunophenotyping and additional hematologic and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse pruritic rash with patches and plaques
Skin biopsy images showing prominent epidermal lymphocyte aggregates suggestive of an epidermotropic T-cell lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Palmoplantar collarettes of scale are not a characteristic finding
Wrinkled axillary plaques are not specific to this malignancy
The leg injury is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: A cutaneous T-cell lymphoma typically presenting with chronic, pruritic patches and plaques. Epidermotropism and intraepidermal lymphocyte collections, called Pautrier microabscesses, support this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy images suggestive of epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
Lymphadenopathy and weight loss can occur with advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: HTLV-1 positivity favors consideration of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma rather than conventional mycosis fungoides
Palmoplantar collarettes of scale are not characteristic
The leg injury is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: A leukemic cutaneous T-cell lymphoma characterized by widespread erythroderma, marked pruritus, lymphadenopathy, and circulating malignant T cells.
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete brown patches and wrinkled plaques rather than documented generalized erythroderma
Palmoplantar collarettes of scale are not characteristic
HTLV-1 positivity suggests an alternative T-cell malignancy

data.diagnosis: Secondary syphilis due to reinfection or treatment failure
data.description: Disseminated Treponema pallidum infection that can produce a generalized rash, palmoplantar lesions, and lymphadenopathy. Prior treatment does not exclude reinfection.
symptoms_in_common: Brown macules and patches involving the palms and soles
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked pruritus is less typical
Wrinkled axillary plaques are not characteristic
Two years of substantial weight loss is not typical of uncomplicated secondary syphilis
Prominent intraepidermal lymphocyte aggregates in the biopsy images favor a lymphoproliferative disorder

data.description: An inflammatory skin disorder causing itching, scaling, and chronic thickened or hyperpigmented plaques. Renal-associated pruritus may aggravate scratching and eczematous changes.
symptoms_in_common: Wrinkled or chronically altered flexural skin
End-stage renal disease, which can contribute to pruritus
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantial unintentional weight loss is not explained
Bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy requires another explanation unless reactive
Palmoplantar collarettes of scale are not characteristic
The prominent intraepidermal lymphocyte aggregates shown are more concerning for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma than routine eczema

data.description: A potentially rapidly progressive inflammatory heart disease causing myocardial injury, conduction block, and ventricular arrhythmias. The biopsy image appears to show multinucleated giant cells within inflamed myocardium, making this a leading possibility; urgent specialist evaluation is warranted.
symptoms_in_common: Recent onset of exertional chest fullness and dyspnea
ECG evidence suggestive of advanced atrioventricular block
Wide-complex tachycardia on the supplied ECG, concerning for ventricular tachycardia
Apparent giant cells and inflammatory infiltration in the myocardial biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal troponin I is less typical of substantial active myocardial injury but does not exclude it
No clinical signs of heart failure despite the potentially severe electrical abnormalities
Family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation involving the heart that can produce atrioventricular block, ventricular tachycardia, and ventricular dysfunction. Histologic distinction from giant cell myocarditis requires assessment for well-formed noncaseating granulomas and the pattern of myocardial injury.
symptoms_in_common: ECG evidence suggestive of advanced atrioventricular block
Wide-complex tachycardia concerning for ventricular tachycardia
Giant-cell-containing myocardial inflammation on the supplied biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported extracardiac manifestations of sarcoidosis, although isolated cardiac disease is possible
The biopsy image does not clearly demonstrate well-formed granulomas
Family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is not explained

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium, often viral or immune-mediated, that may cause chest discomfort, dyspnea, conduction abnormalities, and ventricular arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute onset of chest fullness and dyspnea
Conduction abnormalities on the supplied ECG
Wide-complex tachycardia concerning for ventricular tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous apparent multinucleated giant cells favor another inflammatory myocarditis subtype
No fever or preceding infectious illness is reported
Normal troponin I is less typical but does not exclude myocarditis

data.diagnosis: Coronary artery disease with myocardial ischemia
data.description: Reduced coronary blood flow can cause exertional angina and dyspnea and may provoke ventricular arrhythmias. Normal troponin does not exclude ischemia without infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional central chest fullness without rest symptoms
Precordial ST-T abnormalities on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Giant-cell-containing myocardial inflammation is not explained by ordinary coronary artery disease
Advanced atrioventricular block without evidence of infarction is less typical
Family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is not explained

data.description: An often inherited disorder of myocardial thickening that can cause exertional chest discomfort, dyspnea, and ventricular arrhythmias, with or without outflow obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Previously documented mild left ventricular hypertrophy
Repolarization abnormalities and possible ventricular tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Giant cells and myocardial inflammatory infiltration are not characteristic
Advanced atrioventricular block is not a typical presenting feature
Prior imaging showed only mild hypertrophy, which could also reflect hypertension

data.description: A sterile neutrophilic inflammatory skin disorder that can be triggered by surgery and cause progressive ulceration. The photographed wound's broad ulceration and violaceous borders are suggestive, but infection must be excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing cesarean surgical wound despite treatment
Extensive wound ulceration with violaceous borders in the photograph
Markedly elevated and rising inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Antepartum sore throat and flu-like symptoms
Preterm uterine contractions
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Fetal late decelerations

data.description: A bacterial infection involving the cesarean incision or deeper tissues, potentially causing wound breakdown, abscess formation, and systemic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Inflamed wound margins and yellowish wound material in the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever and flu-like illness beginning before surgery
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Violaceous ulcer borders, which suggest an inflammatory ulcerative disorder rather than routine infection

data.description: A rapidly progressive infection of subcutaneous tissue and fascia that can follow surgery. It is an urgent diagnosis to exclude when wound destruction accompanies persistent systemic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Surgical wound breakdown with extensive tissue ulceration
Failure to improve with initial treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Antepartum headache and sore throat
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
The photographed superficial ulcer with violaceous borders is less characteristic than rapidly spreading deep tissue necrosis

data.description: An acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis associated with pregnancy or preceding infection. Trauma can provoke lesions, although extensive postoperative ulceration is less typical than in pyoderma gangrenosum.
symptoms_in_common: Preceding flu-like illness and sore throat
Inflammatory skin disease arising at a surgical site
symptoms_not_in_common: Large, non-healing ulcerated incision rather than typical raised plaques or nodules
Violaceous ulcer borders
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Fetal late decelerations

data.description: Listeria monocytogenes infection during pregnancy can produce a maternal flu-like illness and infect the placenta or fetus, causing preterm labor and fetal compromise. It would not usually explain the photographed wound by itself.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilic leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive postoperative ulceration with violaceous borders
Persistent non-healing surgical wound
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are not defining features

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with anterior cervical osteophytes
data.description: A disorder causing ossification along spinal ligaments and prominent anterior bony growths. The image appears to show bulky anterior cervical ossification, which can compress the pharynx and impair swallowing; additional imaging is needed to confirm DISH.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive difficulty swallowing over one year
Increasing episodes of choking and aspiration
Posterior extraluminal compression seen on laryngeal examination
Apparent prominent anterior cervical bony growths on imaging

data.diagnosis: Degenerative cervical spondylosis with large anterior osteophytes
data.description: Age-related cervical degeneration can produce anterior bone spurs that mechanically obstruct swallowing and interfere with airway protection.
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent bulky, multilevel anterior ossification may favor DISH over ordinary degenerative spondylosis

data.description: An outpouching of the posterior hypopharynx that retains food and can cause dysphagia, choking, regurgitation, and aspiration in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fixed posterior extraluminal obstruction is less typical than a pouch arising from the pharyngeal wall
Apparent anterior cervical bony growths are not explained by a diverticulum

data.description: Impaired relaxation or thickening of the upper esophageal sphincter can restrict passage of swallowed material and cause aspiration; a cricopharyngeal bar may produce a posterior indentation on swallow imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior narrowing at the pharyngoesophageal region
symptoms_not_in_common: Laryngeal examination describing extraluminal obstruction favors an external structural cause
Apparent bulky cervical bony growths are not caused by cricopharyngeal dysfunction

data.description: A tumor or other space-occupying lesion behind the pharynx can externally compress the swallowing passage. Cross-sectional imaging would distinguish a soft-tissue mass from osteophyte-related compression.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior extraluminal obstruction on laryngeal examination
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied image appears to favor a bony cervical source of compression rather than a discrete soft-tissue mass

data.description: An aggressive, poorly differentiated carcinoma defined by a NUTM1 gene rearrangement, often arising in thoracic midline structures in young people. It can resemble thymic carcinoma; confirmation requires NUT immunohistochemistry or molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with progressive exertional dyspnea
Reduced left-sided breath sounds with extensive left thoracic soft-tissue opacity on the provided CT image
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly contradictory symptoms; the reported findings are compatible but not diagnostic

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from the thymus that can invade adjacent thoracic structures and cause respiratory symptoms. The initial biopsy interpretation supports consideration, although the patient's age is unusually young.
symptoms_in_common: Poorly differentiated carcinoma initially interpreted as thymic carcinoma
Decreased left-sided breath sounds and dullness to percussion
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 22 is less typical than presentation in middle-aged or older adults

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that commonly affects young women and produces a bulky anterior mediastinal mass. Tissue morphology and immunohistochemistry are needed because flow cytometry alone may not reliably exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced breath sounds suggesting associated thoracic compression or pleural involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than lymphoma
Polyclonal B cells without an identified malignant population on tissue flow cytometry

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A lymphoma frequently affecting young adults, often with bulky mediastinal involvement. Routine flow cytometry may be negative because the malignant Hodgkin and Reed–Sternberg cells are sparse.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported fever, although fever is not required for this diagnosis

data.diagnosis: Primary mediastinal nonseminomatous germ cell tumor
data.description: A malignant extragonadal germ cell tumor that can present as a large mediastinal mass in young adults. Some components can resemble poorly differentiated carcinoma; serum AFP, beta-hCG, and tissue immunohistochemistry help distinguish it.
symptoms_in_common: Poorly differentiated malignant tissue on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex is unusual for a primary mediastinal nonseminomatous germ cell tumor
Initial tissue interpretation favored thymic carcinoma rather than a germ cell tumor

data.description: A rare cause of ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome involving small cortisol-producing nodules in both adrenal glands. The apparent small bilateral adrenal abnormalities could fit, but imaging alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Long-standing easy bruising with worsening in later life
Late-night cortisol suggesting loss of the normal nighttime nadir
Dex-CRH results potentially consistent with mild endogenous cortisol excess
History of nephrolithiasis, which can occur with cortisol-related hypercalciuria
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 71 is less typical than presentation in younger patients
Hematuria is not a direct characteristic of this disease

data.description: Bilateral adrenal nodular enlargement that can produce ACTH-independent cortisol excess, often with a mild or slowly progressive presentation in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Possible bilateral adrenal abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
The supplied CT does not clearly demonstrate the bulky enlargement and large nodules characteristic of macronodular hyperplasia

data.description: A benign adrenal tumor that secretes cortisol independently of ACTH, causing mild autonomous cortisol secretion or overt adrenal Cushing syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Dex-CRH findings raising concern for endogenous hypercortisolism
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a usual direct manifestation
Possible bilateral adrenal abnormalities are less typical than a single dominant adrenal mass

data.description: Pituitary ACTH secretion, usually from an adenoma, causing excess adrenal cortisol production. ACTH measurement and further endocrine testing are needed to distinguish it from adrenal causes.
symptoms_in_common: Loss of the normal late-night cortisol nadir
Dex-CRH cortisol values that may support endogenous hypercortisolism, depending on the assay and protocol
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a direct typical feature
Discrete adrenal nodules, if confirmed, are not the primary lesion in Cushing disease

data.description: Also called pseudo-Cushing syndrome, this is cortisol elevation associated with conditions such as depression, alcohol use disorder, or severe physiological stress. Borderline endocrine results can overlap with mild Cushing syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Borderline Dex-CRH results may overlap with this condition
Osteoporosis can coexist, depending on the underlying cause
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive easy bruising is more suggestive of sustained pathological cortisol excess
Adrenal nodules are not explained by this diagnosis
Hematuria and prior nephrolithiasis are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: An immune-mediated glomerular disease causing substantial urinary protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, and edema. Associated hypercoagulability can cause renal vein or inferior vena cava thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Normal creatinine despite substantial protein loss
Abdominal distention consistent with fluid accumulation
Flank pain potentially resulting from associated renal vein thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated TSH and low free thyroxine indicate concomitant hypothyroidism rather than a defining feature
Pain initially provoked by prolonged standing is not specific to glomerular disease

data.diagnosis: Renal vein thrombosis with inferior vena cava involvement
data.description: Venous thrombosis can cause flank pain, hematuria, and impaired lower-body venous drainage. The CT images raise concern for central venous thrombosis with associated soft-tissue edema and pelvic fluid; nephrotic syndrome is a possible underlying trigger.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive edema extending from the feet to the thighs
Possible venous filling abnormalities on the supplied CT images
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hypoalbuminemia and hypoproteinemia suggest an underlying protein-losing disorder rather than thrombosis alone
Urine protein of 3+ may reflect an underlying glomerular disease
Elevated TSH and low free thyroxine are not explained by venous thrombosis

data.description: A podocyte disorder that causes nephrotic syndrome, often with profound protein loss and edema despite preserved kidney function. Diagnosis generally requires kidney biopsy in adults.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal distention potentially due to ascites
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopic hematuria is less characteristic, although possible
A slowly progressive 10-month course is less typical than a more abrupt presentation
Back and flank pain are not typical unless a complication such as thrombosis occurs
Biochemical hypothyroidism is not a defining feature

data.description: Scarring affecting portions of some glomeruli, which can cause nephrotic-range proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and progressive kidney dysfunction. Kidney function may remain normal early in the disease.
symptoms_in_common: Normal creatinine, which does not exclude early disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Flank and back pain are not typical of uncomplicated disease
Pain and swelling specifically following prolonged standing are nonspecific
Elevated TSH and low free thyroxine require a separate explanation

data.diagnosis: Lupus nephritis, particularly class V membranous lupus nephritis
data.description: Immune-complex kidney disease associated with systemic lupus erythematosus. Class V disease can present predominantly with nephrotic syndrome and preserved kidney function.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal distention potentially due to ascites
Normal creatinine, compatible with a predominantly membranous pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Flank and back pain are not typical unless a vascular or other complication is present
Standing-related foot and ankle pain is not characteristic
Biochemical hypothyroidism is not a defining manifestation of lupus nephritis

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

data.description: Gallbladder inflammation without gallstones, occurring as a rare complication of acute Epstein–Barr virus infection. The supplied images appear to show gallbladder wall thickening and edema without an obvious stone, supporting this possibility, although hepatitis can also cause reactive wall thickening.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness
Jaundice and cholestatic liver function abnormalities
Inflamed oropharynx and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and confirmatory Epstein–Barr virus serology
Apparent gallbladder wall thickening and edema on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign is less typical of acute cholecystitis but does not exclude it
Prominent itching, dark urine, and pale stools suggest accompanying cholestatic hepatitis rather than isolated gallbladder inflammation

data.diagnosis: Epstein–Barr virus infectious mononucleosis with cholestatic hepatitis
data.description: Acute Epstein–Barr virus infection causing liver inflammation and impaired bile flow. This strongly fits the confirmed infection, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, and cholestatic jaundice; reactive gallbladder edema may accompany hepatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Positive Monospot and confirmatory Epstein–Barr virus serology
Jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools
Elevated aspartate aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin
Abdominal discomfort and right upper quadrant tenderness
Apparent splenic enlargement on the supplied abdominal image
symptoms_not_in_common: Pronounced focal gallbladder wall abnormalities may indicate concurrent cholecystitis rather than uncomplicated hepatitis
Marked symptomatic cholestasis is an uncommon presentation of infectious mononucleosis

data.diagnosis: Acute ascending cholangitis due to biliary obstruction
data.description: Infection of the bile ducts, usually caused by obstruction such as a common bile duct stone. Fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain warrant consideration of this potentially urgent diagnosis, although the confirmed Epstein–Barr virus infection offers a stronger unifying explanation.
symptoms_in_common: Dark urine, pale stools, and itching
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Generalized cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and confirmatory Epstein–Barr virus serology
Apparent splenic enlargement

data.diagnosis: Acute calculous cholecystitis with possible choledocholithiasis
data.description: Gallstone-related gallbladder inflammation, with a possible common bile duct stone accounting for jaundice and cholestasis. Gallbladder wall thickening is compatible, but the supplied images do not establish a gallstone or ductal obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain and tenderness
Jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools if a common bile duct stone is also present
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Confirmed acute Epstein–Barr virus infection
Marked cholestasis is not typical of uncomplicated cholecystitis without bile duct involvement

data.description: A viral mononucleosis-like illness that can produce fever and liver inflammation, occasionally with cholestasis. It is substantially less likely here because the Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology support Epstein–Barr virus infection.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice and cholestasis can occur, although they are uncommon
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent oropharyngeal inflammation is less typical than in Epstein–Barr virus mononucleosis
Positive Monospot and confirmatory Epstein–Barr virus serology favor a different cause
Focal right upper quadrant tenderness with substantial gallbladder wall edema is not typical
Severe itching, dark urine, and pale stools are uncommon in uncomplicated cytomegalovirus mononucleosis

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa with bilateral renal infarction
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause renal arterial narrowing, microaneurysms, and infarction. The apparent bilateral renal perfusion defects on CT and multiple renal arterial aneurysmal abnormalities on angiography strongly favor this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe abdominal and flank pain
Previous self-resolving episode of contralateral flank pain
Elevated creatinine and proteinuria with bland urine sediment
Elevated LDH, consistent with renal tissue ischemia
Fatigue, mild anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated ESR and CRP
Apparent bilateral renal infarcts and renal arterial microaneurysms on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Groin radiation and relief with lying down are nonspecific rather than characteristic
No reported skin lesions, peripheral neuropathy, or other common systemic manifestations, although these are not required

data.description: A noninflammatory disorder involving degeneration of medium-sized arterial walls, producing aneurysms, dissections, stenoses, and abdominal organ ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe abdominal and flank pain
Elevated LDH and apparent renal infarcts
Multiple arterial aneurysmal abnormalities on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue
Elevated ESR and CRP suggest a systemic inflammatory process, although acute ischemia can also elevate them
Mild anemia is not a defining feature without bleeding or another associated condition

data.diagnosis: Renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia with renal ischemia
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disease causing stenoses and sometimes aneurysms or dissections. Renal involvement commonly causes hypertension and can occasionally cause infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal and flank pain if complicated by arterial dissection or infarction
Elevated LDH and apparent renal perfusion defects
Renal arterial irregularities and aneurysmal changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP with months of fatigue are not typical of uncomplicated fibromuscular dysplasia
Leukocytosis and anemia are not characteristic baseline findings
Multiple distal renal microaneurysms are more suggestive of vasculitis than classic fibromuscular dysplasia

data.diagnosis: Bilateral renal infarction from arterial thromboembolism
data.description: Occlusion of renal arterial branches by emboli or thrombi causes acute renal ischemia. A cardiac embolic source or hypercoagulable disorder can produce infarcts in both kidneys.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe abdominal and flank pain with nausea and vomiting
Apparent bilateral focal renal perfusion defects on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple renal arterial microaneurysms are not explained by uncomplicated thromboembolism
Months of fatigue and systemic inflammatory markers suggest an underlying inflammatory disorder
No reported cardiac disease or known embolic risk factor

data.description: An infection of the renal parenchyma that can cause flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, nausea, leukocytosis, and focal reduced enhancement on CT.
symptoms_in_common: Flank pain and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness
Focal renal enhancement abnormalities can resemble those seen in renal infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or urinary symptoms
Bland urine sediment rather than typical pyuria or bacteriuria
Abrupt onset of severe pain
Marked LDH elevation and severe hypertension favor renal ischemia
Renal arterial microaneurysms are not explained by ordinary pyelonephritis

data.description: Reduced blood flow to the colon can cause ulceration, inflammation, and occasionally a mass-like lesion that mimics cancer. The patient's extensive vascular disease and apparent right-colonic abnormality make this an important possibility, but confirmation requires clinical correlation and biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and mild abdominal tenderness
Advanced age and extensive atherosclerotic disease
Congestive heart failure, which can contribute to reduced intestinal perfusion
Apparent right-colonic thickening and ulceration on the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary nodule, which is not explained by isolated colonic ischemia
Lower-lung crackles and lower-extremity edema, which are more consistent with concurrent heart failure

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the proximal colon that can cause weight loss, altered bowel habits, and an ulcerated mass. The apparent cecal lesion warrants exclusion of cancer by biopsy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-lung crackles and peripheral edema are not typical direct manifestations
Extensive arterial disease and the apparent abdominal aortic aneurysm are not explained by colon cancer

data.description: A malignancy of lymphoid tissue that can involve the cecum and produce substantial bowel-wall thickening, ulceration, and systemic weight loss.
symptoms_in_common: Increased tracer uptake in the colonic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-lung crackles and lower-extremity edema are not typical of localized colorectal lymphoma
Extensive atherosclerosis and the apparent abdominal aortic aneurysm are separate findings

data.description: Intestinal infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis commonly affecting the ileocecal region, where it can produce ulceration and inflammatory thickening resembling malignancy. Microbiologic and histologic evidence would be needed.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent ileocecal or right-colonic inflammatory lesion
Upper-lung nodular abnormality, which could be compatible with pulmonary infection but is nonspecific
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-extremity edema and basal crackles are more readily explained by known heart failure
Extensive arterial atherosclerosis and the apparent abdominal aortic aneurysm are not typical manifestations

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease involving the ileocecal region
data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can cause deep ulcers and mass-like thickening in the terminal ileum and adjacent colon. New presentation at age 80 is possible but less typical.
symptoms_not_in_common: First presentation at age 80 is uncommon
Pulmonary nodule is not a typical manifestation
Lower-lung crackles and lower-extremity edema are more consistent with concurrent heart failure
The apparent abdominal aortic aneurysm is not explained by Crohn disease

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic panniculitis associated with acute pancreatitis
data.description: Pancreatic enzymes released into the circulation cause inflammation and necrosis of subcutaneous fat. This is the leading explanation for the tender nodules; the biopsy appears to show lobular fat necrosis compatible with pancreatic panniculitis.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal CT showing extensive inflammation or fluid near the pancreas
Skin biopsy showing apparent fat necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic hepatitis C and cirrhosis are background conditions rather than characteristic manifestations

data.description: Acute pancreatic inflammation causes abdominal pain and substantial pancreatic enzyme elevation. The CT suggests significant peripancreatic inflammation or fluid, although pancreatic necrosis cannot be confirmed from this image alone.
symptoms_in_common: Serum lipase of 6715 U per liter
Extensive inflammatory changes or fluid near the pancreas on CT
History of alcohol-related disease, a potential etiologic clue
symptoms_not_in_common: Tender skin nodules are an uncommon extra-abdominal complication rather than a typical presentation
Chronic hepatitis C is not a characteristic manifestation

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma with lipase hypersecretion syndrome
data.description: A rare pancreatic malignancy that can release large amounts of lipase, producing subcutaneous fat necrosis and pancreatic panniculitis. It is an alternative underlying cause if enzyme elevation and nodules persist or a pancreatic mass is identified.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy findings compatible with fat necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The acute presentation is more suggestive of pancreatitis
The supplied CT does not clearly establish a discrete pancreatic tumor
Chronic hepatitis C and alcohol-induced cirrhosis are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: An inflammatory disorder of subcutaneous fat that causes tender red nodules, usually on the lower legs. It is a clinical mimic of pancreatic panniculitis but generally shows septal rather than enzymatic lobular inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Tender erythematous nodules on the legs
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked serum lipase elevation
Epigastric pain and vomiting with pancreatic inflammatory changes
Biopsy showing apparent extensive fat necrosis rather than typical septal panniculitis

data.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis associated with chronic hepatitis C, typically causing palpable purpura and sometimes neuropathy, joint pain, or kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Tender inflammatory lesions involving the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Subcutaneous nodules rather than typical palpable purpura
Marked lipase elevation
Epigastric pain and vomiting with pancreatic inflammatory changes
Biopsy appearance favoring fat necrosis rather than small-vessel vasculitis

data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal lambda light chains and causing bone lesions and organ damage. This is the leading diagnosis; low plasma-cell infiltration on an aspirate does not exclude patchy marrow involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain with a thoracic plasma-cell lesion
Slowly enlarging skull mass with a large expansile calvarial lesion on imaging
Lambda light chains in serum and urine
CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells on lesion biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Low plasma-cell infiltration in the marrow aspirate is less typical of extensive marrow-based disease, although sampling can underestimate involvement
A large, smooth, domed skull mass is an unusual presentation compared with conventional discrete lytic skull lesions

data.diagnosis: Solitary bone plasmacytoma with minimal marrow involvement
data.description: A localized clonal plasma-cell tumor in bone with absent or minimal marrow involvement, without systemic myeloma-defining organ damage attributable to the tumor.
symptoms_in_common: A slowly enlarging, firm, non-tender skull mass
Back pain associated with a biopsy-proven plasma-cell bone lesion
CD138 positivity and lambda light-chain restriction
Monoclonal lambda light chains in serum and urine
symptoms_not_in_common: Separate skull and thoracic lesions argue against a solitary tumor
Renal impairment
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Immunoparesis suggests a more systemic plasma-cell disorder

data.description: An uncommon presentation with multiple localized clonal plasma-cell tumors and little marrow involvement, generally without systemic organ damage attributable to myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Skull mass and a separate thoracic plasma-cell lesion
Low-level plasma-cell infiltration in the marrow aspirate
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal impairment attributable to the plasma-cell disorder favors multiple myeloma
Hypercalcaemia attributable to the plasma-cell disorder favors multiple myeloma
Anaemia attributable to the plasma-cell disorder favors multiple myeloma
Immunoparesis supports systemic disease rather than isolated tumors

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma with plasma-cell differentiation that can express CD138 and restricted light chains. Additional morphology, immunophenotyping, and viral studies are needed to distinguish it from plasma-cell neoplasms.
symptoms_in_common: Possible skeletal involvement causing back pain
CD138-positive cells with lambda light-chain restriction
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow skull-mass growth over seven months is less typical of this aggressive lymphoma
The reported plasma-cell morphology does not establish plasmablastic morphology
Serum and urine lambda light chains with renal impairment, hypercalcaemia, and immunoparesis strongly favor myeloma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma with skeletal metastases
data.description: A kidney malignancy that can produce expansile, vascular bone metastases involving the skull and spine. It is an imaging differential but is strongly disfavored by the plasma-cell biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain with a thoracic lesion
Renal impairment, although this is nonspecific
symptoms_not_in_common: A monomorphic plasma-cell population with CD138 positivity and lambda restriction is inconsistent with ordinary renal carcinoma metastasis
Monoclonal lambda light chains in serum and urine
Immunoparesis
Marrow plasma-cell infiltration

data.diagnosis: Chronic extrahepatic portal vein thrombosis with cavernous transformation
data.description: Chronic portal vein obstruction produces collateral veins around the porta hepatis and may cause compensatory caudate-lobe enlargement resembling a liver mass. The apparent vascular collaterals and prominent caudate region make this a leading possibility; Doppler imaging is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Right hypochondrial pain for one month
No fever, consistent with a chronic vascular process
Apparent enlarged caudate region and periportal collateral vessels on CT
Previous abdominal tuberculosis, a possible antecedent to local inflammation and portal vein thrombosis

data.description: Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow can cause abdominal pain, liver congestion, and disproportionate caudate-lobe enlargement. Confirmation requires assessment of the hepatic veins and inferior vena cava.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent periportal collateral vessels are more suggestive of portal vein obstruction than isolated hepatic venous obstruction

data.description: A benign hepatic lesion composed of hyperplastic liver tissue that can appear as a well-defined, relatively homogeneous mass. Multiphase contrast imaging is necessary to distinguish it from enlarged normal liver tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Right hypochondrial pain from a large lesion
Loss of appetite potentially related to mass effect
Apparent homogeneous mass-like tissue near the caudate region
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent periportal collateral vessels are not explained by uncomplicated focal nodular hyperplasia

data.description: Localized hepatic tuberculosis can form a granulomatous mass that mimics a tumor. Previous tuberculosis makes it relevant, but prior successful treatment does not establish active disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever is less typical of active tuberculosis, although it does not exclude it
Relatively homogeneous liver-like tissue and apparent periportal collaterals are less typical than a necrotic or heterogeneous tuberculous mass

data.description: A rare malignant liver tumor affecting adolescents and young adults, often without underlying cirrhosis. It may present as a large hepatic mass, but the supplied images do not establish a discrete tumor.
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively homogeneous tissue resembling an enlarged caudate lobe is less typical than a heterogeneous tumor
Apparent periportal collateral vessels are not a characteristic primary feature

data.description: The most likely diagnosis. Cholesterol crystals released from atherosclerotic plaques after vascular procedures obstruct small arteries, causing renal injury, distal skin ischemia, and systemic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary angiography and bypass surgery three weeks before presentation
Underlying coronary artery disease and hypertension
Painful, dusky toes and fingers consistent with distal ischemia
Severe acute kidney injury requiring dialysis
Altered mental status from systemic involvement or uremia

data.description: Necrotizing inflammation of medium-sized arteries that can cause skin ischemia, renal vascular injury, hypertension, and neurologic abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked eosinophilia is not characteristic
Onset following coronary angiography and bypass surgery is more suggestive of cholesterol embolization

data.description: Infection of the endocardial surface, usually a heart valve, can produce peripheral emboli, cerebral complications, and immune-mediated kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal skin lesions and discoloration
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked eosinophilia is unusual
Diffuse dusky digital ischemia is less typical than discrete embolic lesions
Delayed presentation after arterial instrumentation more strongly favors cholesterol embolization

data.description: Small-vessel platelet-rich thrombosis, including thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura and hemolytic uremic syndromes, can cause severe renal and neurologic injury.
symptoms_in_common: Painful distal ischemic discoloration, which can occur in severe cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked eosinophilia is not characteristic
Prominent dusky toes and fingers are less typical than renal and neurologic manifestations
Delayed onset after coronary angiography is more characteristic of cholesterol embolization

data.description: An inflammatory kidney injury, often caused by recently introduced medications, that may produce eosinophilia, hematuria, proteinuria, and severe renal dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Altered mental status potentially attributable to uremia
Presentation several weeks after hospitalization, when new medication exposure is possible
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful, dusky distal extremities suggest vascular ischemia rather than a typical drug-related rash
The association with arterial instrumentation is not explained by interstitial nephritis

data.description: Profound reduction in core body temperature causing impaired consciousness and cardiovascular depression. The ECG shows marked bradycardia and apparent Osborn (J) waves, strongly supporting this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Core temperature below the thermometer's detection range
Apparent Osborn (J) waves on the ECG

data.description: Life-threatening decompensated hypothyroidism that can cause profound hypothermia, altered consciousness, bradycardia, and hypotension.
symptoms_not_in_common: Preserved respiratory rate and room-air oxygen saturation are less typical of advanced myxedema coma with hypoventilation

data.description: Excessive beta-adrenergic blockade can cause severe bradycardia, hypotension, and impaired consciousness. Ophthalmic beta-blockers used for glaucoma can also produce systemic toxicity, although exposure is not documented here.
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound hypothermia below the thermometer's detection range is not typical of isolated beta-blocker toxicity
Osborn (J) waves are more suggestive of hypothermia than direct beta-blocker toxicity

data.description: Severe infection can cause circulatory failure and altered consciousness; older adults may present with hypothermia rather than fever.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked bradycardia is less typical than tachycardia in septic shock
Extreme hypothermia with Osborn (J) waves is unusual unless substantial secondary cooling has occurred

data.description: Critically low blood glucose can cause coma and impaired temperature regulation, potentially producing secondary hypothermia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked bradycardia is less typical than an adrenergic response with tachycardia
Osborn (J) waves are not characteristic of hypoglycemia itself
Profound hypothermia below the thermometer's detection range is uncommon without additional contributing factors

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (Goodpasture disease)
data.description: An autoimmune disease targeting pulmonary and renal basement membranes, causing alveolar hemorrhage and often glomerulonephritis. Circulating anti-GBM antibodies can occasionally be undetectable; linear tissue IgG deposition makes this a leading consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent hemoptysis consistent with pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage
Bilateral patchy ground-glass pulmonary opacities on the supplied CT
Linear IgG deposits in lung and renal tissues
Microscopic blood in urine, although minimal
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative circulating anti-GBM antibodies, although seronegative disease is possible
Preserved creatinine and absence of proteinuria are atypical for classic renal involvement
Granular IgG deposits suggest an additional or alternative immune-complex process
Seizure, transient right-sided weakness, and multifocal brain MRI abnormalities are unusual manifestations

data.description: Inflammation of small blood vessels associated with immune-complex deposition. Pulmonary, renal, and cerebral involvement could provide a unifying explanation, although the specific cause requires further pathological and clinical characterization.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent hemoptysis compatible with pulmonary capillaritis
Anemia potentially resulting from pulmonary bleeding
Granular IgG deposition in lung and renal tissues
Seizure and transient focal weakness compatible with cerebral vascular involvement
Multifocal signal abnormalities and enhancement on the supplied brain MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear IgG deposition is more characteristic of anti-GBM disease
Normal complement levels are less supportive of some immune-complex disorders
Normal creatinine and absence of proteinuria provide little evidence of clinically active glomerulonephritis

data.description: A necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis that commonly causes pulmonary capillaritis and glomerulonephritis. Some cases lack detectable ANCA, and central nervous system involvement is possible but uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent hemoptysis compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
Seizure and focal neurological deficit could reflect uncommon cerebral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG deposits conflict with the typically pauci-immune tissue pattern
Negative ANCA reduces support but does not exclude the disease
Normal creatinine and absence of proteinuria are atypical for significant renal involvement

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with pulmonary hemorrhage and neuropsychiatric involvement
data.description: A multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause immune-complex renal disease, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, seizures, and cerebrovascular complications.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis and pulmonary ground-glass opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative anti-dsDNA antibodies and normal complement levels reduce support for active lupus
Linear IgG deposition is not the characteristic lupus immune-complex pattern
Absence of proteinuria and preserved renal function are less consistent with clinically significant lupus nephritis
No characteristic skin, joint, or other systemic lupus manifestations are reported

data.description: A diagnosis of exclusion characterized by recurrent alveolar bleeding, pulmonary hemosiderin accumulation, anemia, and lung opacities, generally without systemic vasculitis or renal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Preserved renal function and absence of proteinuria
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissues suggest an immune-mediated systemic process rather than idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis
Seizure and transient right-sided weakness are not characteristic
Multifocal brain MRI abnormalities are not explained by isolated pulmonary hemosiderosis
Renal tissue immune deposits are not expected

data.diagnosis: Metastatic mixed nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: The leading possibility is a testicular cancer containing multiple germ cell components, potentially including teratoma, embryonal carcinoma, and yolk sac tumor. Gastrointestinal invasion or metastasis can cause ulceration and bleeding. Histologic confirmation and staging are required.
symptoms_in_common: Painless enlargement of the right testicle
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin and lactate dehydrogenase
Melena and severe microcytic anemia consistent with gastrointestinal blood loss
Ulcerated gastrointestinal lesions on the endoscopic images
Histologic images showing glandular and cystic structures that could represent mixed germ cell tumor components
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy NSAID use is not explained by the tumor and provides a competing explanation for gastrointestinal bleeding

data.diagnosis: Testicular yolk sac tumor with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: A malignant nonseminomatous germ cell tumor that characteristically produces alpha-fetoprotein. In adults, it more commonly occurs as part of a mixed germ cell tumor than as a pure tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain potentially caused by metastatic disease
Melena and microcytic anemia if gastrointestinal involvement is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin is not typical of a pure yolk sac tumor
Diverse cystic and glandular histologic appearances may favor a mixed tumor rather than a pure yolk sac tumor
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated to the disease

data.diagnosis: Testicular embryonal carcinoma with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: An aggressive nonseminomatous germ cell malignancy that can spread to retroperitoneal nodes and distant organs. It may produce alpha-fetoprotein or human chorionic gonadotropin, particularly when present within a mixed tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult male with painless testicular enlargement
Melena and severe anemia potentially resulting from gastrointestinal invasion
Gland-forming malignant-appearing tissue in the supplied histologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent cystic structures in the histologic images suggest additional differentiated components rather than pure embryonal carcinoma
Heavy NSAID use is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: NSAIDs can damage gastric and duodenal mucosa, causing ulcers, abdominal pain, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding. This could coexist with a separate testicular malignancy but does not explain the entire presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated and bleeding-appearing lesions on endoscopy
Several months of preceding milder gastrointestinal symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless enlarged right testicle
Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin
Tumor-like glandular and cystic tissue on the histologic images

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma involving the testicle and gastrointestinal tract
data.description: Lymphoma can involve both the testicle and gastrointestinal tract, producing painless testicular swelling, abdominal lesions, and gastrointestinal bleeding. It is less likely here because the age and tumor marker pattern favor a germ cell malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Melena and anemia from possible gastrointestinal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked alpha-fetoprotein elevation is not characteristic of lymphoma
Human chorionic gonadotropin elevation is not characteristic of lymphoma
Glandular and cystic histologic structures are not typical of lymphoma
Age 30 is atypical for primary testicular lymphoma, which predominantly affects older men

data.diagnosis: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens due to extensive iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis
data.description: A limb-threatening form of massive venous thrombosis that obstructs venous drainage, producing severe edema, cyanosis, and secondary compromise of arterial inflow. This is the strongest clinical fit and requires emergency vascular evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden-onset, progressively worsening unilateral leg pain
Marked swelling extending from the foot to the upper thigh
Dusky discoloration of the toes and foot
Cold extremity with distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
Hypotension, which can accompany severe fluid sequestration
symptoms_not_in_common: Left calf edema is not explained by an isolated right-sided venous thrombosis and may reflect concurrent heart failure

data.diagnosis: Acute limb ischemia from arterial thromboembolism
data.description: An abrupt reduction in arterial blood supply, potentially caused by an embolus associated with atrial fibrillation. This is a vascular emergency; arterial imaging is needed to establish the obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive pitting edema extending to the upper thigh is less typical of isolated arterial occlusion
Progressive whole-leg swelling over three days suggests substantial venous obstruction
Contralateral calf edema is not explained by a unilateral arterial embolus

data.description: A malignant gastric glandular tumor that can cause a hypercoagulable state and extensive venous thrombosis. The supplied gastric endoscopic and histologic images raise concern for adenocarcinoma, but definitive interpretation requires the formal pathology report.
symptoms_in_common: Acute painful unilateral leg swelling compatible with cancer-associated venous thrombosis
Severe edema and dusky discoloration compatible with a thrombotic complication
Supplied endoscopic images show an irregular ulcerated gastric lesion
Supplied histologic images show atypical gland-forming tissue concerning for adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: A cold foot with diminished pulses is not a direct typical manifestation of gastric cancer and would require a vascular complication
Sudden limb pain is not a typical primary symptom of gastric cancer
Left calf edema is nonspecific and may be related to preexisting heart failure

data.diagnosis: Acute compartment syndrome secondary to severe limb swelling
data.description: Elevated pressure within a muscle compartment compromises tissue perfusion. Severe venous obstruction can precipitate this limb-threatening complication even without trauma.
symptoms_in_common: Cold, dusky foot indicating compromised perfusion
Distal pulses detectable only by Doppler, although pulses may remain present in compartment syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive pitting edema reaching the upper thigh is more suggestive of proximal venous obstruction than isolated compartment syndrome
Contralateral calf edema is not explained by right-sided compartment syndrome
Hypotension is not typical of isolated compartment syndrome

data.description: A rapidly progressive infection of fascia and adjacent tissues that can cause severe pain, swelling, skin necrosis, and shock. It is an emergency alternative diagnosis, although the vascular findings favor thrombosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: A cold limb with diminished distal pulses favors vascular compromise rather than primary infection
Marked whole-leg pitting edema is more characteristic of venous outflow obstruction
Contralateral calf edema is not explained by a localized right-leg infection

diagnoses.title: Adenocarcinoma of stomach

data.diagnosis: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma involving the penis
data.description: A rare aggressive lymphoma in which malignant B cells accumulate within small blood vessels, potentially obstructing penile circulation and causing priapism. The apparent intravascular atypical cells in the biopsy strongly suggest this possibility, although the immunostains require identification and formal interpretation.

Intact penile skin without a visible surface tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: Priapism is a rare presentation of this lymphoma
No skin rash or nodules, although cutaneous involvement can occur

data.diagnosis: Primary penile diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive lymphoma arising in penile tissue that can infiltrate the erectile bodies and impair venous drainage. Tissue immunophenotyping is needed to distinguish it from an intravascular lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, compatible with localized extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete penile mass or nodules were reported
An apparently predominantly intravascular biopsy pattern is less typical than a tissue-based infiltrate

data.diagnosis: Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma involving the penis
data.description: Prostate cancer can rarely spread to the penile erectile tissues and obstruct venous drainage, producing malignant priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Intact penile skin, compatible with deep metastatic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not typical of uncomplicated penile metastasis
No penile nodules or palpable mass were reported
The apparent intravascular large-cell biopsy pattern is less typical than gland-forming carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma involving the penis
data.description: Urothelial cancer of the bladder or urinary tract can rarely metastasize to the penis, causing pain, swelling, and priapism through infiltration or vascular obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Intact skin despite possible internal penile involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a characteristic presenting feature
No penile nodules or surface lesions were reported
The apparent intravascular lymphoid-appearing cells are less typical of urothelial carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia with hyperleukocytosis-related priapism
data.description: A myeloproliferative malignancy that can cause priapism through leukostasis and impaired penile venous outflow when the white blood cell count is extremely elevated. A blood count and BCR::ABL1 testing would be necessary to assess this possibility.
symptoms_not_in_common: No splenomegaly, which is common in symptomatic chronic myeloid leukemia
No hepatomegaly
The biopsy appears to show focal intravascular large atypical cells rather than the expected myeloid proliferation

data.description: An ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue. It can cause benign ascites, pleural effusion, and markedly elevated CA 125 despite normal thyroid function. This is a leading consideration, but histopathology is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Complex left adnexal mass with strongly enhancing solid tissue and thick septa
Low T2 signal in solid components, compatible with colloid-rich thyroid tissue
No fatty components, which is compatible with struma ovarii
Right pleural effusion visible on the chest image and exertional dyspnea
Markedly elevated CA 125 with repeatedly benign ascitic cytology
Normal thyroid hormone levels and absence of thyroid symptoms, as most struma ovarii tumors are nonfunctioning
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear contradictory finding; the presentation is uncommon but recognized
Normal thyroid uptake alone does not establish that the ovarian mass contains thyroid tissue

data.diagnosis: Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma with Meigs syndrome
data.description: A usually benign ovarian stromal tumor that can produce the triad of an ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion. CA 125 may rise substantially because of irritation of the serosal surfaces.
symptoms_in_common: Adnexal mass with low T1 and low T2 signal in solid portions
Massive ascites and marked abdominal distention
Right pleural effusion and exertional dyspnea
Absence of peritoneal dissemination or lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong enhancement is less typical of a collagen-rich fibroma, which often enhances weakly or gradually
Prominent cystic architecture with thick septa and cyst-wall calcifications is less typical than a predominantly solid mass

data.description: A malignant tumor of the ovarian epithelium that commonly presents after menopause with a complex adnexal mass, ascites, and elevated CA 125. Negative ascitic cytology does not exclude it.

symptoms_not_in_common: Repeatedly negative ascitic cytology is less supportive of malignant ascites

Markedly low T2 signal in the solid portions and septa favors some benign fibrous or colloid-containing tumors over typical epithelial carcinoma

data.description: A usually benign epithelial ovarian tumor containing abundant fibrous tissue. Its complex solid-cystic appearance can mimic malignancy, and rarely it accompanies ascites and pleural effusion.
