Ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated CA 125 can occur in associated pseudo-Meigs syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive ascites and a large pleural effusion are uncommon
CA 125 elevation to 1237 U/ml is unusual
Strong enhancement is less characteristic of densely fibrous components

data.description: An ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor that often produces estrogen and may present in peri- or postmenopausal women as an enhancing solid-cystic mass. Ascites can occur, but tissue examination and markers such as inhibin are needed for diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of lymphadenopathy, since nodal spread is relatively uncommon
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported postmenopausal bleeding or other signs of estrogen excess
Low T2 signal throughout solid components is less typical than heterogeneous intermediate or high T2 signal
No described hemorrhagic components
Marked CA 125 elevation and pleural effusion are not characteristic features

data.description: A glial tumor arising within the medulla that can expand the brainstem and enhance variably on MRI. This is a leading consideration for the apparent expansile medullary lesion, although the provided images are not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent expansion and heterogeneous enhancement of the medulla on MRI
Negative plain radiographs, which do not exclude an intracranial lesion

data.diagnosis: Ependymoma of the lower fourth ventricle or medulla
data.description: A tumor of ependymal cells that may arise near the fourth ventricle and extend toward the medulla or upper cervical canal. MRI commonly shows heterogeneous enhancement.

symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears predominantly intrinsic to the medulla rather than clearly centered within the fourth ventricle

data.description: A highly vascular, usually benign tumor that can occur in the posterior fossa or spinal cord. It typically appears as an intensely enhancing nodule, sometimes with an associated cyst or prominent vessels.

data.diagnosis: Subependymoma of the lower fourth ventricle

data.description: A cluster of abnormal, low-flow blood vessels within the brainstem that may cause symptoms through small hemorrhages. Dedicated susceptibility-sensitive MRI is important for identifying characteristic blood products.

symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent expansile enhancement is less typical than a mixed-signal lesion with a hemosiderin rim
Unremitting pain without a reported acute or episodic neurological event is less characteristic of symptomatic hemorrhage

data.description: A rare benign skin malformation containing increased eccrine sweat glands and vascular channels, usually appearing in childhood. This is a leading possibility given the localized sweating; confirmation requires histopathologic assessment.

Intermittent sweating confined to the lesion
Localized increased hair visible in the clinical photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-back location is less common than an extremity location

data.description: A benign developmental overgrowth of smooth muscle in the skin, often presenting in infancy as a firm, hairy plaque on the trunk or lower back.
symptoms_in_common: Localized increased hair visible in the photograph
Absence of pain or other discomfort
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent localized sweating is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A benign localized increase in the number or size of eccrine sweat glands, which may cause focal excessive sweating with little visible skin change or an associated plaque.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent sweating localized to the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressively increasing firmness is less typical
Prominent localized hair growth is not characteristic

data.description: A benign hamartoma composed predominantly of excess dermal collagen, producing a firm, skin-colored plaque that may occur on the lower back.
symptoms_not_in_common: Localized sweating is not characteristic

data.description: A benign soft-tissue lesion arising predominantly in the first two years of life, composed of fibrous tissue, fat, and immature mesenchymal tissue. It usually presents as a painless enlarging subcutaneous mass.
symptoms_in_common: Onset during the first year of life
symptoms_not_in_common: A superficial plaque is less typical than a subcutaneous mass
Intermittent surface sweating is not characteristic
Localized increased hair is not a usual feature

data.description: A clonal disorder of dendritic cells that can involve skin, lungs, bones, and liver. This is the strongest unifying possibility, although tissue biopsy is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary nodules and irregular cysts on the supplied images
Apparent lytic lesion in the sternum
Raised ALT, potentially reflecting liver involvement

data.description: An inflammatory small-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the respiratory tract and kidneys and can cause cavitating lung nodules and skin lesions.

Apparent lytic sternal lesion
Raised ALT is not a principal feature

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the lungs and potentially additional sites such as bone, skin, or liver.

data.description: A fungal infection that can spread from the lungs to the skin and bones. Its likelihood depends strongly on geographic exposure and microbiological or tissue confirmation.

Apparent lytic sternal lesion could reflect bone involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous irregular pulmonary cysts are not characteristic
A scalp rash resembling chronic dermatitis is less typical than verrucous or ulcerative skin lesions
Raised ALT is not a defining feature

data.description: A rare cyst-forming biliary neoplasm occurring predominantly in women that can develop invasive adenocarcinoma. This is less favored because the depicted lesion appears predominantly solid rather than clearly multiloculated and cystic.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent invasive gland-forming tumor on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly solid appearance of the hepatic lesion is less typical than a multiloculated cystic mass
Back pain is less characteristic

anonymization.anonymizedText: A 34-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal and back pain 3 years before evaluation at the oncology clinic. She had been well until this onset. Her medical history was notable for migraines. She did not smoke cigarettes, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She worked full time as a social worker and lived in ************ with her husband and child. Family history included breast cancer in maternal grandmother (70s), uterine cancer in paternal aunt (40s), and colon cancer in two paternal cousins (30s and 50s). On physical examination: temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 108/78 mm Hg, heart rate 78 beats per minute, body-mass index 27.7. The abdomen had well-healed surgical scars; remainder of physical examination was normal. Laboratory results showed elevated tumor marker CA 19-9 at 110 IU per milliliter (reference <35), while alpha-fetoprotein and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were normal.

The abdomen had well-healed surgical scars; remainder of physical examination was normal. Laboratory results showed elevated tumor marker CA 19-9 at 110 IU per milliliter (reference <35), while alpha-fetoprotein and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were normal.

data.diagnosis: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor of the parotid region
data.description: A malignant spindle-cell tumor arising from a peripheral nerve or its sheath. The painful, progressively enlarging mass and spindle-cell histology make this a consideration, but confirmation requires labeled immunohistochemical results and assessment of atypia, mitoses and necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Right facial pain preceding the swelling
Progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear
Spindle-cell proliferation in the supplied histology
No detected distant metastases, which is compatible with localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth, soft, mobile swelling is less typical of an infiltrative malignant tumor
Normal facial nerve function despite a lesion near the facial nerve

data.description: A benign, usually encapsulated tumor of Schwann cells that can arise from the facial nerve or another nerve within the parotid region. It may produce a mobile mass while preserving facial nerve function.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth, elastic, mobile swelling in the parotid region
Facial pain and tenderness can occur with nerve compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive painful enlargement over only three months is less typical than slow, painless growth
The supplied histology does not clearly demonstrate classic Antoni A and Antoni B areas or Verocay bodies

data.diagnosis: Localized neurofibroma of the parotid region
data.description: A benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and other supporting cells. A localized lesion can present as a soft mass associated with a nerve.
symptoms_in_common: Soft, elastic swelling beneath the ear
No systemic symptoms or palpable cervical lymph nodes
Spindle cells within a collagenous background
Pain can occur when the affected nerve is compressed
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent pain and progressive enlargement over several months are less typical of an uncomplicated neurofibroma
A freely mobile, apparently circumscribed mass is less characteristic than for schwannoma

data.diagnosis: Spindle-cell myoepithelial carcinoma of the parotid gland
data.description: A rare malignant salivary gland tumor composed predominantly of myoepithelial cells, sometimes with spindle-cell morphology. Diagnosis requires evidence of invasion and an appropriate epithelial and myoepithelial immunohistochemical profile.
symptoms_in_common: Normal facial nerve function and negative metastasis screening can occur in localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Soft, smooth, mobile swelling is less typical of an invasive carcinoma
The supplied images do not clearly establish epithelial differentiation or an invasive salivary tumor pattern

data.diagnosis: Nodular fasciitis of the parotid region
data.description: A benign, self-limited myofibroblastic proliferation that can mimic a sarcoma because of relatively rapid growth and cellular spindle-cell histology.
symptoms_in_common: Enlargement over a relatively short period
Spindle-cell proliferation in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial pain beginning before the swelling is less characteristic
The organized fascicular appearance is less typical than the tissue-culture-like pattern often seen in nodular fasciitis
The parotid region is an uncommon site

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency, producing progressive neurological deterioration and coarse facial features. The apparent low T2 signal in the globus pallidus and periventricular white-matter abnormalities on the supplied images support consideration of this diagnosis, but are not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive severe cognitive and neurological impairment beginning in early childhood
symptoms_not_in_common: High forehead and hypertelorism are nonspecific rather than defining features

data.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by beta-galactosidase deficiency, leading to lysosomal accumulation of GM1 ganglioside and progressive neurodegeneration. Late-infantile disease can present with developmental decline, spasticity, and dystonia.
symptoms_in_common: Early-childhood onset of progressive neurological impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Deafness is less characteristic
Marked macroglossia is less typical of the late-infantile form
High forehead and hypertelorism are not defining features

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-mannosidase deficiency, characterized by intellectual disability, hearing impairment, coarse facial features, and variable progressive neurological involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe early-childhood tetraparesis is less typical
A prominent mixed spastic-dystonic syndrome is less typical than ataxia

data.diagnosis: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I, severe form (Hurler syndrome)
data.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency, resulting in glycosaminoglycan accumulation, coarse facial features, macroglossia, hearing loss, and progressive developmental impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: A mixed spastic-dystonic movement disorder is not a usual primary manifestation
Severe tetraparesis at this age is less typical unless there is an additional complication such as spinal cord compression

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by neuraminidase deficiency. Childhood forms can cause coarse facial features, developmental impairment, and progressive neurological disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Deafness is not a defining feature
A predominantly spastic-dystonic tetraparesis is less characteristic than a syndrome involving myoclonus or ataxia
Hypertelorism is nonspecific

data.description: Impaired movement of both vocal folds can leave them near the midline, severely narrowing the airway. The apparent narrow glottic opening is compatible with this diagnosis, but confirmation requires assessment of vocal fold movement during breathing.
symptoms_in_common: Apparently narrow glottic opening on endoscopic images
History of severe perinatal asphyxia, a possible contributor to neurologic dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms becoming apparent after six days of intubation also suggest a mechanical or inflammatory airway injury rather than paralysis alone

data.description: A congenital membrane connecting the anterior vocal folds can restrict the glottic airway and cause neonatal stridor. The apparent tissue spanning part of the glottis raises this possibility, although the provided images are not definitive.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory difficulty beginning in the neonatal period
Recurrent dyspnea after removal of the endotracheal tube
Apparent tissue bridging part of the glottic opening
symptoms_not_in_common: Stridor specifically emerging after prolonged intubation is also suggestive of an acquired airway problem
Severe perinatal asphyxia is not a characteristic manifestation of a glottic web

data.description: Inflammatory swelling following endotracheal intubation can narrow the neonatal larynx and produce post-extubation airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Narrow laryngeal airway on the provided images
symptoms_not_in_common: Respiratory compromise before prolonged intubation cannot be explained by post-intubation edema
An apparent organized tissue bridge would be less typical of uncomplicated edema

data.description: Intubation-related injury to the posterior larynx can cause adhesions or scarring that restrict vocal fold movement and mimic bilateral vocal fold paralysis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation immediately after only six days of intubation is less typical of mature scar-related stenosis
Respiratory distress at birth predates the proposed intubation-related scarring

data.description: Dynamic inward collapse of supraglottic structures during inspiration is a common cause of infant stridor. Diagnosis requires observing supraglottic collapse during spontaneous breathing.
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparent glottic-level narrowing or tissue bridge is not the typical supraglottic abnormality of laryngomalacia
A clear temporal relationship to extubation is more suggestive of intubation-related injury
Severe asphyxia requiring chest compressions is not a typical presentation of uncomplicated laryngomalacia

diagnoses.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
diagnoses.title: Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx[Bilateral]

data.diagnosis: Infected pyriform sinus fistula, likely a fourth branchial pouch anomaly
data.description: A congenital tract arising from the pyriform sinus that can cause recurrent left-sided neck abscesses or thyroid infection. The apparent tract near the left hypopharynx on the supplied image supports this possibility, although confirmation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent left-sided neck abscesses over several years
Swelling at the level of the thyroid cartilage

data.description: A congenital sinus communicating with the pyriform sinus that can become infected and produce recurrent lateral neck abscesses. Distinguishing it from a fourth pouch anomaly requires defining the tract's anatomical course.
A congenital lateral neck cyst that may first become apparent in young adulthood when infection causes enlargement or abscess formation.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with a lateral neck mass
symptoms_not_in_common: The swelling is at the thyroid cartilage level rather than the more typical upper lateral neck location
The apparent tract near the pyriform sinus is not typical of a second branchial cleft cyst

data.diagnosis: Acute suppurative thyroiditis with thyroid abscess
data.description: A bacterial infection of the thyroid that can produce fever and an anterior neck abscess. Recurrent left-sided episodes in a young person can be associated with a congenital pyriform sinus fistula.
symptoms_not_in_common: The described swelling is at the thyroid cartilage level rather than clearly within the lower thyroid region

data.description: A congenital remnant along the thyroid's developmental descent that can become infected, causing recurrent neck swelling or abscess formation.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior neck swelling near the laryngeal framework
symptoms_not_in_common: The swelling is distinctly left-sided rather than typically midline
The apparent tract near the pyriform sinus is not typical of a thyroglossal duct cyst

data.description: Inflammation of small skin vessels producing persistent urticaria-like lesions, often with burning, pain, and residual pigmentation. Normal complement supports the normocomplementemic subtype; the biopsy is suggestive but not definitively diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Painful, burning wheals persisting longer than 24 hours
Angioedema of the hands and feet
Vessel-wall fibrin and erythrocyte extravasation on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe disabling headache is not a characteristic feature
Lymphopenia is nonspecific rather than a typical diagnostic finding
Predominantly lymphocytic and eosinophilic inflammation without reported leukocytoclasia is less typical of classic histology

data.description: A systemic hypersensitivity reaction, often triggered by a medication, causing fever, urticarial rash, joint symptoms, and extremity swelling, usually without complement consumption or renal injury.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to over-the-counter diet pills
Swelling of the hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe headache is not a defining feature
Residual pigmentation and vessel-wall fibrin raise concern for vasculitis rather than an uncomplicated serum sickness-like reaction
Lymphopenia is not a characteristic laboratory finding

data.description: A medication-associated hypersensitivity reaction producing itchy wheals and deeper tissue swelling. The diet pills are a possible trigger, although ordinary urticaria does not explain all findings.
symptoms_in_common: Pruritic, confluent wheals and erythematous macules
Nonpitting swelling of the hands and feet
Dermal edema and eosinophils on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Individual lesions persisting longer than 24 hours
Pain and burning with residual pigmentation
High fever with severe headache, myalgia, and arthralgia
Vessel-wall fibrin and erythrocyte extravasation
Lymphopenia

data.description: An acute viral illness can trigger urticaria or an urticaria-like exanthem alongside systemic inflammatory symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fixed, painful wheals lasting longer than 24 hours with residual pigmentation
Vessel-wall fibrin suggesting vascular injury
Prominent nonpitting extremity angioedema is less characteristic of a viral exanthem

data.description: A systemic autoinflammatory disease causing high fevers, joint symptoms, and an inflammatory rash. Persistent pruritic or urticarial eruptions can occur, but this presentation lacks several usual supporting findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymphopenia rather than the usual neutrophilic leukocytosis
Prominent angioedema of the hands and feet
Burning wheals with residual pigmentation and vascular injury on biopsy
Severe headache is not a characteristic feature
Normal liver tests provide less support, although they do not exclude the disease

data.diagnosis: Gastric trichobezoar with possible distal small-bowel involvement
data.description: A mass of swallowed hair accumulates in the stomach and can cause obstruction, ulceration, or passage of obstructing fragments into the intestine. The visible hair-containing mass strongly favors this diagnosis; Rapunzel syndrome requires confirmation of a continuous tail extending into the small bowel.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively frequent, severe epigastric and upper-quadrant pain
Nausea and recurrent vomiting with relief of pain
Dehydration, fatigue, dizziness, and generalized weakness
Endoscopic and specimen images showing a large tangled hair-containing mass
CT showing a heterogeneous intragastric mass and a possible additional distal intraluminal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported current hair ingestion, although this behavior may be undisclosed
Pain worsening with ibuprofen is nonspecific and may reflect associated mucosal injury

data.description: An accumulation of indigestible plant fibers in the stomach can produce abdominal pain, impaired gastric emptying, and intestinal obstruction. This is an alternative bezoar diagnosis, but the visible hair strongly favors a trichobezoar.
symptoms_not_in_common: The endoscopic and specimen images show tangled hair rather than predominantly plant fibers
No reported dietary exposure or gastric surgery predisposing to a phytobezoar
Iron-deficiency anemia is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease with possible gastric outlet obstruction
data.description: An ulcer in the stomach or duodenum can cause epigastric pain and bleeding; associated inflammation or scarring can impair gastric emptying. Ibuprofen can worsen mucosal injury.
symptoms_in_common: Pain waking the patient from sleep
Microcytic anemia, potentially compatible with chronic gastrointestinal blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Brief, intermittent colicky attacks are less typical than sustained burning or gnawing pain
Worsening constipation is not a primary feature
No consistent relationship between pain and food
A large hair-containing intragastric mass is not explained by isolated peptic ulcer disease

data.description: A segment of bowel telescopes into an adjacent segment, causing intermittent obstruction. In adolescents, an intraluminal lesion or foreign-body mass may serve as a lead point.
symptoms_in_common: Severe episodic abdominal pain lasting approximately 15 minutes
Possible distal intraluminal mass on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly epigastric and upper-quadrant pain is less characteristic
No reported bloody stool
The provided CT does not clearly demonstrate the characteristic bowel-within-bowel appearance
Intussusception alone does not explain the large gastric hair mass

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without mechanical obstruction causes nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal discomfort, and reduced intake. It can predispose to bezoar formation but would not independently explain the demonstrated hair mass.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe, brief colicky pain with guarding is less typical
Symptoms have no reported relationship to food intake
Leukocytosis is not typical of uncomplicated gastroparesis
A large hair-containing mass suggests a mechanical cause rather than isolated delayed gastric emptying
A possible distal bowel mass and worsening constipation suggest additional intestinal involvement

data.description: The most likely diagnosis: disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving the lungs, ileum, and possibly kidney. The images show granulomatous inflammation, necrosis, and numerous acid-fast bacilli. Ileal perforation with purulent peritonitis provides a plausible cause of death.
symptoms_in_common: Poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes
Widespread small nodules in both lungs
Multiple ileal ulcers with perforation and purulent peritonitis
Small pale renal lesion compatible with dissemination
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and acid-fast bacilli in the supplied images
Previous osteomyelitis, potentially compatible with skeletal tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital kyphoscoliosis is not explained by tuberculosis
Previously treated testicular seminoma is a separate condition

data.description: An opportunistic nontuberculous mycobacterial infection that can involve the lungs and gastrointestinal tract, particularly in patients with significant immune suppression. Species identification is necessary to distinguish it from tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: History of chemotherapy, a potential risk factor depending on timing and residual immune suppression
Pulmonary nodules and impaired respiratory function
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-formed necrotizing granulomas favor tuberculosis over the usual macrophage-rich pattern of advanced disseminated infection
Ileal perforation is an uncommon manifestation
No profound ongoing immune deficiency is documented

data.description: A member of the tuberculosis complex that can cause intestinal tuberculosis and systemic dissemination, classically after exposure to infected animals or unpasteurized dairy products. Histology cannot reliably distinguish it from Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules and possible renal involvement
Previous osteomyelitis potentially consistent with disseminated mycobacterial disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital kyphoscoliosis is unrelated
Testicular seminoma is not a manifestation
No relevant animal exposure, unpasteurized dairy consumption, or intravesical BCG treatment is reported

data.description: A systemic fungal infection that can produce pulmonary nodules, granulomatous inflammation, and gastrointestinal ulcers, sometimes with perforation. It is substantially less likely given the apparent acid-fast bacilli.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules and poor respiratory function
Previous chemotherapy as a potential susceptibility factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous acid-fast bacilli are inconsistent with Histoplasma organisms
No intracellular yeast forms are evident in the supplied images
Previous elbow osteomyelitis is an uncommon manifestation

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by transmural inflammation, ileal ulceration, and sometimes granulomas or perforation. It does not adequately explain the acid-fast organisms and disseminated necrotizing lesions.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acid-fast bacilli in tissue indicate an infectious process rather than Crohn disease alone
Necrotizing pulmonary granulomas and widespread bilateral lung nodules are not typical
A pale renal nodule suggesting disseminated infection is not typical
Previous osteomyelitis is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A reflex autonomic response causing hypotension and slowing or transient arrest of the sinus node. This is the leading explanation for the observed episode.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea, sweating, and pallor before the episode
Systolic blood pressure falling to 89 mm Hg
A 3–4 second cardiac pause without P waves
symptoms_not_in_common: Epigastric pain progressing to central chest pain is not a defining feature and warrants separate evaluation
Recent flu-like illness is not a characteristic feature, although illness can trigger a reflex episode

data.diagnosis: Sinus node dysfunction with intermittent sinus arrest
data.description: Failure of the sinus node to generate or transmit impulses, producing pauses and symptoms of reduced cerebral perfusion. A vagally mediated pause must be distinguished from intrinsic sinus node disease.
symptoms_in_common: A 3–4 second pause with absent P waves
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior phlebotomy-associated syncope favors a reflex mechanism
Nausea, sweating, and pallor preceding the pause favor vasovagal presyncope
Epigastric and chest pain are not typical primary manifestations
Intrinsic sinus node dysfunction is less typical at age 33

data.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle, sometimes following a viral illness, that can cause chest pain, arrhythmias, or conduction disturbances. The supplied ECGs alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: A transient rhythm disturbance with hypotension
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous syncope specifically during phlebotomy is not explained by acute myocarditis
The stereotyped nausea, pallor, sweating, and sensory dimming favor reflex presyncope
Bilateral hand tingling is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm causing myocardial ischemia and episodic chest pain, occasionally accompanied by bradyarrhythmias. Confirmation requires evidence of ischemia during symptoms or specialized testing.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt central chest pain that resolved before admission
Transient hypotension and a cardiac pause could accompany ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Phlebotomy-triggered syncope is more characteristic of a vasovagal response
Blurred vision, muffled hearing, and bilateral hand tingling are not specific features of coronary spasm
Recent flu-like illness is not a typical feature

data.description: Excessive ventilation can lower carbon dioxide levels and cause chest discomfort, breathlessness, dizziness, and distal tingling. It could explain some symptoms but does not adequately explain the documented pause by itself.
symptoms_in_common: Distal paresthesias and tingling in both hands
symptoms_not_in_common: A documented 3–4 second pause without P waves is not typical
Marked hypotension is not usually explained by isolated hyperventilation
Prior phlebotomy-related syncope and the autonomic prodrome favor a concurrent vasovagal mechanism
Epigastric pain with vomiting is not a defining manifestation

data.description: Air leaks from ruptured alveoli into the mediastinum without trauma. This is the leading diagnosis: the CT shows mediastinal air around the trachea and great vessels, and precordial crepitus is consistent with Hamman's sign.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and supraclavicular fossae
Normal oxygen saturation, breath sounds, and inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear atypical findings; absence of a reported precipitating event does not exclude this diagnosis

data.description: Air enters the pleural space spontaneously, often in young adults. It may coexist with pneumomediastinum, although no definite pneumothorax is evident in the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous emphysema can occur with an associated air leak
symptoms_not_in_common: Equal chest expansion and normal breath sounds make a large pneumothorax less likely
Pain is not exacerbated by inspiration
Precordial crepitus and cervical emphysema favor mediastinal air rather than an isolated pneumothorax

data.description: A tear in the esophagus can release air and digestive contents into the mediastinum. This is an important dangerous alternative, although the history and lack of inflammatory abnormalities make it less likely.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported vomiting, retching, instrumentation, or trauma
Normal inflammatory markers and full blood count despite several days of symptoms
No reported fever, swallowing difficulty, or systemic toxicity

data.description: An airway tear can allow air to escape into the mediastinum and cervical tissues. It usually follows trauma or airway instrumentation; spontaneous rupture is rare.
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding trauma or reported airway instrumentation
Normal breath sounds and preserved oxygen saturation
No reported hemoptysis or severe cough
No airway wall defect is established by the supplied images

data.description: Air accumulates within the pericardial sac, sometimes accompanying other thoracic air leaks. The supplied CT favors pneumomediastinum rather than demonstrating pericardial air.
symptoms_in_common: Precordial abnormal sounds can occur with air near the heart
symptoms_not_in_common: Cervical subcutaneous emphysema is better explained by pneumomediastinum
Precordial crepitus is more characteristic of pneumomediastinum
No preceding trauma, procedure, or positive-pressure ventilation is reported
No definite air within the pericardial sac is demonstrated

data.diagnosis: Lyme disease presenting as erythema migrans
data.description: A tick-transmitted Borrelia infection that can cause an expanding erythematous patch with central clearing. This is a leading consideration given the appearance and Highland exposure; a negative early serology and lack of a recalled tick bite do not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Expanding rash on the right flank
Large annular erythematous patch with relative central clearing in the photograph
Regular visits to the Scottish Highlands, where exposure to infected ticks is possible
Untreated erythema migrans can persist for weeks to months
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent itching is less typical, although mild itching can occur
Persistence for three months is longer than the usual course
Negative Borrelia serology at four weeks lowers support but does not exclude early localized infection

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte fungal infection producing an itchy, expanding ring-shaped rash, usually with a raised, scaly border.
symptoms_in_common: Annular appearance with relative central clearing
Trunk involvement and persistence over months
symptoms_not_in_common: The photograph does not show an obvious scaly, raised advancing edge
The lesion appears unusually large and broadly bordered for a typical isolated ringworm lesion

data.description: A reactive inflammatory eruption characterized by slowly expanding annular or arcuate lesions, sometimes with a fine trailing scale inside the advancing border.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic trailing scale is not apparent in the photograph
A single very large, broadly erythematous lesion is less characteristic than multiple smaller rings or arcs

data.description: A benign inflammatory skin condition causing persistent rings of smooth dermal papules, usually without surface scale.
symptoms_in_common: Annular configuration with relative central clearing
No obvious surface scale in the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Itching is less typical because lesions are usually asymptomatic
A broad red patch rather than a ring of discrete firm papules
Marked outward expansion of a large flank lesion is less typical of localized granuloma annulare

data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction to an external allergen that can produce persistent itchy erythema when exposure continues.
symptoms_in_common: Persistence over months could occur with repeated exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: An expanding annular lesion with central clearing is not a typical pattern
No obvious vesicles, crusting, or eczematous scale in the photograph
No specific contact exposure is described

data.description: Transient constriction of an epicardial coronary artery causes myocardial ischemia, typically at rest overnight or in the early morning. This is the leading possibility given the timing, smoking, alcohol association, and apparent variation in coronary narrowing between angiographic panels, although the imaging sequence and medication response are not provided.
symptoms_in_common: Squeezing left-sided chest pain lasting approximately 30 minutes
Early-morning episodes associated with alcohol consumption
Current smoking, a major risk factor for coronary spasm
Mild troponin-T elevation consistent with transient ischemic myocardial injury
ECG appears to show inferior and lateral ST-segment depression
Preserved left ventricular function without regional wall motion abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia is not explained by coronary spasm

data.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic acute coronary syndrome, potentially non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
data.description: Acute coronary plaque disruption or erosion can reduce coronary blood flow and cause myocardial injury. Chest pain, ischemic ECG changes, and elevated troponin warrant consideration, but myocardial infarction requires a troponin rise or fall and supporting evidence of ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent inferior and lateral ST-segment depression on ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Early-morning alcohol-associated episodes favor vasospasm over a fixed obstructive lesion
The provided angiographic images do not clearly establish a fixed obstructive culprit lesion
Microcytic hypochromic anemia is not directly explained by plaque disruption

data.diagnosis: Coronary microvascular dysfunction with microvascular angina
data.description: Abnormal dilation or spasm of small coronary vessels causes ischemia despite the absence of major epicardial coronary obstruction. Angiography alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: No clearly established fixed obstructive coronary lesion in the supplied images
Mild troponin elevation, which can occur with microvascular ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent changes in epicardial coronary caliber would favor epicardial spasm if confirmed
The early-morning alcohol-associated pattern more strongly favors vasospastic angina
Microcytic hypochromic anemia is not explained by microvascular dysfunction

data.description: A coronary artery segment, usually in the left anterior descending artery, travels beneath heart muscle and may undergo dynamic compression. Confirmation requires demonstration of systolic compression or characteristic intravascular imaging findings, which cannot be established from these still images alone.
symptoms_in_common: Chest pain compatible with myocardial ischemia
Apparent narrowing involving the left anterior descending coronary artery
symptoms_not_in_common: Early-morning resting pain after alcohol is more characteristic of coronary spasm
No exertional or clearly tachycardia-associated trigger is reported
Microcytic hypochromic anemia is not caused by myocardial bridging

data.description: Reduced oxygen delivery from anemia can provoke myocardial ischemia or injury, particularly when another coronary abnormality is present. Type 2 myocardial infarction would require a dynamic troponin change and evidence of ischemia rather than a single elevated measurement.
symptoms_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL
symptoms_not_in_common: A discrete early-morning episode after alcohol is not a characteristic anemia-related pattern
Apparent dynamic epicardial coronary narrowing is not explained by anemia alone
No marked tachycardia, hypotension, or other major acute physiological stress is documented

data.description: A possible prenatal drug-related developmental disorder involving limb and dental abnormalities. Acetazolamide exposure has been reported with these findings, but a causal relationship in humans is not established.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal acetazolamide exposure before and throughout pregnancy
Apparent bilateral reduction or absence of digits in the hands and feet
Panoramic radiograph suggesting multiple missing permanent teeth
Low birth weight at full term
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe spontaneous dental pain and multiple carious teeth are not specific features of embryopathy
Hypocalcified upper incisors are nonspecific and do not establish a drug-related cause

data.description: A usually TP63-related genetic disorder characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations, ectodermal abnormalities, missing teeth, and variably present cleft lip or palate.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent bilateral ectrodactyly or digital reduction affecting the hands and feet
Radiographic suggestion of multiple missing permanent teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal skin, hair, and nails argue against prominent ectodermal dysplasia
Normal upper lip and palate, although clefting is not obligatory
No major dysmorphic features reported
Acute severe dental pain is more consistent with a secondary dental complication

data.description: A genetically heterogeneous congenital limb disorder involving absent or underdeveloped central digits, sometimes with syndactyly, without a broader syndromic phenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent bilateral missing or reduced digits in the hands and feet
Normal skin, hair, nails, lip, and palate
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple apparently missing permanent teeth are not typical of an isolated limb disorder
Hypocalcified permanent upper incisors
Retained primary lower central incisors
Low birth weight is not a defining feature

data.description: A TP63-related disorder, also called ADULT syndrome, that can combine split-hand/split-foot malformations, syndactyly, dental agenesis, and variable skin, nail, and lacrimal abnormalities, usually without clefting.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent ectrodactyly affecting both hands and feet
Radiographic suggestion of permanent tooth agenesis
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal nails and skin argue against characteristic ectodermal involvement
No lacrimal abnormalities reported
Low birth weight is not a characteristic feature
Severe spontaneous dental pain is not a primary syndrome feature

data.description: A TP63-related developmental disorder characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations and mammary or nipple hypoplasia, sometimes accompanied by dental agenesis and cleft palate.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic suggestion of multiple missing permanent teeth
Normal hair, skin, and nails can occur in this syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: No mammary or nipple abnormalities reported, although these were not specifically assessed

Hypocalcified incisors are not a defining feature

data.description: Intermittent episodes of disorganized atrial electrical activity causing an irregular heartbeat. This diagnosis is documented by the Holter report and is the strongest explanation for the patient's symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Two episodes of atrial fibrillation documented on Holter monitoring
Normal, regular heart rate between episodes
Hypertension, a risk factor for atrial fibrillation

data.description: An alcohol-associated atrial arrhythmia, most commonly atrial fibrillation. This is a possible trigger for the documented atrial fibrillation rather than a separate rhythm diagnosis; the amount and timing of alcohol consumption require clarification.

Rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented on Holter monitoring
Normal heart and lung examination between episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Two other episodes had no reported association with alcohol
Heavy or binge alcohol consumption was not established

data.description: Early electrical impulses arising in the atria that can cause palpitations and trigger atrial fibrillation. The Holter report documents a substantial burden of supraventricular ectopy, although rhythm-strip review is needed to characterize it precisely.

data.description: An episodic rapid rhythm originating from an atrial focus. It could coexist with atrial fibrillation and account for some Holter-reported supraventricular runs, but those runs require direct rhythm review before this diagnosis can be established.

Normal heart rate between symptomatic episodes

data.description: An organized atrial reentrant rhythm that can cause episodic tachycardia and may coexist with atrial fibrillation. It is a less likely alternative here because the report identifies atrial fibrillation and does not document flutter.

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colonic mucosa, sometimes involving the entire colon. The endoscopic findings are compatible but not diagnostic.

Colonic ulceration with a normal ileum
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical direct manifestations

Colonic disease with a normal ileum
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical features of isolated cytomegalovirus colitis

data.description: An intestinal infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica that may produce chronic diarrhea and discrete, exudative colonic ulcers resembling inflammatory bowel disease.

symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical
Diffuse granular inflammation throughout the entire colon is less characteristic than patchy ulceration

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the bowel that can mimic inflammatory colitis. The dense lymphoid-appearing infiltrates in the supplied biopsy images warrant consideration, but classification requires pathology review, labeled immunostains, and potentially clonality testing.

symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical without urinary tract involvement

data.diagnosis: Late-presenting congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic stomach

Apparent enteric tube looping within the left thoracic abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: First presentation at age 9 is less typical than presentation in infancy, although delayed presentations occur

data.diagnosis: Acute gastric volvulus associated with diaphragmatic herniation
data.description: Twisting of a herniated stomach can cause obstruction, rapid gastric distension, and potentially ischemia. It is an urgent possible complication, although radiographs alone do not confirm the rotation.

Large left thoracic air-fluid level suggesting a distended stomach
symptoms_not_in_common: The presentation is predominantly respiratory rather than the more usual severe epigastric pain and retching
Apparent successful tube passage is less typical of a completely obstructing volvulus

data.diagnosis: Left diaphragmatic eventration with gastric distension

data.description: Air and fluid in the pleural space can compress the lung and produce a horizontal air-fluid level. It is an important imaging mimic but is less supported by the subsequent tube configuration.

symptoms_not_in_common: A rounded, apparently bounded air-containing structure is less typical than free pleural air

data.description: A congenital cystic lung lesion may remain undetected until childhood and can develop an air-fluid level when infected. This is a less likely alternative to an intrathoracic stomach.

Diminished breath sounds over the affected side
symptoms_not_in_common: Very abrupt onset over 6 hours is less typical of infection in a congenital lung lesion
The apparent enteric tube loop within the lesion is not expected in a pulmonary malformation

data.diagnosis: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
data.description: A localized tumor of clonal plasma cells outside bone marrow. This is the leading consideration given the plasma-cell-like biopsy appearance and absence of systemic myeloma findings; confirmation requires immunophenotyping and light-chain restriction studies.

Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Normal calcium, renal function, and hematological indexes
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly contradictory clinical findings are reported

data.description: A systemic plasma-cell malignancy that can occasionally form an extramedullary hepatic mass. The normal systemic evaluation makes this substantially less likely than a solitary plasmacytoma.

Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Normal calcium and renal function
Normal hematological indexes
Normal skeletal radiography
Normal beta-2 microglobulin

data.diagnosis: Primary hepatic marginal zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent plasma-cell predominance is less typical than a mixed small B-cell and plasmacytic infiltrate

symptoms_not_in_common: Normal hematological indexes and liver tests are less typical of an actively inflammatory presentation

No reported cirrhosis or chronic liver disease

data.description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can cause cervicitis and abnormal vaginal discharge. Symptoms may develop within days of exposure; laboratory testing is needed for diagnosis.
A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that is often asymptomatic but can cause cervicitis and vaginal discharge. Recent intercourse with a new partner makes it an important consideration.
A sexually transmitted parasitic infection that can cause vaginal discharge, sometimes accompanied by odor, irritation, or painful urination.

An imbalance of vaginal bacteria that commonly causes thin discharge and a fishy odor. It is associated with new sexual partners but is not classified as a conventional sexually transmitted infection.
An overgrowth of Candida yeast that can cause thick vaginal discharge, usually with itching or vulvar irritation. It is generally not sexually transmitted.

data.description: Extensive emphysema with giant air-filled bullae that compress functioning lung. Tobacco and cannabis exposure are risk factors. The images show very large left-sided bullae, making this the leading diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of tobacco and cannabis use
Large left-sided air spaces with compression of adjacent lung on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset of pleuritic chest pain is less typical of uncomplicated bullous emphysema and suggests an acute complication

data.description: Air entering the pleural space because of underlying lung disease, often following rupture of an emphysematous bulla. This is an urgent consideration, although the supplied images predominantly demonstrate giant bullae rather than a clearly established pneumothorax.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe persistent airflow obstruction requires underlying lung disease rather than pneumothorax alone
Large air spaces with internal walls on CT favor intrapulmonary bullae rather than isolated pleural air

data.diagnosis: Smoking-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysema
data.description: Chronic airflow limitation caused by smoking-related airway injury and destruction of alveolar tissue. Bullous emphysema is one manifestation.

Markedly asymmetric giant bullae at age 44 are less typical of ordinary smoking-related COPD

data.description: A smoking-associated lung disease producing nodules and irregular cysts, usually in the upper and middle lung zones. It can cause airflow obstruction and spontaneous pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: Acute pleuritic pain potentially associated with pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Dominant giant left-sided bullae are less typical than numerous irregular cysts
The supplied images do not demonstrate the characteristic upper-zone nodular and cystic pattern

data.description: An inherited FLCN-related disorder causing pulmonary cysts and recurrent pneumothorax, sometimes accompanied by characteristic skin lesions and renal tumors.

Acute dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain compatible with pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe obstructive spirometry is unusual because lung function is often preserved
Extensive giant bullous destruction is less typical than multiple discrete basal and medial cysts
The smoking-associated emphysematous presentation favors an acquired rather than inherited disorder

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with extramedullary involvement and light-chain cast nephropathy
data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal immunoglobulin. This is the leading possibility given anemia, hypercalcemia, renal failure, elevated total protein, apparent marrow plasma-cell infiltration, and renal tubular casts. The abdominal mass could represent extramedullary disease; confirmation requires monoclonal protein studies and tissue immunophenotyping.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Upper abdominal pain with a bulky abdominal mass
Marrow histology suggestive of plasma-cell infiltration
Renal tubular casts compatible with light-chain cast nephropathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome is uncommon except in highly aggressive disease
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is an unusual presenting complication

data.description: An aggressive plasma-cell malignancy characterized by circulating malignant plasma cells, often accompanied by extensive marrow and extramedullary involvement. A peripheral blood smear and flow cytometry are necessary to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: High LDH and biochemical tumor lysis syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is possible but not a defining or usual feature

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma with plasma-cell differentiation that can form bulky extranodal masses and involve bone marrow. It can resemble aggressive myeloma histologically, requiring immunophenotyping, Epstein–Barr virus testing, and monoclonal protein evaluation for distinction.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Bulky abdominal mass and abdominal pain
Severe anemia and thrombocytopenia from possible marrow involvement
Elevated LDH and tumor lysis syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated total protein is less characteristic than in multiple myeloma
Hypercalcemia with apparent light-chain cast nephropathy favors a plasma-cell malignancy
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is not a typical presenting feature

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that may produce bulky abdominal lymphadenopathy, marrow infiltration, elevated LDH, and spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome. Tissue immunophenotyping is needed to distinguish it from plasma-cell neoplasms.

symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated total protein is not typical

Renal tubular casts suggestive of light-chain nephropathy favor multiple myeloma
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is uncommon

data.description: A lymphoplasmacytic B-cell malignancy usually producing monoclonal IgM, which can cause elevated total protein, cytopenias, constitutional symptoms, and lymphadenopathy. The aggressive presentation here is less typical unless transformation has occurred.

symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is unusual
Light-chain cast nephropathy is much less typical than in multiple myeloma
Spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome and markedly elevated LDH are atypical without transformation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is not characteristic

data.description: A rare skin-predominant vasculopathy causing persistent macules or livedoid patches. Subtle reddish-brown, irregular or livedoid patches in the clinical photograph
Apparent lymphocyte-rich inflammation around an artery with a prominent eosinophilic ring in the biopsy image
Normal blood tests and autoimmune screen
symptoms_not_in_common: Multifocal peripheral nerve damage is uncommon in this usually skin-predominant condition

data.description: A skin-predominant necrotizing vasculitis of small and medium-sized arteries that can cause livedo, painful nodules, ulcers, and occasionally peripheral neuropathy.

Normal autoimmune screening and lack of systemic symptoms

data.diagnosis: Classical homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency

data.diagnosis: Brainstem cavernous malformation with recent hemorrhage

data.description: A rapidly progressive inflammatory disease causing myocardial destruction, heart failure, arrhythmias, and cardiogenic shock. Myocardial biopsy appearance suggestive of giant-cell inflammation and myocyte injury

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock

Severe chest discomfort with diaphoresis and dyspnea

Basilar rales and elevated jugular venous pressure

data.description: An aggressive eosinophil-mediated myocardial inflammation that can cause extensive myocyte necrosis and fulminant cardiogenic shock. It may be related to hypersensitivity, systemic eosinophilic disease, or occur without an identified trigger.

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation of the myocardium can cause conduction abnormalities, ventricular arrhythmias, and heart failure. data.description: Acute myocardial inflammation, often associated with a viral infection or immune response, can mimic myocardial infarction and progress rapidly to severe heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Biopsy typically shows lymphocyte-predominant inflammation with myocyte injury.
