Tachycardia, hypotension, and signs of impaired perfusion
Elevated jugular venous pressure, hepatic congestion, and basilar rales
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent multinucleated giant cells are not typical of ordinary lymphocytic myocarditis
Exertional chest heaviness progressing to rest pain more strongly resembles coronary ischemia
Prominent bloating is nonspecific and not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A multisystem calcium-channel disorder causing prolonged cardiac repolarization and potentially fatal ventricular arrhythmias, sometimes accompanied by syndactyly and distinctive facial features. The illustrated heterozygous p.G406R variant strongly supports this diagnosis; normal neurodevelopment does not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
ECG findings suggestive of prolonged QT intervals and abnormal repolarization
Apparent bilateral finger syndactyly in the hand photographs
Distinctive facial features, including a round face and small upper jaw and teeth
Illustrated heterozygous c.1216G>A, p.G406R variant characteristic of CACNA1C-related Timothy syndrome
Normal cardiac structure despite a life-threatening electrical disturbance
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal neurodevelopment, although developmental abnormalities are variable
Normal toes, although syndactyly can be confined to the hands
The sister's isolated epinephrine-induced QT prolongation is not sufficient to establish the same syndrome

data.description: An inherited potassium-channel disorder causing delayed ventricular repolarization and susceptibility to torsades de pointes, particularly during adrenergic stimulation. Resting QT intervals can be normal in affected relatives.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest with a structurally normal heart
ECG findings suggestive of QT prolongation
Sister's paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine testing
Absence of earlier syncope does not exclude concealed disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent finger syndactyly
Distinctive facial and dental features
Nearly bald head
The illustrated p.G406R variant favors CACNA1C-related disease rather than KCNQ1-related disease

data.description: An inherited potassium-channel disorder that prolongs the QT interval and predisposes to ventricular arrhythmias, which may be precipitated by sudden arousal or QT-prolonging medications.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest during exposure to an anesthetic that can prolong QT
ECG findings suggestive of prolonged repolarization
Normal echocardiographic anatomy and ventricular function
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent finger syndactyly
Distinctive facial and dental abnormalities
Nearly bald head
Sister's epinephrine-induced QT response is more suggestive of type 1 than type 2 long QT syndrome
The illustrated p.G406R variant favors CACNA1C-related disease

data.description: An inherited ion-channel disorder characterized by ventricular arrhythmias, prominent U waves or prolonged QU intervals, periodic paralysis, and variable facial and skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Life-threatening arrhythmia despite normal cardiac structure
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported episodes of periodic paralysis
Normal toes without reported characteristic toe abnormalities
Nearly bald head is not characteristic
The illustrated p.G406R variant favors Timothy syndrome rather than Andersen-Tawil syndrome

data.description: An inherited calcium-handling disorder causing adrenergically triggered bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, usually with a normal resting ECG and structurally normal heart.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest in early childhood
No preceding syncope does not exclude the disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: QT prolongation on the supplied ECG is not characteristic
Sister's epinephrine-induced QT prolongation rather than documented ventricular tachycardia
Apparent finger syndactyly
Distinctive facial and dental features
The illustrated p.G406R variant favors CACNA1C-related Timothy syndrome

data.diagnosis: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine kinase gene fusion
data.description: A clonal blood disorder, often associated with FIP1L1::PDGFRA, that causes excessive eosinophil production and tissue injury. The marked blood and marrow eosinophilia shown is suggestive but requires molecular testing for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Diarrhea potentially caused by gastrointestinal eosinophilic infiltration
Images suggest abundant eosinophils in blood and bone marrow
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent travel to rural India favors a competing parasitic explanation
Preexisting biopsy-confirmed ulcerative colitis is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A syndrome of marked eosinophilia with eosinophil-mediated organ injury, diagnosed only after excluding parasitic, drug-related, clonal, and other secondary causes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible eosinophilic infiltration of gastrointestinal tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent residence and travel in parasite-endemic regions require exclusion of a secondary cause
Established ulcerative colitis is not a defining feature

data.description: Intestinal infection with Strongyloides stercoralis, acquired through contaminated soil in endemic areas. Chronic infection can cause diarrhea, weight loss, skin manifestations, and eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in Indonesia and recent rural travel in India
Absence of fever is compatible with uncomplicated infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable spleen tip is not typical of uncomplicated infection
Anterior thoracic papules are less characteristic than urticaria or a rapidly migrating serpiginous rash
Pronounced eosinophilic marrow expansion warrants investigation for a clonal disorder

data.description: An eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorder causing bowel dysfunction and tissue eosinophilia after secondary causes, including parasites and systemic eosinophilic disorders, are excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal biopsy image compatible with an eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate
symptoms_not_in_common: Splenic enlargement is unusual for an isolated gastrointestinal disorder
Papular thoracic rash suggests additional systemic involvement
Marked leukocytosis and extensive marrow eosinophilia are less typical of isolated disease
Absence of abdominal pain, although it does not exclude the diagnosis

data.description: An uncommon medication reaction that can produce rash, eosinophilia, and systemic symptoms. A temporal relationship to medication initiation or dose changes and evidence of organ injury would help establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparently longstanding mesalamine treatment without a reported recent dose change
Absence of fever
Splenic enlargement is not typical of a simple drug eruption
Recent tropical travel provides an alternative explanation
Marked marrow eosinophilic expansion raises concern for another systemic cause

data.diagnosis: High-grade astrocytic glioma with intratumoral hemorrhage
data.description: An aggressive glial brain tumor that can bleed and provoke seizures. The ring-enhancing frontal lesion and apparent GFAP and OLIG2 positivity favor a glial neoplasm; definitive subtype and grade require formal pathology and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Hyperdense left frontal lesion on CT, suggesting hemorrhage
Ring enhancement and surrounding edema on MRI
Apparent glial-marker positivity in the supplied pathology images
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt presentation without preceding progressive neurological symptoms is less typical unless hemorrhage occurs
Normal neurological examination despite substantial surrounding edema

data.description: A low-flow vascular malformation that can cause intracerebral bleeding and seizures and may be invisible on conventional angiography.
symptoms_in_common: No obvious vascular malformation on the supplied angiographic views
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ring enhancement and extensive edema are less typical of an uncomplicated cavernous malformation
Apparent proliferating glial tumor cells on the supplied pathology images are not explained by a cavernous malformation

data.description: An abnormal connection between cerebral arteries and veins that can rupture, producing a lobar hemorrhage and seizures in a young adult.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with an abrupt neurological presentation
Frontal hyperdense lesion compatible with intracerebral hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: No obvious vascular nidus or early draining vein on the supplied angiographic views
Ring-enhancing mass rather than a clearly demonstrated vascular lesion
Apparent glial neoplasm on the supplied pathology images

data.description: A secondary brain tumor, sometimes from melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, or another cancer, that can bleed and produce a ring-enhancing mass with edema.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known cancer or systemic illness
Young age makes metastasis less likely
Apparent GFAP and OLIG2 positivity favors a primary glial tumor rather than most metastases

data.description: A localized intracerebral infection that may appear as a ring-enhancing lesion with edema and cause seizures or impaired consciousness. Diffusion-weighted imaging and microbiological evaluation help distinguish it from a tumor.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal routine laboratory tests
No reported infectious history or source
Hyperdense, apparently hemorrhagic lesion is less typical
Apparent glial tumor pathology rather than suppurative inflammation

data.description: A rare fungal infection of the vertebrae caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. The destructive lumbar lesion, adjacent soft-tissue involvement, calcified thoracic lymph nodes, and apparent yeast forms in the biopsy make this an important possibility; fungal culture or molecular testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening back and left hip pain over six months
Pain sometimes waking him from sleep
Lumbar vertebral and endplate destruction with adjacent soft-tissue abnormality
Apparent fungal organisms in the biopsy
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes compatible with previous granulomatous infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or night sweats, although these can be absent in localized infection
No spinal tenderness despite substantial pain

data.description: An uncommon bone infection caused by Cryptococcus species that can produce destructive vertebral lesions and chronic pain. Rounded yeast-like structures in the biopsy warrant consideration, but organism size, capsule-specific staining, and culture are needed to distinguish it from other fungi.
symptoms_in_common: Left hip pain potentially referred from the lumbar lesion
Rounded yeast-like structures in the biopsy
Absence of fever, which can occur with localized cryptococcal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Calcified thoracic lymph nodes are less characteristic of cryptococcosis
No reported headache or neurologic symptoms to suggest associated central nervous system infection

data.description: A chronic mycobacterial infection of the spine that can destroy adjacent vertebral endplates and produce paraspinal extension. Its indolent course can occur without fever, although apparent fungal organisms in the biopsy favor another cause.
symptoms_in_common: Six months of worsening back pain
Vertebral endplate destruction and adjacent soft-tissue involvement
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes compatible with prior granulomatous disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent yeast forms in the biopsy are not explained by tuberculosis
No fever or night sweats, although their absence does not exclude spinal tuberculosis
No spinal tenderness or deformity

data.description: A bacterial infection of the vertebral bodies and intervening disc, commonly acquired through bloodstream spread. Older adults may have chronic pain without fever or neurologic deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Adjacent vertebral endplate abnormalities and paraspinal soft-tissue involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent fungal organisms in the biopsy rather than bacterial findings
No fever or chills
No focal spinal tenderness
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes are not explained by a typical pyogenic spinal infection

data.diagnosis: Metastatic malignancy involving the lumbar spine
data.description: Cancer spreading to vertebral bone can cause destructive lesions, persistent pain, and weight loss. The clinical red flags support consideration, but endplate-centered destruction and apparent fungal organisms favor infection.
symptoms_in_common: Destructive vertebral lesion with adjacent soft-tissue abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent fungal organisms in the biopsy
Destruction centered on adjacent vertebral endplates is more suggestive of spondylodiscitis
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes more strongly suggest previous granulomatous infection than active metastatic disease

data.description: A rare cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma involving subcutaneous fat, often causing fever and weight loss. The apparent lymphocytic infiltration around adipocytes in the biopsy makes this an important possibility, but confirmation requires immunophenotyping and molecular studies.
symptoms_in_common: Eyelid swelling potentially caused by subcutaneous infiltration
Apparent adipocyte-rimming lymphoid infiltrate in the supplied biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and opacities are unusual
Prominent painless axillary lymphadenopathy is less typical because disease usually remains confined to subcutaneous tissue
Cough, shortness of breath, and moist rales are not usual primary manifestations

data.description: An aggressive cutaneous T-cell lymphoma that can infiltrate subcutaneous fat and resemble panniculitis. Distinguishing it from subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma requires specific immunohistochemical testing.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary abnormalities potentially reflecting extracutaneous dissemination
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated eyelid swelling is an uncommon presentation
No ulcerated or necrotic skin lesions are described
Painless axillary lymphadenopathy is not a defining feature

data.description: An aggressive, usually Epstein-Barr virus-associated lymphoma that commonly involves nasal structures but can affect skin, orbital tissues, and lungs. Diagnosis requires tissue examination, immunophenotyping, and Epstein-Barr virus testing.
symptoms_in_common: Right eyelid swelling potentially indicating orbital or adjacent tissue involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No nasal obstruction, epistaxis, or destructive nasal lesion is reported
An adipocyte-rimming infiltrate is less characteristic than an angiocentric, necrotizing infiltrate
No ulcerative skin lesions are described

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus panniculitis
data.description: An autoimmune disease that can produce inflammation of subcutaneous fat, lymphadenopathy, and pulmonary inflammation. Lupus panniculitis can resemble a panniculitic lymphoma histologically, so clinical findings and laboratory testing are needed.
symptoms_in_common: Eyelid swelling potentially associated with periorbital inflammation
Cough and shortness of breath potentially associated with pulmonary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple discrete pulmonary nodules are not a typical lupus lung pattern
No characteristic rash, arthritis, oral ulcers, or renal manifestations are reported
No typical tender subcutaneous nodules or residual lipoatrophy are described

data.description: A small-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the respiratory tract and kidneys and can cause orbital inflammation. Pulmonary nodules and eyelid swelling make it a consideration, although the supplied biopsy appears less characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules and opacities
Right eyelid swelling potentially reflecting orbital inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless axillary lymphadenopathy is not a typical dominant feature
Apparent lymphoid rimming of adipocytes is not characteristic of necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis
No sinus symptoms, epistaxis, hematuria, or other renal manifestations are reported

data.description: Prenatal Zika infection can disrupt fetal brain development and cause ventriculomegaly and cortical abnormalities, sometimes without microcephaly. This is the leading consideration given residence in an endemic area, the maternal illness, and positive maternal serum NAT results shown in the timeline. Negative amniotic-fluid NAT does not reliably exclude fetal infection.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache during pregnancy
Possible sexual exposure through an affected spouse
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of microcephaly is less characteristic of classic congenital Zika syndrome, although it does not exclude infection

data.description: Congenital CMV can cause fetal ventriculomegaly, periventricular injury, calcifications, and abnormal cortical development. The negative TORCH evaluation reduces its likelihood; the strength of exclusion depends on the specific tests performed.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal fever and headache compatible with a nonspecific viral illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal conjunctivitis with maculopapular rash is not a characteristic CMV presentation
Widening of the cavum septum pellucidum is not a defining CMV finding

data.description: Transplacental Toxoplasma gondii infection can cause fetal hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications, and chorioretinitis. Negative TORCH testing makes this less likely, depending on the testing method and timing.
symptoms_in_common: Severe fetal ventriculomegaly consistent with hydrocephalus
Maternal fever and headache can occur during acute infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are not typical
Abnormal cavum septum pellucidum is not a characteristic diagnostic feature

data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct produces enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles. It may be isolated or associated with genetic conditions not detected by chromosomal microarray.
symptoms_in_common: Marked bilateral lateral ventricular enlargement measuring 20–25 mm
Dangling choroid plexus associated with severe ventriculomegaly
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal fever, headache, maculopapular rash, and conjunctivitis are not explained by aqueductal stenosis
Dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum is not a defining feature of isolated aqueductal stenosis

data.description: Prenatal infection with this rodent-associated virus can cause severe hydrocephalus, ventriculomegaly, intracranial calcifications, and chorioretinitis. It is generally not included in routine TORCH panels, although no rodent exposure is documented here.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal fetal central nervous system development
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are less characteristic
Widened or dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum is not a defining finding
Sexual exposure is not a typical route of transmission

data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 variants. Progressive spastic weakness, cognitive decline, and a thin corpus callosum are characteristic. The depicted SPG11 p.M245fs and p.F2343fs variants make this the strongest diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive lower-limb weakness beginning in young adulthood
Scissors gait and severe lower-limb spasticity
Apparent corpus callosum thinning and periventricular white-matter abnormalities on MRI
Compound heterozygous SPG11 variants inherited from unaffected parents

data.description: An autosomal recessive complicated spastic paraplegia caused by ZFYVE26 variants, often associated with cognitive impairment, a thin corpus callosum, and sometimes retinal degeneration or peripheral neuropathy.
symptoms_in_common: Young-adult onset of progressive spastic lower-limb weakness
Apparent thin corpus callosum and white-matter abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: The identified compound heterozygous variants involve SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26

data.description: An autosomal recessive FA2H-related disorder that can produce complicated spastic paraplegia, cognitive deterioration, dysphagia, and white-matter changes. Brain iron accumulation, dystonia, and cerebellar involvement may occur.
symptoms_in_common: White-matter abnormalities and apparent corpus callosum thinning
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at age 24 after normal development is less typical than childhood onset
The identified variants involve SPG11 rather than FA2H

data.description: A recessively inherited disorder, usually caused by ARSA deficiency, in which sulfatide accumulation damages central and peripheral myelin. Adult presentations can include cognitive decline followed by progressive motor dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-limb spastic paraplegia preceding cognitive symptoms is less typical of the adult presentation
The identified compound heterozygous SPG11 variants support hereditary spastic paraplegia rather than metachromatic leukodystrophy

data.description: An autosomal recessive CYP27A1-related disorder of bile acid synthesis that causes cholestanol accumulation. Neurologic manifestations can include progressive spasticity, cognitive impairment, ataxia, and swallowing difficulties.
symptoms_in_common: Spastic lower-limb weakness and abnormal gait
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent thin corpus callosum with predominantly periventricular abnormalities is less characteristic than cerebellar and dentate-region abnormalities
The identified variants involve SPG11 rather than CYP27A1

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: An extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumor arising from paraganglia near the heart that can secrete catecholamines. This is the leading diagnosis given the apparent pericardiac mass and marked norepinephrine and normetanephrine elevations.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Normal epinephrine, compatible with an extra-adrenal catecholamine-secreting tumor
Apparent tracer-avid mass adjacent to the heart on the supplied imaging

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting tumor of the adrenal medulla that causes spells of headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension. The biochemical findings fit, but the identified abdominal lesion was brown fat rather than an adrenal tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated urinary catecholamines and their metabolites
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent tumor on the supplied imaging is near the heart rather than within an adrenal gland
The initially suspected juxta-adrenal lesion was subsequently identified as brown fat

data.description: A usually benign sympathetic nervous system tumor that can arise in the mediastinum and occasionally secrete catecholamines. It is a less likely alternative to paraganglioma.
symptoms_in_common: Headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension if hormonally active
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked normetanephrine elevation is more characteristic of pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma
Severe paroxysmal hypertension is uncommon in ganglioneuroma
The apparent pericardiac location is less typical than a posterior mediastinal location

data.description: Excess thyroid hormone production can cause adrenergic symptoms, including palpitations, sweating, and elevated blood pressure, but does not adequately explain the tumor imaging or biochemical pattern.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe episodic hypertension with a diastolic pressure of 130
Marked urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine elevations
Apparent tracer-avid pericardiac mass
Paroxysmal headache accompanying hypertensive spells

data.description: A pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder developing after 20 weeks, associated with proteinuria or maternal organ dysfunction. It is an important initial differential but was reportedly excluded in this case.
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal palpitations and sweating
Marked urinary catecholamine and normetanephrine elevations
Apparent pericardiac tumor on imaging
Initial work-up reportedly excluded pre-eclampsia

data.description: An opportunistic bacterial infection that can cause multiloculated brain abscesses in immunosuppressed patients. The enhancing left frontal lesion, surrounding edema, suppurative histology, and apparent filamentous organisms make this a leading possibility; microbiologic testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Multiloculated enhancing left frontal lesion with surrounding edema
Suppurative inflammation and apparent filamentous organisms in the supplied tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset with briefly resolving confusion is less typical of an abscess itself, although associated seizures could explain it
Disconjugate gaze is not specifically explained by the frontal lesion
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: An uncommon central nervous system infection that can produce brain abscesses, particularly in older or immunosuppressed adults. Culture or molecular testing would be required to distinguish it from other bacterial infections.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent filamentous organisms are less consistent with Listeria, which is a short rod
Briefly resolving and recurrent confusion is less typical unless seizures occur
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: An opportunistic parasitic infection that causes necrotizing brain lesions, often with ring enhancement and edema, in patients with impaired cellular immunity.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing cerebral lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: A predominantly solitary frontal lesion is less typical than multiple lesions, often involving the basal ganglia
Apparent bacterial filamentous organisms and suppurative histology favor a bacterial abscess
Sudden fluctuating onset is less typical without associated seizures
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: A lymphoma confined to the central nervous system that can cause enhancing brain masses and focal neurologic deficits. Immunosuppression increases risk, and lesions in immunocompromised patients may be necrotic or ring-enhancing.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing brain mass with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppurative inflammation and apparent microorganisms are not typical of lymphoma
Abrupt, transiently resolving symptoms are less typical than progressive neurologic decline
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: An aggressive primary brain tumor, most common in older adults, that frequently appears as an irregular enhancing mass with central necrosis and extensive surrounding edema.
symptoms_in_common: Expressive aphasia from a dominant frontal lesion
Irregular enhancing lesion with extensive surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppurative inflammation and apparent microorganisms favor infection rather than glioblastoma
Abrupt onset and temporarily resolving confusion are less typical unless tumor-associated seizures occur
Disconjugate gaze is not directly explained by the frontal location
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: An acute bacterial lung infection, often caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, producing airspace consolidation. This is a strong initial consideration, although imaging alone cannot identify the organism.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds
Right lower lung consolidation with subsequent bilateral airspace opacities
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Mantoux test is not explained by ordinary bacterial pneumonia

data.description: A fungal infection acquired by inhaling Blastomyces spores from soil, particularly in wooded areas near freshwater in endemic regions. It can mimic bacterial pneumonia and cause progressive multifocal consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent stay near a lake, providing a possible environmental exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset only one week after the reported exposure is shorter than the usual incubation period
Positive Mantoux test is not explained by blastomycosis

data.description: A bacterial pneumonia acquired through inhalation of contaminated water aerosols. Diabetes and smoking increase susceptibility, and pulmonary infiltrates may progress rapidly.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel with possible, but unconfirmed, exposure to contaminated water aerosols
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent yellow sputum is less characteristic than a dry or minimally productive cough
Positive Mantoux test is unrelated to Legionella infection

data.description: An infection caused by Francisella tularensis that can involve the lungs after inhalation of contaminated environmental material or dissemination following an arthropod bite. Outdoor exposure and a short incubation period make it a consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Recent outdoor sleeping with potential environmental or arthropod exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Yellow sputum is less typical than a dry cough
Positive Mantoux test is not explained by tularemia

data.description: A lung infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Diabetes increases the risk of active disease, but a positive Mantoux test indicates immune sensitization and does not establish active tuberculosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt five-day illness with chills and high fever is less typical than a prolonged course
Acute purulent sputum is more suggestive of bacterial pneumonia
Rapidly progressive predominantly lower-lung consolidation is less typical than classic upper-lobe disease
Recent lake exposure does not explain tuberculosis acquisition

data.diagnosis: CHRNE-related congenital myasthenic syndrome with acetylcholine receptor deficiency
data.description: An inherited postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder, usually caused by recessive CHRNE variants that reduce functional acetylcholine receptors. The electron micrographs appear to show abnormal postsynaptic junctional architecture, supporting a congenital neuromuscular junction disorder but not establishing its genetic subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and weak breathing and crying from birth
Early respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Bilateral ptosis and limited upward gaze
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Marked decrement with repetitive nerve stimulation
Normal cognition and intact deep tendon reflexes
Absence of repetitive CMAPs after a single stimulus
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature
Severe neonatal ventilator dependence is possible but more severe than many presentations

data.description: An inherited disorder of acetylcholine receptor clustering at the motor endplate. It can cause severe neonatal weakness and respiratory crises, often exacerbated by infections.
symptoms_in_common: Weak breathing and crying at birth
Respiratory failure during the first month
Recurrent respiratory infections associated with respiratory vulnerability
Ptosis and facial, bulbar, and proximal limb weakness
Preserved cognition and deep tendon reflexes
symptoms_not_in_common: Limitation of upward gaze is less characteristic because extraocular movements are often relatively spared
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A rare inherited defect in muscle-specific kinase signaling that disrupts neuromuscular junction formation and maintenance. This genetic disorder is distinct from autoimmune MuSK-antibody myasthenia gravis.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Scoliosis associated with chronic muscle weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not an established characteristic feature

data.description: An inherited impairment of signaling required for motor endplate development, typically producing limb-girdle weakness and sometimes severe respiratory involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Normal cognition and preserved deep tendon reflexes
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe weakness and ventilator dependence beginning in the neonatal period are less typical than later childhood presentation
Limitation of upward gaze is less typical because extraocular muscles are usually relatively spared
Prominent facial and bulbar weakness is less typical than limb-girdle weakness
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature

data.description: An inherited presynaptic defect in acetylcholine synthesis, classically causing episodic apnea and respiratory crises beginning in infancy, particularly during infections or other stress.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal hypotonia and weak respiratory effort
Recurrent respiratory infections that can precipitate respiratory crises
symptoms_not_in_common: The described persistent respiratory impairment is less characteristic than episodic apnea with improvement between attacks
Persistent limitation of upward gaze and extensive proximal weakness are less characteristic of the classic presentation
Marked postsynaptic structural abnormalities, if confirmed on the electron micrographs, would favor a postsynaptic disorder
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature

data.description: Toxic alcohol poisoning in which acidic metabolites cause severe metabolic acidosis and calcium oxalate deposition causes kidney injury. This is the leading diagnosis; the urine microscopy appears to show elongated crystals compatible with calcium oxalate monohydrate.
symptoms_in_common: Shortness of breath with deep, rapid compensatory breathing
Elevated serum osmolality and osmolal gap
Urinary crystals suggestive of calcium oxalate monohydrate
Elevated lactate, which may reflect true elevation or assay interference from ethylene glycol metabolites

data.description: Toxic alcohol poisoning in which formic acid accumulation causes high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, neurological impairment, and characteristic retinal or optic nerve injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary crystals suggestive of calcium oxalate monohydrate
Acute kidney injury with haematuria is less characteristic than in ethylene glycol poisoning

data.description: Accumulation of propylene glycol, often from solvent-containing medications, can cause hyperosmolality, lactic acidosis, neurological dysfunction, and kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: Deep, rapid breathing associated with metabolic acidosis
Elevated serum osmolality and osmolal gap
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary crystals suggestive of calcium oxalate monohydrate
Haematuria is not a characteristic finding

data.description: Salicylate toxicity causes respiratory stimulation and impaired cellular energy metabolism, typically producing respiratory alkalosis combined with high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid breathing and shortness of breath
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated osmolal gap is not a characteristic finding
Urinary crystals suggestive of calcium oxalate monohydrate
Haematuria is not a characteristic finding
The blood gas suggests predominantly metabolic acidosis rather than the characteristic additional primary respiratory alkalosis

data.description: Severe infection can impair tissue perfusion and cellular metabolism, causing lactic acidosis, encephalopathy, and acute kidney injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated osmolal gap is not a characteristic finding
Urinary crystals suggestive of calcium oxalate monohydrate
Haematuria is not a defining feature

data.description: A usually postviral inflammatory thyroid disorder that can cause prolonged fever and transient thyrotoxicosis. The apparent diffuse thyroid enlargement and low attenuation on the provided CT images support thyroid inflammation, although laboratory testing is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Preceding throat symptoms and possible viral exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid; substantial thyroid tenderness is more typical
Absence of odynophagia, which can accompany painful thyroid inflammation

data.description: An uncommon bacterial infection of the thyroid that can cause high fever and neck swelling, sometimes with an abscess. The supplied images suggest thyroid involvement but do not clearly demonstrate a discrete drainable collection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid rather than marked focal tenderness
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Persistent symptoms despite amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, although an abscess or resistant organism could explain treatment failure

data.description: A destructive inflammatory thyroid disorder that releases stored thyroid hormones, producing temporary thyrotoxicosis without thyroid pain. Thyroid function tests and, when appropriate, uptake testing help distinguish it from other causes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prolonged high fever reaching 39.5°C
Discomfort with neck movement
Preceding throat swelling, which more strongly suggests a postviral inflammatory process

data.description: Autoimmune thyroid inflammation that often produces a firm, painless goiter and occasionally a temporary hyperthyroid phase before normal or reduced thyroid function develops.
symptoms_in_common: Tachycardia, if a transient thyrotoxic phase is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset of prolonged high fever
Discomfort with neck movement

symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytosis is not a characteristic lymphoma finding and may reflect concurrent iron restriction
Mildly elevated INR is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma involving the spleen
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy characterized by Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background. Splenic involvement can cause fever, night sweats, weight loss, and anemia, although isolated splenic disease is rare.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells within an inflammatory background in the pathology images
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of detectable lymphadenopathy is unusual
An apparently isolated splenic mass is an uncommon presentation
Microcytosis and mildly elevated INR are not defining features

data.diagnosis: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma with possible large-cell transformation
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma predominantly affecting the spleen and bone marrow in older adults. Transformation to an aggressive large-cell lymphoma could explain severe constitutional symptoms and a focal splenic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, night sweats, and weight loss if transformation has occurred
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound weight loss and sustained fever are less typical of untransformed disease
A dominant splenic mass and apparent large atypical cells are less typical of the indolent form
Mildly elevated INR is not characteristic

data.description: A rare aggressive malignancy of histiocytic cells that may involve the spleen and produce large atypical cells with abundant cytoplasm. Diagnosis requires a histiocytic immunophenotype and exclusion of lymphoma and other malignancies.
symptoms_in_common: Splenomegaly with an apparent splenic mass
Large atypical cells in the supplied pathology images
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytosis is not characteristic
Mild INR elevation is nonspecific rather than a typical diagnostic feature

data.description: An uncommon extrapulmonary tuberculosis presentation producing splenic granulomas or abscess-like lesions. Negative initial testing does not completely exclude it, but the apparent atypical-cell pathology makes malignancy more concerning.
symptoms_in_common: Splenomegaly and a focal splenic lesion
Anemia and elevated ferritin from chronic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: The previous tuberculosis evaluation was unrevealing
Apparent large atypical cells are not typical of tuberculous granulomas
Mildly elevated INR is not a characteristic finding

diagnoses.name: Splenic involvement
diagnoses.title: Fibrosis of spleen[Schistosomiasis involving the skin]

data.diagnosis: Fabry disease with cardiac and renal involvement
data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A, producing glycosphingolipid accumulation in the heart, kidneys, and other tissues. This is the leading diagnosis given the markedly reduced leukocyte enzyme activity.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal insufficiency previously requiring dialysis and transplantation
Marked ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
High-voltage ECG complexes with repolarization abnormalities
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Epigastric discomfort, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Benign prostatic hypertrophy with obstructive nephropathy is a separate potential cause of renal dysfunction
Hyperparathyroidism is not a characteristic primary manifestation
Bilateral cataracts are less characteristic than the corneal changes associated with Fabry disease

data.diagnosis: Hypertensive heart disease with left ventricular hypertrophy
data.description: Chronic hypertension can cause ventricular hypertrophy and impaired relaxation, predisposing to atrial fibrillation and myocardial injury during severe tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: History of hypertension and chronic kidney disease
Ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Chest pressure and troponin elevation during tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Epigastric burning and vomiting are not characteristic manifestations
Bilateral cataracts are not explained by hypertensive heart disease

data.description: A usually inherited myocardial disorder characterized by ventricular hypertrophy not adequately explained by loading conditions, sometimes with outflow obstruction, diastolic dysfunction, and arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Marked ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
High-voltage ECG complexes with repolarization abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity suggests a storage disorder rather than sarcomeric disease
Chronic renal insufficiency and proteinuria are not typical primary manifestations
Epigastric burning and vomiting are not characteristic
Bilateral cataracts are not characteristic

data.description: An infiltrative cardiomyopathy caused by amyloid deposition, producing increased ventricular wall thickness, impaired filling, and arrhythmias. Some forms also cause proteinuric kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: High-voltage ECG complexes are less typical than the voltage-to-wall-thickness mismatch often seen in cardiac amyloidosis
Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity is not explained
Unremarkable serum protein electrophoresis and free light-chain ratio argue against light-chain amyloidosis, although they do not exclude all amyloid types
Bilateral cataracts are not characteristic

data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia with myocardial injury, potentially from coronary plaque disruption. Severe atrial fibrillation can alternatively cause supply-demand myocardial injury without an acute coronary blockage.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric burning, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness can be atypical ischemic symptoms
Hypertension and chronic kidney disease as cardiovascular risk factors
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Marked ventricular wall thickening is not explained by an acute coronary event
Longstanding proteinuric renal disease is not explained by an acute coronary event
Bilateral cataracts are unrelated

data.diagnosis: Perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, likely involving the left middle cerebral artery territory
data.description: A focal interruption of cerebral arterial blood flow around birth. The supplied MRI appears to show focal left-sided diffusion restriction, making acute arterial infarction the leading possibility; definitive interpretation requires the complete imaging study.
symptoms_in_common: Repeated right-sided limb clonic seizures, consistent with a left cerebral lesion
Seizure onset within the first day of life
Alertness and a normal neurological examination between seizures, which can occur in neonatal stroke
Apparent focal diffusion restriction on the supplied MRI

data.diagnosis: Neonatal cerebral sinovenous thrombosis with venous infarction
data.description: Thrombosis of cerebral veins or dural sinuses can cause focal brain injury and neonatal seizures. MR venography is needed to assess this possibility; the supplied arterial angiographic images do not exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Focal clonic seizures in the neonatal period
Repeated seizures affecting the same side
symptoms_not_in_common: Preserved alertness rather than encephalopathy
Flat anterior fontanelle without clinical evidence of raised intracranial pressure
Normal muscle tone and primitive reflexes

data.description: Brain injury from inadequate oxygen delivery or cerebral perfusion around delivery. Early seizures and fetal distress can fit, but the reassuring neonatal condition and apparently focal imaging abnormality make this less likely than stroke.
symptoms_in_common: Seizure onset approximately 6 hours after birth
Frequent fetal heart rate decelerations before delivery
Cerebral diffusion restriction can occur with hypoxic-ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Apgar scores of 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
Alertness and good responsiveness
Normal muscle tone and primitive reflexes
Repeated strictly right-sided clonic seizures with an apparently unilateral focal lesion rather than a typical diffuse injury pattern

data.description: Bleeding within or around the brain can irritate the cortex and produce focal neonatal seizures. Susceptibility-sensitive MRI or other appropriate imaging is necessary to identify blood products.
symptoms_not_in_common: Flat anterior fontanelle
Normal alertness, tone, and primitive reflexes
Stable vital signs without systemic deterioration
The supplied MRI appears more suggestive of focal restricted diffusion than a clearly demonstrated hemorrhage

data.description: An early-life epilepsy syndrome, sometimes associated with KCNQ2 or KCNQ3 variants, characterized by brief recurrent seizures in otherwise well newborns. A structural cerebral lesion argues against this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Normal responsiveness and neurological examination between episodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at 6 hours of life, earlier than the usual onset after the first day
An apparent focal diffusion-restricting cerebral lesion
Consistently right-sided seizures suggesting a localized structural cause

data.diagnosis: Takayasu arteritis with aortic regurgitation and acute heart failure
data.description: Large-vessel vasculitis affecting the aorta and its major branches, most often in young women. The images suggest diffuse aortic and branch-vessel wall thickening, branch-vessel narrowing, and substantial aortic regurgitation, making this the leading possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Right shoulder, flank, and intermittent back pain
Progressive exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough
Hypoxemic respiratory failure compatible with cardiogenic pulmonary edema
Cardiac murmur compatible with aortic regurgitation
Apparent aortic and branch-vessel wall thickening and narrowing on CT
Echocardiographic regurgitant flow and descending-aortic diastolic flow reversal
symptoms_not_in_common: Brief episodes of diarrhea are not characteristic
Recent dental cleaning is not a typical precipitating factor

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with severe aortic regurgitation
data.description: Infection of a cardiac valve can damage its leaflets and cause acute regurgitation, pulmonary edema, and systemic emboli. Blood cultures and detailed valve imaging would be needed to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive dyspnea and hypoxemic respiratory failure
Flank and back pain could reflect embolic or infectious complications
Recent dental cleaning provides a possible, but nonspecific, bacteremia exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse aortic and branch-vessel wall thickening with arterial narrowing is not typical of isolated endocarditis
Six months of intermittent back pain is less typical of an acute valve infection
Brief diarrhea is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with aortitis and valvular involvement
data.description: An autoimmune disease that can cause sterile valvular lesions, regurgitation, and, rarely, inflammation of the aorta. It is a less likely alternative to primary large-vessel vasculitis in this case.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac murmur and apparent aortic regurgitation
Dyspnea and respiratory failure potentially related to cardiac involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive aortic and major branch-vessel narrowing is uncommon in lupus
Isolated shoulder, flank, and back pain without other reported lupus manifestations is not a typical presentation
Brief episodes of diarrhea are not characteristic

data.description: A fibroinflammatory disorder that can produce thickening around the aorta and other arteries. Its vascular imaging findings can resemble large-vessel vasculitis, although it is very unusual in a 19-year-old woman.
symptoms_in_common: Aortic wall thickening suggested by CT
Possible involvement of multiple arterial territories
Dyspnea and murmur could occur if aortic involvement causes regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Age and sex are strongly atypical
Rapid progression to severe regurgitation and hypoxemic respiratory failure is an uncommon presentation
Brief diarrhea is not characteristic
Extensive branch-vessel stenosis is more suggestive of Takayasu arteritis

data.diagnosis: Bicuspid aortic valve with severe aortic regurgitation and associated aortopathy
data.description: A congenital two-leaflet aortic valve can become incompetent and may coexist with ascending-aortic disease. Severe regurgitation can cause heart failure, but this would not adequately explain diffuse inflammatory arterial changes.
symptoms_in_common: Nonproductive cough and hypoxemic respiratory failure compatible with pulmonary edema
Apparent substantial aortic regurgitation on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse aortic and branch-vessel wall thickening is not typical of congenital valve disease
Branch-vessel narrowing is not explained by uncomplicated bicuspid aortopathy
Shoulder, flank, and longstanding intermittent back pain are not typical without an additional complication
Brief diarrhea is not characteristic

data.description: A clot in the vein draining the small intestine, potentially causing intestinal congestion and ischemia. The arrowed mesenteric venous filling defect on the supplied CT appears most consistent with this diagnosis, although formal radiological confirmation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening abdominal pain over seven days
Failure to improve with proton pump inhibitor therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Belching is nonspecific rather than a characteristic manifestation

data.description: Thrombosis of the portal vein, sometimes extending from the superior mesenteric vein. The second CT image appears to show a portal venous filling defect, making combined portomesenteric thrombosis a significant possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Normal liver tests, which can occur in acute portal vein thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Left iliac fossa tenderness is less characteristic of isolated portal vein thrombosis
Belching is not a characteristic symptom

data.description: Inflammation of the pancreas causing upper abdominal pain and nausea. Recent orlistat exposure warrants consideration of a possible medication association, but normal pancreatic enzymes and the apparent vascular CT abnormalities make this diagnosis less likely.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal amylase and lipase despite ongoing symptoms
Left iliac fossa tenderness is not a typical principal finding
Apparent portomesenteric venous filling defects are not the defining imaging finding of pancreatitis

data.description: Inflammation of mesenteric fat that can produce abdominal pain and increased inflammatory markers. It can cause mesenteric haziness on CT, but true intravascular filling defects would favor thrombosis instead.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal tenderness with a relatively soft abdomen
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapidly worsening symptoms over one week are less typical than an indolent course
Apparent portal and mesenteric venous filling defects are not typical of uncomplicated mesenteric panniculitis
Belching is nonspecific

data.description: Inflammation of sigmoid colonic diverticula, usually producing left lower abdominal pain and inflammatory marker elevation. It could explain the left iliac fossa tenderness, but the dominant epigastric symptoms and apparent venous CT abnormalities favor another diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly epigastric pain and tenderness
Belching is not a characteristic symptom
Apparent portomesenteric venous filling defects are not typical of uncomplicated diverticulitis

data.description: A congenital blockage of the vaginal opening causes menstrual blood to accumulate in the vagina, sometimes extending into the uterus. The images appear to show a large pelvic fluid collection with internal echoes, favoring retained blood, although examination is needed to establish the obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episodes of less intense abdominal pain
Large pelvic collection containing internal echoes on ultrasound
Presentation at an age when menstruation commonly begins

data.description: A congenital partition across the vagina can obstruct menstrual outflow and produce a blood-filled, distended vagina. It can resemble an imperforate hymen clinically and on ultrasound.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic fluid collection with internal echoes compatible with retained blood

data.diagnosis: Obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly syndrome
data.description: A congenital reproductive tract anomaly, typically involving a duplicated uterus and obstruction of one vaginal compartment, causes retained menstrual blood and pelvic pain. Associated renal abnormalities and uterine duplication must be assessed; neither is established by these images.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent episodes of lower abdominal pain
Worsening hypogastric pain during early adolescence
Pelvic collection potentially representing retained menstrual blood
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparently single midline pelvic collection is less characteristic than a unilateral obstructed vaginal compartment

data.diagnosis: Ovarian torsion associated with an ovarian cyst
data.description: Twisting of the ovarian vascular pedicle can compromise blood supply and requires urgent assessment. An ovarian cyst can predispose to torsion, but these still images do not establish ovarian origin or assess blood flow.
symptoms_in_common: Acute, progressively worsening lower abdominal pain
Previous milder episodes that could reflect intermittent torsion
symptoms_not_in_common: Midline hypogastric localization is less typical than unilateral pelvic pain
The collection's appearance favors retained fluid or blood rather than a clearly enlarged torsed ovary

data.description: Inflammation of the appendix causes progressive abdominal pain, sometimes localized to the hypogastrium when the appendix lies in the pelvis. The supplied images do not demonstrate an inflamed appendix.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive worsening over the last few hours
Hypogastric pain, which can occur with a pelvic appendix
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous episodes of similar, less intense pain are less typical of a single acute appendicitis episode
A large pelvic collection with relatively homogeneous internal echoes is not a typical uncomplicated appendicitis finding

data.description: The strongest diagnostic fit: a contiguous-gene deletion syndrome characterized by multiple osteochondromas, enlarged parietal foramina, developmental impairment, and craniofacial abnormalities. The supplied microarray appears to show a deletion encompassing EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A, supporting this diagnosis despite a normal conventional karyotype.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple exostoses, with radiographs showing bony outgrowths around the wrist, proximal femora, and knees
Bilateral enlarged parietal foramina visible on skull imaging
Severe global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Hypotonia and inability to sit or walk independently
Craniofacial abnormalities, including a prominent nasal bridge and high-arched palate

data.description: A contiguous-gene deletion disorder involving TRPS1 and EXT1 on chromosome 8, causing multiple osteochondromas, short stature, characteristic facial features, sparse hair, and variable intellectual disability. It is an important clinical alternative, but the supplied chromosome 11 deletion favors Potocki-Shaffer syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Marked short stature and growth retardation
Prominent nasal and other craniofacial abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral enlarged parietal foramina
Profound early hypotonia with inability to sit or walk independently
Ptosis and nystagmus
Microcephaly is not a defining feature

data.description: An autosomal dominant skeletal disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EXT1 or EXT2, producing multiple cartilage-capped bony outgrowths near the growth plates. It explains the skeletal lesions but does not ordinarily explain the neurological and cranial findings.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic bony outgrowths involving several long bones
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Profound hypotonia
Microcephaly
Bilateral enlarged parietal foramina
Ptosis and nystagmus
Dysmorphic facial features
Low birth weight and marked generalized growth retardation

data.description: A genetic skull-ossification disorder, usually caused by a heterozygous ALX4 pathogenic variant, characterized by paired defects in the parietal bones. Isolated ALX4-related disease explains the skull findings but not the full multisystem presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral enlarged parietal foramina on skull radiographs and three-dimensional CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple exostoses
Severe global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Profound hypotonia and inability to sit or walk independently
Microcephaly
Marked growth retardation
Ptosis and nystagmus
The extensive combination of facial abnormalities

data.description: A disorder caused by PHF21A haploinsufficiency, associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and craniofacial abnormalities. Isolated PHF21A involvement could explain much of the neurological phenotype, but additional deletion of EXT2 and ALX4 better explains the complete case.
symptoms_in_common: Craniofacial abnormalities, including a prominent nasal bridge and down-turned mouth
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple exostoses
Bilateral enlarged parietal foramina
Microcephaly and marked growth retardation are not defining features
Ptosis and nystagmus are not defining features

data.description: Infestation by Sarcoptes scabiei that can present atypically in immunocompromised patients, with minimal itching and ulcerated or crusted lesions. The mite shown within the stratum corneum strongly supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Mite visible within the stratum corneum on the supplied histology
Multiple persistent skin lesions with crusting and ulceration
Scalp involvement, which can occur in atypical scabies
Underlying hematologic disease and impaired host defenses
Absence of itching can occur in immunocompromised patients
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ulceration is unusual in classic scabies and may indicate secondary infection
Normal IgE and eosinophil counts are less characteristic of extensive crusted scabies, although they do not exclude it

data.description: A deeper bacterial skin infection, usually caused by streptococci or Staphylococcus aureus, producing crusted ulcers. It could complicate an underlying scabies infestation.
symptoms_in_common: History of recurrent bacterial skin infections
Severe congenital neutropenia increasing susceptibility to infection
symptoms_not_in_common: An epidermal mite is not explained by bacterial ecthyma alone
Extensive scalp and abdominal involvement is less typical than lower-extremity involvement
Markedly elevated IgG is nonspecific rather than a defining feature

data.description: An inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis causing progressive ulcers, often associated with myelodysplastic syndromes and other hematologic disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying refractory anemia with excess blasts, a myelodysplastic disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: The epidermal mite favors infestation rather than a primary sterile inflammatory disorder
The photographs do not clearly demonstrate the classic undermined violaceous ulcer borders
Severe ulcer pain, a common feature, is not reported

data.description: An opportunistic Fusarium fungal infection that can produce multiple necrotic skin lesions in patients with neutropenia or hematologic malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple ulcerated lesions at separate body sites
Crusted or necrotic areas within some lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied histology shows a mite rather than fungal hyphae
Current neutrophil count is normal on G-CSF
Fever or other evidence of disseminated infection is not reported

data.description: An acute neutrophilic dermatosis associated with myeloid disorders and sometimes G-CSF exposure. It usually produces tender erythematous plaques, with ulceration occurring in atypical cases.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous lesions involving the scalp and trunk
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent ulcerations are less typical than tender, edematous plaques
An epidermal mite is not explained by Sweet syndrome
Fever and lesion tenderness are not reported
The supplied histology does not establish the characteristic dense dermal neutrophilic infiltrate

data.description: An aggressive pattern of podocyte injury characterized by collapse of glomerular capillaries and proliferation of overlying epithelial cells. The supplied biopsy image raises this possibility, although additional stains and pathology review are needed to distinguish it from crescentic glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible glomerular tuft collapse with prominent epithelial cells in the biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: RBC casts and prominent hematuria are more characteristic of inflammatory glomerulonephritis
Persistent fever is not typical of isolated collapsing glomerulopathy

data.description: A rapidly progressive inflammatory kidney disease with crescent formation and little or no immune deposition. It can be confined to the kidneys and occur despite negative ANCA testing.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid deterioration of kidney function over seven days
Negative ANCA does not exclude this diagnosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy proteinuria is less typical than moderate proteinuria
The apparent tuft collapse and epithelial proliferation in the image are not specific for pauci-immune disease

data.description: An autoimmune disease causing rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis, sometimes accompanied by pulmonary hemorrhage. Kidney-limited disease is possible; confirmation requires anti-GBM antibody testing and assessment for linear IgG staining on biopsy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Heavy proteinuria is less typical than a predominantly nephritic presentation
Normal chest CT does not support pulmonary involvement, although it does not exclude kidney-limited disease

data.description: An immune-complex glomerular disease caused by predominantly mesangial IgA deposition. A severe crescentic variant can cause rapidly progressive kidney failure in adolescents and young adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Four weeks of persistent fever and systemic illness are not typical of primary IgA nephropathy
Heavy proteinuria with rapid kidney failure is unusual outside severe crescentic disease

data.description: Immune-mediated glomerular inflammation associated with a recent or ongoing infection. Severe cases can develop crescents and rapidly progressive renal failure.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal complement levels are less typical, particularly for poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
Normal leukocyte count provides less support for an active bacterial infection
Heavy proteinuria is less typical than a predominantly nephritic presentation

data.diagnosis: Isolated myeloid sarcoma of the bile duct
data.description: An extramedullary tumor of immature myeloid cells that can obstruct the bile duct even when blood counts and bone marrow are normal. This is a leading consideration; confirmation requires myeloid markers such as myeloperoxidase, CD33, CD117, and lysozyme.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging suggesting hilar bile duct obstruction with upstream duct dilation
Tumor cells positive for CD45 and negative for several lymphoid markers
Normal blood counts and bone marrow, compatible with isolated extramedullary disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear contradictory findings; absence of marrow leukemia does not exclude isolated myeloid sarcoma

data.diagnosis: Primary biliary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma rarely arising in or around the bile ducts and causing obstructive jaundice. CD20, PAX5, and other B-cell markers are needed to assess this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Negative CD3 and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
Normal marrow, compatible with localized extranodal lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No strong contradictory findings in the supplied clinical data; the available immunostains do not establish B-cell lineage

data.diagnosis: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of the bile duct
data.description: An indolent mature B-cell lymphoma that can rarely involve biliary tissue and produce a localized stricture. Diagnosis requires characteristic morphology and confirmation of B-cell lineage.
symptoms_in_common: Conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and elevated alkaline phosphatase
Normal blood counts and uninvolved bone marrow
symptoms_not_in_common: The pictured infiltrate appears relatively atypical and blast-like rather than clearly showing the small mature lymphocytes expected in this lymphoma

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising near the hepatic bile duct confluence, commonly producing a hilar stricture and obstructive jaundice. It is an important imaging differential but is strongly disfavored by the reported tumor immunophenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging suggesting hilar obstruction and intrahepatic bile duct dilation
symptoms_not_in_common: CD45 positivity in the tumor cells is inconsistent with a conventional epithelial carcinoma
Histology appears to show a predominantly nonepithelial cellular infiltrate around preserved glands rather than malignant gland formation

data.diagnosis: Histiocytic sarcoma involving the biliary tract
data.description: A rare malignant tumor showing mature histiocytic differentiation that can arise outside lymph nodes. Confirmation requires markers such as CD163, CD68, and lysozyme, with exclusion of myeloid and lymphoid tumors.
symptoms_in_common: A localized biliary lesion causing jaundice
Negative tested T-cell markers and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
symptoms_not_in_common: The pictured cells appear less markedly pleomorphic and less abundant in cytoplasm than is typical of histiocytic sarcoma
